people.bio: Aaron M. Roth is a science fiction author and leader in artificial intelligence.  He has led research teams studying robotics, artificial intelligence, and safe/explainable AI in government and academic research labs including Carnegie Mellon University and University of Maryland.  In private industry he has contributed to consumer application, autonomous maritime vessels, AI for logistics, and more. He has published science fiction and academic papers and given talks on science and science fiction around the world. Additionally, he offers speculative fiction editing and game design consulting services. You can sign up for his mailing list at www.aaronmroth.com.
people.name: Aaron M. Roth

people.bio: Abhijeet is an Indian writer living in the US, a Viable Paradise alum, and an associate editor at Escape Pod. His work has appeared or is forthcoming in Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Adventitious, Translunar Travelers Lounge
people.name: Abhijeet Sathe

people.bio: Ada Palmer’s Terra Ignota series explores a future of borderless nations and globally commixing populations. The first volume Too Like the Lightning was a Hugo finalist and Compton Crook winner, while Ada received the Astounding Award for Best New Writer. Terra Ignota was a finalist for the Hugo for Best Series. Her next project is the Norse mythology fantasy "And Loki in His Prison" (2027; book 1 of "Hanged God's Game"). She teaches history at the University of Chicago, studying the Renaissance, Enlightenment, heresy, atheism, and censorship. Her pop history Inventing the Renaissance: Myths of a Golden Age (2025) uses Machiavelli to look at the origins of the myth of a bad Middle Ages & good Renaissance, and how golden and dark ages recur in our fiction and imaginations. She composes music including Sundown: Whispers of Ragnarok, and performs with the group Sassafrass. She studies anime/manga, especially Osamu Tezuka, post-WWII manga and feminist manga, and consults for anime and manga publishers.
people.name: Ada Palmer

people.bio: Adrian Collins founded Grimdark Magazine and leads a global team of passionate volunteers and freelancers in creating a quarterly print magazine, novellas, anthologies, and video story recordings. The team also runs a website producing hundreds of books reviews, interviews, and articles each year in support of the publishing, reading, artistic, and writing communities--all done by people and without AI.
people.name: Adrian Collins

people.bio: Adrienne Bengtson, who writes science fiction as Adrienne Miles, picked back up her lifelong interest in writing after retiring from the US Air Force and a 25-year career as a librarian. Instead of slowing down, she published her debut novel, Spider's Wyrd, in March 2025 and is working on a sequel. A handful of short stories set in the same universe are also in the works.
people.name: Adrienne Miles

people.bio: Ai Jiang is a Chinese-Canadian writer, Ignyte, Bram Stoker, and Nebula Award winner, and Hugo, Astounding, Locus, Aurora, and BFSA Award finalist from Changle, Fujian currently residing in Toronto, Ontario. Her work can be found in F&SF, The Dark, Clarkesworld, The Masters Review, Prairie Fire, Ex-Puritan, among others. She is the recipient of Odyssey Workshop's 2022 Fresh Voices Scholarship and the author of A Palace Near the Wind, Linghun and I AM AI. Find her at www.aijiang.ca
people.name: Ai Jiang

people.bio: A. J. Hackwith is a queer writer of fantasy and science fiction living in the cryptid-filled woods of the Pacific Northwest. A.J. is the author of a number of fantasy novels, including the acclaimed LIBRARY OF THE UNWRITTEN fantasy trilogy, TOTO, and the upcoming cozy fantasy, GOBLIN MARKET. Her work has been featured in Uncanny Magazine, the Washington Post, and assorted anthologies. You can find A.J. ensconced on Instagram, Patreon, and other dark corners of the Internet as @ajhackwith.
people.name: A. J. Hackwith

people.bio:
AK Llyr is an American veteran, writer, speaker, Freemason, and futurist.

He has a lifetime of global experience with military & government service, including: Intelligence analysis, engineering, physical & network security, with hands-on work in some of the world’s most challenging environments.

Born into a generational military family on an American base in Europe, he learned personal Honor, Duty to Humanity, and Patriotism early. These principles shaped his path through decades of service and exploration to where he is today.

AK holds degrees in Computer Science, Business and Engineering. He continues his education when possible through college and online education in physics, engineering, political science and philosophy.

Other skills he has honed in millitary and civilian life over the decades inclue high level competencies in construction, desert, arctic and jungle survival, modern history, scuba, skydiving and predictive modeling.


He also walks dogs.
people.name: AK Llyr

people.bio: Akua Lezli Hope, a Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry (SFPA), is a multi-award-winning creator, wisdom seeker & paraplegic, in print since 1974 with 500+ poems published. Her collections include Embouchure: Poems on Jazz and Other Musics (Writer’s Digest book award), Them Gone, & Otherwheres (Elgin Award). Her honors include NEA, NYFA, NYSCA, IGNYTE, Rhysling, & Critter awards. She edited NOMBONO, the first anthology of BIPOC speculative poetry. Her new collection is TELEPATH from Gnashing Teeth Publishing. She created the ongoing Speculative Sundays Poetry Reading series, now in its 7th year. Her short fiction appears in Dark Matter, Africa Risen & AfroFuturism Short Stories, among others. A multimedia artist creating sculpture, wearables, and adornment, she sings, practices her soprano sax and hopes for the end of all suffering for all sentience. akualezlihope.com speculativepoetry.com
people.name: Akua Lezli Hope

people.bio: A. M. Vincent is a historian of religion who specialises in religion and SFF.
people.name: Alana M. Vincent

people.bio: I'm a retired software engineer. I was a mentor for a high school FIRST Robotics team for twenty years. I am a professional Klingon speaker and translator, and some of my work appears in multiple Star Trek series.
people.name: Alan Anderson

people.bio: Alasdair Stuart is a professional enthusiast, pop culture analyst, writer and voice actor. He serves on the board of the Escape Artists Foundation and hosts their weekly horror fiction podcast, PseudoPod. Alasdair is an Audioverse Award winner, a Hugo and BFA finalist, and has won the Karl Edward Wagner award twice. He writes the award-nominated free weekly pop culture newsletter THE FULL LID. Follow him on Bluesky for daily writing exercises, podcast and movie recommendations, and photos of his cat.
people.name: Alasdair Stuart

people.bio: Alex Mui is the founder of the Con History Project and TransformARTive. They are the creator of the comic series Wrath of Con which is a historical retelling of the rise of First Fandom and road to Worldcon 1939, along with So You Want to be a Con Artist, Shifter School, and Would've Bit You.
people.name: Alexander Mui (Con History)

people.bio:
Alexandra Carlota Velasco is a Mexican creative director, filmmaker, and multimedia artist based in Los Angeles. A graduate of Parsons School of Design, she creates visually striking work that blends horror, magical realism, surrealism, and social commentary through a distinctly female perspective.

With a background in performance art, film, and digital storytelling, her work explores themes of transformation, justice, identity, and the supernatural. Her films and multimedia projects have screened internationally at festivals and museums, including Final Girls Berlin, Fashion Film Festival Milano, and NewFilmmakers LA, and have been featured in Vogue, i-D, Elle, IndieWire, NoBudge, and Variety.

Velasco is the founder of Dreams Incarnate, a creative studio dedicated to bold visual storytelling, and co-founder of Sunstock, Los Angeles’ first solar-powered music and arts festival. In 2021, she was selected for Blackmagic Collective’s Future Directors of Studio Features program. Her latest film, Infierno Eterno (Eternal Inferno), premiered at Final Girls Berlin in 2025.
people.name: Alexandra Carlota Velasco

people.bio: Alexandra Rowland is the author of a dozen fantasy novels, such as A Taste of Gold and Iron, Yield Under Great Persuasion, Running Close to the Wind, and the recent runaway Kickstarter success The Wisdom of Emperors. They are also a four-time Hugo Award nominated podcaster, they hold a degree in world literature, mythology, and folklore, and all their work is supervised by their feline quality control manager.
people.name: Alexandra Rowland

people.bio: Alex Brown is a queer Black librarian, local historian, writer, and author of two books on the history of Napa County, California’s marginalized communities. They have a BA with honors in Anthropology and Sociology, a Master's of Library and Information Science, and a Master's in US History. They are an Ignyte award winning and Hugo award nominated writer and critic who covers speculative fiction and young adult literature for Reactor Magazine, Locus Magazine, NPR Books, Reader's Digest, and elsewhere. They also write on topics such as queerness, Black history, librarianship, and pop culture.
people.name: Alex Brown

people.bio: Alex Gurevich is the CIO and founder of HonTe Investments, located in the Bay Area. He was born in St. Petersburg, Russia and earned a Ph.D. in Mathematics from the University of Chicago. He has published several science fiction and fantasy stories, as well as two bestselling investment books and a number or articles.
people.name: Alex Gurevich

people.bio: Alex Kingsley (they/them) is a writer, comedian, game designer, and playwright. They are a co-founder of the new media company Strong Branch Productions. They are the author of Empress of Dust, Relic of Haven and The Strange Garden and Other Weird Tales, as well as short fiction appearing in Translunar Travelers Lounge, Radon Journal, Sci-Fi Lampoon, and more. Alex’s sci-fi plays have been produced in LA, Philadelphia, and Chicago. Alex’s SFF-related non-fiction has appeared in Strange Horizons, Interstellar Flight Magazine, and Ancillary Review of Books. Alex is currently a graduate student studying speculative fiction at the University of Illinois Chicago.
people.name: Alex Kingsley

people.bio: Alex Pheby is a writer and academic, author of the Cities of the Weft trilogy, and professor of Creative Writing at Newcastle University
people.name: Alex Pheby

people.bio: Computer systems engineer and hard sci-fi author Alex Pimienta brings real-world grit and technical expertise to his novel, Deep Dream. An instrument-rated private pilot, inshore skipper, and Advanced Space Academy alumnus, his passion for exploration extends far beyond the page. Alex is also a proven survivalist, having successfully conquered the grueling 21-day challenge on Discovery Channel's Naked and Afraid. Whether navigating the skies, the seas, or the harsh wilderness, he channels his adventurous spirit and technical background into crafting deeply grounded, high-stakes science fiction.
people.name: Alex Pimienta

people.bio: Alex Shvartsman (Brooklyn, NY) is the author of The Best of All Possible Planets (2026), Kakistocracy (2023), The Middling Affliction (2022), and Eridani’s Crown. Over 120 of his stories have appeared in Analog, Nature, Strange Horizons, etc. He won the WSFA Small Press Award for Short Fiction and was a three-time finalist for each the BSFA and Canopus Awards. His translations from Russian have appeared in Clarkesworld, Reactor, Analog, Asimov’s, F&SF, etc. Alex has edited over a dozen anthologies, including the long-running Unidentified Funny Objects series. Alex is the Narrative Director for Card Advantage Games, working on Reclusion video game (www.reclusionthegame.com). His website is http://www.alexshvartsman.com.
people.name: Alex Shvartsman

people.bio: Alison Belle is Skyboat's publishing and production coordinator, as well as a director of over 150 Adamant podcasts and over 50 audiobooks, including her Earphones Award winning compilation EGYPTIAN NIGHTS & OTHER TALES OF IMAGINATION AND ROMANCE by Alexander Pushkin and the Audie-nominated THE QUEST OF THE SILVER FLEECE by W.E.B Du Bois. One of Alison's specialties at Skyboat is the creation of original audio short story compilations. Aside from direction and production, Alison is one of the co-producers of Adamant's Lightspeed and Nightmare podcasts, and a host of Lightspeed, and has also begun narrating. Outside of Skyboat, Alison is also the lead singer, rhythm guitarist, pianist, and co-songwriter for Meteor Street, a literary rock band based in Los Angeles.
people.name: Alison Belle Bews

people.bio: Alison has been Running Children's Programming at Conventions for nearly 40 years, yes she started early. She has her degree in elementary education, and has also been involved in music programming, costuming, reading and and a whole lot of crafting and diy work, and she currently is a Specialist at The Home Depot in the San Francisco Bay Area. Come on over the Camp Fuzzy to see her work in action.
people.name: Alison Stern

people.bio: A. L. Kaplan's love of books started as a child and sparked a creative imagination. Born on a cold winter morning in scenic northern New Jersey, she is the author of the novel, Star Touched, and several short stories including Hummingbird and Mark of the Goddess, which includes original illustrations. She is a member of the Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Association, is the past president of Maryland Writers' Association, and holds an MFA in sculpture from the Maryland Institute College of Art. When not writing or indulging in her fascination with wolves, this proud mother of two lives in Maryland with her husband and dog. Learn more about A. L. at ALKaplanAuthor.com, @ALKaplanAuthor on social media.
people.name: A. L. Kaplan

people.bio: A L Raden (she/her) is an award-winning multidisciplinary storyteller (artist, writer, designer) who loves exploring layered, character-driven storytelling, especially with an emphasis on magic, myth, and nature. Her art primarily features joyful fantasy and science fiction original charcoal drawings and pointillism-style paintings. She’s also contributed to multiple comic, essay, and prose fiction anthologies and stories as a writer, inker, and letterer. In the convention space, she's volunteered for local MN conventions for more than a decade, including seven years as a con co-chair.
people.name: A. L. Raden

people.bio: Alyc Helms likes tea, foxes, and making stuff up for fun and profit. They are the author of the Adventures of Mr. Mystic novels from Angry Robot and, as M.A. Carrick, the co-author (with Marie Brennan) of the Rook & Rose trilogy and the Sea Beyond duology from Orbit Books.
people.name: Alyc Helms

people.bio: Amal El-Mohtar writes fiction, poetry, and criticism. She won the Hugo, Nebula, and Locus Awards for her short story “Seasons of Glass and Iron” and again for her novella This Is How You Lose the Time War, written with Max Gladstone, which also won the BSFA and Aurora awards, became a New York Times bestseller, and has been translated into over ten languages. Her reviews and articles have appeared in the NYT and on NPR Books. Seasons of Glass and Iron: Stories, her long-awaited collection, is out now from Tordotcom Publishing. She lives in Ottawa, Canada. Online at: amalelmohtar.com.
people.name: Amal El-Mohtar

people.bio: Librarian and Hugo-nominated blogger, frequent WSFS Con volunteer based in Edmonton, Co-Chair of the Edmonton in 2030 Worldcon Bid
people.name: Amanda Wakaruk

people.bio: Amy Salley is a longtime SFF fan, having cut her teeth on teen urban fantasy and Star Trek:TNG in her youth. Amy resides in Atlanta, lawyers as a day job, and co-hosts the hilariously feminist podcast Hugo, Girl! with her three besties Haley Zapal, Lori Anderson, and Kevin Anderson.
people.name: Amy Salley

people.bio: Anand Gandhi is widely regarded as the film auteur who ushered in a new wave of Indian cinema. His first film, Ship of Theseus, won the National Award for Best Picture - the Indian equivalent of an Academy Award. It was also on The Critics’ Circle, UK’s list of 15 “life-changing” films of the past century. His next film, Tumbbad - a genre film which used horror as an allegory - became the region’s most-watched genre film of the last two decades. His non-fiction production, An Insignificant Man, was India’s most commercially successful documentary film. Anand’s films have won the highest honors at the international film festivals of Toronto, Venice, Transylvania, Tokyo, Hong Kong, and have been globally distributed by Disney, Netflix, PrimeVideo, and Channel4.
people.name: Anand Gandhi

people.bio: Anastasia Hunter is a Master Class costumer and droid builder with a passion for science fiction, fantasy, and steamy things that go bump in the night. During the week she can be found working for the California Dept. of Transportation as an eminent domain and Utility relocation specialist. By night she moonlights as a 30 year veteran con runner, 501st Tusken Raider, avid 3D printer, a half-elven pirate D&D gamer, National Park enthusiast, and card carrying member of AARP.
people.name: Anastasia Hunter

people.bio: I am a Visiting Assistant Professor of English at Illinois Wesleyan University, with a focus on 19th-century literature and science fiction (and thus, the emergence of sci-fi in the 19th century). I have taught and presented broadly on these topics for the past decade.
people.name: Anastasia Klimchynskaya

people.bio: I am the Director of Silicon Valley Robotics and the Robotics Fellow at Singularity University. I have delivered keynotes at major tech conferences around the world. I speak about robots and startups, the commercialization and promise of robotics, the potential impact of robotics on society, career journeys in the emerging deep tech sector, human-robot interaction and ethics, and on creating intentional innovation communities to maximize our potential.
people.name: Andra Keay

people.bio: Andrea Blythe is an award-winning author, poet, game writer — and lover of the fantastical, horrifying, and weird. She is the author of four poetry chapbooks, the most recent being Necessary Poisons (Interstellar Flight Press, 2024). She written, designed, and published several video games, including Monochrome Heights (One Frog Games, 2025) and What Lies Underneath (2022). She is also a member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Poetry Association and the Horror Writers Association. Learn more at: https://linktr.ee/andreablythe.
people.name: Andrea Blythe

people.bio: Andrea Hairston ran away from the physics lab to the theatre as a young thing and has been a scientist, artiste, and hoodoo conjurer ever since. She is a novelist, poet, playwright, and L. Wolff Kahn 1931 Professor Emerita of Theatre and Africana Studies at Smith College. Andrea is the author of Archangels of Funk, shortlisted for the 2025 Le Guin Prize; Mindscape, a Carl Brandon award winner and finalist for the Phillip K. Dick and Otherwise awards; Will Do Magic For Small Change, a New York Times Editor’s pick and finalist for the Mythopoeic, Lambda, and Otherwise Awards; Redwood and Wildfire, a 2022 Washington Post Best Book, Otherwise and Carl Brandon award winner; and Master of Poisons on the Kirkus Review’s Best SF&F of 2020. Andrea bikes at night year-round, meeting bears, multi-legged creatures of light and breath, and the occasional shooting star. The Redemption Center is Closed on Sundays is out May, 2026.
people.name: Andrea Hairston

people.bio: Andrea Horbinski earned her PhD in history and new media from the University of California, Berkeley. She is the author of Manga’s First Century: How Creators and Fans Made Japanese Comics, 1905-1989 (2025, University of California Press), which won the 2026 Eisner Award for Best Scholarly/Academic Work. She also serves as a judge for the Sidewise Awards.
people.name: Andrea Horbinski

people.bio: Andrea is the author of Man Made Monsters, a YA horror story cycle novel and The Art Thieves, a YA Indian Territory futurism. She wrote Chooch Helped, illustrated by Rebecca Kunz (Cherokee) who won the 2025 Caldecott. All published by Levine Querido. Her first book, Mary and the Trail of Tears was published by Capstone and was on the NPR best books list. Oklahoma Children’s book winner When We Gather was published by Heartdrum/Harper Collins and illustrated by Madie Goodnight (Chickasaw). She is a contributor to several anthologies including Never Whistle at Night, Legendary Fry Bread Drive-In (Printz Award Winner) and Ancestor Approved. Death in the Tallgrass, MG historical fiction was released in September.
people.name: Andrea L. Rogers

people.bio: I've been a lifelong science fiction and fantasy fan and have always had a strong interest in 80's movies/animation, pop culture, and martial arts. I was a founding member of the University of Washington’s Anime Discovery Project in the early 90's and was one of the founders of Sakura-Con, Seattle's largest anime convention. In the mundane world I make my living as a structural engineer specializing in seismic design with over 30 years of experience in the design of building structures throughout the Pacific Northwest.
people.name: Andreas Quinn

people.bio: Andrea Stewart is the Sunday Times bestselling author of The Drowning Empire trilogy and The Hollow Covenant trilogy, the forthcoming thriller Someone Else’s Daughter, and works as a writing coach at The Novelry. The Bone Shard Daughter was a finalist for numerous awards, including the Goodreads Choice Award and the British Fantasy Award. She now lives in sunny California, and in addition to writing, can be found herding cats, looking at birds, and falling down research rabbit holes.
people.name: Andrea Stewart

people.bio: andré carrington is the author of Audiofuturism: Science Fiction Radio Drama and the Black Fantastic Imagination, as well as Speculative Blackness: The Future of Race in Science Fiction, and editor of The Black Fantastic: 20 Afrofuturist Stories. He is an English professor at the University of California-Riverside where he directs the program in Speculative Fiction & Cultures of Science.
people.name: andré m carrington

people.bio: Andrew Givler is the bestselling author of the urban fantasy series the Debt Collection and the progression fantasy saga Ironbound, published by Aethon Books. In addition to his writing, he runs the YouTube channel Sigils, where he creates gaming content for an audience of more than 1.4 million subscribers.
people.name: Andrew Givler

people.bio:
Andrew Kelly Stewart’s writing spans the literary, science fiction, fantasy, and horror
genres. His short fiction has appeared in The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction and
ZYZZYVA. He is a Clarion Workshop alum and holds an MFA in Creative Writing from San Diego
State University. We Shall Sing a Song into the Deep is his first publication with Tor.com.
Stewart teaches and writes in southern California.
people.name: Andrew Kelly Stewart

people.bio: Andrew Majors writes sci-fi, horror, fantasy and the weird. His work has been published with 34Orchard, tdotSpec, House of Long Shadows, and The NoSleep Podcast. His essays and other writing can be found at andrewmajors.wordpress.com. He lives near Boise.
people.name: Andrew Majors

people.bio:
Andrew Ross is a person of several identities who was dragged to a filksing in 1997 by an over-enthusiastic friend, and found the first members of his adopted family in fandom. Today, his songs tend to focus on various media plots, political rants, and true stories from legal situations too crazy to make up. He occasionally performs with a geek band called Possible Side Effects.

In the mundane world, Andrew is an attorney and proud father of three in Eugene, Oregon.
people.name: Andrew Ross

people.bio: Andrew Rubin is filmmaker, screenwriter, and author of Hell or High Winter (Rare Bird / Simon & Schuster). As a WGA screenwriter, Andrew has spent over 15 years working in screenplay development with successful Hollywood companies such as Roth/Kirschenbaum Films and eOne, and has been a mentor with the Veteran's Writing Program at the Writers Guild Foundation for the past six years. Andrew co-directed the inspirational documentary Ride with Larry, about Parkinson's, inspired by his father's battle against the disease. The film’s exploration of Parkinson's and medical marijuana received global attention, and helped spark a broader conversation about dignity, treatment, and the role of alternative medicine. He is also the cofounder and president of Symptom Media, an innovative mental health education platform used by over 500 universities, hospitals and medical schools worldwide to help train students and clinicians and destigmatize mental illness.
people.name: Andrew Rubin

people.bio: Executive industry leader with over 30 years of experience driving successful results in large enterprises, foundations and startups operating in fast-paced, cutting edge environments. Extensive experience working across all aspects of tech-focused organizations including CxO leadership, strategy & innovation, business development & sales, marketing, product development and operations in both US and across international markets.
people.name: Andrew Tauhert

people.bio: Andy Dudak’s original stories have been in Analog, Apex, Asimov’s, Clarkesworld, Daily Science Fiction, Interzone, The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction, Science Fiction World (科幻世界), and numerous Year’s Best anthologies. His story ‘Love in the Time of Immuno-Sharing’ was a finalist for the Eugie Foster Award. His translations of Chinese sci-fi are widely published. His novel 'A Killing in Souls' is forthcoming from Dark Matter Ink. Andy believes in the healing power of D&D.
people.name: Andy Dudak

people.bio: I am, first and foremost, a storyteller and an artist--words are my palette. Fantasy and science fiction are my genres of choice, and I love to explore the darker side of human nature through the filter of heroes, villains, and everything in between. I'm also a book lover and a guy who just loves to meet new people and spend hours talking about my fascination for the worlds I encounter in the pages of fantasy and sci-fi novels.
people.name: Andy Peloquin

people.bio: Angela Acosta, Ph.D. (she/her) is an Assistant Professor of Spanish at the University of South Carolina. She is a 2022 Dream Foundry Contest for Emerging Writers Finalist, 2022 Somos en Escrito Extra-Fiction Contest Honorable Mention, and Utopia Award nominee. Her Rhysling nominated poetry has appeared in Heartlines Spec, Shoreline of Infinity, Apparition Lit, Radon Journal, and Space & Time. She is author of the Elgin nominated poetry collections Summoning Space Travelers (Hiraeth Publishing, 2022) and A Belief in Cosmic Dailiness (Red Ogre Review, 2023). She has published on female life-writing, poetry, and literary personas in Persona Studies, Ámbitos Feministas, and Feminist Modernist Studies.
people.name: Angela Acosta

people.bio: I am a biologist (PhD, MS) specializing in biomechanics, or how organisms move. I am also an avid video gamer, science fiction fan, and want nothing more than an epic TV series based on NK Jemison's Inheritance trilogy and for the Expanse series to continue on for another 20 novels. I am terrible at trivia, but it doesn't deter me from playing.
people.name: Angela Horner

people.bio: Angela Liu is a Chinese-American writer/poet based in NYC and Tokyo. She is a three-time Nebula Award and 2025 Astounding Award Finalist. Her work has also been nominated for the Hugo, Locus, Ignyte, and Rhysling Awards. She previously researched mixed reality at Keio University in Japan with a focus on new narrative platforms. Her stories and poems are published/forthcoming in Clarkesworld, Strange Horizons, Uncanny Magazine, and Lightspeed, among others. Check out more of her work at liu-angela.com or find her on Twitter/Instagram @liu_angela and on Bluesky @angelaliu.bsky.social.
people.name: Angela Liu

people.bio: Annabelle is a Filipino-American immigrant who’s loved stories since she was a child. She currently works for an independent romance bookstore sharing her latest reads in Temecula, CA.
people.name: Annabelle Fletcher

people.bio: Anna Faktorovich is the Director and Founder of the Anaphora Literary Press. In 2025, she began teaching as an Assistant Professor of English at Dickinson State University. She previously taught for over four years at schools including the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley, Edinboro University of Pennsylvania and the Middle Georgia State College. She has a Ph.D. in English Literature and Criticism, and an MA in Comparative Literature. She published with Routledge a textbook called: Introduction to the Attribution of Literature (2025). She published two academic books with McFarland: Rebellion as Genre in the Novels of Scott, Dickens and Stevenson (2013) and The Formulas of Popular Fiction: Elements of Fantasy, Science Fiction, Romance, Religious and Mystery Novels (2014). She edits three periodicals for Anaphora tri-annually: Pennsylvania Literary Journal (2009-), Cinematic Codes Review (2016), and Speculative: The Magazine (2025-). She has presented her research at the MLA, SAMLA, EAPSU, SWWC, BWWC and many other conferences. And she won the MLA Bibliography, Kentucky Historical Society and Brown University Military Collection fellowships.
people.name: Anna Faktorovich

people.bio: Annalee Newitz is a science journalist who writes science fiction. They are the author, most recently, of the novella "Automatic Noodle" and the nonfiction book "Stories Are Weapons: Psychological Warfare and the American Mind."
people.name: Annalee Newitz

people.bio: Anne Keck writes speculative fiction of many flavors and is published in several short story anthologies. She's working on several novels, one of which will be her debut! Anne believes in ocean swimming, outrigger paddling, live music, public libraries, climate action, feminism, inclusivity, and cooking as an expression of love. Originally from Sonoma County, California, she and her husband now call Maui home. Find Anne in the ocean at Kahekili Beach or at her website, www.annekeck.com
people.name: Anne Keck

people.bio: I’m a geek in training and a dedicated consumer who loves tech, fandoms, and getting lost in media. Curious and culture driven, I plunge into whatever sparks my interest next.
people.name: Annie Shin

people.bio: Born in Jamaica and raised in Atlanta, Ann Michelle Harris writes sci-fi/fantasy and anime reviews for the Hugo and Ignyte Award winning Nerds of a Feather. She recently won the Georgia Author of the Year Award in the Sci-Fi/Fantasy category for her debut YA fantasy novel North, and she has speculative short stories published in various anthologies and literary magazines, including FIYAH and Midnight & Indigo. Find her at annmichelleharris.com.
people.name: Ann Michelle Harris

people.bio: By day, Anthony Francis creates intelligent machines and emotional robots; by night, he writes science fiction and draws comic books. Anthony co-edited the award-winning anthology THE NEURODIVERSIVERSE: ALIEN ENCOUNTERS and wrote the award-winning urban fantasy FROST MOON and its sequels BLOOD ROCK and LIQUID FIRE, all starring magical tattoo artist Dakota Frost. His steampunk includes JEREMIAH WILLSTONE AND THE CLOCKWORK TIME MACHINE and stories in TWELVE HOURS LATER, THIRTY DAYS LATER, SOME TIME LATER and NEXT STOP ON THE #13. Anthony lives in South Carolina with his wife and cats but his heart belongs in Atlanta. Follow Anthony at dresan.com.
people.name: Anthony Francis

people.bio: Antonia Hodgson is the author of The Raven Scholar, a Sunday Times bestselling fantasy epic and the first novel in the Eternal Path trilogy. She is currently working on its sequel, The Fox in Winter. Her first novel, The Devil in the Marshalsea, won the CWA Historical Dagger and was shortlisted for the Theakston Crime Novel of the Year. She lives in Kent, UK.
people.name: Antonia Hodgson

links.othersocialmedia: I am not on social media - I have old Facebook and X accounts but don't use them.

people.bio: Anuja Varghese is an award-winning writer of literary fiction, fantasy, and erotica/romance where women of color get leading roles! In 2023, her genre-blending short story collection, titled CHRYSALIS, won the Governor General’s Literary Award for Fiction, and in 2024, was longlisted for the Carol Shields Prize for Fiction, among others. Her debut novel, A KISS OF CRIMSON ASH, the first in a new medieval India-inspired romantasy trilogy, was released earlier this year, with book two scheduled for release in spring 2027. Anuja lives in Canada with her partner, two kids, and two cats. Find Anuja at anujavarghese.com or on social (@anuja_v).
people.name: Anuja Varghese

people.bio: Aparna Verma was born in Rajasthan, India, and grew up in the United States. She graduated from Stanford University with Honors in the Arts and a B.A. in English. In 2021, she self-published The Boy with Fire, which quickly went viral on TikTok, and was later republished by Orbit Books as The Phoenix King in 2023. When she is not writing, Aparna likes to lift heavy (arm days are her favorite), dance to Bollywood music, and find cozy cafes to read myths from ancient worlds. You can connect with Aparna on TikTok at @aparnawrites, and Twitter and Instagram at @spirited_gal.
people.name: Aparna Verma

people.bio: Arendse Lund won the 2021 Staunch Prize for a thriller in which no woman was hurt. Her work has appeared in Analog, Ellery Queen, Shotgun Honey, and The Fabulist, among others. You can find her at www.arend.se
people.name: Arendse Lund

people.bio: Ariela is a lifelong fan of speculative fiction. She is a professional artist and calligrapher who does tie-in work based on novels as well as general geekery, and a three-time Hugo finalist in the Fan Artist category. Ariela is powered by tea and a desire to leave a better world for the next generation.
people.name: Ariela Housman
Ari Rabkin

people.bio: Arkady Martine is the author of the Teixcalaan series, the novella Rose/House, a multitude of short stories, and various other science fiction, fantasy, & horror. she is also Dr. AnnaLinden Weller, who is a Byzantinist, a climate & energy policy analyst, and a city planner. She is not bored, but she is often tired.
people.name: Arkady Martine

people.bio: ARLEY SORG is an associate agent at kt literary and Senior Editor at Locus Magazine. He is a two-time World Fantasy finalist and three-time Locus Award finalist for his work as co-Editor-in-Chief at Fantasy Magazine. He is also a three-time Ignyte finalist, a Solstice recipient, and more. Arley is a book reviewer for Lightspeed, an interviewer for Clarkesworld, and a columnist for F&SF, among other projects. He was the week five instructor at the six-week Clarion West workshop, and has taught at and been a guest speaker for numerous other organizations, including the Odyssey workshop, Cascade workshop, Wayward Wormhole, and many more.
people.name: Arley Sorg

people.bio: Arnold Leibovit Produced-Directed The Puppetoon Movie (1987, 2026), The Fantasy Film Worlds of George Pal (1986), The Puppetoon Movie Volume 2 & 3 (2020, 2023), Executive Produced The Time Machine (2002) (Warner Bros.-Steven Spielberg), Producing a new reimagined The Time Machine with Warner Bros., Produced the Original Motion Picture Soundtrack Score for The Time Machine, Co-Directed Rascal Dazzle (1978) (Narrated by Jerry Lewis) and others. Friends with Mr. & Mrs. George Pal for over 20 years and has been the keeper of the flame for Pal.  Recipient of many awards including The George Pal Memorial Award (Saturn) from the Academy of Science Fiction, Fantasy & Horror, the Rondo Award and 10 film festival awards.
people.name: Arnold Leibovit

people.bio: Arturo Serrano is an Ignyte-winning, Hugo-winning reviewer and editor at the blog Nerds of a Feather, as well as a member of the editorial teams at Strange Horizons and Galactic Journey. He wrote the alternate history novel To Climates Unknown.
people.name: Arturo Serrano

people.bio: Ashaya has been podcasting since 2012 with History of Westeros and attended their first WorldCon in 2018. They are nominated for their first Hugo Award this year, 2026! While their podcast focuses on the world of Westeros, they are also a science-fiction fan, cosplayer, and gamer.
people.name: Ashaya

people.bio:
Hi, I’m Ash, I’m 402 gay years old, and have been a major F/SF fan and not-always-successful writer all that time. However, I’ve just self-published his ‘The Thin Woman’, first in a series of detective stories set on a generation ship fleet, so all that’s about to change!
	Until then, my day job is as a psychologist, psychotherapist (one of those is a science and the other is a mostly made up, so in a way it’s still SF!) and facilitator/trainer, running courses on people skills and writing and editing for the UN.
people.name: ASH CHARLTON

people.bio: Ash Huang is the author of The Secret Lives of Immortals, forthcoming in 2027 from Orbit. Her short fiction appears in Lady Churchill’s Rosebud Wristlet, Nightmare, Lightspeed, Ecotone, and elsewhere. She won the 2022 Diverse Worlds Grant from the Speculative Literature Foundation, and is a grateful alum of the Roots. Wounds. Words. Workshop, the Tin House Winter Workshop and Reading Fellowship, and the Periplus Fellowship. She is currently a Brown Handler Resident with Friends of the San Francisco Public Library and an editor at Orion’s Belt.
people.name: Ash Huang

people.bio: Ashlyn Frank is a Writer and Director based in New York City. She writes plays for the stage and screen in addition to short tales of speculative fiction and horror. Recent collaborations & publications include: Chamber Theatre Productions, Commonwealth Shakespeare Company, Chango Film, The Iris Theatre, Theatre Right Now, The Road Theatre, Ellipses Magazine, Rooted Literary Magazine, Spectral Film Journal, and Apricity Magazine. You can follow Ashlyn on instagram @ash.grace.frank, and view her work on ashlynfrank.com.
people.name: Ashlyn Frank

people.bio: A.T. Greenblatt is a Nebula Award winning writer and mechanical engineer. She lives in New York City where she's known to frequently subject her friends to various cooking and home brewing experiments. Her work has been nominated for a Hugo, Locus, World Fantasy, and Sturgeon Award, has been in multiple Year's Best anthologies, and has appeared in Reactor, Uncanny, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Nightmare, and Clarkesworld, as well as other fine publications. You can find her online at http://atgreenblatt.com and on Bluesky at @AtGreenblatt
people.name: A. T. Greenblatt

people.bio: A volcano of encouragement shaped a lot like a person, I've been commissioning editor at Improbable Press for the last eleven years, have published two books of fiction, and edited hundreds of stories and dozens of books, including Spark: How Fic and Fandom Can Set Your Writing On Fire. I'm highly focused on raising the voices of LGBTQIA+, neurodivergent, BIPOC, disabled, and other people from whom we do not yet hear enough.
people.name: Atlin Merrick

people.bio: Auston Habershaw is the author of If Wishes Were Retail (Tachyon), Faceless Galaxy (JAB Books), and The Saga of the Redeemed (Harper Voyager). Habershaw has also published numerous science fiction and fantasy short stories in Analog, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, and The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, among other places. Habershaw has worked as a lifeguard, barista, waiter, QA tester, dog walker, hotel bellhop, pedicab driver, SAT tutor, office drone, and a bunch of other random things. He currently teaches composition and literature at MCPHS University in Boston, Massachusetts. You can find him online at aahabershaw.com
people.name: Auston Habershaw

people.bio: Dr. Avani Vaghela is an Indian-American speculative fiction writer and cyberpunk utopian living in San Francisco. She is a wheelchair-rocking professor of computer science, where she works on data storage, brains, security, and insecurities. She is a 2023 graduate of Viable Paradise, a Writers of the Future finalist, and has fiction published in Club Chixulub, Nature Futures, and of course this anthology. When not tied to her laptop, you can find her giving talks on esoteric topics at Odd Salon, picking locks, or lighting fires in her jewelry workshop. She stalks the Internet from a perch at linktr.ee/circumviso .
people.name: Avani Vaghela

people.bio:
Since her first published novel, Time of the Dark, in 1982, Barbara Hambly has touched most of the bases in genre fiction: fantasy, science fiction, horror, media tie-ins, graphic novels, screenplays, murder mysteries, occult romance, “respectable women’s fiction” and Saturday morning cartoons. Currently she writes mostly historical murder mysteries (the long-running Benjamin January series, and the fairly new Silver Screen mysteries about Hollywood in the silent film era), but her sword-and-sorcery epic The Iron Princess appeared through Open Road Media in 2023. She also publishes novelettes and short stories about the further adventures of the characters from her earlier fantasy series through Amazon and Smashwords. Her work has been translated into Spanish, Russian, Japanese, French, and in some cases Czech and Slovakian (though those would be pretty hard to locate these days!)

Barbara was born in San Diego, California, in 1951 – in fact, she will celebrate her 75th birthday at the 2026 Worldcon. She attended the University of California, Riverside (with one year at the University of Bordeaux, France) and holds an M.A. in medieval history. In 1998 she married science fiction writer George Alec Effinger, and lived part-time in New Orleans for several years.

From 1994-1996, Barbara served as President of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America (SFWA)1. She taught history, part-time, at Pierce College in Woodland Hills, California, from 2006 to 2023. She earned a black belt in Shotokan karate back in the 1970s (though she had to quit because of injuries) and in 2022 earned a black belt in Nishikaze-style iaido; she still trains in that as well as aikido.

Barbara has over 70 novels to her credit, including dozens of original works — such as her novel series Darwath, Winterlands, and Sunwolf and Starhawk — as well as novels in the Star Trek, Star Wars and Beauty and the Beast universes. Her views on writing, her cats, research, or her travels are posts (when she has time) on barbarahambly.com, or on Facebook as Barbara Hambly, Writer. (You can also see some of her paintings on her website, too). Her entry on Wikipedia has an extensive list of her writing. Now a widow, she shares a house in Los Angeles with several small carnivores.

1 Known since 2022 as the Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA).
people.name: Barbara Hambly

people.bio: Beatrice Erkers is Program Director of Existential Hope at Foresight Institute, where she leads initiatives exploring positive futures through AI and emerging technology. Her work spans podcast production, essay commissioning, grant-making, and worldbuilding education. Podcast guests have included science fiction authors Hannu Rajaniemi and Ada Palmer, David Deutsch, Steven Pinker, and Kevin Kelly. She developed a free worldbuilding course teaching participants to construct evidence-based scenarios of futures worth building, drawing on science fiction and foresight methods.
people.name: Beatrice Erkers

people.bio: Ben Francisco’s work ranges from magic realism to space opera and has featured oversexed ghosts, depressed precognitives, and vampire aliens who reproduce like moss. Their fiction has won the Indiana Review Fiction Prize, been featured in Locus’s Recommended Reading List, and appeared in Strange Horizons, PodCastle, and From Macho to Mariposa: New Gay Latino Fiction. Ben’s first novel, Val Vega: Secret Ambassador of Earth, was featured in BookLife’s Best of 2024 and Reactor Magazine’s Notable YA SF of 2024. A Kirkus starred review called it, “A captivating, heartfelt tale about family, diplomacy, and finding one’s place in the universe.”
people.name: Ben Francisco

people.bio: Benjamin C. Kinney is a SFF writer, neuroscientist, and former assistant editor of Escape Pod. His short stories have previously appeared in Analog, Lightspeed, Strange Horizons, and elsewhere. You can find him and his work across the internet via linktr.ee/benckinney.
people.name: Benjamin C. Kinney

people.bio: Benjamin Liar has been a writer, musician, filmmaker, game developer, bartender, cartographer, estimator, semi-professional drinker, ditch-digger, file organizer, rockabilly bassist, bad actor, screenwriter, house painter, passionate fort-builder, reformed preacher, drywall hanger, decent friend and terrible lover. His first novel is 'The Failures' from DAW, and is hard at work on the sequel.
people.name: Benjamin Liar

people.bio: Benjamin Rosenbaum has been a finalist for the Hugo, Nebula, BSFA, Sturgeon, World Fantasy, Locus, Otherwise, and Ennie Awards. He is the author of far-future coming-of-age novel of love and social unrest _The Unraveling_, two Jewish historical fantasy games (interactive novel _The Ghost and the Golem_ and tabletop roleplaying game _Dream Apart_), and 50 short stories, translated into 25 languages. He lives near Basel, Switzerland, where he helps run a synagogue and co-hosts the podcast _Mohanraj and Rosenbaum are Humans_. With David Moles, he is the author of the forthcoming posthuman SF TTRPG Numinous. Find him online at benjaminrosenbaum.com.
people.name: Benjamin Rosenbaum

people.bio:
Hi I’m Ben, and I love to read books! Science Fiction & Fantasy has been a cornerstone of my personal development from a very young age, teaching me about morality, compassion, and humanity.

I’m now an active reviewer and influencer in the community on both Instagram and TikTok.
people.name: BenTalksBooks

people.bio:
Bernard Fallon B.A. is a graduate of the Liverpool College of Art in the UK. He has spent a lifetime in the visual arts as a painter, teacher and photographer.

Fallon’s strong landscape and sky paintings derive from the thoroughly grounded traditions of fine art and direct observations of nature and the heavens; and ably aided by a strong imagination of what lies beyond!
people.name: Bernard V. Fallon

people.bio: Bert-Oliver Boehmer is the award-winning author of the Galacticide series. With a background in computer science and bioinformatics, his work blends exotic biology, military strategy, and large-scale space opera. He is a member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association and co-chair of its Independent Authors Committee.
people.name: Bert-Oliver Boehmer

people.bio: Beth Anderson (who also publishes as A.E. Dethlefsen) is a writer and night person from Austin, Texas. Her work has appeared in Not One of Us, Extrasensory Overload: An Anthology of Speculative Excess, Akashic, Beneath Strange Stars, Trembling with Fear, and other publications. A graduate of the University of Southern Maine's Stonecoast MFA Creative Writing Program, she teaches writing at Austin Community College and has presented at ICFA and other conferences. She is also a long-time film nerd who spent many years working in the industry. Follow her at seebethwrite.com, @bethanderson.bsky.social, and seebethwrite.substack.com.
people.name: Beth Anderson / A.E. Dethlefsen

people.bio: Beth Goder is an archivist and author. Her stories have appeared in venues such as Escape Pod, Clarkesworld, Lightspeed, Flash Fiction Online, Apex, Strange Horizons, and Horton's The Year's Best Science Fiction & Fantasy. She loves chocolate, hiking, and checking out too many books from the library. You can find her online at http://www.bethgoder.com.
people.name: Beth Goder

people.bio: Beth Tabler is the head magazine editor at Grimdark Magazine. As well as EIC and owner of the review site Beforewegoblog.com
people.name: Beth Tabler

people.bio: Betsy Aoki is a game producer, poet, and fiction writer. She currently serves as poetry editor for Uncanny Magazine and has work forthcoming in Strange Horizons. Her debut poetry collection, Breakpoint, was a National Poetry Series finalist and winner of the Patricia Bibby First Book Award. Its signature poem was selected by Pulitzer Prize winner Jericho Brown for the Auburn Witness Poetry Prize. Most recently, her fiction is included in Critical Role: The Mighty Nein --Stories Untold.
people.name: Betsy Aoki

people.bio: Bill Higgins is a retired physicist; formerly he was involved in the transport of high-energy particle beams at Fermilab. He has a deep interest in astronomy and spaceflight. He has also written about the history of science and the history of science fiction. As a volunteer speaker since 1999 in NASA's Solar System Ambassador program, his quest for learning has taken him to observatories, labs, and launch sites. He has been an eyewitness to spacecraft encounters with Neptune, Pluto, and the icy asteroid Arrokoth. He resides in Aurora, Illinois, not far from Chicago.
people.name: Bill Higgins

people.bio: Bita Behzadi writes fantasy novels of all kind, with a pechant for blending genres and balancing the sweet with the bittersweet. She possesses a conditionally useful engineering degree from The University of California, Berkeley, and a love of analytically sampling sweet treats. Her debut cozy historical romantic fantasy novel, Letters from the Last Apothecary, is out now. Visit her online at BitaBehzadi.com.
people.name: Bita Behzadi

people.bio: Started in fandom in the 1940s. Costuming, writing, art and organizing. With the suggestion and help of my husband John Trimble we started the letter writing campaign to save Star Trek and got it out into syndication. We ran Equicon Filmcon from the 1970s-80s and began ought up 3 daughters in fandom.
people.name: Bjo Trimble

people.bio: B.L. Blanchard is the author of THE PEACEKEEPER (winner of the 2023 Sidewise Award for Best Alternate History Novel) and THE MOTHER (finalist for the 2023 Dragon Award for Best Alternate History Novel). Her work has appeared in Vox and Inquest Magazine. She is a lawyer and citizen of the Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians. She has lived in San Diego for so long that she can no longer handle cold weather.
people.name: B.L. Blanchard

people.bio: Blue Delliquanti is a comic artist and writer based in Minneapolis, MN. From 2012 to 2020 Blue drew and serialized the science fiction comic O Human Star at ohumanstar.com. Blue is also the creator of graphic novels and novellas like Across a Field of Starlight, Adversary, and Unauthorized Bread (with Cory Doctorow and J.R. Doyle). They teach comics courses at the Minneapolis College of Art and Design.
people.name: Blue Delliquanti

people.bio: Bobbo Byrnes is a singer-songwriter, author, and international touring troubadour whose music blends folk, Americana, and roots rock. As a member of the The Fallen Stars trio with wife Tracy Byrnes and drummer Matt Froehlich, he has performed across the U.S. and Europe. At LosCon, he and The Fallen Stars will perform songs from their shiny "Leaves on the Wind" collection. Songs inspired by the beloved TV series and film Firefly, celebrating the spirit of adventure, resilience, and found family that continues to inspire fans across the 'verse.
people.name: Bobbo Byrnes

people.bio: 6 years of USAF computer programming started my professional career, followed by 34 years as an intelligence analyst, systems engineer, and program analyst. I’m a vocal Space Exploitation Advocate, read hard-SF whenever I can, give blood six times a year (230 pints & counting!), run & drink (at the same time!) with Hash House Harrier groups, and judge several Science Fairs every year. At LAconV you’re likely to spot me in my Space-kilt on science panels. I’m also an avid Wargamer (www.EPGS.org) and a US Army “Mad Scientist”. My Worldcon Nuclear Rockets panel notes got published in Amazing Stories.
people.name: Bob Hranek

people.bio: Bradford Lyau has been a life-long reader of science fiction, part of fandom for over fifty years, and panelist for over thirty years. He is a historian by training (BA, UC-Berkeley; MA, PhD, University of Chicago) and has taught at several universities in California and Europe. Presently, he works for a start-up company and is also a political activist/consultant. He remains active in formal scholarship, publishing academic articles on American, British, European, and Chinese science fiction. He was an invited program participant in 1984 for the George Orwell Conference held in London, and in 1991 for the Utopian Conference held in Yverdon-les-Bain, Switzerland, as part of Switzerland’s 700th Anniversary celebration. One of his recent articles analyzed Cixin Liu’s recently translated novels, his first attempt to analyze science fiction from a non-Western culture. His book analyzing French science fiction, The Anticipation Novelists of 1950s French Science Fiction: Stepchildren of Voltaire, received very positive reviews from leading academic SF journals and is listed as a reference for further reading in the “France” entry in the Encyclopedia of Science Fiction. In 2019 he received the Sam Moskowitz Archive Award (given by First Fandom), for both collecting and scholarship, at the Dublin World SF Convention.
people.name: Bradford Lyau

people.bio: I grew up in Chester County outside of Philadelphia. After earning a degree in Communications and Creative Writing from Carnegie Mellon University, I studied film at UCLA. As a trailer editor, writer, and producer, I’ve created thousands of pieces of advertising for motion pictures and TV. My fiction has been published in "Best Indie Speculative Fiction: Volume IV", "Bards & Sages Quarterly", "Mobius Blvd.", and on RipplesInSpace.com and Teleportmagazine.com. My first novels "Z vs V: Among the Living – Books 1 and 2" have recently been published by Raven Tale Publishing.
people.name: Brad Goldberg

people.bio: Brandon Case is a golden retriever who writes of unsettling worlds. He has work in Escape Pod, Flash Fiction Online, and Small Wonders, among others. You can catch his alpine adventures on Twitter and Instagram @BrandonCase101.
people.name: Brandon Case

people.bio: Brandon Ketchum is a speculative fiction writer from Pittsburgh, PA who enjoys putting a weird spin or strange vibe into every story, dark or light. He is a member of SFWA and the Horror Writers Association, and his work has been published with Air and Nothingness Press, Perihelion, Mad Scientist Journal, and many other publications, including the short story collections Legio Damnati and its sequel Civili Bellum.
people.name: Brandon Ketchum

people.bio: Brandon O’Brien is a writer, performance poet, teaching artist, and tabletop roleplaying game designer from Trinidad and Tobago. His work is published in Uncanny Magazine, Fireside Magazine, Strange Horizons, and New Worlds, Old Ways: Speculative Tales from the Caribbean. He is the former Poetry editor of the Hugo Award-winning magazine FIYAH: A Magazine of Black Speculative Fiction. His debut poetry collection, Can You Sign My Tentacle? is the winner of the 2022 Elgin Award. He recently served as Poet Laureate of the 2025 World Science Fiction Convention in Seattle, Washington--the first Poet Laureate Guest of Honor in the convention's history.
people.name: Brandon O'Brien

people.bio: Brandon Sowers is the President of Esperanto-USA. He first became aware of the connections between Esperanto and early sci-fi fandom in 2022, when he spent the year working on translating Charles Hornig's diary for 1940-42.
people.name: Brandon Soewrs

people.bio: Brandy J. Lewis is a independent researcher and bookseller from Santa Barbara, California. She holds Ph.D. in English from the University of California, Riverside, with special emphasis in Science Fiction and comics.
people.name: Brandy J. Lewis

people.bio: With Masters degrees in literature, molecular biology, and creative writing and PhD in creative writing, Breeann Kyte Kirby is a master of all trades and doctor of one. A former research biologist on how the hepatitis C virus talks to our cells, Breeann keeps her science legs by collaborating with microbial ecologists. She has a forthcoming popular science book from MIT Press (Fall 2027) that looks at bacteriophage/bacterial host dynamics in the human ecosystem and how these interactions affect your health, disease, weight and mental state. Breeann loves science and the arts, keeping herself grounded in both fields by facilitating collaborations between artists and scientists to communicate research beautifully and accurately. She is also a professor of creative writing and environmental studies at a small liberal arts college in San Diego. Her (short) works have been published in places like The Scientist, City Creatures, Orion magazine’s “Place Where You Live,” The Eeel, Diagram, Embark, and as an NFT in The Tickle.
people.name: Breeann Kyte Kirby

people.bio: Brenda Cooper is a futurist, a writer, and an editor. She holds an MFA from Stonecoast and is an Imaginary College Fellow at the Center for Science and the Imagination, CSI, at Arizona State University. Her fiction has won two Endeavour awards and been shortlisted for the Phillip K. Dick Award. Brenda's most recent work includes a collection of stories and poems about strong women and the environment, When Mothers Dream, from Fairwood Press. Brenda lives in Washington State where she can be found riding bikes and walking dogs.
people.name: Brenda Cooper

people.bio: Brenda W. Clough is the first female Asian-American SF writer, first appearing in print in 1984. Her latest work is a science fiction novel, His Selachian Majesty Requests. A novelette, ‘Clio’s Scroll’, which appeared in Clarkesworld in July 2023. A historical novel A Door In His Head won the 2023 Diverse Voices Award. Her novella ‘May Be Some Time’ was a finalist for both the Hugo and the Nebula awards and became the novel Revise the World. Marian Halcombe, first in a series of 12 neo-Victorian thrillers appeared in 2021. Her complete bibliography is up on her web page, brendaclough.net
people.name: Brenda W Clough

people.bio: Brent Scarcliff is a UCLA-trained linguist and mythologist specializing in the Austronesian, Indo-European, and Uto-Aztecan language families; a long-standing member of the indigenous-centered Gabrielino-Tongva Language Committee; a Fortune 500 naming consultant, with hundreds of brands in his portfolio; and the author of The Earthy Language Cycles, an epic science fantasy series set in our world’s past, present, and future, debuting in 2027 with THE LAST INTERGLACIAL and AUSTRONESIA. He, his wife, and their three Filipino British American sons call LA’s Beach Cities home. With a name like Scarcliff, he’s easy to find on Bluesky, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and the like.
people.name: Brent Scarcliff

people.bio:
Briana N Cox (she/they) is the oldest of seven children and a first-generation academic. She holds a BA in cognitive science from Swarthmore College and an MS in speech-language pathology from Purdue University. Briana has been a writing Fellow through The TN Playwright’s Studio, Stowe Story Labs, Bend Base Camp Feature Lab, Stage 32 Feature Competition, and the Moonshot Initiative Feature Accelerator. She has won Best Script at the San Francisco Independent Film Festival and Best Tennessee Writer at the Nashville Film Festival. They have additionally been highlighted in Variety magazine and on the 2024 Next List of screenwriters to watch for. Her debut horror novel, INDIGENT, released in March 2026 and was praised by horror greats Clay McLeod Chapman, Erin E. Adams, and Johanna van Veen.

Briana writes genre stories from the margins, illuminating the experiences of overlooked demographics with authenticity, dignity, and dark humor.
people.name: Briana N Cox

people.bio: Hailing from sunny Sacramento, California, Brian C. E. Buhl is trying to save the world. Formerly enlisted in the U.S. Air Force, Brian now spends most of his time writing software for the solar industry. When he’s not engineering technical solutions, he can sometimes be found playing saxophone with local community bands. Also, he writes science fiction and fantasy.
people.name: Brian C. E. Buhl

people.bio: Brian K. Lowe has wanted to be a writer almost longer than he can remember. He has self-published several science fiction and fantasy novels and his Stolen Future trilogy is published by Water Dragon Publications. He also serves as the Chair of SFWA's Grievance Committee.
people.name: Brian K. Lowe

people.bio: Author and filmmaker, Brian Young is a graduate of both Yale University with a Bachelor's in Film Studies and Columbia University with a Master's in Creative Writing Fiction. An enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, he grew up on the Navajo Reservation but now currently lives in Brooklyn, New York. As an undergraduate, Brian won a fellowship with the prestigious Sundance Ford Foundation with one of his feature length scripts. He has worked on several short films including Ts'idii Naatsilid (Sid-dee Naw-see-lid); Rainbow Bird and A Conversation on Race with Native Americans for the short documentary series produced by the New York Times. He was a participant of the 6th Annual Native American TV Writer's Lab with the Native American Media Alliance, where he learned to write Television Scripts. He has published two middle grade novels; Healer of the Water Monster; Heroes of the Water Monster, and the Young Adult Shards of Silence as well as contributed short stories to Ancestor Approved; A Little Bit Super; and Legendary Frybread Drive-In. In addition to writing for middle grade, Brian is working on another several Young Adult and Adult fiction books and has worked as a cultural consultant on Jamie Lee Curtis and Russell Goldman's graphic novel Mother Nature.
people.name: Brian Lee Young

people.bio: Brianne Shiraki is the managing editor and co-founder of Shiraki Press. After a varied career in and out of administration, software, video games, and other odds and ends, she finds herself back at the beginning, with her first loves—reading stories and making plans.
people.name: Brianne Shiraki

people.bio: Brian Nisbet started running running gaming (Leprecon, Gaelcon, K2) and SF conventions in Ireland in the mid-90s. In 1998 he got involved in the International Discworld Convention, held in the UK, and went on to chair it twice in 2010 & 2012. He co-chaired Shamrokon, the 2014 Eurocon. Since then he's mostly been on the committees of Worldcons (Helsinki, San Jose, Dublin, Washington DC, Chicago, Glasgow) or Worldcon bids (Dublin in 2029) in a variety of roles, including substantial work (along with many others) to implement and improve codes of conduct. He has written for a number of published TTRPGs as well as many, many convention scenarios. He's been a huge fan of fantasy, sci-fi and gaming for over 30 years and he's so looking forward to all the things to come!
people.name: Brian Nisbet

people.bio: Brian U. Garrison is President of the Science Fiction & Fantasy Poetry Association. His chapbook Micropoetry for Microplanets earned 3rd place in the 2025 Elgin Awards. His latest release is The Future is Antifascist. Find him online at bugthewriter.com and ilikethispoem.com.
people.name: Brian U. Garrison

people.bio: Brick Barrientos is a long time science fiction fan and quiz enthusiast. He won a national championship in College Bowl and was a one-day champion on Jeopardy. Brick has been regularly hosting trivia contests since the days of reading questions off cards instead of tablets. He can be found all over Maryland winning pub quiz trivia cash. Since lockdown, remote technology has enabled him to be both a contestant and host for quizzes with participants over four continents. He is the proud father of a daughter who is also a science fiction fan and science journal editor. He may also have a cat.
people.name: Brick Barrientos

people.bio:
So.Calif. native and lifelong artist painted sci-fi themes throughout a 46 year career in entertainment as a union scenic artist in Local 800 Art Directors Guild for 46 years, and in her private artwork. Education: UCLA, Art Center College of Design.Did backdrops, paintings, sets, props, and scenery for TV. Theater, Film, Theme Parks, and Awards shows such as: Oscars, Emmys, Golden Globes, AMA and Country Music Awards and many others. Worked at: ABC, NBC,CBS,Fox, KCET, Warner Bros., Universal, and Paramount and others. Was a panelist and solo presenter and ran art painting (plein aire & sketching from costumed models) at former
 World Cons: Reno, San Antonio, and 8 events in Dublin. My show I did art for, "The Good Place" won a Hugo. Did a painting as special request from most decorated shuttle Astronaut, Gen. Kevin P. Chilton, that was carried in payload of Endeavor's maiden voyage, on the mission and
later presented to our mutual school in 1992. Current Art Groups: California Art Club, Pastel Society of So. Calif., pastel Society of the West Coast, and Destination Art Gallery. Have been in several art galleries, museums, and national
competitions.
people.name: Bridget Duffy

people.bio: I am participating as part of the SCA, middle ages re-enactment. But I have also been going to Science Fiction Fandom conventions since 1976!
people.name: Bridget Lucia MacKenzie

people.bio: Brigitte Winter is a novelist writing fabulist fiction about your favorite monster ex-girlfriends. She is also an award-winning narrative game designer. Her short fiction has appeared in PodCastle, New Year, New You: A Speculative Anthology of Reinvention, and City of Weird. Her game, Psychic Trash Detectives, won a 2024 CRIT Award for Best Indie TTRPG, and her debut novel, The Normal Monster Club, was a 2024 PNWA Literary Award Finalist and will be published by Generous Press in 2027. Find her at brigittewinterauthor.com and @bwinterose on IG.
people.name: Brigitte Winter

people.bio: Brittany Johnson is a romantasy author, journalist, and creative based in Southern California.
people.name: Brittany Johnson

people.bio:
Brittany is a paper artist known for combining layered paper and light into shadow box sculptures that she calls Oneiroframes. Based in Seattle, Washington since 2012, she made her first paper sculpture in 2016. She has since further developed her own techniques of cutting and layering paper and light to create her own unique and illustrative voice.

Each line is painstakingly hand cut with a blade. Her work is influenced by her love of fantasy, biology, and struggles with mental health to create transformative, dream-like portals that draw the viewer into expressive worlds that shine brightest when surrounded by darkness.
people.name: Brittany Otto

people.bio: Brittany Yost is a developmental book editor and publishing consultant focused on commercial fiction, specializing in diverse manuscript editing, inclusive language, and controversial storylines. She has her MA in Publishing Studies from University College London.
people.name: Brittany Yost

people.bio: Britton is a polyglot and former international tech professional turned entertainment-industry conlanger and conlang documentarian. Based in California’s Coachella Valley, he’s best known for creating the Yautja language for Predator: Badlands (2025) and Predator: Killer of Killers (2025), and for his decade-long role as Xenolinguist for Cloud Imperium Games’ Star Citizen, inventing multiple alien languages for the franchise’s non-human species. He also directed Conlanging: The Art of Crafting Tongues (2017), a documentary on the global history and phenomenon of language invention.
people.name: Britton Watkins

people.bio: Brooks Peck is a pop culture museum curator specializing in science fiction, fantasy, gaming, movies, TV, costume and more. He worked at Seattle's Museum of Pop Culture for 17 years where he was Senior Curator. Exhibit highlights include Star Trek: Exploring New Worlds, Minecraft: the Exhibition, Infinite Worlds of Science Fiction. Recently he's worked on exhibits about Marvel comics and films and James Cameron.
people.name: Brooks Peck

people.bio:
Bruce Davis is a Mesa AZ based general and trauma surgeon. He is also a writer of science fiction, fantasy, and historical novels. His independently published works include the YA novel Queen Mab Courtesy, and the military science fiction novel That Which Is Human. His nonfiction memoir, Dancing in the Operating Room, is a glimpse into the life and training of a Trauma Surgeon. Glowgems for Profit, Thieves Profit, Profit and Loss, and Profit Motives are a continuing series of stand-alone novels about Zach Mbele, former Republic of Mars commando and captain of the fast freighter, Profit. They and his latest works, Platinum Magic, Gold Magic, Silver Magic, and Aluminum Magic, forays into fantasy world much like our own, are published by Brick Cave Media are available on their website or through Amazon. His recently published historical novel, Proud Waves Be Stilled is a thrilling espionage novel based on real events in Liverpool during the early years of the America Civil War. The Union and the Confederacy carry on a clandestine war in the streets of that cosmopolitan port city. Both sides are vying for influence with Britain, both sides clawing for advantage through any means available. Assassination, assault, robbery, bribery, and blackmail, all are tools of their trade.
When not working or writing, he can be found paddling a kayak on the nearby Salt River, or practicing Shinkendo, a school of Japanese swordsmanship that involves cutting targets with sharp swords.
people.name: Bruce Davis

people.bio:
Bruce McAllister’s short fiction has over the decades appeared in SFF&H magazines, literary journals, and “year’s best" volumes; and won or been shortlisted for awards from the National Endowment for the Arts, the Nebula, the Hugo, the Shirley Jackson Award, and others.
His books include the novels HUMANITY PRIME, DREAM BABY, and THE VILLAGE SANG TO THE SEA : A MEMOIR OF MAGIC; and three collections, THE GIRL WHO LOVED ANIMALS, STEALING GOD AND OTHER STORIES, and a collection forthcoming from The Fabulist Press.
His Hugo-nominated short story, “Kin,”—about a boy from the projects in a future LA who hires the scariest assassin in the known universe--was chosen by LeVar Burton to launch his podcast series LEVAR BURTON READS.
people.name: Bruce McAllister

people.bio: Bruce Schneier is an internationally renowned security technologist, called a “security guru” by the Economist. He is the New York Times best-selling author of 14 books – including Rewiring Democracy and A Hacker’s Mind -- as well as hundreds of articles, essays, and academic papers. His long-running newsletter and blog, “Schneier on Security,” is one of the most popular sources of cybersecurity news on the internet. Schneier is a Fellow and Lecturer in Public Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School and the Munk School at the University of Toronto. He has been actively involved in fandom since 1978.
people.name: Bruce Schneier

people.bio: Bryce O'Connor is the CEO of the specialty edition publisher Wraithmarked Creative, as well as the bestselling author of the Warformed: Stormweaver series.
people.name: Bryce O'Connor

people.bio: Caitlin Rozakis is the New York Times bestselling author of Dreadful as well as the Everyday Enchantments novels, The Grimoire Grammar School Parent Teacher Association and Startup Hell. Her contemporary romance novella Leah’s Perfect Christmas, written as Catherine Beck, was adapted as the Hallmark Channel Original Movie Leah’s Perfect Gift. She lives in Jersey City with her husband and son. Visit her online at www.caitlinrozakis.com.
people.name: Caitlin Rozakis

people.bio: Caitlin Starling is the nationally bestselling author of The Starving Saints, The Graceview Patient, The Death of Jane Lawrence, the Bram Stoker-nominated The Luminous Dead, and Last To Leave The Room. Her work showcases her love of genre-hopping horror; her bibliography spans besieged castles, alien caves, and haunted hospitals. Her short fiction has been published by GrimDark Magazine and Neon Hemlock, and her nonfiction has appeared in Nightmare, Uncanny, and Nightfire. Caitlin also works in narrative design, and has been paid to invent body parts. She’s always on the lookout for new ways to inflict insomnia.
people.name: Caitlin Starling

people.bio:
Callie Hart is an obsessive romantic who loves
throwing a dark twist into her stories. Her characters
are imperfect, flawed individuals who dictate when
she eats, sleeps, and breathes.

A British expat now living in California, Callie can most likely be found sequestered away in the corner of a library, fantasizing about exciting new realms and the brooding anti-heroes who occupy them.
people.name: Callie Hart

people.bio: Cameron L. Mitchell is an international artist known for his transformative storytelling. He is the author of “Breaking the Block: Building a path to write the story.” Cameron stars in the Feature film “Dating My Past” that premiered internationally in Curacao and has streamed over a million views on Amazon Prime, Apple TV, and Tubi. As a speaker he has presented for: Disney, Legacy Foundation in Japan, Nafasi Art Space in Tanzania, and Fatih Temple in Germany among others. Honored as a Poet Laureate, Cameron mentors youth across Tennessee and continues to make strides to inspire the next generation.
people.name: Cameron L. Mitchell

people.bio: Cameron Reed is a science fiction writer and the winner of the 1998 Otherwise Award. Both she and the award had different names in 1998, but as part of a late-in-life gender transition she chose a new one, which is an anagram of “remade crone.” She is an avid dragonfly-watcher, a moderately skilled insect photographer, and a hopeless birder. She lives with her found family in an old house full of books and cats.
people.name: Cameron Reed

people.bio: Camille Hernandez (she/they) is Anaheim’s third Poet Laureate (2024-2026), the first Black and Filipina woman to hold the position. She authored the books Motherlands (Finishing Line Press, 2025). The Hero and the Whore (Westminster John Knox Press, 2023). Camille’s writing honors the women who kept their secrets intact and their altars clean. She is a fellow of The Watering Hole, an inaugural fellow of the McCormack Writing Institute (formerly Tin House) and an inaugural fellow of Roots.Wounds.Words. In 2025, OC Register named Hernandez as one of Orange County’s 125 Most Influential People for her contributions to establishing accessible literary arts programming.
people.name: Camille Hernandez

people.bio: Cara King is a caller and organizer of English country dance (ECD) and historical dance events in Southern California. For over a decade she has been an ECD caller with Monrovia English Country Dance in Los Angeles County, and for many years she has been active with the Historical Tea And Dance Society (HTDS) in Pasadena, California, as a caller, organizer, dancer, and choreographer. With HTDS she co-created their annual Middle-Earth themed Moonlight Summer Ball, and she uses her years of research of Jane Austen, Regency England, and Regency dance when she calls their annual Jane Austen Tea Social. She has called dance events for the Southwest Region of the Jane Austen Society of North America and for the Beau Monde Regency chapter of the Romance Writers of America.
people.name: Cara King

people.bio: Carl Engle-Laird (he/him) is a Hugo-nominated editor at the Tor Publishing Group, where he edits science fiction, fantasy, and horror novels and novellas. He has worked on books that have won the Nebula, Locus, and World Fantasy Awards, among many others. Selected titles include Gideon the Ninth by Tamsyn Muir, The Saint of Bright Doors by Vajra Chandrasekera, and Even Though I Knew the End by C. L. Polk. Carl lives and works in New York City.
people.name: Carl Engle-Laird

people.bio:
Carl Fink is the Division Head, Programme for the Montréal 2027 Worldcon. His proudest fannish accomplishment was when Hugo winner Paul "John Grant" Barnett dedicated a book to him. He has also chaired a couple of cons, and worked for many Worldcons and regionals in multiple areas at every level.

In "real" life he is a former science teacher, former software developer, former freelance writer, current Instructional Designer.
people.name: Carl Fink

people.bio:
Carmilla Jo is a San Francisco Bay Area-based cosplayer and model. She has been featured on magazine covers, and is available for diverse opportunities, including cosplay appearances and campaigns, animation projects, video games, and audiobook narration. Her corporate brand clients include Adult Swim, Riot Games, T-Mobile, and Penguin Teen.
She is also a UC Berkeley alumni, a current Master’s student at Brown University, and an author represented by Aevitas Creative Management Literary Agency under the name Jo Wu.
people.name: CARMILLA JO

people.bio: Carole is known for combining traditional and contemporary dyeing techniques that allows her to get different results from most dyers. She has won masquerade workmanship awards for her dyework, as well as being a workmanship judge at Chicon7.
people.name: Carole Parker

people.bio: I am a science fiction fan and conrunner from Stockholm, Sweden. I have attended and worked at worldcons for over 25 years. I am the current chair of the European Science Fiction Society and have served as chair for two Eurocons. Traveling around the world and meeting fans is a major interest of mine. It’s best when I can combine travel with hiking. I work at the Swedish Patent and Registration Office as a patent engineer.
people.name: Carolina Gomez Lagerlöf

people.bio:
Author. Poet. Novelist. Librettist. Sporadic puppeteer. Work featured in The Washington Post, The Guardian, New Scientist, and BBC radio. Shortlisted for a Golden Tentacle Award (The Kitschies). Caroline Hardaker lives in the north east of England and writes about everything speculative, from folklore to future worlds. Her two poetry collections and her two novels are available everywhere online. Caroline speaks regularly on panels exploring cross-genre writing, literary theory, fantasy, horror, the uncanny, science fiction, philosophy, and more.

Her second novel – Mothtown – was published by Angry Robot in November 2023.

Caroline’s poetry has been published worldwide, most recently in Macmillan anthologies Gods and Monsters and We Will Soar, Magma, The Interpreter’s House, The Emma Press, Neon Magazine, Shoreline of Infinity, Eyewear Publishing’s Best New British and Irish Poets, and Contemporary British Poetry from Platypus Press.

Caroline speaks regularly on panels exploring cross-genre writing, literary theory, fantasy, horror, the uncanny, science fiction, philosophy, and more.
people.name: Caroline Hardaker

people.bio:
UK fan continuously involved since Seacon '79 with Worldcons and other conventions, APAs and fanzines, and other SF-related activities.

Conrunner with committee and staff roles in Worldcons, Eastercons and smaller conventions, most recently Chair of Conversation, the UK Eastercon in 2023, and staff roles for Glasgow: A Worldcon for our Futures in 2024.
