Eighteen years as a Trustee of the Science Fiction Foundation, and Judge for the Arthur C. Clarke Award in 2001 and 2002.

Founding member of TWP, and fanwriter with published work in Banana Wings and other fanzines. Played Nurse Chapel in Spock in Manacles at BECCON '85. Guest of Honour at the 2015 Eastercon, Dysprosium, and Fantastika 2016 in Stockholm.

A Virtual Member of LACon.
people.name: Caroline Mullan

people.bio:
Carolyn Ives Gilman is a Hugo, Nebula, and Sturgeon Award-nominated author of science fiction and fantasy. Her books include Dark Orbit, a space exploration adventure; Isles of the Forsaken and Ison of the Isles, a two-book fantasy about culture clash and revolution; and Halfway Human, a novel about gender and oppression. Her short fiction has appeared in Analog, Tor.com, Lightspeed, Clarkesworld, Fantasy and Science Fiction, Interzone, Realms of Fantasy, and others. Her work has been translated into a dozen languages and appeared in numerous Best Science Fiction of the Year anthologies.
Gilman lives in Washington, D.C., and works as a freelance writer and museum consultant.
people.name: Carolyn Ives Gilman

people.bio: Carrie is a writer, scholar, and community-engaged arts practitioner working at the intersection of storytelling, public humanities, and civic imagination. She serves as Assistant Director of the Ray Bradbury Center at Indiana University Indianapolis, where she leads literary and cultural programming including Festival 451Indy and the Multilingual Read Aloud. Her work explores participation, belonging, and the social power of stories.
people.name: Carrie Cooper

people.bio: Carrie Vaughn's work includes the Philip K. Dick Award winning novel Bannerless, the New York Times Bestselling Kitty Norville urban fantasy series, over twenty novels and upwards of 150 short stories, two of which have been finalists for the Hugo Award. Her latest novels are historical fantasies, The Naturalist Society and The Glass Slide World, about 19th century ornithologists and the magic of binomial nomenclature. An Air Force brat, she survived her nomadic childhood and managed to put down roots in Boulder, Colorado. Visit her at www.carrievaughn.com
people.name: Carrie Vaughn

people.bio: Cassidy Ellis Salter is a fantasy author from London, England. Their latest book is These Shattered Spires, the first instalment in the queer, undead nun- and tooth-filled gothic Wyrdos trilogy published by Bloomsbury. Upcoming publications include These Hollow Ruins and These Violent Ends.
people.name: Cassidy Ellis Salter

people.bio: Cass Morris lives her life at the intersection of storytelling, performance, and education as a writer and editor of novels, short fiction, and immersive experiences. Her novels, The Aven Cycle, are Roman-flavored historical fantasy. She is also one-third of the team behind the six-time Hugo Award Finalist podcast Worldbuilding for Masochists. Cass works as Story Editor at Mythik Camps, providing writing and developmental editing for the mythology-themed summer camps' interactive theatrical experiences, as well as other programming and media projects. Previously, she worked in the education department at the American Shakespeare Center in Staunton, VA.
people.name: Cass Morris

people.bio: Cat Aquino is the co-creator of CHAMPION OF THE ROSE: Volume 1 (July 2026, VIZ Originals), co-created and illustrated by Dominique Duran. Cat is a Filipino writer, Otherwise Award fellow, speculative fiction editor, and memory and trauma studies researcher. Once a Philippine history teacher in Manila, they moved to Glasgow, Aarhus, and Barcelona for their master’s degree in children’s literature. They currently divide their time between Manila and London.
people.name: Cat Aquino

people.bio: Catherine Cruzan is a Southern California writer and avid reader of Fantasy, Steampunk, Science Fiction, Cyber Punk, and Horror. Her books are available at various retailers, including Amazon & Audible. Visit her Amazon Author page for more information about her books. Read chapters & listen to audible excerpts.
people.name: Catherine Cruzan

people.bio:
I started my career as a graphic artist freelancing for several TV Stations in the Denver area.
I put blind trust in fate as a single mom with two, moving to LA, not knowing a soul in the late 80’s. By 1990, I was a painter on my first movie. I worked on several movies as a painter and continued to freelance graphic design. I worked on every soap opera in town, I painted for Disney Theme parks, I painted the Rose Parade Floats. I worked on a Taiwan Theme park parade in Taipei . Scenic art and painting has taken me to places I never would have imagined.
Currently , I’m the lead graphic artist for General Hospital.
people.name: Catherine Koon

people.bio: Catherine Lundoff is a Minneapolis-based award-winning writer and editor of fantasy, horror and other genres. She is also the publisher at Queen of Swords Press, a small press specializing in science fiction, fantasy and horror with LGBTQ protagonists. Catherine was a 2025 Alice B. Reader’s Appreciation Award Winner, a 2024 IBPA Innovative Voices Finalist and a recipient of a 2021 Ladies of Horror Fiction Writing Grant. She has taught writing, editing and publishing workshops at the Loft Literary Center, Cat Rambo’s Rambo Academy, Springboard for the Arts, Clarion West Online, Novel in Progress Bookcamp and other venues.
people.name: Catherine Lundoff

people.bio: Catherine Sharp is a conrunner and technical writer from Wales, who spent many years living in Northern Ireland and working on Irish conventions plus others including Glasgow 2024 and some Eastercons. She's currently Chair of Octocon, the National Irish Science Fiction Convention. In her limited free time, she's an endurance athlete, cat wrangler, and occasional set painter.
people.name: Catherine Sharp

people.bio: Catherynne M. Valente is the NYT & USA Today bestselling author of over fifty books of science fiction, fantasy, & horror, including Space Opera, Deathless, Radiance, The Refrigerator Monologues, and the Fairyland novels, as well as writing for IP such as Mass Effect, Star Wars, and World of Warcraft. They have won the Hugo, Nebula, Otherwise, Sturgeon, Locus, and Lambda Awards, among others. They live in Maine with their child and many, many animals.
people.name: Catherynne M. Valente

people.bio: Been an SF/F pretty much since birth because my mother fed me while watching Star Trek TOS in its first run. Became active in fandom when I moved to DC and joined WSFA. 1st Worldcon - Millenium Philcon. Started working Worldcon with Discon III. First time I chaired a Capclave in 2011, had Sir Terry Pratchett as a surprise guest, and probably should have rested on my laurels, but there's always that one more thing you want to try to do. Recovering lawyer.
people.name: Cathy Green

people.bio: PhD, Northern Illinois University, Biological Sciences, specializing in Paleontology, studying Smilodon fatalis. Published Author; 1)Determination of Smilodon fatalis (Carnivora: Felidae) brain volume and its place among extant felids by use of MicroCT scans, Biological Journal of the Linnean Society January 1, 2026; 2) Smilodon fatalis canine and alveolus junction gap: Using MicroCT scans and 3D Slicer, Integrative Organismal Biology: A Journal of the Society for Integrative and Comparative Biology2026; 3)The Misty Method: A new technique to improve and increase the efficiency of airscribes in matrix removal, Journal of Paleontological Sciences 2019. Additionally, more articles in Review or Revision. Lead author presenting at twenty six conferences.
people.name: Cat Woman

people.bio: C.B. Lee is a New York Times bestselling author of young adult and middle grade fiction, including Coffeeshop in an Alternate Universe, A Clash of Steel, and the acclaimed Sidekick Squad series. Their works have received seven starred reviews and been finalists for multiple awards, including the Lambda Literary Award.
people.name: C. B. Lee

people.bio: Cecilia Amo is an estate planning attorney, fandom enthusiast, and author of Your After-Credits Scene: A Nerd's Guide to Wills, Trusts, and Legacy, which debuted as a #1 New Release on Amazon. With 25+ years of legal experience, she founded AMO LAW Legacy Planning to help families — including childfree individuals, blended families, and chosen families — protect what matters most. A self-described nerd, Cecilia has served on the board of the nonprofit that organizes Anime Expo, the largest anime convention in North America. She's on a mission to inspire fellow fans to step into their own hero's journey and protect what they love.
people.name: Cecilia Amo, Esq.

people.bio: Cecilia Eng has been a singer/songwriter since 1984 and has performed in England, Canada and across the US. She is active in both the filk and folk communities and is an active member of the Portland FolkMusic Society where she has introduced filk music and filkers to their events online and in person. Cecilia has also performed at the Northwest Folklife Festival at the Seattle Center and at the Tumbleweed Music Festival in Richland, WA. She was inducted into the Filk Hall of Fame in 2013 and has won three Pegasus Awards: 2022 Best Classic Filk Song for "Helva's Song", 2022 Best Writer/Composer, and 2024 Best Risqué Song for "Passion Flower".
people.name: Cecilia Eng

people.bio: A bigender biracial bisexual who spans the gamut of genre and gender, Cecilia Tan is the author of over 100 short stories in publications ranging from Ms. Magazine to Asimov’s, Strange Horizons to Best American Erotica, and over 30 novels including the Magic University series, Daron's Guitar Chronicles, The Prince's Boy, and The Velderet. RT Book Reviews awarded her Career Achievement in Erotic Romance in 2015 and her novel Slow Surrender (Hachette/Forever, 2013) won the RT Reviewers Choice Award and the Magnolia Award. “ctan” (see-tan) as she is commonly known accepts all pronouns but uses she/her for society’s convenience.
people.name: Cecilia Tan

people.bio: centreoftheselights is a fanfic author and fandom statistician who has been active in fandom spaces since 2011. She is best known for her data projects, the AO3 Ship Stats (a twice-annual review of the fastest-growing pairing tags on AO3) and the AO3 Demographics Survey 2024 (a demographics survey of AO3 users with over 16,000 responses).
people.name: centreoftheselights

people.bio: Charlaine Harris is a NYT bestselling author. Her career has spanned forty-five years and has been translated into thirty languages. She has grandchildren, rescue dogs, and a house on a bluff above the Brazos River.
people.name: Charlaine Harris

people.bio: Charlie Jane Anders is the author of Lessons in Magic and Disaster, coming August 2025 from Tor Books. Her other novels include All the Birds in the Sky, The City in the Middle of the Night and the young-adult Unstoppable trilogy. She's also the author of the short story collection Even Greater Mistakes, and Never Say You Can't Survive, a book about how to use creative writing to get through hard times. She's won the Hugo, Nebula, Sturgeon, Lambda Literary, Crawford and Locus Awards. She co-created Escapade, a transgender superhero, for Marvel Comics and wrote her into the long-running New Mutants comic. And she's currently the science fiction and fantasy book reviewer for the Washington Post. With Annalee Newitz, she co-hosts the podcast Our Opinions Are Correct.
people.name: Charlie Jane Anders

people.bio: Self-published writer of science fiction and horror, music fan, fabric art afficionado, from San Francisco
people.name: Charon Dunn

people.bio: Two Awards winning from USA - ALBA, IIBA. Hugo Award 2026 eligible author of The Architects of the Universe. Independent researcher and founder of Mankind Foundation. Dr. C. M. Mane proposes the CMM1 Hypothesis — microbes as the hidden architects and controllers of life, planets, climate, and the cosmos itself. His work bridges speculative fiction, microbiology, astrobiology, and quantum biology, challenging the view of the universe as a lifeless machine and presenting it as a living microbial ecology.
people.name: Charusheel Manikrao Mane

people.bio: Chelsea Sutton is an LA-based wrier and director. She’s a PEN America Emerging Voices Fellow, a Humanitas PlayLA award-winner, a graduate of the 2022 Clarion Science Fiction and Fantasy Workshop, and holds an MFA in Creative Writing from UC Riverside. She co-wrote the Emmy-nominated Welcome to the Blumhouse Live, an interactive film event for Blumhouse/Amazon. Her short fiction has appeared in Uncanny Magazine, Apex Magazine, Bourbon Penn, and the podcast It's Storytime with Wil Wheaton, among others. She is the author of the flash fiction chapbook Only Animals (Wrong Publishing, 2024) and the novella Krackle’s Last Movie (Split/Lip 2026).
people.name: Chelsea Sutton

people.bio: Cheryl Morgan is a writer, editor, and publisher. She has won four Hugo Awards and owns Wizard’s Tower Press. Her non-fiction has appeared in venues including Locus, the SF Encyclopaedia, Vector and Strange Horizons. Her fiction has appeared in various small press magazines and anthologies. Cheryl was a Guest of Honour at the 2012 Eurocon in Zagreb and the 2019 Finncon in Jyväskylä. She was a keynote speaker at Worlding SF at the University of Graz in 2018, and at When It Changed, a conference on feminist science fiction organised by the University of Glasgow in December 2022.
people.name: Cheryl Morgan

people.bio: Chloe Smith's short fiction has appeared in Bourbon Penn, Three-Lobed Burning Eye, and Daily Science Fiction, among other places, and her debut novella, Virgin Land, came out from Luna Press Publishing in 2023. She is a graduate of Your Personal Odyssey 2024 and a member of the Clarion Workshop class of 2025. When she's not writing, she works as a middle school teacher librarian. At other times, she's been a classroom teacher, a proofreader for Locus and Fantasy magazines, a barista, and a ballet dancer. She lives in the San Francisco Bay Area in California.
people.name: Chloe Smith

people.bio: Chloie Piveral is a writer whose work often combines the dark and whimsical. She is an alumnus of The Odyssey Writing Workshop and holds an MFA in creative writing from the University of Southern Maine’s Stonecoast program. Her most recent publications include stories with alien technology, psychopomps updating their uniforms, and a tiny rebel who wants to reclaim art from the regimes of her world. Her work appears in Shoreline of Infinity, the Flame Tree Press anthology Robots & Artificial Intelligence, Manawaker Flash Fiction Podcast, and more. To explore more of her work, visit her website at www.cpiveral.com
people.name: Chloie Piveral

people.bio:
Chris Campbell’s stories have appeared in Asimov’s, Escape Pod, FIYAH, khōréō, and more. His novelette In the Palace of Science was selected for Best of Weird Vol 1 and translated into Chinese for Science Fiction World. He is the editor of the award-winning New Year, New You: A Speculative Fiction Anthology of Reinvention. His research and critical analysis have appeared in the Journal of the Fantastic in the Arts and Speculative Insight.
A graduate of the Clarion West and Viable Paradise workshops. Follow him at @chriscampbell.bsky.social or visit www.clundycampbell.com.
people.name: Chris Campbell

people.bio: Chris Gerrib has been an avid fan of science fiction and space exploration since he was a child riding his bicycle to his small town’s library where he memorized every book they had on the subject. Since then he spent a tour in the US Navy, got an MBA, and now has a day job with a multi-national software company as a Project Manager. He lives in the Chicago suburbs and is active in his local Rotary Club. His fifth science fiction novel, Gunmaker, is out now.
people.name: Chris Gerrib

people.bio: Chris Kluwe is a former NFL player who spent 8 years with the Minnesota Vikings, setting multiple team records, is the author of "Beautifully Unique Sparkleponies," "Otaku," and "Shades of Forever," is the lead designer of the tabletop card game "Twilight of the Gods," advocates relentlessly for social justice and empathy, once wrestled a bear for a pot of gold, and occasionally lies in his bios to see if anyone is actually paying attention.
people.name: Chris Kluwe

people.bio: C.W. Maurer is a New England author, engineer, gamer, crafter, musician, and mom. She writes epic fantasy and low-tech sci-fi, and runs the Tunesdays with Maurer blog, where she discusses video game soundtracks and the musical tools composers use to tell stories and evoke emotion through their scores. Her short fiction has appeared on Escape Pod and in the anthology Brave New Girls: Tales of Girls Who Invent and Imagine.
people.name: Christena Maurer

people.bio: Christina Orlando is the Senior Books Editor for Reactor Mag. Find them on Bluesky at @cxorlando.bsky.social and Instagram at @thechristinaorlando
people.name: Christina Orlando

people.bio:
Christine Amsden writes speculative fiction built on the principle that an ordinary human can sometimes be extraordinary. As an ordinary human herself, one who has been legally blind since the age of eighteen, she looks for heroes outside the traditional Hero’s Journey. That’s how she met her favorite character, Cassie Scot, the only nonmagical member of a magical family.

In her own life, Christine attempts the extraordinary by being a liberal political activist in Kansas.

She is also an assistant editor at Escape Pod where she is constantly delighted and amazed by the creativity of her fellow authors.

Christine enjoys role playing, board games, and a good cup of tea.
people.name: Christine Amsden

people.bio: Dr. Christine Doyle is a physician trained in anesthesiology and critical care, who practices in Silicon Valley. She has been active in fandom for over 2 decades, mostly working on program and costuming for local and regional conventions as well as multiple Worldcons. She is a lifelong computer geek with a master's degree in Biomedical Informatics.
people.name: Christine Doyle

people.bio: Christine Taylor-Butler is the author of more than 95 books for children including the Lost Tribes Series. A graduate of MIT she focuses on including STEM in her books and recently was selected to interview Victor Glover prior to his piloting the Artemis II mission. She was selected as a Visiting Scholar at MIT for two terms. Christine lives in Kansas City with fellow WorldCon alum, Ken.
people.name: Christine Taylor-Butler

people.bio: Christine Valada is a photographer (usually under the credit line M.C. Valada) whose work is known to the SF community for the black and white Worldcon Portrait Project. Her work has been published internationally. An essayist whose work has appeared in several DC Comics Absolute compilations, she wrote trading card collections for two of The Hobbit movies, and co-wrote the Classics Illustrated Autobiography of Frederick Douglass. She is now an inactive attorney who represented SFWA, Harlan Ellison, and numerous writers and artists in her career. Christine has appeared on Jeopardy! six times: as a four-time champion and in the Tournament of Champions in Season 26. She currently sits on the Board of Directors of Clarion and is the photographer for the Go Fact Yourself Podcast and NPR show. An avid cook, she established a successful cookbook book club more than 10 years ago. She is the widow of writer Len Wein.
people.name: Christine Valada

people.bio: Christopher Ambler is the creator of Concellation, the pandemic era convention that was cancelled before it could be announced.
people.name: Christopher Ambler

people.bio: Christopher Caldwell is a Black queer British-American writer. His collection Call and Response won the IAFA William L. Crawford award for 2025, and was a Locus Award Finalist for Best Collection, it is nominated for a BFA for Best Collection, an Ignyte award, and the Ursula K. Le Guin Prize for Fiction.. He is an Octavia E. Butler scholarship recipient and Clarion West alumnus.
people.name: Christopher Caldwell

people.bio: Chris Garcia is a Fanzine Editor, Historian, Curator, and Pro Wrestling Enthusiast from Boulder Creek, California. He's won a couple of Hugos, is raising a couple of kids, and likes Pie.
people.name: Christopher J. Garcia

people.bio: Chris Allen Weber is a professional writer with experience across television animation, comic strips, comic magazines, interactive multimedia, technical writing, and song lyrics. Often collaborating with his wife and co-writer Karen Willson, he has written more than 50 episodes of television animation, including work on GI Joe, Superman, and ADR scripts for Digimon. His books include "He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: The Newspaper Comic Strips" and "Sentient Chili and Stranger Filk.:
people.name: Chris Weber

people.bio: Chris Willrich’s stories have appeared in Asimov’s, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Clarkesworld, F&SF, Lightspeed, Reactor, Strange Horizons, and Tales from the Magician’s Skull. His work’s been reprinted in The Best American Science Fiction & Fantasy 2023, The Year’s Top Robot and AI Stories (6th Annual Collection), and Think Weirder: The Year’s Best Science Fiction Ideas. His books include The Scroll of Years (Pyr, 2013) and its sequels. He’s currently working on a text-based adventure game. Chris has been a busboy, a deckhand, a copy editor, and a librarian. He lives in the SF Bay Area with his family.
people.name: Chris Willrich

people.bio: Ciel Pierlot is a Canada-based author with three novels published and more in the works! As a queer woman, much of her work focuses on bringing historically underrepresented characters into the Scifi/Fantasy space.
people.name: Ciel Pierlot

people.bio:
Citlali Arvizu (Tongva, Kumeyaay) Native American Community Wellness Provider and Advocate; Cultural Education Consultant; Culture Bearer, Tongva Language Archival Apprentice-
Citlali's lifelong direct involvement in her community includes teaching and sharing traditional knowledge with a focus on intergenerational cultural preservation. She is an archival apprentice for the National Breath of Life's Archival Insititute for Indigenous Languages and a member of the Tongva Language Committee. She is a culture bearer, circle leader, and rites of passage facilitator for indigenous girls. Citlali is an alum of CSULB and has dedicated her energies to community building and involvement in programming that services her tribal community, as well as the wider Native communities, in Los Angeles and Orange Counties. Her advocacy focuses on generating resources, supports, and capacity to foster healing from the impacts of past and current systems and wellness and sustainability for future generations. Citlali was born and raised in Anaheim, the area known as Hotuuknga.
people.name: Citlali Arvizu

people.bio: CJ grew up in Southern California loving fantasy and science fiction. She has four children and an ever growing number of grandchildren. Adopted at eigth months old, she recently found her birth parents. She has a Masters Degree in Public History from Southern New Hampshire University, and if she's not writing you can generally find her quilting, costuming, or traveling to spend time with those she loves. She's a wannabe dress historian, and has worked with museums on historical dress recreation. The Slayer's Magic, The Traveler's Magic, and The Healer's Magic make up her Beads of Bone trilogy. You can find her at her website at cjhosack.com and on Instagram @cj_hosack.
people.name: CJ Hosack

people.bio: USA Today Bestselling author Claire Davon has written for most of her life, starting with fan fiction when she was very young. She writes across a wide range of genres, and does not consider any of it off limits. Her novels can be found in the paranormal romance and contemporary romance sections, while her short stories run the gamut. If a story calls to her, she will write it. She currently lives in Los Angeles and spends her free time writing novels and short stories, as well as doing animal rescue and enjoying the sunshine. Claire’s website is www.clairedavon.com.
people.name: Claire Davon

people.bio: As an award-winning author, international speaker, and experienced strategist who has been in the publishing industry since 2006, Claire E. Jones (she/her) specializes in unconventional strategies to gain visibility ethically and efficiently. Her novels have sold in six countries, been picked up by bookstores across the U.S., and ranked at #81 in her Ingram genre category. She works from Seattle WA, where she lives with her precious pup, Karma.
people.name: Claire E. Jones

people.bio: Clara Ward spends their time in or near the Pacific Ocean in California. Their new novella, Dream the Deep, and their previous novel, Be the Sea, explore sea creature perspectives, marine technology, and chosen family, while delving into our oceans, our selves, and how all futures intertwine. Their shorter works are featured in The Neurodiversiverse: Alien Encounters, Strange Horizons, and Tales & Feathers by Augur. When not using words to teach or tell stories, Clara uses wood, fiber, and glass to make practical or completely impractical objects.
people.name: Clara Ward

people.bio: CL Fors is an award-winning illustrator, author, publisher, and metalsmith artisan. She writes science-fiction and other blends of speculative fiction and paints fantasy and sci-fi worlds in vibrant watercolors. CL believes in creating hopeful art to save the world through story. She is the author and illustrator of The Primogenitor Series, a Sci-fi epic of humanity stolen and reclaimed, More Than One, a sappic solar-punk sci-fi, and the cover artist for Chaotic Cupids: When Loves Goes Awry, Requiem: Tales of the Undead, and The Heads of Cerberus by Francis Stephens(WordFire Press). She has short stories in Into The Deep Dark Woods(At the Root), Weird Wilderness:A Cryptid Bestiary(Out of the Woods) and The Vampire Survival Guide(Leeches).
people.name: CL Fors

people.bio:
CL Hellisen lives somewhere between Scotland and the Hypnagog. Their stories and poems have appeared in The Magazine of Science Fiction and Fantasy, Apex, Shimmer, BCS, Strange Horizons, Shoreline of Infinity and others, and their work has been shortlisted for multiple awards.

Their latest novel The Shape of Monsters is a dark, gothic fantasy where two siblings are slowly corrupted by the magic they think will save them.

They like exploring rivers in cities, and drinking in pubs with crows carved into the beams and pictures of imaginary saints on the walls.
people.name: CL Hellisen

people.bio: Cliff Winnig’s work appears on the Escape Pod podcast, in Mad Scientist Journal, and in anthologies such as Many Worlds, High Noon on Proxima B, and Southern Truths. He co-edited Alternative Liberties. A Clarion workshop graduate, he has taught writing workshops at local conventions. He hosts the SF in SF reading series and third Sundays for the B Cubed Sunday Morning podcast. He plays sitar, studies martial arts, and sings in the San Jose Symphonic Choir. He lives in Silicon Valley with his family, which frequently causes him to think about the future. He can be found at cliffwinnig.com.
people.name: Cliff Winnig

people.bio: A former Fulbright scholar, C.N. Kuster attained her MFA in Creative Writing from Regis University and holds an MA in Secondary Education as well. She teaches high school language arts, is an avid collector of fountain pens and loves spending time outdoors. Her debut novel, The Bloodweaver, will be published in Summer 2026 through Podium Entertainment. She’s an active member of Rocky Mountain Fiction Writers and the Lighthouse Writers Workshop, and a founding member of the Tejon Writers Collective. She lives in the Denver area with her husband, daughter, and a very precocious cat.
people.name: C. N. Kuster

people.bio:
Though best known for helping write and design Cyberpunk the Role Playing game and various supplements, I’ve written many published games and short stories.
In my mundane life, I’ve has been working with technology companies for more than thirty years, having worked on everything from the QuickCam, to setting up the social systems in Second Life optimizing eProcurement systems and testing games for slot machines.
I currently live in Fort Wayne, IN with my wife Margaret and, in my spare time, I am working on creating new worlds, as well as gardening for my kitchen.
people.name: Colin Fisk

people.bio: Cora Buhlert was born and bred in Bremen, North Germany, where she still lives today – after time spent in London, Singapore, Rotterdam and Mississippi. Cora holds an MA degree in English from the University of Bremen. Cora has been writing, since she was a teenager, and has published stories, articles and poetry in various international magazines. Cora is the winner of the 2022 Hugo Award for Best Fan Writer and the 2021 Space Cowboy Award. When she is not writing, she works as a translator and teacher. Visit her on the web at www.corabuhlert.com or follow her on social media under @CoraBuhlert.
people.name: Cora Buhlert

people.bio: Author, Ph.D. physicist, data geek. Corry’s Russian-inspired epic fantasy trilogy, beginning with Weave the Lightning (Solaris), concluded in April 2026: lightning mages navigate romance, torn loyalties, and dangerous magic while fomenting rebellion against the fascist state. Corry won the Writers of the Future Award & multiple teaching awards. During Ph.D. research at Harvard, they studied rare sub-atomic particles. In the tech industry, they connected science & technology to improve the user experience. Corry loves cross-country skiing, tai chi & queer books.
people.name: Corry L. Lee

people.bio: Coye Lloyd is a third-year PHD student at Indiana University Indianapolis. In 2019 she graduated from Ohio University with a Master of Art in Film Studies. In the American Studies program at IUI, she will continue to explore the topics of her thesis in film, minority (re)presentation, high/low culture, and mass media. She believes popular culture has been and persists to show how culture functions and reproduces ideology. With each presentation, class, and paper she hopes to elevate not only her beloved genre films, but also challenge notions of the canon, academia, and hegemonic oppression.
people.name: Coye Lloyd

people.bio: Long-time fan Craig Miller’s career started in Hollywood as a publicity executive, working with Lucasfilm, Warner Bros., Disney, Jim Henson, etc. on such films as Star Wars, The Empire Strikes Back, The Dark Crystal, The Muppets Take Manhattan, Splash, The Thing, The Last Starfighter, Real Genius, The Wicker Man, and others. Wanting to do something more directly creative, he switched to writing scripts and, since then, has written and produced over 300 episodes of television, primarily animation, on shows ranging from Curious George and G.I. Joe to Showtime’s live-action horror anthology series The Hunger. He has two books out: Star Wars Memories and More Movie Memories.
people.name: Craig Miller

people.bio: Science Fiction writer, producer, researcher, and professor. PhD in Communication. Editor and director of the Hispanic-American digital science fiction magazine "Teoría Ómicron" and editor of the science fiction publishing house "Omicron Books." He has published the books: "Between Science Fiction and Fantasy"; "Dark Nights, Loudmouths"; "Mission Antares"; "Twelve Hours"; "The Return of Light"; "Under Risk"; "Dead Time"; "The Unproductive Ones"; "The Instinct of Light"; and "The Infinite Name of the Stars." He has received several literary awards. He has written, directed, and produced various documentaries and documentary series. His articles on science fiction have been published in scientific journals.
people.name: Cristián Londoño-Proaño

people.bio:
Cylia likes books, dragons, and cats. She taught herself to read with the Young Years collection of Nursery Rhymes and Fairy Tales, found her morality in The Dark Crystal, and learned about chosen families from Anne McCaffrey's Harper Hall trilogy.
A volunteer with SFWA in the NW Reading Series, her newest story related project is a podcast: Connect the Plots with Cylia and Erik with her writer friend, Erik Grove.
Cylia has probably read your book, but if not, she really wants to...
people.name: Cylia Amendolara

people.bio: Cynthia is an award-winning paranormal romance author that writes for sassy nerds with a sharp sense of humor. Starting her adult life in theater, she earned a Masters of Fine Arts in Costume Design, but her first love was telling stories. After some encouragement, she dove down the writing rabbit hole, creating magical worlds, snarky heroines, and sexy heroes with a dash of "cinnamon roll".
people.name: Cynthia Diamond

people.bio: Cynthia Ward has published stories in Analog, Asimov’s, Nightmare, Reactor (with Nisi Shawl), Weird Tales, Worlds of If, and elsewhere. She's the editor of Lost Trails: Forgotten Tales of the Weird West Volumes 1-2 (WolfSinger Publications) and a coeditor of Weird Trails (Sam Teddy Publishing). With Nisi Shawl, Cynthia co-created the Locus Award-winning Writing the Other. Her most recent novel is The Adventure of the Golden Woman (Aqueduct Press). She lives in Los Angeles, where she is not working on a screenplay.
people.name: Cynthia Ward

people.bio: Dale Thomas Vaughn is a science fiction author, anthology editor, and owner of Space Bar, a science fiction-themed molecular mixology venue in Pittsburgh, PA. His debut novel Birthright: Recall was published in 2024. He is the editor of Tales from a Space Bar, a forthcoming original short fiction anthology featuring work by Hugo and Nebula Award winner Mary Robinette Kowal, publishing summer 2026. A communications professional since 2005, he has worked with organizations including Google, Microsoft, and Southwest Airlines. He is also the author of Wine Snobs Are Boring and a member of Mary Robinette Kowal's writing group.
people.name: Dale Thomas Vaughn

people.bio: I identify as a Space nerd, SF reader, and Fan. My background is in medicine. As a Pulmonary/Critical care/Sleep physician, I have been on the frontline during earlyAIDS through COVID. Current medical challenges and those postulated in the future with SF and their social implications are strong interests. As a fan I have been involved in running conventions for 40+ years from gopher to Con-chair. I’ve also been a L5 member, including volunteering at the Intrepid before it opened as a museum, worked to popularize space exploration, and then STEM in the local community. In addition, I've raissed 3 wonderful children in fandom and I'm so proud of them.
people.name: Dana Bridges

people.bio: Danielle Kane is the Computational Research Librarian at University of California, Irvine. She manages and supports the Programming Workshop Series, teaching introductory workshops in R, Python, Git and Unix. She also supports faculty, students, and staff with GIS.
people.name: Danielle Kane

people.bio: Danielle Weinberg won The Script Lab’s 2024 Free Screenplay Contest, placing first out of more than 15,000 submissions. Previously, she worked in development for Alex Kurtzman and Roberto Orci (STAR TREK, FRINGE) and Orlando Jones. She recently sold an original feature screenplay and is currently in development on several independent features as a multi-hyphenate. Her influences include Steve Martin, Mel Brooks, and Steven Spielberg. INVASION '53 is her directorial debut.
people.name: Danielle Weinberg

people.bio:
Managing editor at First Fandom Experience. Bringing to life the history and impact of science fiction fandom.

https://firstfandomexperience.org/
people.name: Daniel Ritter

people.bio: Dan Moren is an author, podcaster, tech journalist, and two-time Jeopardy! champion. His works include the supernatural detective novel All Souls Lost and the Galactic Cold War series of sci-fi espionage capers, and he writes about technology at Six Colors. A prolific podcaster, he serves as the co-host of tech shows Clockwise and The Rebound, writes and hosts nerdy quiz show Inconceivable!, and is a frequent panelist on the Parsec-award-winning podcast The Incomparable. He’s represented by Joshua Bilmes of JABberwocky Literary Agency.
people.name: Dan Moren

people.bio: Dannye Chase (she/her) is a queer writer in the US Pacific Northwest. She claims to write in many genres, but her oldest offspring suspects it all boils down to romance or horror…or somehow both. Her short fiction has appeared in over 30 publications. Find her on Bluesky as Dannye Chase, and at DannyeChase.com, where she posts steamy queer romance, writing advice, and weird writing prompts.
people.name: Dannye Chase

people.bio:
Dan Rathke is an actor, writer, and producer based out of Austin, Texas.

As a young boy growing up in Tecumseh, Michigan, the bright lights, energy, and action of acting and filmmaking made his small town seem huge. The first time he felt the heat of stage lights as "Buster" in a 4th grade school play, Christmas at the OK Corral, he knew this was something he wanted to do well into the future.

Now, with the same childlike wonder, Dan is acting, producing, writing scripts, and recently co-founded a film company, Broken Spoke Film House.

His first role was in the short film, Stairclimbing: The Documentary, which he also wrote and produced. Recently, he starred, wrote, and produced acclaimed Horror-Comedy shorts, The Party (2022) and Who Invited The Robots? (2023).

Dan has a degree in Broadcasting & Cinematic Arts from Central Michigan University. He resides in Austin, Texas where he works with Broken Spoke Film House and spoils his dog, Stella.
people.name: Dan Rathke

people.bio: Daphne Singingtree is an author, educator, and Water Protector whose work weaves Indigenous knowledge, resilience, and environmental justice. Her Circle for the Earth series blends history and speculative fiction to explore survival, healing, and community in a changing world, grounded in respect for land and tradition.
people.name: Daphne Singingtree

people.bio: Darcie Little Badger is a Lipan Apache writer with a PhD in oceanography. Her critically acclaimed debut novel, Elatsoe, was featured in Time Magazine as one of the best 100 fantasy books of all time. Elatsoe also won the Locus award for Best First Novel and is a Nebula, Ignyte, and Lodestar finalist. Her second fantasy novel, A Snake Falls to Earth, received a Nebula Award, an Ignyte Award, and a Newbery Honor and is on the National Book Awards longlist. Her third book, Sheine Lende, is the prequel to Elatsoe and was a USA Today bestseller and won the Lodestar Award for Best Young Adult Book. Darcie is married to a veterinarian named Taran.
people.name: Darcie Little Badger

people.bio:
Darlene Marshall is an award-winning author of historical romance featuring pirates, privateers, smugglers, and the occasional possum. While writing historical romance is her day job, science fiction fandom is her hobby, and she's a regular attendee at Boskone and the World Science Fiction Convention (Worldcon).

Marshall is Section Leader of Erotic Writing at the LitForum.com, and Membership Director at Regency Fiction Writers, an organization for all writers of fiction set in the long Regency period--historical fiction, science fiction and fantasy, romance, horror, mystery.

She has worked as a broadcast and print journalist, news anchor, radio station owner, obituary writer, and a few other odd jobs. Her books have been published in English, German, French, and Estonian.

Represented by Barbara Collins Rosenberg of The Rosenberg Group.
people.name: Darlene Marshall

people.bio: Daryl Gregory is a Seattle writer whose novels and short stories have been translated into a dozen languages and have won multiple awards, including the World Fantasy, Shirley Jackson, and Crawford awards, and have been nominated for the Hugo, Nebula, Edgar, and other awards. His latest novel is When We Were Real (2025). His seven other novels include Revelator, Spoonbenders, and Pandemonium. Other books include the novellas The Album of Dr. Moreau and We Are All Completely Fine, and the collection Unpossible and Other Stories. He also teaches writing and is a regular instructor at the Viable Paradise Writing Workshop.
people.name: Daryl Gregory

people.bio: DaVaun Sanders resides in Phoenix, Arizona. He serves as publisher and executive editor for the award-winning FIYAH Literary Magazine and author of Marvel's "What If...The Multiverse Was Doomed?"
people.name: DaVaun Sanders

people.bio: Dave is the author of eleven novels, including fantasy, science fiction, and mysteries. His book Kenai was the winner (out of 221 entries) of the 3rd Self-Published Science Fiction Competition founded by Hugh Howey. He also designs games. His shareware game Snood became one of the most popular games of the early Internet. He’s also published four puzzle card games in the Doctor Esker’s Notebook series. Dave taught geology and other topics at Guilford College for 24 years. He performs improv comedy at the Idiot Box in Greensboro. He’s also played the world’s largest tuba in concert.
people.name: Dave Dobson

people.bio: I am a long time SFF fan who loves both classic and modern fiction. I have focused more on short SFF over the last 5 years. I have been writing a blog, "A Deep Look by Dave Hook", since 2022, mostly book reviews and thoughts on SFF. I came to active fandom fairly late in life.
people.name: Dave Hook

people.bio: A 2026 Hugo Nominee for Best Professional Artist, Dave Kellett is the cartoonist of the sci-fi graphic novel DRIVE -- which blends high stakes wih hijinx. He's also the cartoonist of the comic strip SHELDON, the co-director of the comics documentary STRIPPED and the co-host of the podcast COMICLAB. He's a three-time Eisner Award nominee, has won the Silver Reuben Award for cartooning, and lives in Los Angeles.
people.name: Dave Kellett

people.bio:
SF author and tech entrepreneur type person (mobile, cloud, phones), fan, regular con goer to worldcons and other cons since the 1990s (I'm so old)

Once an engineer working in, among other things aerospace and rockets.

Writer of quite silly SF.

Original a brit, irish by birth and American by naturalization.
people.name: Dave O'Neill

people.bio: A Nebula Award finalist, Dave is the author of novels, short fiction, comic book scripts, and screenplays. His writing spans several sub-genres of science fiction and fantasy including sword-and-sorcery, hard sf, contemporary fantasy, superhero, martial arts, and horror. His books include The War of the Dragons trilogy, X-Men: Law of the Jungle, Piper in the Night, and the collections Raiding the Hoard of Enchantment, Futures Near and Far, and Swords, Magic, and Heart. Over a hundred stories have appeared in magazines such as Asimov’s SF, Realms of Fantasy, and F&SF, and anthologies such as Full Spectrum 4, Peter S. Beagle’s Immortal Unicorn, Return to Avalon, In the Field of Fire, and over a dozen installments of the Sword & Sorceress series.
people.name: Dave Smeds

people.bio: David Agranoff is a novelist, screenwriter, and Horror and Science Fiction critic. He is the Splatterpunk and Wonderland book award-nominated author of fourteen books including the novels the WW II Vampire novel - The Last Night to Kill Nazis, the science fiction novel Goddamn Killing Machines from CLASH BOOKS, The Cli-fi novel Ring of Fire, Punk Rock Ghost Story(Deadite) People’s Park and the science fiction novel Great America in Dead World from Quoir books. He is co-author of the novel Nightmare City, with Anthony Trevino, which he likes to pitch as “The Wire if Clive Barker and Philip K Dick were on the writing staff.” As a critic, he has written more than a thousand book reviews on his blog Postcards from a Dying World, which has become a podcast. Since 2018, David has co-hosted the Dickheads podcast, a deep-dive into the work of Philip K. Dick, reviewing his novels in publication order as well as the history of Science Fiction. His non-fiction essays have appeared on Reactor, Foundation, Nightmare magazine, NeoText, Cemetery Dance, and he is a regular columnist for Amazing Stories. His most recent novella is Sim Cop and the Haunted City, which you can buy now! He just finished writing a book, Unfinished PKD, on the unpublished fragments and outlines of Philip K. Dick. He can be found riding Amtrak around California, eating at vegan restaurants, or playing pickup basketball.
people.name: David Agranoff

people.bio: David Bogen is a veteran power-system engineer with more than four decades of experience in transmission modeling, grid reliability, and utility data standards. He serves as Manager of Transmission & Distribution Services – System Modeling at Oncor Electric Delivery and is a Licensed Professional Engineer in Texas. David has played a leading role in developing real-time network models supporting State Estimation and market operations, including the IEC-CIM–based model used in the ERCOT nodal market. He is an active contributor to international CIM interoperability efforts and is currently a PhD candidate at the University of Texas at Arlington.
people.name: David Bogen

people.bio: David Bratman has been a book reviewer and critic specializing in fantasy for many years. He edited The Masques of Amen House by Charles Williams (2000). His articles on Tolkien and other authors have been collected as Gifted Amateurs (2023). In fandom, David has been a member of various apas and has worked on a few convention committees, most notably as three-time Hugo administrator. David lives in northern California with a soprano (his wife, Berni Phillips) and two cats.
people.name: David Bratman

people.bio:
David Brin is an astrophysicist whose international best-selling novels include The Postman, Earth, Existence and Hugo Award winners Startide Rising and The Uplift War.
 A Caltech Distinguished Alumnus, David consults for NASA, companies, agencies and nonprofits about how science, technology and evolving values will affect our onrushing future. Hs first nonfiction book, The Transparent Society, won the Freedom of Speech Award. Another is Vivid Tomorrows: Science Fiction and Hollywood. His new book on AI will be about raising these new entities to be good citizens.
 (http://www.davidbrin.com)
people.name: David  Brin

people.bio: David D. Levine is the author of Andre Norton Nebula Award winning novel Arabella of Mars, sequels Arabella and the Battle of Venus and Arabella the Traitor of Mars, space-opera caper novel The Kuiper Belt Job, and over sixty SF and fantasy stories. His story "Tk'Tk'Tk" won the Hugo, and he has been shortlisted for awards including the Hugo, Nebula, Campbell, and Sturgeon. Stories have appeared in Asimov's, Analog, Clarkesworld, F&SF, Tor.com, numerous Year's Best anthologies, and his award-winning collection Space Magic.
people.name: David D. Levine

links.othersocialmedia: My YouTube channel is https://www.youtube.com/@DavidDLevine which doesn't seem to be accepted by this form for some reason.

people.bio: David Gerrold has been a member of the Science Fiction and fan communities since 1968. He has written more than 70 books, hundreds of stories and articles, and has won both the Hugo and the Nebula for "The Martian Child," the story of his son's adoption. He is also the author of "The Trouble With Tribbles" and "The Man Who Folded Himself."
people.name: David Gerrold

people.bio: David Hirsch is a husband, father, writer, and a lifelong science fiction fan. He has been attending local, national, and international SFF conventions since the 1980s. David coordinates the Phandemonium science fiction book club as well as another local SFF book group. A retired high school teacher, David created a science fiction class at his school. David has assisted with programming at local conventions and has held various staff positions at past Worldcons. He is currently working on the LACon V program communication team. A passionate Star Trek fan, David is an avid reader and viewer of all kinds of science fiction, fantasy, and related genres.
people.name: David Hirsch

people.bio:
An early hire at Pixar Animation Studios, Mr. Salter was one of a handful of pioneers applying the principles of live action film editorial to the new medium of computer animated feature films. At Pixar, Mr. Salter edited a number of films, including Toy Story 2 and Finding Nemo, which won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature of 2003, and remains the top selling DVD of all time worldwide, as well as one of the top grossing movies of all time.

Mr. Salter also developed a number of feature film properties for DreamWorks Animation, and directed Shrek the Halls during pre-production. Mr, Salter has also edited the pilot episode of Arcane for Riot Games/Netflix, Ice Age: Continental Drift for Blue Sky Studios, SpongeBob: Sponge Out of Water and Under the Boardwalk, both for Paramount Pictures, and documentaries for Errol Morris, among other projects. His latest project will be released theatrically by DreamWorks/Universal in early 2027.

In an earlier life, Mr. Salter was active in Boston fandom/NESFA in the 80s, volunteering on many cons and serving on the committee of at least one, Boskone XXI in 1984. (There were likely others, but memory gets a bit hazy after a few decades, and the 1984 program book was the only documentary evidence that currently shows up when searching Salter's name on fanac.org. He does remember Kelly Freas doing a quick sketch of him as recompense for his name having been inadvertently left off the staff list in the Noreascon II program book, a trade any fan would surely consider more than fair.)

Mr. Salter relocated from Boston to L.A. to attend film school in 1988, supporting himself by reporting on SF film and TV including two Star Treks (Next Generation and Deep Space 9) and Babylon 5, for a number of genre media magazines including Cinefantastique (CFQ).

Mr. Salter holds a Master of Fine Arts from the School of Cinematic Arts of the University of Southern California and a Bachelor of Arts from Brandeis University. He is a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, the American Cinema Editors (ACE), the British Film Editors (BFE) and the Screen Actors Guild (SAG-AFTRA).
people.name: David Ian Salter

people.bio: David J. Peterson is an author and language creator. He's created languages for HBO's Game of Thrones, Legendary's Dune, and Warner Bros. Superman.
people.name: David J. Peterson

people.bio: David’s fiction has appeared in Clarkesworld, Strange Horizons, Asimov’s, F&SF, and various anthologies.
people.name: David Moles

people.bio: I attended my first convention in 1973, Starcon, Detroit MI (One of the earliest Star Trek Conventions). A friend of mine and I conned our parents to allow two 13 year olds to spend the day at Cobo Hall in Detroit for the whole day. Attend more and more convention after that. Worked my first convention, Confusion, 1979. Spend many years running film, then video rooms at most of the Detroit based conventions. I have created conventions ("Contraption"), been chair of several cons. Attended my first WorldCon in 1982. Work for many years with "Team Team, Eh", Elizabeth Pearse's legendary Art Show team. Was on the Hugo Award team for Chicon 2000 and ran Events at the most recent Chicon. I'm primarily know as "The TV and Movie Guy" who before the Internet would get drunken phone calls at 2:00am "Who Was That Guy In The Movie With That THING??" "Ray Walston". Since 1983 I've been married to multi Hugo Award nomindated Artist Diana Harlan Stein, and father of an up and coming Web and animation artist Sabrina Fathom Stein. I've proudly been a member of The Dorsai Irregulars since 1993. Had to honor of getting Thunderbirds creator Gerry Anderson to answer a Fireball XL-5 quesion that had haunted me since childhood. KUNGALOOSH
people.name: David M Stein, DI

people.bio: David Raiklen: American composer, producer, educator, and host. David was mentored by Oscar winner John Williams and Pulitzer Prize winner Mel Powel. Dr. Raiklen studied at USC and CalArts and later taught at those universities. He works for the major studios including Sony, Fox, Disney, Sprint, Mattel, Warner Bros and PBS, plus independents. His projects have starred Elliott Gould, Doug Jones, Blythe Danner, and Martin Sheen. David made the New York Film Critics Top Ten with the documentary Heist, short listed for an Academy Award® for Worth, and Mia, A Dancer's Journey won the Emmy. He co-created the Space Command series, and worked on the X-Files movie. He loves creating augmented realites and soaring concert music.
people.name: David Raiklen

people.bio:
David Ritter lives in Cambridge, Massachusetts. He blames his lifelong love for science fiction on E.E. “Doc” Smith, whose epic space opera catapulted his 12-year-old imagination into intergalactic space, never to fully return. As for The Lord of the Rings – he was that kid who spent as much time studying the appendices as reading the story.

David is the Editor-in-Chief and principal author for First Fandom Experience, a collaborative publishing project that brings to life the history and impact of science fiction fandom. Our works include three volumes of The Visual History of Science Fiction Fandom and The Earliest Bradbury, all of which have been finalists for the Locus Award for Non-fiction. Most recently published, The Ultimate Cosmos: How a 1933 Serial Novel Reshaped Science Fiction is recognized as “great fun, making a convincing argument that like an asteroid careening through the early science fiction world, the round-robin novel Cosmos had a powerful impact on the careers of all involved (Fred Nadis, author of The Man from Mars, Ray Palmer’s Amazing Pulp Journey).

David and the First Fandom Experience team designed and orchestrated the 1946 Project at Chicon 8, which included extensive program sessions focused on that seminal year in science fiction and fandom, as well as an authentic recreation of an early fan’s den. More recently, David and Daniel Ritter organized and led fan history panels at the 2023 NASFiC in Winnipeg, the 2024 Worldcon in Glasgow and the 2025 Worldcon in Seattle.

David writes and edits the First Fandom Experience blog, a unique source of insight on early fan history. The work draws on a comprehensive archive of fan material from 1930 – 1946, assembled from a wide range of sources over 20 years. The project is open to researchers, students and authors with interest in the history and impact of fandom.
people.name: David Ritter

people.bio: 46 years, NASA JPL Opto-Mechanical, Instruments, and Flight System Engineer
people.name: David Rosing

people.bio: David Sandner is a 2025 Finalist for a Shirley Jackson Award for His Unburned Heart (Raw Dog Screaming). He is a Mythopoeic Award nominated scholar who recently published The Afterlife of Frankenstein: A Century of Mad Science, Automata, and Monsters inspired by Mary Shelley, 1818-1918 (Lanternfish, 2023). Recent novel Egyptian Motherlode (2024) and novelettes Mingus Fingers (2019) and Hellhounds (2022), co-written with Jacob Weisman, came out from Fairwood Press. Recent short work appears in Abyss & Apex and Penumbric. His stories and poems appear in Asimov's, Weird Tales, the HWA Poetry Showcase, The Mammoth Book of Dark Magic, and others.
people.name: David Sandner

people.bio:
Dr. David Tucker, his life mirrors his novels, a combination of experiences as a homeless construction worker facing injury and death, a research scientist specializing in intelligent systems, a pilot and world traveler immersed in African cultures and wars, all fused together by a passion for science fiction and fantasy.

As a fantasy author with three decades of experience in scientific research, David has established considerable skill with incorporating scientific concepts into fantasy world building and story development. His experiences war-torn Africa have unfortunately provided him considerable insight into large-scale conflict and life under tyrannical rule.
people.name: David Tucker, Ph.D.

people.bio: Dean Wells is a writer of retro-futurist science fantasy, alternatively humorous or laced with existential dread. He doesn’t know why, they just come out that way. His published works include the neo-steampunk novel The Clockwork Mechanicals, with short fiction appearing in Queer Sci Fi, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, and their respective anthologies. Other publications include Ideomancer, 10Flash Quarterly, Quantum Muse, ShadowKeep Magazine, Demensions, and The Nocturnal Lyric. He has also written for the performing arts in various capacities. Dean is an active member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association.
people.name: Dean Wells

people.bio: I love costuming and cosplay, both on stage and hall costuming. While attending Costume Con 42, I entered the Historical Masquerade and won ;Best in Journeyman Stage Presentation that was a definite highlight!
people.name: Debbie Bretschneider

people.bio: Debora Godfrey co-edited and wrote in the best-selling Alternative Apocalypse and Alternative War as well as Alternative Liberties, and Post Roe Alternatives: Fighting Back. She is a SFWA member. Her background includes working as a kindergarten teacher as well as 30 years in IT (the difference in professions is not as great as one might think).
people.name: Debora Godfrey

people.bio: Denise A. Gendron has been a music teacher since 1976. She writes music books, owns her own desktop publishing company (Destiny Press) and is a singer-songwriter (performing on cello, bass, and guitar). She believes everything she writes is filk, as science fiction is at her core. Her primary goal is to find the joy in everything, even when it’s hard to find.
people.name: Denise A. Gendron

people.bio: Denise Dumars is a retired Professor of English and writer of science fiction and horror poetry and short stories. She's won many awards including the Rhysling and the N3F Laureate award. Her most current book of poetry, Animal Gnosis, is nominated for the Elgin Award. She has had hundreds of poems and short stories published in journals and magazines. She has two published collections of short fiction and six collections of poetry. She is best known as a writer of cosmic horror, as in her short fiction collection, Lovecraft Slept Here. She also writes metaphysical nonfiction.
people.name: Denise Dumars

people.bio:
Dennis K. Crosby is an author, editor, speaker, and workshop leader with an MFA in Creative Writing. Since 2020 he has published three urban fantasy novels in his award-winning Kassidy Simmons series, and twenty-two short stories found in multiple anthologies, including Weird Tales and Creepshow: 13 Tales of Terror. He is the co-editor of the charity anthology Dread Coast: SoCal Horror Tales and has been a panelist and moderator at multiple conventions including, WonderCon, Comic-Con International, Nebula, Bouchercon, and StokerCon 2024 where he also served as Co-Chair. In March 2025 he was awarded the Jonathan Maberry Inspiring Teens Award from the Creative Writing Club at Canyon Crest Academy.

Dennis lives in San Diego, CA. where he is secretary of the local chapter of the Horror Writers Association, a member of Crime Writers of Color, a board member of Partners in Crime, the local chapter of Sisters in Crime, and San Diego Writer’s, Ink.

For more information on his work go to https://denniskcrosby.com
people.name: Dennis K. Crosby

people.bio: Desmothene is a member of the Renegade Bookbinding Guild, and she is currently on the Guild's first board of directors. She started bookbinding in 2021, and she binds under the imprint Celestial Sphere Press. In the course of her bookbinding journey, she has taken bookbinding classes in Greece and Japan. Her fandom participation is wide and varied, but some favorites include Star Wars, The Murderbot Diaries, and Temeraire. As part of the Renegade Bookbinding Guild's volunteer crew, she has worked on several projects, including the development of the Code of Conduct, in-person events such as HavenCon & the Renegade Retreat, server moderator, & translations team lead.
people.name: Desmothene | Celestial Sphere Press

people.bio: DestinationToast has been gathering and analyzing data about transformative fanworks since 2013. They share their work under the moniker "toastystats" on both Tumblr and AO3.
people.name: DestinationToast

people.bio: DIANA BURBANO is an award winning, feminist Colombian immigrant playwright, performer, and teaching artist based in Southern California. Her work explores themes of identity, resistance, and belonging, and has been produced at theaters nationwide. Works include Sapience, punk musical Fabulous Monsters, with music by FEA, Ghosts of Bogota, and the Latinx speculative play Policarpa: Apocalypse Sur Amerikka. She is committed to elevating underrepresented voices through her writing and her work with Breath of Fire Latina Theater Ensemble, where she mentors new storytellers using anti-racist and anti-bias techniques. Diana serves on the Dramatists Guild Council as the representative for Southern California. She is a company member of the Latino Theatre Company and a resident artist at Center Theatre Group and teaching artist at South Coast Repertory.
people.name: Diana Burbano

people.bio:
DIANA FEDORAK is a speculative fiction writer, aerospace aficionado, and time traveler. In a prior life, she retired as a colonel from the United States Air Force. She enjoys writing complex characters in high-stakes science fiction and fantasy worlds.

Diana’s debut novel, Children of Alpheios, was released by
The Wild Rose Press in early 2023 and won numerous awards. When she’s not writing, she spends time in her own universe with her husband, two children, and their German Shepard.
people.name: Diana Fedorak

people.bio: Diana M. Pho is a two-time Hugo Award-winning fiction editor with nearly 20 years of experience in publishing, including roles at Hachette, Tor Publishing Group, and the Science Fiction Book Club. Presently, she is Editorial Director at Erewhon Books, acquiring and editing genre-bending and game-changing fiction. Books she has edited have won the Thriller Award, the American Library Association’s Alex Award, the Nebula Award, the Lambda Literary Award, and a Kirkus Best Book of the Year Selection, among other honors. She lives in New York City with her wife and their two cats.
people.name: Diana M. Pho

people.bio: Dilman Dila is a writer and filmmaker. His books include Where Rivers Go To Die, which was shortlisted for the Philip K Dick Awards (2024), and The Future God of Love. He was shortlisted for the BSFA Awards (2021), the Nommo Awards for Best Novella (2021), and the Commonwealth Short Story Prize (2013), among many accolades. His short fiction appeared in The Best Science Fiction of the Year: Volume Six, and in The Best of World SF V.2, among many anthologies. His first novel, Dreams of a Yellow Balloon, is coming in 2028. His films have won multiple awards, and include The Felistas Fable (2013) which was nominated for Best First Feature at the Africa Movie Academy Awards, and The Night Dancer (2025).
people.name: Dilman Dila

people.bio: I love Science Fiction, especially Star Trek, and dabble in many areas of pop culture.
people.name: Doctor Beth

links.facebook: https://facebook.com/Doctor Beth's Star Trek 35mm Film Project

people.bio: Literary agent at The Howard Morhaim Literary Agency. Podcast host of Writing Excuses.
people.name: DongWon Song

people.bio:
Don Schechter is an author, filmmaker, professor, and lifelong science-fiction fan. He is the author of the 2026 science-fiction novel Ascendants, which became an Amazon bestseller in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia.

Don is also the founder and CEO of Charles River Media, a Boston-based media production company, and a Professor of the Practice in Film and Media Studies at Tufts University. He co-hosts No Win Scenario, a science-fiction podcast featuring conversations with authors, filmmakers, and other genre creators.

His TEDx talk, “Overcoming Imposter Syndrome: Storytellers, Sci-Fi, and Unreliable Mirrors,” explores how storytelling shapes the way we see ourselves, our abilities, and our place in the world.
people.name: Don Schechter

people.bio: Douglas A. Van Belle is a multi-disciplinary scholar with a diverse research portfolio. Publications include: simulations of international politics, rational choice and revolutionary collective action, global media freedom, the social nature of science and SETI, Palaeontology and scientific progress in the Social Sciences, media’s influence on foreign aid bureaucracies, international information flows and the necessary conditions for the adoption of disaster risk reduction policies, the role of science fiction in society, and the use of science fiction to teach politics. He is currently examining how science fiction as thought experiment shapes its role in the conceptual space between science and society. The diversity of his expertise is driven by his creative works, including several science fiction novels, as well has his introduction to politics textbook, A Novel Approach to Politics, which is in its 7th edition. His latest novel, A World Adrift, is set in the skies of Venus, 800 years after it was first colonized, and explores the human impact of the politics of extreme resource scarcity. Doug spent 11 Years as the Editor-in-Chief of first Foreign Policy Analysis (Oxford) and then International Studies Perspectives (Oxford), and was previously the series editor for Foreign Policy Analysis (Routledge).
people.name: Douglas A. Van Belle

people.bio:
Dr. Anita Sengupta is a rocket scientist, aerospace engineer, professor, and commercial pilot who for over 20 years has been developing technologies that have enabled the exploration of Mars, Asteroids, and Deep Space. She started her career working on the launch vehicles and communications satellites at Boeing Space and Communications. Next her journey took her to the forefront of the US space program. At NASA, her doctoral research focused the developing the ion engines that powered the Dawn spacecraft to reach Vesta and Ceres in the main asteroid belt launched in 2006. She worked on the supersonic parachute system and skycrane that was integral to the landing of the Curiosity Rover on Mars in 2012, as part of the Mars Science Laboratory mission. From 2012 to 2017, while at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Pasadena, California, she led the development of the Cold Atom Laboratory, a laser-cooling quantum physics facility which is now on board the International Space Station.

Her next engineering role took her to the private sector as a senior executive leading the development of an in-vacuum, magnetically levitating, electrically propelled high-speed transportation system known as the Hyperloop. She led the product planning, systems architecture, regulatory compliance, and human safety certification as Senior Vice President of Systems Engineering at Virgin Hyperloop.

Her current venture is leading the development of hydrogen fuel cell powered aircraft as CEO and founder of Hydroplane Ltd. As an aviation entrepreneur Dr. Sengupta is putting her space program skills to help solve challenges here at home. With her companies novel hydrogen-based powerplant technology, the path to decarbonize aviation can happen within the decade.

Dr. Sengupta is also a Research Associate Professor at the University of Southern California. She teaches the only Entry Descent and Landing class on the West Coast for Graduate students in the Astronautics and Space Technology Department.

She is also a professional public speaker and STEM outreach advocate. She keynotes events around the world sharing with audiences her personal and professional experiences of Engineering the Red Planet and From Flying Cars to Humans on Mars.

In her spare time she is an avid commercial pilot, motorcyclist, snow boarder, bicyclist, and science fiction enthusiast.
people.name: Dr. Anita Sengupta

people.bio: Deb Nickelson is a veterinarian with her own consulting business. She has participated in several WorldCons and led Stroll with the Stars in San Jose, Dublin and Washington DC. She organized science-based programming and Strut Your Stuff (dance program) at Phoenix Fan Fusion. She lives in Kansas City MO with a couple cats, Inigo and Montoya and 13 Bantam chickens
people.name: Dr. Deb

people.bio: JA Grier (ee/em/eir) is a planetary scientist, poet, astronomy educator, EDIA specialist, science fiction writer, and fountain pen enthusiast, who has published scientific papers, textbooks, professional publications, poems, short stories, and run-on sentences. JA has presented at multiple cons as both a scientist and poet, including WorldCons in Dublin and Glasgow, the Tucson Science Fiction Convention, and Balticon. Most recently, JA conducted a speculative poetry workshop on the (in)famous JoCo Cruise 2026.
people.name: Dr. JA Grier

people.bio: I’m a professor of American Studies and English Literature and Director of the Ray Bradbury Center. I teach high-enrolling courses on conspiracy theories, the American supernatural, science fiction, and banned books. I use UFOs, moral panics, and forbidden novels as gateways to skeptical thinking and cultural history. At the Ray Bradbury Center, we preserve a legacy, but we also carry Bradbury’s ideas forward through public programs, festivals, and conversations with writers and readers who believe science fiction is not an escape from reality, but a way of interrogating it. If you need someone to talk conspiracies, censorship, or why science fiction still matters, I’m your guy.
people.name: Dr. Jason Aukerman

people.bio:
I am a licensed psychologist based in Dieppe, New Brunswick, Canada. My main goal throughout my career has been to help people understand their mental health challenges and find ways to cope with them. I specialize in treating anxiety, depression, and trauma, utilizing various evidence-based treatment methods such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT).

One of my areas of expertise is Geek Therapy. This unique and innovative approach utilizes popular culture, including books, movies, TV shows, and video games, to provide evidence-based therapy. The stories and characters from these sources can help us gain valuable insights into ourselves and lead us toward greater self-discovery as we navigate life’s journey.
people.name: Dr. Jean-Luc Williams

people.bio: Dr. Katherine L Morse is half of the award-winning, husband and wife writing team of the steampunk adventure series, The Adventures of Drake & McTrowell. She is also an internationally renowned expert in distributed, federated simulation.
people.name: Dr. Katherine L Morse

people.bio:
Dr. Marcus Norris's childhood foray into music came through producing rap beats on pirated software, installed on a Windows 98 computer that he Macgyvered together from spare parts. He came to composing concert music later and transferred that same imagination to writing music of all kinds. Marcus most recently composed the score for the hit Netflix series BANDI, becoming the top watched non-english show globally on the platform for the week following its release. His cross-genre mastery resulted in Beyoncé asking Marcus to orchestrate several songs for her and 50-piece orchestra as part of her 2023 Dubai return to live performance. Marcus founded South Side Symphony in 2020, which he describes as "like if Quincy Jones grew up on 90s R&B and Rap." He has been commissioned by the LA Phil, Juilliard, the Atlanta Opera, New World Symphony, Jackson Symphony Orchestra, the CYSO, Long Beach Opera, and many more.

For more information on Marcus and his music, visit www.MarcusNorris.com and www.SouthSideSymphony.org
people.name: Dr. Marcus Norris

people.bio:
Dr. Price is a fan scholar and has presented papers on SF, anime, and manga at academic conferences such as Mecademia, The Eaton Conference, and the International Conference on the Fantastic in the Arts. He has published two academic papers one on isekai manga and a second on the hard SF anime series Planetes. A third paper on early space operas has been accepted for publication.

He has presented academic talks at two Worldcons (Seattle Worldcon and Chicon 8). He has presented at multiple panels at both Worldcons. In addition to the Worldcons he has presented talks at several SF and Anime conventions including, Arisia, USA Anime, Anime Iowa, and Animazement.

Dr. Paul Price is retired from the Envionmental Protection Agency and has worked for forty five years assessing risks from chemicals. He has 90+ technical publications. He has an undergraduate degree in chemistry and graduate degrees in theology, environmental engineering, and environmental toxicology.
people.name: Dr. Paul Price

people.bio: Lifetime SF/F fan and occasional WorldCon attendee/participant; PhD in Mathematics; retired University Professor (Mathematical Logic and Algebra); 30 years of Union activism; lifelong interest in 'classical' and 'contemporary' 'serious music' (labels are difficult);
people.name: Dr. T. G. Kucera

people.bio: Dustin is an Emmy-nominated character animator with 25 years of work in Hollywood. He's also a game developer that's created eight videogames with his company, Scary Robot, which he founded in 2011.
people.name: Dustin Adair

people.bio: D. Wes Rist is an atrocity prevention professional with nearly 20 years of experience in international human rights law, transitional justice, and international criminal justice. He previously served as an Atrocity Prevention Officer in the U.S. Department of State, the Deputy Executive Director at the American Society of International Law, the Assistant Director of the Center for International Legal Education, a professor at the University of Pittsburgh School of Law, and a lecturer in international Law at UWE Bristol Law School. Wes is a cofounder of Project Lodestar, a think tank focused on the ethics of space law and policy and a cofounder of Former Feds & Friends, a YouTube channel made up of former federal employees using pop culture to discuss democracy, governance, and human rights. Wes holds a JD and an LL.M. (with distinction) in international human rights law.
people.name: D. Wes Rist

people.bio: A graduate of the University of North Texas where she studied film and playwriting, E.A. Williams often imbues her stories with the diverse and challenging landscape of her home state. From her thrilling debut series, The Line of Tepes, to her short stories featured in publications like Mixed Bag of Tricks, Femme Fairytales, and Grimoire for Honeyed Spells, no matter how fantastical, Williams brings a unique Texan voice to her writing. Williams learned just how invaluable a writing community could be while helping run a writer's collective during university. Whether she is working on her own writing or helping to coordinate events for Armadillo Authors Society, Williams is always looking for ways to connect with the arts community.
people.name: E.A. Williams

people.bio:
Eboni Dunbar (she/her) is a queer, black woman who writes speculative fiction. She received her BA from Macalester College and her MFA from Mills College. She is a VONA Alum, and the former managing editor for the Hugo Award-Winning FIYAH Literary Magazine. She is also the winner of the Lambda Literary 2023 Randall Kenan Prize for Black LGBTQ Fiction.
Her work can be found in FIYAH Magazine of Black Speculative Fiction, Anathema: Spec from the margins, and Beneath Ceaseless Skies. Her novella, Stone and Steel, is out from Neon Hemlock. You can find more information on her website www.ebonidunbar.com
people.name: Eboni J. Dunbar

people.bio: 40 Years a mechanical engineer 56 an SF writer combining my mech eng and all the science I can garner.
people.name: EdBuchan

people.bio: Long-time fan Edie Stern is webmaster for the FanHistory Project (FANAC.org). She ran con programs including for MagiCon (1992), chaired a few & was a stalwart of south Florida fandom for years. She’s pubbed her ish & collects SF art. With Joe Siclari, she provided art exhibits for World Fantasy Conventions and Boskones. In 2016, she & Joe won the Big Heart Award. In 2022, they were Worldcon Fan Guests of Honor. Edie retired as a Distinguished Engineer (IBM), and is an inventor on 200+ patents.
people.name: Edie Stern

people.bio: Edward Carmien began writing early in life and never stopped, though he did detour through an academic career teaching college writing and fantasy and science fiction. A (lapsed) poet, short story writer, game designer, and novelist, his first publications were game-related working as a freelancer for TSR, Inc. After appearing in the fiction anthology EARTH, AIR, FIRE, WATER he earned membership in the SFWA. He has won awards for his fiction and non-fiction, edited a volume of essays about writer C.J. Cherryh, and lives with his family near Princeton, New Jersey.
people.name: Edward Carmien

people.bio: New Jersey born and raised, Edward A. Greaves spends his days working with technology, and his nights working with the fantastic. He still resides in New Jersey, with his wife--also a life-long New Jersey resident-- and their two sons.
people.name: Edward Greaves

people.bio: Effie Seiberg is a Nebula-winning, Hugo- and Sturgeon-nominated fantasy and science fiction writer. Her stories can be found in Lightspeed, Analog, Fantasy Magazine, Diabolical Plots, and PodCastle, amongst others. Effie lives in the San Francisco Bay Area. She's disabled with ME/CFS and is an ambulatory wheelchair user, and has done disability activism including op-eds in the San Francisco Chronicle and readings at No Kings events.
people.name: Effie Seiberg

people.bio: E.G. Condé (he/him/Él) is a queer Boricua writer of speculative fiction. He is one of the creators of Taínofuturism, an emerging genre of art and storytelling that imagines decolonized futures that center indigenous Caribbean traditions and cosmologies. Condé is the author of Sordidez, an indigenous futurist clifi novella published with Stelliform Press. His short fiction appears in Analog SF, Interzone, Reckoning, Future Tense, Solarpunk Magazine, and more.
people.name: E.G. Condé

people.bio: E. J. Wenstrom believes in complicated heroes, horrifying monsters, and standing to the right on escalators so the left side can walk. She writes dark speculative fiction for adults and teens, including her witchy, murdery September release, Roots and Wrath.
people.name: E. J. Wenstrom

people.bio: Elaine Ho is an award-winning Asian American illustrator and author. She bounces between the US and Singapore, belonging to both and neither. Her work primarily explore themes of identity and home, while also being drawn to the broken and the beautiful. She is the author of Cry, Voidbringer, which was a Lambda Literary Award finalist in LGBTQ+ Speculative Fiction. Find her work at artofelaineho.com.
people.name: Elaine Ho

people.bio: Elaine Hungenberg is Senior Vice President of Partnerships and Impact at XPRIZE, where she leads efforts to deliver large-scale competitions and to measure their real-world impact. With two decades of experience in impact evaluation, she develops frameworks that track not only groundbreaking solutions, but what works—and why.
