Her work ensures prize-backed innovations are rigorously tested, scalable, and ready for application. A champion of catalytic partnerships, Elaine unites diverse stakeholders to accelerate transformative ideas. She brings a commitment to systems-level thinking and a belief in bold, data-driven solutions to shift the trajectory of our shared future.
people.name: Elaine Hungenberg

people.bio:
Elektra Hammond emulates her multi-sided idol Buckaroo Banzai by going in several directions at once. She's been involved in publishing since the 1990s now she writes, concocts anthologies & edits science fiction for various and sundry. When not freelancing or appearing at science fiction conventions, she travels the world judging cat shows.

Elektra is a graduate of the Odyssey Writing Workshop and a member of SFWA. She lives in Delaware with her husband, Mike, and more than the usual allotment of felines.
people.name: Elektra Hammond

people.bio: Eliane Boey (she/her) is a writer of speculative fiction, with stories in Clarkesworld, the Penn Review, Galaxy, Solarpunk, and others. She is the author of noir mystery "Club Contango", and space horror and mystery novella duology “Other Minds”, both from Dark Matter INK of Chicago. Forthcoming works include "Small Bites" a weird horror novella with Space Cowboy Books (11.11.26) , and “The Ah Huat Engineering Cookbook and Organizing Manual”, a cosy SF novella, with Stars and Sabers (Spring 2027).
people.name: Eliane Boey

people.bio: Elijah Kinch Spector is a novelist and dandy raised in the Bay Area counterculture who now lives in Brooklyn. He is a British Fantasy Award finalist whose writing has received acclaim from NPR, Reactor, Nerds of a Feather, Foreword, and Paste Magazine, among others.
people.name: Elijah Kinch Spector

people.bio: Elis Montgomery is a speculative fiction writer from Vancouver, Canada. She's a Hugo and Rhysling Finalist and a member of SFWA and Codex. Her work has appeared in venues like Strange Horizons, Small Wonders, and Year's Best Canadian Fantasy and Science Fiction. When she's not writing, she's usually hanging upside down in an aerial arts class or a murky cave. Find her there, on Bluesky @elismontgomery.bsky.social, or at https://www.elismontgomery.com/.
people.name: Elis Montgomery

people.bio: Elizabeth Bear was born on the same day as Frodo and Bilbo Baggins, but in a different year. She is the Hugo, Sturgeon, Locus, and Astounding Award winning author of over 30 novels and more than a hundred short stories.
people.name: Elizabeth Bear

people.bio: Elizabeth is a long time fan who typically runs art show, but has been branching out again to other aspects of con-running. She is part of SCIFI, where she works with other judges on creating the Roster award banners seen at many a worldcon and at Loscon. She is also a Dorsai Irregular, and she works as an aerospace engineer in her other life.
people.name: Elizabeth Klein-Lebbink

people.bio: Elizabeth Sandifer is a crowdfunded critic best known for Last War in Albion, her occult history of British comic books, and TARDIS Eruditorum, a cultural history of Britain through the lens of Doctor Who.
people.name: Elizabeth Sandifer

people.bio: Elle Beck enjoys cooking simple delicious food and showing how easy it is to use and understand Esperanto for everyday tasks.
people.name: Elle Beck

people.bio:
Ellen Datlow has been editing sf/f/h short fiction for more than four decades. She currently acquires short stories and novellas for Tor.com and Nightfire. She has edited numerous anthologies for adults, young adults, and children, including The Best Horror of the Year annual series, Night and Day, and the reprint anthology Fears: Tales of Psychological Horror. She’s won multiple awards and was named recipient of the 2007 Karl Edward Wagner Award, given at the British Fantasy Convention for "outstanding contribution to the genre," the Lifetime Achievement Award given by the Horror Writers Association, and the World Fantasy Life Achievement Award at the 2014 World Fantasy Convention.
She runs the Fantastic Fiction at KGB reading series in the NYC, with Matthew Kressel.
She can be found on the website Datlow.com, and on twitter, Blue Sky, facebook (google her).
people.name: Ellen Datlow

people.bio: Ellen Rachlin is the author of the historical fantasy novel, Enheduanna’s Song From the Sands, from Histria Fiction. She is the author of five collections of poetry. At the Big Bang Resort is forthcoming from Red Hen Press. Her most recent book, Permeable Divide, received the IBPA Benjamin Franklin Silver Award. Her poems have appeared in various journals and anthologies, including American Poetry Review, Granta, Literary Imagination, and The Eloquent Poem. She serves on several non-profit boards, including the Poetry Society of America where she is the treasurer.
people.name: Ellen Rachlin

people.bio: Elliott Kay is the author of the military sci-fi series Poor Man's Fight and the fun, steamy urban fantasy series Good Intentions. He's lived in Seattle for a couple decades, but his roots are in Los Angeles and it still shows.
people.name: Elliott Kay

people.bio: Elontra Hall is a Watering Hole and Obsidian Fellow, Poetry School MA graduate, and Magma board member. He has been published in Poetry, Poetry London, Prairie Schooner, Shō, and other journals.
people.name: Elontra Hall

people.bio: Elsie is an 8-year old calico cat who “talks” with buttons. She is not speaking English in the same way that someone with 130 words doesn't speak French. Think of Elsie like a toddler, whose native language isn’t English – and she’s an alien. She has been using a tool called Augmentative Interspecies Communication for five years. AIC is a scientifically-studied approach to fostering meaningful dialogue between humans and the animals we share our lives with. Her hobbies are sunbathing, going for walks, and doing honest reviews.
people.name: Elsie the Cat

people.bio: elumish is an author, fan, and more-than-casual enthusiast of fandom data
people.name: elumish

people.bio: E.M. Faulds is a British science fiction and fantasy author who lives in Scotland. She won the British Fantasy Award for best collection in 2023 and the British SF Association award for best short story in 2026. Find out more at emfaulds.com
people.name: E.M. Faulds

people.bio: Emiko Ogasawara is a multimedia sculptor and arts educator whose recent work focuses on ceramic sculpture, printmaking, and paper engineered pop-up artist books. She is the 2026 sculptor of the Lodestar Award.
people.name: Emiko Ogasawara

people.bio: Emily Hockaday (she/her) is the interim editor of Asimov's Science Fiction Magazine. She worked on both Analog Science Fiction and Fact and Asimov's Science Fiction for fifteen years.
people.name: Emily Hockaday

people.bio: Emily Loretta Flummox (Grok Amiri, flurp, Skunkheart, and 15 other names; pronouns: fey / fem / fear / fierce / femself and 2 other sets) recently published fear first book, *Civilization Stained These Young Things, and Other Works by Emily Loretta Flummox* (Dooky Zines) and has had stories and poetry published in *Wickedly Abled* (Iconoclast Productions), *Cæsura* (Poetry Center San Jose), *Weird Fiction Quarterly*, and *The HorrorZine*, and role-playing game content in *Girls Write These Worlds*. A member of two National Poetry Slam teams, fey now works as a professional Game Master for tabletop role-playing games. Follow fem at linktr.ee/queermythopoeia
people.name: Emily Loretta Flummox (et alia)

people.bio: Emily O'Malley Liu grew up in Palm Beach County, Florida and has lived in the American Southwest, the Midwest, New England, and Japan. Em now resides with her husband and three kids in the greater Washington, D.C. metro area, where she researches financial systems by day and devises magic systems by night. Her first novel, WINE FOR ROSES, was published by Shiraki Press in April 2026.
people.name: Emily O'Malley Liu

people.bio: Emily Paxman is an author and artist from Vancouver Island in beautiful British Columbia, Canada. She publishes science fiction and fantasy with Titan Books, including her debut novel, DEATH ON THE CALDERA, a fantasy murder mystery. Her next novel is ALL WE HAVE LEFT, a cozy, post-apocalyptic romance. She’s a huge fan of gardening, cats, watercolour painting, and several other hobbies that befit an octogenarian. She has her Master’s of Fine Arts in Creative Writing from Chatham University, has written for indie video game company Wizard Games. You can read her webcomic, Neptune Bay, on Webtoon.
people.name: Emily Paxman

people.bio: Emily Skrutskie is six feet tall. She lives and works in Los Angeles. Skrutskie is the author of THE ABYSS SURROUNDS US series, HULLMETAL GIRLS, the Bloodright Trilogy, starting with BONDS OF BRASS, and THE SALVATION GAMBIT. Her latest novel, A LEGIONNAIRE'S GUIDE TO LOVE AND PEACE, is now available.
people.name: Emily Skrutskie

people.bio: I'm an SF/F/H book reviewer who also runs the only Hugo Awards space on Quora to document my journey through reading all Hugo Award nominees. I also answer questions on SF/F/H and review various nonfiction (science/cooking/occult and magic).
people.name: E. M. Serpentsblade

people.bio: Eric was not a _real_ talk show host, but he did play one on TV. He was Fan Performer GoH at Arisia 2008, Special Guest at LunaCon 2011, and hosted the 1943 Retro Hugos. He also is an avid GM for narrativist TTRPG's.
people.name: Eric "in the Elevator" Zuckerman

people.bio: I have written for science television programs such as Futurama and Krapopolis and my science fiction writing has appeared in the New York Times and several anthologies. My first novel "The Legend of the Wolf Whale" is being published by Rare Bird Press. I am from Brooklyn, New York and in addition to writing I have a sideline as a philosopher studying Buddhism, existentialism and the philosophy of artificial. I have a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley and a podcast "Terrifying Questions and How not to be Terrified By Them."
people.name: Eric Linus Kaplan

people.bio: Eric Schwitzgebel is Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at University of California, Riverside, and University of California MacArthur Foundation Chair. Recent books include AI and Consciousness and The Weirdness of the World. Look for his forthcoming edited anthology (with Rich Horton and Helen De Cruz) Best Philosophical Science Fiction in the History of All Earth and his forthcoming monograph Humanlike: A Defense of AI Rights. He has published his own short philosophical science fiction in Clarkesworld, F&SF, Nature, and elsewhere.
people.name: Eric Schwitzgebel

people.bio: Erika T. Wurth is the author of WHITE HORSE and THE HAUNTING OF ROOM 904. She's a New York Times editors pick, a Good Morning America buzz pick, and an Indie Next, Target book of the Month, and BOTM Pick. She’s both a Kenyon and Sewanee fellow, has published in The Kenyon Review, Buzzfeed, and The Writer’s Chronicle, and is a narrative artist for the Meow Wolf Denver installation. She’s an urban Native of Apache/Chickasaw/Cherokee descent. She's a professor at Western Illinois University. Find her: Insta | Goodreads |Amazon | TikTok Native Voices | Medium. Representation: Mark Gottlieb at Trident.
people.name: Erika T Wurth

people.bio: Erik Grove is a writer, writing teacher, editor, and dog wrangler living and doing things in Portland, OR. You can find his short fiction in places like NIGHTMARE MAGAZINE, ESCAPE POD, numerous anthologies, and carved into the bark of gnarled trees in the haunted woods behind your house. He is also the editor of THE MUDDY GOOSE GUIDE TO THE WEIRD NORTHWEST: A PLAYABLE ADVENTURE and his debut novel THE LONG RED TOMORROW is forthcoming form Podium Publishing.
people.name: Erik Grove

people.bio:
Growing up in Boston Massachusetts, Erik was surrounded by scientists and doctors from MIT, Harvard, and the scientific institutions around New England. At a young age, he hoped to become an astrophysicist, to help humanity reach the stars and seek a brighter future. His love for stories, however, pulled him in a different direction.

Erik wanted to help as many people as possible with his life, and after the culture shock of moving out of the city, he believed that mending the divides between people was most important. His love for pictures and writing brought him to film school in New York, and finally to Hollywood many years later.
He has directed advertisements for political campaigns, nightlife venues, and Kickstarter campaigns. His work contributed to landslide victories, exceeding funding goals, and overwhelmingly positive results.

Erik has also revisited love for science by publishing the hard science fiction novel “Icarus Dawns”, and later he published his “how to” guide on writing, complete with a feature length screenplay he’s been developing since 2011 titled “Tears of Anemoia”.
Erik is now working on getting his first feature film funded: a comedy action thriller titled “Calameda Road”.
people.name: Erik James Troy

people.bio:
Erik has been creating stories since he could read and write. Encouraged by high-school writing and literature teachers, he decided to become a professional author one day. That day, as it turns out, just happened to be a couple of decades later. Now that he’s a short story author, he’s threatening to write a novel. He enjoys public speaking because he is odd that way.
Erik is a graduate of Taos Toolbox.
Erik thinks referring to himself in the third person is strange and is getting tired of starting sentences with ‘Erik.’
people.name: Erik M. Johnson

people.bio:
Erin Brown is a black, neurodivergent poet and author of horror, fabulist, and fantasy short fiction. She has been published in FIYAH Magazine, Nightmare Magazine, Midnight and Indigo, The Deadlands, Eastover Press, Baffling Magazine, the Escape Pod, and And One Day We Will Die: Neutral Milk Hotel anthology, Fantasy Magazine, and many other publications and anthologies. Erin’s debut novelette “Garden of the Bloodpotter” through Psychopomp Press published in September 2025, made the BFSA Awards Longlist 2026, and the anthology she is coediting, “The Cookout,” will be published in early 2027.
Erin currently resides in Los Angeles, and will be finishing her M.A. in Creative Writing in Winter of 2026
Previously published works can be found at https://ebrownwrites.com/.
people.name: Erin Brown

people.bio: Erin K. Dancer is a neurodivergent, queer writer who lives in the Ozarks with her family, two spoiled dogs and a cat named Archimedes to rule them all. She writes fantasy and science fiction, fantasy, and whatever else pleases her. She holds a B.S. in Earth Science that has been mostly used to create geologically terrifying settings. Her work has been featured in an episode of 4LPH4NUM3R1C and in Belladonna's Garden.
people.name: Erin K. Dancer

people.bio: Erin Hardee is one half of the writing duo MK Hardy, along with her wife, Morag Hannah. Their debut novel, The Needfire, came out in 2025.
people.name: Erin/MK Hardy

people.bio: Eris Young is a transgender writer of speculative fiction. Their debut novel, Hunger in the Blood, will be published in the UK in Spring 2027 with Tor Nightfire. Their short stories have appeared in Escape Pod, GigaNotoSaurus, Extra Teeth, Fusion Fragment, Gutter, and the Immigrant Sci Fi Short Stories anthology from Flame Tree Press, among others. They are fiction editor at British Fantasy Award-winning sci fi magazine Shoreline of Infinity.
people.name: Eris Young

people.bio:
Fan, artist, and crafter. As well as traditional and digital art, I also hand-paint folding fans.

American, born in Spain, formerly of San Francisco, now living in Newcastle upon Tyne. Over the years I have been involved in many areas of fandom including volunteering, fanzines, and cosplay.
people.name: España Sheriff

people.bio: Eugen Bacon is an African Australian author. She is a Solstice, British Fantasy, Ignyte, Locus, Foreword Indies and BSFA Award winner. She’s also a twice World Fantasy and Shirley Jackson Award finalist, and a finalist in the Philip K. Dick Awards and the Nommo Awards for speculative fiction by Africans. Eugen is an Otherwise Fellow, and was announced on the honor list for ‘doing exciting work in gender and speculative fiction’. Danged Black Thing made the Otherwise Award Honor List as a ‘sharp collection of Afro-Surrealist work’. Visit her at eugenbacon.com.
people.name: Eugen Bacon

people.bio:
Eugene Wesley “Rod” Roddenberry, Jr. serves as guardian of the Roddenberry legacy, which traces back to the original Star Trek. Through inspiring science fiction projects and philanthropy, he champions its timeless and universal ideals as embodied by the philosophy of IDIC: Infinite Diversity in Infinite Combinations.

The son of legendary science fiction producer Gene Roddenberry, whose Star Trek series changed the face of television and continues to inspire today, Rod has followed in his father’s footsteps to be a catalyst in the creation of a world where humanity works together for the greater good.

In the early 2000s, Rod founded Roddenberry Entertainment, a science fiction leader with a tradition of groundbreaking entertainment, and currently serves as its CEO. Roddenberry Entertainment builds on the best of Gene Roddenberry’s work and continues to pioneer the development of a multimedia portfolio of smart and provocative science fiction that incorporates graphic novels, podcasts, television and film projects, including the 2011 critically-acclaimed documentary TREK NATION, which details Roddenberry’s 10-year exploration of his father’s life.

Roddenberry serves as an executive producer on Paramount+’s Emmy-nominated Star Trek: Strange New Worlds and was an executive producer on Star Trek: Prodigy, among several other projects. He also serves as an executive producer of the newest podcast series which launched in 2025 on Star Trek Day, “Star Trek: Khan.” Roddenberry also created the audio podcast series “Mission Log,” the objective of which is to analyze and explore Star Trek by journeying through each and every episode.

Over the past many years Roddenberry has been inspired to fully embrace Star Trek’s vision and invest in our future. One expression of this was the founding of The Roddenberry Foundation in 2010. The Roddenberry Foundation funds innovative solutions that address humanity’s greatest challenges across such areas as science, technology, education and the environment, with the objective of pursuing a more humane and abundant future for all.
people.name: Eugene "Rod" Roddeberry

people.bio:
Eugene Randolph Young is an award-winning cartoonist, illustrator, graphic designer, vis dev artist, and educator based in the San Francisco Bay Area. He creates independent science fiction and fantasy illustration and comics inspired by indigenous lore, 80s cyberpunk, Japanese mechs, 50s pin-up art, and afro hair culture. 
Eugene completed his MFA in Illustration at the Academy of Art University, BFA in Graphic Design Graphic Design with distinction at the California College of arts and Crafts, AA in Graphic Design at City College of San Francisco, and graduated from Berkeley High School. He has taught at Dominican University of California, the California College of the Arts, City College of San Francisco, and is currently Assistant Professor of Design Visualization in the School of Design at San Francisco State University.
people.name: Eugene R Young

people.bio: Euphridia is a self-certified adult, irresponsible author, and completely made-up pen name that its creator chose because it sounded "quite fancy, like the name of a goddess." She is the author of A Hero Returned (The Last Rae of Hope, Book 1) from Riverfolk Books — a satirical isekai fantasy in which she also appears as a character.
people.name: Eura “Euphridia” Abrams

people.bio: Evan Leikam is a fantasy author published with Tor/Macmillan and book content creator known for championing epic sci-fi and fantasy stories across social media. With a deep love of immersive worldbuilding, complex characters, and emotionally devastating plot twists, Evan has built a passionate online community of readers while developing his own original works in the genre. He blends thoughtful literary analysis with high-energy fandom enthusiasm, making him a trusted voice in the modern fantasy space.
people.name: Evan Leikam

people.bio: Eva Whitley started attending cons 49 years ago and decided it would be fun to run them 48 years ago. She raised 2 children in Fandom, and they inherited her belief that it's more fun to be part of the cast than the audience. She was married to Jack L. Chalker for 26.5 years and enjoys reading speculation about our relationship on Reddit. /s
people.name: Eva Whitley

links.othersocialmedia: Facebook: Fannish Widows, the Official Jack L. Chalker page, Dear Worldcon,  For Your Consideration

people.bio: Fabrice Guerrier is a Haitian artist, writer, and collaborative worldbuilder whose practice spans painting, drawing, sculpture, and speculative literature. He has been named the Root 100 Most Influential African Americans in the United States between the age of 25 to 45. He lives and works in Los Angeles, CA.
people.name: Fabrice Guerrier

people.bio: Farah Mendlesohn won a Hugo with Edward James in 2005 for The Cambridge Companion to Fantasy Literature, is the author of Diana Wynne Jones: The Fantastic Tradition and Children's Literature, Rhetorics of Fantasy; with Edward James, A Short History of Fantasy, The Inter-galactic Playground: A Critical Study of Children's and Teens' Science Fiction, with Michael M. Levy Children’s Fantasy Literature: An Introduction, which won the World Fantasy Award and the Mythopeic Award in 2017. The Pleasant Profession of Robert A. Heinlein was published in 2019. Considering The Female Man by Joanna Russ, or, As the Bear Swore … was released by Luna Press Publishing in 2026
people.name: Farah Mendlesohn

people.bio: Born and raised in Singapore, Felicia has an MA in Literary Theory and Asian Studies with a focus on anime and manga. She co-writes the bestselling middle-grade mystery series Sherlock Sam and is the writer of Tiger Girls, a young adult fantasy graphic novel selected for the White Ravens 2025 list. She was a bookseller and now works in comics publishing.
people.name: Felicia Low-Jimenez

people.bio: Felicia Martínez is the author of The Other Lives of Altagracia Sanchez, and the forthcoming These Bright and Perilous Designs (Thinking Ink Press, 2026). She is a Latinx writer and artist originally from eastern New Mexico, though she now makes her home in California. She has been guest poetry editor at The Deadlands, the SFPA Elgin Awards Chair, a Dream Foundry Contest for Emerging Writers finalist, and received her PhD in English from Stanford University. Find more of her words at The Deadlands, Star*Line, Asimov's Science Fiction, The Razor, The Acentos Review, and others. Reach out at feliciamartinez.com
people.name: Felicia Martinez

people.bio: Felicity Harley is a published science fiction writer who has recently completed a five book science fiction series. She has received positive reviews on her work. Her forcus in her writing is on climate change and hard science. Her books have a contemporary slant and are focused on a younger audience.
people.name: Felicity Harley

people.bio:
Finn McLellan (they/he) is an autistic disabled transmasc butch fantasy writer, hailing from the wilds of the northern UK.

When they’re not writing they’re busy immersing themselves in a variety of ridiculous hobbies, most of which also involve disappearing into fantasy worlds and/or waving swords at people.
people.name: Finn McLellan

people.bio: Fonda Lee is the award-winning, New York Times-bestselling author of a dozen fantasy and science fiction books, including the science fiction novel The Last Contract of Isako, and the modern epic fantasy Green Bone Saga, which has been translated into seventeen languages and named one of Time magazine’s 100 Best Fantasy Books of All Time. She is also the author of the novella Untethered Sky and several young adult novels: Zeroboxer, the Exo duology, and, cowritten with Shannon Lee, the Breathmarked duology. Fonda is a winner of the World Fantasy Award and the Locus Award, as well as a six-time winner of the Aurora Award and a finalist for the Nebula Award and the Hugo Award. A former corporate strategist and black belt martial artist, she hails from Canada and the Pacific Northwest and currently resides in New England. Learn more at fondalee.com.
people.name: Fonda Lee

people.bio: Foz Meadows is a queer Australian SFF author and essayist currently based in California. His most recent works include A Strange and Stubborn Endurance, All the Hidden Paths and Finding Echoes, and in 2019, he won the Hugo Award for Best Fanwriter.
people.name: Foz Meadows

people.bio: Francesca Myman is a senior editor and art director at Locus Magazine, where she has worked for nineteen years. She also works as a cover artist and designer, and has designed over 140 Locus covers, many featuring her vivid and imaginative original artwork. Her editorial duties include convention coverage and photography, event support for the Locus Awards, art books wrangling for the renowned Locus Recommended Reading List, undersea beastie upkeep, and many other strange and wonderful tasks. Art, science, and technology are areas of interest. She lives in Oakland, CA with her two polydactyl calicos, Magic and Marginalia.
people.name: Francesca Myman

people.bio: I have been playing, writing and running roleplaying games for 37 years. I have been running games at conventions since my first one at San Diego comic Con in 1996. I owned my game store. I have a show on you tube and my own channel Gamingfixx247. My first time playing Shadowrun was 1995 with my group that met at the stage in the Fullerton college student center. Since then I have ran off and on including on session that lasted a year long. I love gaming and giving back to the community.
people.name: Frank

people.bio:
Two-time Nebula Award-winner Fran Wilde has (so far) published nine novels, a poetry collection, and over 70 short stories for adults, teens, and kids. Her stories have been finalists for six Nebula Awards, a World Fantasy Award, four Hugo Awards, four Locus Awards, and a Lodestar. They include her Nebula- and Compton Crook-winning debut novel Updraft, and her Nebula-winning, Best of NPR 2019, debut Middle Grade novel Riverland. Her short stories appear in Asimov’s Science Fiction, Tor.com, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Shimmer, Nature, Uncanny Magazine, and multiple years' best anthologies.

The Managing Editor for The Sunday Morning Transport, Fran teaches or has taught for schools including Vermont College of Fine Arts’ MFA and St. Mary’s College of Maryland. She writes nonfiction for publications including The Washington Post, The New York Times, NPR, and Tor.com. You can find her on Instagram, Bluesky, and at franwilde.net.
people.name: Fran Wilde

people.bio: Frauke Uhlenbruch, PhD, is a writer and linguist with an academic background in sociology and religious and biblical studies. She has worked as a computational linguist developing voice AI applications, as a language instructor, and translator. Combining her interests in linguistics and genre fiction, she teaches workshops on constructing languages for SFF writers. Her academic publications include books and articles about science fiction and religion, as well as fan fiction and ancient scribal cultures. Her short fiction, published as Anna Ziegelhof, has appeared in a variety of publications, most recently in Shoreline of Infinity, Fusion Fragment, and Mythaxis.
people.name: Frauke Uhlenbruch

people.bio: Retired Computer Systems Professional. Interests include Critical Thinking, futurism, technology and interesting social questions.
people.name: Fred C. Moulton

people.bio:
Fred Lerner is a recovering librarian who spent most of his career at the National Center for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder creating an online index to scientific literature on PTSD. (He claims to have seen more of this literature than anyone on the planet.) He has been involved with science fiction for over sixty years and was one of the founders of the Science Fiction Research Association..

His book MODERN SCIENCE FICTION AND THE AMERICAN LITERARY COMMUNITY is a detailed study of SF's changing reputation over the years. He also wrote THE STORY OF LIBRARIES: FROM THE INVENTION OF WRITING TO THE COMPUTER AGE and the recently published IN MEMORIAM: A NOVEL OF THE TERRAN DIASPORA. He lives in Vermont.
people.name: Fred Lerner

people.bio: Volunteer for Friends of the Island Fox since 2005
people.name: Friends of the Island Fox

people.bio: Gabriela Lee teaches creative writing and children’s literature at the University of the Philippines. She is the co-editor of the anthology "Mapping New Stars: A Sourcebook on Philippine Speculative Fiction," which received a 2025 World Fantasy Award. Her latest fiction has appeared in the anthology "Silk & Sinew: Folk Horror from the Asian Diaspora."
people.name: Gabriela Lee

people.bio:
Gabrielle is a veteran audiobook producer, publisher and director. Her company, Skyboat Media, specializes in helping independent authors get their work onto audiobooks. She has narrated hundreds of audiobooks specializing in fantasy, humor, and titles requiring extensive foreign language and accent skills. Her “velvet touch” as an actors’ director makes her the foremost choice for best-selling authors and celebrities. She is currently working with Wil Wheaton’s It’s Storytime Podcast. She has worked with Cory Doctorow, LeVar Burton and John Scalzi on their audiobooks. She created the DragonCon Award short film THE DELIVERY, She has successfully funded two Kickstarter campaigns. She spent her childhood in Rome growing up with her wildly artistic and cinematic father, John de Cuir, three-time Oscar winning Production Designer. She is currenty story producer for Wil Wheaton's It's Storytime weekly podcast.
www.skyboatmedia.com
people.name: Gabrielle de Cuir

people.bio: Gabrielle Harbowy is a literary agent with Corvisiero Literary Agency. She is also a published author and anthologist, and award-nominated editor. She is an active member of SFWA and the American Association of Literary Agents.
people.name: Gabrielle Harbowy

people.bio: Gail Carriger has multiple NYT bestsellers and millions of books in print in dozens of different languages. She writes book hugs - comedies of manners mixed with steampunk, urban fantasy, or sci-fi (and cozy queer joy as GL Carriger). She is best known for the Parasol Protectorate and Finishing School series. She was once an archaeologist and is fond of shoes, octopuses, and tea. gailcarriger.com
people.name: Gail Carriger

people.bio: Gail is a professional software engineer, a volunteer conrunner, an avid tabletop gamer, and she loves to sing and do fiber arts in her "spare time".
people.name: Gail "RGB" Terman

people.bio:
Garrett S. Broussard, author of Cacophony of Crowns, lives with his wife in California where both chase their Animation dreams. Broussard enjoys writing stories whenever he can find time; on airplanes, in cars, and even in the middle of the street. His creations sometimes manifest as wooden furniture, photographs, and even houses in video games that happen to have a build mechanic.

Broussard enjoys hiking, petting all the dogs, eating all the buffalo wings, and tasting all the good whisky. He also enjoys ruminating on everything and obsessing over Jungian archetypes.
people.name: Garrett S Broussard

people.bio: Gary K. Wolfe is an award-winning science fiction critic, and Emeritus Professor of Humanities at Roosevelt University. His books include Soundings, Bearings, Sightings, Evaporating Genres, The Known and the Unknown, Harlan Ellison (with Ellen Weil), and American Science Fiction: Nine Classic Novels of the 1950s (editor). His lecture series How Great Science Fiction Works is available from The Great Courses, his reviews appear in Locus magazine, and he co-hosts The Coode Street Podcast with Jonathan Strahan.
people.name: Gary K Wolfe

people.bio: Gay Haldeman has managed SF Grandmaster Joe Haldeman’s career since it began in 1969. She taught writing for 30 years in the Writing Center at MIT. In 2011 she was given the Big Heart Award. She’s been going to SF conventions since 1963 and serves as the Ombudsman for SFWA. She received the Service to SFWA Award in 2026. After 60 years of marriage, she still thinks Joe is the best thing that ever happened to her.
people.name: Gay Haldeman

people.bio:
Gerald Nordley is an author, a consulting astronautical engineer, and retired USAF officer with experience in spacecraft operations and engineering. A writer of nonfiction and science fiction as "G. David Nordley," he has degrees in physics and systems management
He has over a hundred publications of nonfiction and fiction. His writing won four Analog "Anlab" readers' awards and nominations for both a Hugo and a Nebula award. His two novels and five story collections are available from Brief Candle Press. His stories focus on the human experience in scientifically plausible futures, many of them in astronomical settings. His latest story is "Titan of Chaos" in Life Beyond Us from Lucas Media.
Gerald was born in Minneapolis, lives in Sunnyvale CA with his wife Gayle Wiesner, has three adult children and one grandchild. See: www.gdnordley.com.
people.name: G. David Nordley

people.bio: Dr. Geoffrey A. Landis is a science-fiction writer, a scientist, a poet, and a swordsman. He has won the Hugo, Nebula, Sturgeon, and Robert A. Heinlein awards for science fiction, and is the author of the novel Mars Crossing and short-story collection Impact Parameter (& Other Quantum Realities). He works for NASA on developing advanced technologies for spaceflight. He is also known for work on concepts for interstellar flight. In his spare time, he goes to fencing tournaments to stab people. Sometimes they stab back. More information can be found at his very-much out-of-date web page: http://www.geoffreylandis.com/, or just look him up on Wikipedia.
people.name: Geoffrey A. Landis

people.bio:
Gerardo "Gerry" Maravilla is a Mexican-American writer/director based in Los Angeles. Born and raised in the San Fernando Valley, he escaped his suburban Catholic upbringing through punk rock and horror movies. A bicultural lovechild of Tim Burton and Guillermo del Toro, he crafts supernatural horror stories with heart.
He's been a Film Independent Project Involve Writing Fellow, a New York Film Festival Artist Academy Fellow, and a Latino Film Institute Inclusion Fellow, and developed work through Hola Mexico's Tomorrow's Filmmakers Today, the Mexican-American Cultural Education Foundation's Masterclass, and Stowe Story Labs.

His films have screened at Palm Springs ShortFest, LALIFF, and Bogotá Shorts, among others. His feature script, Niño de Vidrio (Child of Glass), was developed at Cine Qua Non's Storylines and Script Revision Labs. The short version won the Roadmap Writers Short Script Competition, and the feature recently won the BendFilm Basecamp Pitch Competition.
people.name: Gerardo Maravilla

people.bio: Geri is a fanzine fan. She’s won 5 FAAn awards including #1 Fan Face in 1998 and the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2022 Corflu. She is also a 2007 Hugo winner, 2019 TAFF delegate, susceptible to special projects, and loves hosting parties most of all. As a member of the Board of Governors for the Ig Nobel Prizes, Geri invites you to the Improbable Research Dramatic Readings at LAcon V. Her Video Archeology Project will premiere the reconstruction of the 1976 Star Wars Slide Show on Monday.
people.name: Geri Sullivan

people.bio: Serling-winning and seven time Hugo Finalist science fiction author Gideon Marcus has just had published Majera, fourth book in The Kitra Saga. His short fiction can be found in Dark Matter, Utopia, Simultaneous Times, and elsewhere. He is the editor of the Rediscovery: Science Fiction by Women anthology series. He is also the founder of Journey Press, an independent publisher focused on unusual and diverse speculative fiction, and he runs the award-winning time machine project, Galactic Journey. He is a professional space historian, public speaker, and a lecturer at Cal State University San Marcos and UC San Diego.
people.name: Gideon Marcus

people.bio: Gigi Coulson is the founder and Executive Director of Costumers of Color, a nonprofit expanding access and belonging in historical costuming through education, scholarships, events, and cultural travel. A costumer, historian, and sociologist, she has spent more than fifteen years researching historical daily life and material culture, particularly in medieval and Renaissance Italy. A retired federal scientist, she is passionate about connecting scholarship, creativity, and community through immersive historical experiences.
people.name: Gigi Coulson

people.bio: Gina Saucier will talk about empire and science fiction/fantasy even when it is a massive stretch to weave it in. Pacific Northwest born and raised, MSc in Empires, Colonialism, and Globalization from the LSE. Gina grew up doing local theater, costuming, and sewing. @reginaroams on socials.
people.name: Gina Saucier

people.bio: Glen Olson is a fiction and non-fiction author. His two novels, Tears of a Thousand Years, and Desperate Endeavor, and the non-fiction book Fifty Years of Polyamory in America have made the Bold Authors curated suggested reading lists. He grew up in the San Fernando Valley, a suburb of Los Angeles. He would have had an absolutely normal childhood except for one fact: his best friend’s father worked in cold war aerospace . . . and the friend's father owned a mimeograph machine, allowing Glen and friends to put out a neighborhood newspaper— and they shamelessly did so! This encouraged his lifelong love of writing. Glen became a paramedic for a fire department where he had several roles, including disaster preparedness educator, inspector, and captain, writing training manuals by day and fiction by night. Today he is a fulltime writer, the author of four books and working on a fifth (with possible screenplay).
people.name: Glen Olson (G.W.Olson)

people.bio: Gloria Jackson-Nefertiti is a Black bisexual autistic elder, workshop facilitator, and creator of transformative discussions about neurodivergence (specifically autism and ADHD/ADD), consent, polyamory, shame, and intersectionality. Her work centers inclusive, compassionate storytelling that helps people feel seen, affirmed, and connected. Finally, she is hard at work on her memoir, "A Different Drum: A Black, Autistic, Polyamorous, Mentally Ill, Former Fundamentalist Christian/Cult Member and Breast Cancer Survivor WHO JUST WANTS TO FIT IN."
people.name: Gloria Jackson-Nefertiti

people.bio: Gregory A. Wilson is Professor of English at St. John's University in New York, where he teaches creative writing and speculative fiction. He is author of the epic fantasy The Third Sign, the award-winning graphic novel Icarus and dark fantasy Gray Assassin Trilogy, and the D&D adventure/sourcebook Tales and Tomes from the Forbidden Library, plus many stories. He co-hosts the AP podcast Speculate! and was Craft of Writing track co-lead at Seattle Worldcon. Under the moniker Arvan Eleron, he runs a narrative-focused Twitch channel with many TTRPG campaigns. He lives with his family in Connecticut; his virtual home is www.gregoryawilson.com.
people.name: gregawil@gmail.com

people.bio:
I have read SF since I was 11, got my first fanzine in 1968 in a bundle of them from SETH JOHNSON. The first fanzines I subscribed to was FILE 770 and Science Fiction Review. I have pubbed fanzines since I970. consider myself a fanzine Fan. Have worked on local Conventions in every dept. since 1977 (Midsouthcon in Memphis). Have degrees in Chem. and History. Daughter is a fan, who will be here. Have 15000 books (SF and misc.) in our home. Last of the Print fanzine publishers, I think - MEMPHEN (up to #284)

Working on local history about Memphis lately - fannish and about my childhood home. YES, met Elvis a time or two - he even went to see my dad once (Dr. J.T.Bridges). Worked at the hospital where he was pronounced dead and held a syringe of his blood as well.

Went to my first SF con in 1971 in Kansas City(met George RR Martin there(took his photo too). Did an Index to Richard Geis's Science Fiction Review. Went to LACON in 1972 and many other worldcons.

I am not to be confused with the Australian SF artist - GREGORY BRIDGES, btw. I met him at a previous LAcon, tho!
people.name: Greg Bridges

people.bio: Gregg Castro [t'rowt'raahl Salinan/rumsien-ramaytush Ohlone], has worked to preserve his Ohlone and Salinan heritage for over three decades. Gregg is the Society for California Archaeology’s Native American Programs Committee Chairperson. Gregg is a Facilitator for the annual California Indian Conference, a 30+ year annual gathering about California Indigenous culture and a Co-Founder/Advisor of the California Indian History Curriculum Coalition, based at CSU-Sacramento, promoting accurate school curriculum. He is now Culture Director the Association of Ramaytush Ohlone, advising within their San Francisco Peninsula homelands. Gregg is a nonfiction writer-activist within the California indigenous community. He has been attending scifi cons for nearly 50 years, the last 20 as a panelist including 3 previous Worldcons. This is his 9th Worldcon, third LACon - YAY!
people.name: Gregg Castro

people.bio: Greg Kasavin is creative director at Supergiant Games, where he has worked on the writing and design of each of the studio's titles, including Bastion, Transistor, Pyre, Hades, and Hades II. Prior to Supergiant, Kasavin worked in publishing at 2K Games, as a producer on the Command & Conquer franchise at Electronic Arts, and as editor-in-chief of GameSpot.com. Born in Moscow, he has lived in the San Francisco Bay Area since early childhood. He holds a B.A. in English literature from U.C. Berkeley.
people.name: Greg Kasavin

people.bio:
Greg Morris is president of Scaled Composites and is a Test Pilot for Scaled. Prior to Scaled, he was President of Gauntlet Aerospace, including teaching in the Qualitative Evaluation Program at United States Air Force Test Pilot School, and target & chase support for the 412th Test Wing at Edwards Air Force Base.

Greg has Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Southern California and a Master of Science in Flight Test Engineering from National Test Pilot School. He is an Associate Fellow of the Society of Experimental Test Pilots.
people.name: Greg Morris

people.bio:
Gregory Amato made a career of selling his quill as a mercenary writer for many years. He wrote true and important things for newspapers, magazines, academia, and, for over a decade, intelligence analysis for the FBI.

Now, he writes fantasy stories based on the myths and sagas of the vikings. He published his first novella, The Skald, in 2023. He followed it with three novels (Burden to Bear, Rune to Ruin, and Fallen to Fury), completing his Spear of the Gods Saga in 2025. The series has been praised for its solid grounding in the cultural history of the time, the fight scenes, but above all else, the dry and dirty sense of saga-like humor that runs throughout.

Outside his time spent spinning yarns about vikings and wizards, he practices martial arts, brews beer, and plays DnD when he gets the chance. He lives happily with his family in the Pacific Northwest.
people.name: Gregory Amato

people.bio:
Gregory Kontaxis was born in December 1989 in Athens. He studied Informatics and Financial Mathematics in Greece and the United Kingdom and has worked as a Risk Analyst in Vienna and London. He currently resides in London, where he is occupied with investment risk and writing. A lifelong admirer of Greek mythology, Gregory aims to revive ancient myths through modern fantasy in his books.
He is the author of The Dance of Light, a planned pentalogy. The first book, The Return of the Knights, was followed by his novella The Knight of the Moon. He later published the second and third installments of the series, The Fall of the Giants and The Rise of the West. His fourth novel in the series, The Sin of War, is forthcoming in 2026.
people.name: Gregory Kontaxis

people.bio: Greg Wylie is known in the Society for Creative Anachronism (SCA) as Master Laertes McBride. Joining in the Kingdom of Ansteorra (TX/OK) (1990), he relocated to the Kingdom of Caid (Southern California) in 1996. A rapier enthusiast, he has earned the SCA’s highest accolades for skill, teaching, and service, including recognition as a premier member of the Order of Defense. He has also received the SCA’s highest recognition for service. He has held numerous leadership roles, including oversight of all combat in Caid, serving as the Society Rapier Marshal, and most recently serving as Vice President of Operations for Caid.
people.name: Greg Wylie

people.bio:
Griff grew up playing piano and singing in various choirs. He took up guitar in his early 50s. Since entering filk, he’s written songs, given concerts, held the Creating While Neurodivergent Workshop, been nominated for the Writer/Composer Pegasus, and released three albums (so far).

He and his husband, author Cozy Joe Petty, are also both published fiction writers (together and separately), and are owned by an obstreperous tortoiseshell cat named Molly. They live in Long Beach, California.

Website: https://griffthefilker.com/
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@GrifftheFilker
Bandcamp: https://drgriff.bandcamp.com/
people.name: Griff the Filker

people.bio: Grigory Lukin (rhymes with "story" and "win") is an award-winning filmmaker and an internationally published author of science fiction and nonfiction. His words have appeared in Phano, The Colored Lens, and multiple anthologies. Originally from Russia, he also lived in the US and Canada (currently in Montreal), and may add a fourth passport to his collection someday. He enjoys pastries, good conversations, and hiking from Mexico to Canada.
people.name: Grigory Lukin

people.bio: G.R. Theron is a Seattle-based fantasy author and member of the Mythopoeic Society. In addition to writing, he is also an active artist, panelist, and host of Northwest Speculative. Find his work at grtheron.com.
people.name: G.R. Theron

people.bio:
I specialize in the operational transformation required to turn capital into high-multiple returns.

The biggest challenge for institutional investors is finding leaders who possess both C-suite execution and an investor mindset.

I operate as a hybrid: a C-suite Executive with a background in leading global P&L, combined with the strategic accountability of a Private Equity Operating Partner. My role is to not just advise, but to step into the engine room, re-architect the enterprise, and drive value creation from the top-down.
people.name: Guy Ronen

people.bio: Gwynne Garfinkle is the author of a novel, CAN'T FIND MY WAY HOME, and two collections, SINKING, SINGING and PEOPLE CHANGE, all published by Aqueduct Press. Her work has appeared in such publications as STRANGE HORIZONS, UNCANNY, ESCAPE POD, and NOT ONE OF US. Her poem "the jacarandas are unimpressed by your show of force" is a 2026 Rhysling Award finalist.
people.name: Gwynne Garfinkle

people.bio: Harry Turtledove is an escaped Byzantine historian. For the past 35 years, he has made a poor but not too honest living writing alternate history, others, fantasy (a lot of it historically based), and, every now and then, historical fiction. He is married to fellow writer and Broadway maven Laura Franks. They have three daughters, two grand granddaughters, and three spoiled cats.
people.name: Harry Turtledove

people.bio: Heather Fawcett is the New York Times, USA Today, and Sunday Times bestselling Canadian author of books for adults, kids, and teens, including Emily Wilde’s Encyclopaedia of Faeries, Even the Darkest Stars, Ember and the Ice Dragons, The Grace of Wild Things, and more. Her books, which somehow all include dragons in one form or another, have been translated into more than twenty languages and nominated for various awards, including the Locus, Mythopoeic, and Silver Birch. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature and a Bachelor’s in Archaeology. She lives on Vancouver Island.
people.name: Heather Fawcett

people.bio: Heather Rose Jones writes queer fantasy and historical fiction, including the Alpennia series and the fairy-tale novella The Language of Roses, as well as multiple short stories. She has non-fiction publications on topics ranging from biotech to historic costume to naming practices and creates the Lesbian Historic Motif Project blog and podcast, presenting research on sapphic themes history as a resource for authors writing historic-based fiction.
people.name: Heather Rose Jones

people.bio:
Heather Tracy (she/her) is a travel agent by day, and a masked copy editor and writer by night. As a travel agent, she plans Nerdventures--travel for the nerd in all of us. These can be anything from visiting New Zealand to see as many Lord of the Rings filming locations as you can to visiting castles in Europe to following in the footsteps of your favorite author.
As a copy editor, she's found hundreds of typos, comma splices, and other grammatical nitpicks for Space Wizard Science Fantasy since before 2016. With over 30 titles copyedited, she's now turned her hand to short stories in the Fiery Deeps, Lesbians in Space: Where No Man Has Gone Before, and Lesbians in Space: The Sapphics Strike Back anthologies, and her first novel, Only a Chapter, which features some of her personal journey surviving breast cancer.
Heather lives in Raleigh with her husband of over twenty years, William C. Tracy, where they have two rambunctious cats and several beehives. They enjoy taking their own Nerdventures--as much as they can be away from their small businesses--and cosplaying at various markets and cons throughout the year.
You can find her on Facebook as @heathertracyauthor, on Bluesky as @heathertracyauthor.bsky.social and on Instagram as @hunnyjar319. For her travel agency, Melvin's Travel Adventures, you can find her on Facebook and Instagram as @melvinstraveladventures or on Bluesky as @melvinsta.bsky.social.
people.name: Heather Tracy

people.bio: Heidi Kasa is the author of the poetry collection The Bullet Takes Forever, the flash fiction collection The Beginners, winner of the 2023 Digging Press Chapbook Contest, and Split. She received the 2024 Plaza Prose Poetry Prize and the 2023 Poetry Super Highway Prize for poems from The Bullet Takes Forever. Kasa's work has appeared in Barrelhouse, The Brooklyn Rail, The Pinch Journal, and elsewhere. She works as an editor in Austin and creates handmade artist books. She has edited for 20 years in a wide range of book genres and materials. Find her at www.heidikasa.com.
people.name: Heidi Kasa

people.bio:
Helen Montgomery has been active in the Chicago fannish community since 2000 and Worldcon fandom since 2004. She has worked on twelve Worldcons and three NASFiCs in total, including as Chair of Chicon 8: The 80th World Science Fiction Convention in 2022, and most recently the Seattle Worldcon 2025 and the upcoming LAcon V in 2026. Helen has held many roles for Capricon in Chicago since 2000, including ConChair (twice) and serving on the Board of Directors (thrice). She also chaired Smofcon 2016, a convention for convention runners, in Chicago.

Additionally, she is the President of the Science Fiction Outreach Project, a charitable organization that promotes literacy and fandom through the reading of science fiction and fantasy.

Helen is a retired psychiatric social worker who enjoys reading (SF/F, romance, and mystery), watching most sports, attending live theatre and concerts, board gaming, photography, traveling, acrylic paint pouring, LEGO, and container gardening. She collects more art than she can display, and is an avid collector of all things related to Maleficent (the original animated version).
people.name: Helen Montgomery

people.bio: H.E. Milla is a second-generation immigrant with roots in Honduras, China, and Vietnam. They are a Clarion West alumnus (2024), recipient of the NESFA Short Story Contest Award (2025), and PhD candidate studying epigenetics and stress-related diseases. You can read their thoughts on queer villainy and futurity in the December 2025 Issue of Speculative Insight. H.E. lives in North Carolina with their wife and two cats.
people.name: H.E. Milla

people.bio: Henry Herz has written short stories for Daily Science Fiction, Weird Tales, Pseudopod, Metastellar, Titan Books, Highlights for Children, Ladybug Magazine, and anthologies from Penguin-Random House, Albert Whitman, Blackstone Publishing, Third Flatiron, Brigids Gate Press, Baen Books, elsewhere. He's edited ten anthologies and written fourteen picture books. henryherz.com
people.name: Henry Herz

people.bio: Henry Lien is a graduate of Brown University, UCLA School of Law, and Clarion West Writers’ Workshop. He is the author of the Peasprout Chen fantasy series and the non-fiction book Spring, Summer, Asteroid, Bird: The Art of Eastern Storytelling. His books have received starred reviews from Kirkus, Publishers Weekly, and Booklist and New York Times acclaim. His writing has appeared in publications including Literary Hub, Poets & Writers, Asimov’s, Analog, and F&SF, and he is a four-time Nebula Award finalist. Henry also teaches for institutions including the UCLA Extension Writers’ Program, the University of Iowa, Clarion West, and Writing the Other. He won the UCLA Extension Department of the Arts Outstanding Instructor of the Year Award. Henry has previously worked as an attorney and fine art dealer. Born in Taiwan, Henry currently lives in Hollywood, California. Hobbies include writing and performing campy anthems for his books and losing Nebula Awards. www.henrylien.com
people.name: Henry Lien

people.bio: Henry Spencer is a systems programmer and spacecraft engineer, with sidelines in spaceflight history and open-source software. As a consultant to University of Toronto's Space Flight Laboratory (now being re-established as SFL Missions Inc.), he is creator and maintainer of much of SFL's most critical on-board software, now running in orbit on 50+ satellites. Earlier, he was one of the founders of the open-source software movement -- there is probably some of his code in your computer. He is a Fellow of the British Interplanetary Society, and a member of the Senior Advisory Board of the Space Studies Institute. Asteroid 117329 Spencer is named after him.
people.name: Henry Spencer

people.bio: H.H. Pak is a Korean-American Nebula, Hugo, and Astounding nominated writer from Los Angeles whose speculative fiction has been published in Clarkesworld, among other venues. When they are not writing or surviving medical school, they co-edit Wyrmhole Magazine and make art of all kinds.
people.name: H.H. Pak

people.bio: Dr. Hirotaka Osawa is a professor at Keio University. His research field includes human-agent interaction, the development of anthropomorphic devices, simulation using social games for social agents, and exploring humanity studies through science fiction literature. He focuses specifically on how human-like appearance and attitude enhance the interaction between users and machines, as well as examining the role of social intelligence in improving our society. He earned his PhD in Engineering in Computer Science from Keio University. He published many SF related research books and also short story "Clash of Considerations" in 2026 ("short-short na SF").
people.name: Hirotaka Osawa

people.bio: Holly Black is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of fantasy books, including the Cruel Prince series, the Spiderwick Chronicles, and the Charlatan Duology. She has been a finalist for an Eisner Award and a Lodestar Award, and the recipient of a Mythopoeic Award, a Nebula Award, and a Newbery Honor. Her books have been translated into thirty-two languages worldwide and adapted for film and television. She currently lives in New England with her husband and children in a house with a secret library.
people.name: Holly Black

people.bio:
Howard Davidson was captured by a Heinlein book in second grade, and hasn't been seen much since. Inspired to do science fiction by reading it, he went off and got a Ph.D. in physics, the best training available for becoming a crackpot inventor.

He is currently a senior physicist in the computer industry. He holds more than 50 patents, has published and presented numerous technical papers and one technical book chapter, taught Computer Engineering at Stanford, done technical editing for Hugo winning novels, and goes to cons. He gets to write science fiction for the annual budget cycle.
people.name: Howard Davidson

people.bio: Howard Tayler is the writer and illustrator behind SCHLOCK MERCENARY, and is one of the founding hosts of Writing Excuses.
people.name: Howard Tayler

people.bio: Howard V. Hendrix holds a BS in Biology (Xavier University, Ohio) and MA and PhD in English Literature, the latter both from University of California, Riverside. He taught at the college level for over thirty years, the last twenty at CSU Fresno. He has published six novels and four collections of stories; has authored, coauthored, or coedited seven works of nonfiction; and has written numerous articles, reviews, and editorials. His most recent book is Living Fossils, Lost Worlds, Last Humans: The Science and Fiction of Population and Extinction, releasing in 2026 from McFarland.
people.name: Howard V. Hendrix

people.bio: Humphrey Price is a space systems engineer who has contributed to robotic exploration missions to the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. His interests include planetary exploration, spacecraft design, solar sails, interstellar spaceflight, aliens, human missions to Mars, and strangely enough, eschatology. Info on his publications can be found at https://humphreyprice.com.
people.name: Humphrey Price

people.bio: Hyeonsu Kim is a master’s student in English Language and Literature at Chungbuk National University in South Korea. Her research examines disability, trauma, and agency in contemporary literature and speculative fiction. She has presented at the 2025 BK Graduate Student Conference and the 2026 annual conference of the British Society for Literature and Science in Glasgow.
people.name: Hyeonsu

people.bio: Ian Patterson is an award winning author of science fiction, horror, and poetry. His debut, Transference, won the Colorado Book Award for science fiction in 2025, and is part of a complete series called The Narrator Cycle. His work aims to critique capitalism, inequality, and environmental destruction by centering philosophical discussions in the trappings of fast-paced, genre-bending narratives. He believes all people should have bodily autonomy, equality, freedom, and that a more just future can be built on compassion and empathy. He can usually be found on his bike somewhere in the mountains of Colorado, or spending time with his family and his two cats.
people.name: Ian Patterson

people.bio: Inez Ray is a California born, Puget Sound based author. She is a former doula and midwife assistant. After working in reproductive healthcare for over a decade she burned out and needed to put all her anxieties into a creative project. What emerged was her debut novel, Buzzard, which is being published with Left Unread and Bindery Books September 22nd. Buzzard is a dystopian sci-fi with a strong Feminist perspective about reproductive health in America. Inez the granddaughter of immigrants on both sides with proud Chicana and Irish heritage. When she isn't writing devastating fiction, she is walking her dogs or feeding her children.
people.name: INEZ RAY

people.bio:
Ingrid Moon writes science fiction and fantasy, teaches STEM subjects, and edits other people's worlds when she isn't busy building her own. Her background spans biology, physics, technology, business, gaming, and education, all of which she uses to inform her stories, settings, and characters. She was awarded a NASA Endeavor Distinguished STEM Leadership award in 2018.

She is the author of the Saxen Saga, a dark space opera set in a grim future; The Biohunter, a post-apocalyptic adventure; and a handful of shorter works in science fiction and fantasy. She has also written science reference guides for writers, translating real-world science into practical knowledge for worldbuilding. Currently she is deep in an epic fantasy series that started as one book and has, predictably, become several.

When she's not writing or teaching, she's probably reading outside with her two pigs and dozens of squirrels, or drawing on the couch with six cats fighting for her lap. She loves the outdoors and spent much of her life climbing mountains, sleeping on glaciers, teaching teens outdoor survival skills, or playing “normal” sports like soccer, ice hockey, and triathlon.
people.name: Ingrid Moon

people.bio: Born in Nigeria, Inua Ellams is a poet, playwright & performer, graphic artist & designer and founder of: The Midnight Run (an arts-filled, night-time, urban walking experience.), The Rhythm and Poetry Party (The R.A.P Party) which celebrates live literature and music, and Poetry + Film / Hack (P+F/H) which celebrates poetry and film. Identity, Displacement & Destiny are reoccurring themes in his work, where he tries to mix the old with the new: traditional African oral storytelling with contemporary poetics, paint with pixel, texture with vector. His books are published by Flipped Eye, Akashic, Nine Arches, Penned In The Margins & Bloomsbury.
people.name: Inua Ellams

people.bio: Iris Almaraz is an award-winning Chicana filmmaker, screenwriter, and director whose work blends horror, dark comedy, and social commentary. Her short film Lucky Bastard screened internationally and received multiple festival awards. A three-time Sundance Writing Lab finalist, Almaraz is currently developing several genre projects, including Mother May I, a horror feature screenplay that was named a Semi-Finalist at Screamfest, and Bloody Maria, a horror series centered on a Latina anti-heroes. Through her work, Almaraz explores identity, power, folklore, and the ways horror can illuminate the fears and tensions that shape contemporary life.
people.name: Iris Almaraz

people.bio: Iro is a nerd’s nerd who has been teaching fictional space languages since their first immersion Belter workshop at Worldcon in Helsinki. Previously a voracious but solitary reader, they have enjoyed becoming a tremendously involved part of the SFF community through The Expanse. More recently, they fell in love with Andor, adding the language of Ghorman to their Languages of Resistance workshop series. Previously educated and employed in physics, computer science, and early music performance, Iro is finally going back to school in the subject that should have been obvious from the start: linguistics.
people.name: Iro

people.bio: isaac dwyer (they/them/theirs) is an essayist, literary translator, Islamic studies scholar, and immigration and trans* rights advocate. They are currently a PhD student in comparative literature at the University of California, Los Angeles. In addition to English, they work in Spanish, Portuguese, Urdu-Hindi, Romanian, Farsi and Tajiki. Recent work can be found in Asymptote Journal, Foglifter, Body Shots, Erotic Review, Trans and Queer Studies in Religion, and The Journal of Gender Studies.
people.name: isaac dwyer

people.bio: Isabel J. Kim is a speculative fiction author who lives near New York City in an apartment filled with books and swords. Her short fiction has won the Nebula, Locus, and Shirley Jackson Awards, was a finalist for the Hugo and Sturgeon Awards, and she has previously been a finalist for the Astounding Award. She has been published in Clarkesworld, Lightspeed, and Strange Horizons, among other venues, and has been reprinted in multiple best of the year anthologies, including Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy ‘23, ‘24, and ‘25, translated into Chinese and Japanese, and optioned for film and television. She is a two-time graduate of the University of Pennsylvania, and is delighted that she uses the creative writing degree more than the law degree. When she’s not writing, she’s either co-hosting her internet culture podcast, Wow if True, or contemplating returning to her biglaw career.
people.name: Isabel J. Kim

people.bio: Isabel has been active in fandom for almost 30 years. She has been published in Argentus; Drink Tank; Invisible 2: Personal Essays about Race and Representation in Science Fiction and Fantasy; Uncanny: A Magazine of Science Fiction and Fantasy; and The WisCon Chronicles, and is Co-Editor of The WisCon Chronicles Volume 12: Boundaries and Bridges. Isabel is a co-host of The Incomplete Worldcon Podcast. She has served on the boards of library-related organizations, and is the Library Coordinator for House of Puerto Rico San Diego, a cultural organization established to share Puerto Rican culture.
people.name: Isabel Schechter

people.bio: Izzy Wasserstein, a queer and trans woman, is the author of two poetry collections, the 2022 short story collection All the Hometowns You Can’t Stay Away From (a Lambda Literary Award finalist), the novella These Fragile Graces, This Fugitive Heart (Tachyon, 2024), and the flash-fiction chapbook This Next Song is Called Punk Rock Valhalla (Neon Hemlock, 2025). She teaches writing and literature at a public university. A born-and-raised Kansan, she currently lives in Southern California, where she shares a home with the writer Nora E. Derrington and their animal companions. She wants to hear about your TTRPG character.
people.name: Izzy Wasserstein

people.bio: I am an Associate Professor Emeritus of Physics at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville (USA). Previously, I was Director of Laser Development at the Nevada Terawatt Facility. I have also worked at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and the US Air Force Research Laboratory. I hold a Ph.D. in Optical Sciences and an MS in Physics from the University of New Mexico and a BS in Physics from the University of Arizona. My wife and I live in an earth-shelter house with two cats, one dog, and whatever has crept in when we weren't looking.
people.name: Jack Glassman

people.bio: Jack Kiraly is the Director of Government Relations for The Planetary Society, the world's largest independent space advocacy nonprofit. In this role, Jack leads the organization's D.C. presence, implementing The Society’s advocacy strategy, maintaining relationships with elected officials and key decision makers, organizing events to foster community engagement, and serving as the eyes and ears of the organization in the nation’s capital. A key goal of Jack’s is to use this opportunity to not only involve the scientific community in the policy-making process, but to also engage and empower members of the general public to take action to support space science and exploration. Prior to joining The Planetary Society, Jack worked in electoral politics and community organizing. This experience gives him a skillset of working with various constituencies, building diverse coalitions, and mobilizing activists to successfully advocate for their values. Jack graduated from American University with a Bachelor's degree in Political Science and Master of Public Policy degree focusing in Science & Space Policy.
people.name: Jack R. Kiraly

people.bio: Jacob John White (Jake) is the creator of the graphic novel series BellRinger, the writer of the short fiction serial A Many Tale, and co-creator of the immersive dance-theater event ASCEND.
people.name: Jacob John White

people.bio: Jake Casella Brookins is a critic, scholar, and editor. His reviews & writings appear in Locus, the Chicago Review of Books, and elsewhere. He is the publishing editor at the Ancillary Review of Books (a Hugo & Ignyte finalist) and the host of the podcast A Meal of Thorns (also a Hugo finalist).
people.name: Jake Casella Brookins

people.bio: James Islington is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Will of the Many (the first novel in the Hierarchy series), The Licanius Trilogy (beginning with The Shadow of What Was Lost), and Scion. He has sold more than two million books, and his work has been translated into twenty-three different languages. He lives on the Mornington Peninsula in Victoria, Australia, with his wife and two children.
people.name: James Islington

people.bio: James Patrick Kelly has won two World Science Fiction Society’s Hugo Awards as well as the Science Fiction Writers of America’s Nebula Award and the Locus Award. Already in 2026 he has published robot stories in Reactor and Clarkesworld. A new collection of his robot stories The BOOK OF BOTS will debut at LAcon from Fairwood Press. His fiction has been translated into eighteen languages. He writes a column on SF and the internet for Asimov's Science Fiction Magazine.
people.name: James Patrick Kelly

people.bio: Jane Shevtsov is an ecologist and space biologist. She is the co-founder and CEO of the Propagule Space Ecology Institute, which does R&D on closed biospheres for space exploration. She also taught mathematical biology at UCLA and co-authored the textbook "Modeling Life: The Mathematics of Biological Systems". Outside of science, Jane's highest priority is the establishment of a democratic United Federation of Nations.
people.name: Jane Shevtsov

people.bio: Janet Catherine Johnston is an astrophysicist, geophysicist, engineer, and alumna of MIT. She worked for the US Air Force as a space scientist, including a stint at the Pentagon and a 4-year assignment in Europe, traveling to over 60 countries. She is a dance teacher, singer, master costume designer, martial artist, private pilot, and fortune teller. Her novellas appeared in Analog Science Fiction and Fact and she writes plays and screenplays. Her hard science fiction stories have been described as a kind of “Lovecraft meets Arthur C. Clarke.” Janet lives on Plum Island with her Siberian Husky.
people.name: Janet Catherine Johnston

people.bio: By day, Janet Forbes (she/her) is the CEO and founder of World Anvil, the award-winning worldbuilding platform, novel writing software and RPG campaign manager with over 3 million users. By night, she's a published author (FlameTree Press, Bona Books, Dream Theory Media) and game writer (Dark Crystal RPG - lead author, Kobold Press, Infinite Black). Janet's past experience as an archaeologist, opera singer, teacher and educator, motivational speaker, polyglot, dinosaur-lover, entrepreneur and, somehow, professional recorder player, all find their way into the rich worlds woven through her stories. Her work explores everything from dungeon delving and dinosaurs, to feminism and freedom.
people.name: Janet Forbes | World Anvil

people.bio: Janice Gelb has worked on many conventions, notably running Program Operations at ten Worldcons (and LAcon V will make 11!) and running the Hugo ceremony at LAcon III. She's also published numerous apazines and spends way too much time posting on social media. She was the DUFF (Down Under Fan Fund) representative at Aussiecon 3 where, in a fit of madness, she also ran Program Ops. She liked Australia (and one particular Aussie fan) so much that she migrated there from the US. In Real Life, she's a technical editor.
people.name: Janice Gelb

people.bio: Janine Wardale's  eclectic style of costuming combines sewing, crocheting, embroidery, bead work, dying, fabric painting, aging and distressing and macrame. She loves to reuse, re-purpose, and reinvent vintage finds and to turn them into unique pieces of wearable art and masquerade attire. Her claim to fame is that she spends six hours of embellishing for every one hour of  sewing. The results speak for themselves and she is just a fun person to be around, share a laugh with and simply enjoy life over a cup of coffee. 's eclectic style of costuming combines sewing, crocheting, embroidery, bead work, dying, fabric painting, aging and distressing and macrame. She loves to reuse, re-purpose, and reinvent vintage finds and to turn them into unique pieces of wearable art and masquerade attire. Her claim to fame is that she spends six hours of embellishing for every one hour of sewing. The results speak for themselves and she is just a fun person to be around, share a laugh with and simply enjoy life over a cup of coffee.
people.name: Janine Wardale

people.bio: Jared Pechacek is a writer and illustrator. His novel The West Passage was nominated for the Locus and Astounding Awards and the Le Guin Prize, and won the 2025 Crawford Award. He lives in Seattle.
people.name: Jared Pechacek

people.bio: Jasmine Kuliasha was born in Peru and grew up in Guatemala. She left a career in robotics to pursue her dream of writing, and now her ongoing JERICHO JAMES series is published by Orbit Books. Today Jasmine writes from Colorado, where she’s living her own Happily Ever After with her children and husband. When she’s not creating chaos for her characters, Jasmine is training for her next marathon, or trying to get her personal assistants (two cats) to do anything at all.
people.name: Jasmine Kuliasha

people.bio: Jason P. Crawford is a science educator and speculative-fiction author from Lancaster, California. A full member of SFWA, he writes epic fantasy, mythic retellings, and science-driven SF. His short fiction appears in Once Upon a Future Time Vol. 4, The Vampire Survival Guide, and the Superstars Writing Seminars anthology. He was a top-ten Finalist in the 2024 Baen Fantasy Adventure Award and won third place in the 2025 Jim Baen Memorial Short Story Award. Jason is an energetic panelist and moderator, known for blending scientific insight with storytelling craft, and will also serve as a moderator at LACon V.
people.name: Jason P. Crawford

people.bio: Jason Sanford is an award-winning science fiction and fantasy writer who’s also a passionate advocate for fellow authors, creators, and fans, in particular through reporting in his Genre Grapevine column. He’s also published dozens of stories in magazines such as Asimov’s Science Fiction, Interzone, and Beneath Ceaseless Skies along with appearances in various “year’s best” anthologies and The New Voices of Science Fiction. His first novel Plague Birds was a finalist for both the Nebula and Philip K. Dick Awards. Born and raised in the American South, Jason’s previous experience includes work as an archaeologist, journalist and a Peace Corps Volunteer. His website is www.jasonsanford.com.
people.name: Jason Sanford

people.bio: Jason Schachat is an independent writer, filmmaker, and video game designer. He received his MFA in Creative Writing from UC Riverside and has spent the years since both teaching English and producing Patreon-supported works for his generous fans.
people.name: Jason Schachat

people.bio: Jason Snell is a journalist and podcaster. He runs The Incompatable and Six Colors and hosts Upgrade.
people.name: Jason Snell

people.bio: Jay is a book blogger and several types of nerd. He lives in Maryland with his wife and three children.
people.name: Jay Brantner

people.bio: Jay Hartlove is the author of the fantasy romance Mermaid Steel, which won Silver at the BookFest Awards. He also wrote the urban fantasy Goddess Rising Trilogy, which won Best Thriller at the Independent eBook Awards (endorsed by Bram Stoker Award winning author John Shirley). And he wrote the science fiction thriller The Insane God, which was a Finalist in the Chanticleer Cygnus Awards (endorsed by Hugo Award winning author David Brin). He wrote, produced and directed The Mirror’s Revenge, the musical sequel to Snow White. He was selected for 50 Authors You Should Be Reading by The Authors Show.
people.name: Jay Hartlove

people.bio: Jay Kristoff is a #1 international, NYT and Sunday Times bestselling author of fantasy and science fiction novels, including the EMPIRE OF THE VAMPIRE and NEVERNIGHT series.
people.name: Jay Kristoff

people.bio: Jaymee Goh writes, reviews, and edits speculative fiction. Her work has been published in Science Fiction Studies, The Los Angeles Review of Books, and Best American Science Fiction & Fantasy. She is a graduate from the Clarion Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Workshop and is an editor at Tachyon Publications.
people.name: Jaymee Goh

people.bio:
Table top gamer since 1975. Part of some original AD&D development. Publishing my own TTRPG.
US Army 30 years, combat veteran/infantry, cavalry, special forces & intelligence. US Army War College graduate. 7 Tainted Patriot poetry collections published, #8 in progress.
Fictional world creator, some stories go back 50 years. 5 Metaerie books currently available, 3 others in progress.
Frequent speaker on fantasy, military and writing.
people.name: JD

people.bio: The poetic storytelling of Jeané D. Ridges—rendered from abundant melanin, Southernness, good eatin’, breath, ill living, care—has most recently been published in Strange Horizons and is forthcoming in Tales from the Cryptids. They’ve been a copyeditor at khōréō since 2023. In 2026, they co-launched Spec Colorways In Verse, a newsletter and community space centering queer BIPOC speculative poetry, with Lysz Flo and taught “The Language of (Dis)ability and Chronic Illness in Speculative Fiction” for the Carl Brandon Society. They’re grateful to be in community with the Carbon Collective as well as Fellowship of the Griots, and a member of Codex. jeanedridges.carrd.co | @jdridges (bsky).
people.name: Jeané D. Ridges

people.bio: I'm retired from the day job and write both pro original fiction and fanfiction. I live in south central Oregon a short drive from the California border. Pro credits include a few short stories, I have eight novels indie published on Amazon, and an account on fanfiction.net.
people.name: Jean Lamb

people.bio: Jean Martin is a five-time Hugo Awards nominee as a contributing editor for the fanzine Journey Planet and was an editor for the fanzine Science Fiction/San Francisco. Jean has won awards as part of masquerade teams at international and local conventions and won a FAAn Achievement Award for Best New Fan from Corflu. She is an experienced moderator/panelist at pop culture, sci-fi and fantasy conventions. Jean is an organizer for the Bay Area English Regency Society and a volunteer for the Period Events and Entertainments Re-creation Society. She was a board member/communications coordinator for the Greater Bay Area Costumers Guild.
people.name: Jean Martin

people.bio: I've been reading and watching science fiction (and some fantasy) for many years. I attend conventions, participate on panels, and coordinate a small apa (Amateur Press Association). I am a selective extrovert, which means sometimes I feel introverted and other times I'm more extroverted. I can interact with both groups. I'm a fan of Mad Libs.
people.name: Jeanne Mealy

people.bio: Jean-Paul L. Garnier is the owner of Space Cowboy Books bookstore and publishing house, producer of Simultaneous Times Podcast (2023/25 Laureate Award Winner, 2024 BSFA, Ignyte, and British Fantasy Award Finalist), and was the editor of the SFPA's Star*Line magazine from 2021-2025.
