He is also Editor-in-Chief of Electronic Brain magazine. In 2024 he won the Laureate Award for Best Editor. He has written many books of poetry and science fiction. https://spacecowboybooks.com/
people.name: Jean-Paul L. Garnier

people.bio: Jed Hartman (he/him) is a writer and editor. He’s editor-in-chief of Constellation Press, and a member of the Motherboard for the Otherwise Awards. He was the coordinator for the Hugo Awards Voter Packet in 2025 and 2026, and he was a _Strange Horizons_ fiction editor from 2000 through 2012. His extracurricular interests include logodaedaly, interdigitation, sesquipedalia, ludophilia, and lapsus linguae. His fiction and nonfiction have appeared in _All-Star Zeppelin Adventure Stories_, _Clean Sheets_, _Fishnet_, _Flytrap_, _Queers Dig Time Lords_, _Strange Horizons_, and _Wet_.
people.name: Jed Hartman

people.bio: Jeffrey Sun is a lifelong SF fan and editor of The Daily Tomorrow, a daily SF serial magazine.
people.name: Jeffrey Sun

people.bio:
Jeff Sturgeon is a northwest artist known for his beautiful, award-winning metal paintings. His career spans over thirty years, coming up through the ranks as a young fan artist in the 80s to being hired in the first wave of computer game artists in the late 80s and early 90s. A long career in the 90s as an artist, animator, concept artist, lead artist, game designer, and art director followed most notably for Electronic Arts. He continued to paint and display his work at science fiction conventions around the country and created new cover and interior work for clients such as Harper Collins Publishing and NASA JPL.
Jeff left the game business behind and went to painting full time with aluminum as his new canvas though he did not give up traditional canvas completely. Through the new millennium, Jeff's work became nationally known with increased appearances as a exhibitor, guest, panelist, and Guest of Honor at conventions around the country. Jeff's world-sharing anthology Jeff Sturgeon's Last Cities of Earth was released in Jan. 2022 by Word Fire Press. His continued work in the Last Cities of Earth; universe and book and magazine cover assignments now take up most of his time as he creates new art and stories and works towards releasing a second LAST CITIES OF EARTH anthology. A tabletop/board game is in the design stages.
people.name: Jeff Sturgeon

people.bio: Jen Cheng (she/ella/kir) is the fifth West Hollywood City Poet Laureate (2023-2026) and author of Braided Spaces. A Poet Laureate Fellow with the Academy of American Poets and a California Arts Council Fellow, she is a multidisciplinary artist who blends East-West influences as Feng Shui Poetry. She was named one of the Top 50 LGBTQ+ Impact Leaders by LA Magazine (2025). Jen’s writing is published in Passengers Journal, Colossus:Current, Altadena Poetry Review, and elsewhere. As a teaching artist, she has taught at UCLA Extension and other national organizations. Online at JenCvoice.com or on social media @JenCvoice.
people.name: Jen Cheng

people.bio: Jennifer Brozek is an award winning author, editor, and tie-in writer. A Secret Guide to Fighting Elder Gods, Never Let Me Sleep, and The Last Days of Salton Academy were finalists for the Bram Stoker Award. She was awarded the Scribe Award for best tie-in Young Adult novel for BattleTech: The Nellus Academy Incident and for Shadowrun: Auditions. Grants Pass won an Australian Shadows Award for best edited publication. A two-time Hugo finalist for Best Editor, Short Form and a finalist for the British Fantasy Award, Jennifer is an active member of SFWA, HWA, and IAMTW. She keeps a tight writing and editing schedule and credits her husband Jeff with being the best sounding board ever. Visit Jennifer's worlds at jenniferbrozek.com
people.name: Jennifer Brozek

people.bio: Jennifer Hudak is a Nebula Award-winner and Hugo Award-finalist whose work can be found in The Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy, Strange Horizons, Lightspeed, The Sunday Morning Transport, and Lady Churchill's Rosebud Wristlet. Originally from Boston, she now lives with her family in Upstate New York where she teaches yoga, knits pocket-sized animals, and misses the ocean.
people.name: Jennifer Hudak

people.bio: Jennifer Mandula lives in Cleveland, OH with her husband, three daughters, and a neurotic corgi. She first learned of the historical Mary Anning while studying for her master's in education at the University of Oxford. In her spare time she visits local bakeries and plans her next escape to the beach. The Geomagician is her debut novel.
people.name: Jennifer Mandula

people.bio: Jennifer Mosier (MFA; USC, SAG-AFTRA) is Board President for Synecdoche Works, an arts nonprofit focused on new play development. Most recently a co-founder of Old Bat Films, she is a Magician Member of the Magic Castle in Hollywood. She has served on the faculties at UC Santa Barbara, Cal State San Bernardino, and Northern Arizona University, and was published in The Journal of American Culture with “Hold Your Horses! The Elephants are Coming!” prior to her departure from academia.
people.name: Jennifer Mosier

people.bio: Jennifer Skwarski has been coming up with costumes for SF conventions since the mid-eighties starting with the second con she ever attended. She is intrigued by different approaches and techniques to making things and how to combine those with science fiction and fantasy costuming. She strives for excellence in her sewing and construction, always wanting to improve her skills and expand her knowledge of making things. She did not start competing in costume contests until 2012 but is glad she finally jumped into that pool. It has greatly improved her confidence and her ability to stand in front of people as the focus of their attention and not freak out. She now competes and wins awards at Master level.
people.name: Jennifer Skwarski

people.bio:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen is an award-winning author and creative producer specializing in stories with emotional and philosophical depth. She is the Lead Writer and Voice & Localization Producer for the breakout hit Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and an independent creative consultant for gaming and entertainment studios. She has been warmly praised by partners around the world for her expertise and thoughtful collaboration style.

She loves puzzles and snacks (traits she shares with her dog Trunks) and often composes stories in her sleep. She is usually deeply immersed in a book or tv show, and/or hunting platinum trophies for her favorite games.
people.name: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen

people.bio: Jeremy Clift is a science fiction author and former international journalist whose career covered wars, economic crises, and environmental change across multiple continents. He writes the Sci-Fi Galaxy series, including Born in Space: Unlocking Destiny, the award-winning Space Vault: The Seed Eclipse, and the forthcoming Space Shield. His work blends hard science with deeply human stories, exploring themes of genetic engineering, corporate power, and motherhood in humanity’s expansion beyond Earth. Clift draws on real-world experience to imagine near-future worlds where technology reshapes identity, and where survival depends on who controls the future.
people.name: Jeremy Clift

people.bio: Jeremy Szal was raised by wild dingoes, which should explain a lot. He writes epic fantasy and dark space opera of a character-driven, morally grey nature. He sold The Common trilogy to Gollancz/Orion when he was 23, which includes STORMBLOOD, BLINDSPACE, and WOLFSKIN, about a drug harvested from alien DNA that makes users permanently addicted to adrenaline and aggression. He’s the author of over fifty short stories, translated into seventeen languages, many of which appear in his short fiction collection BROKEN STARS. He was the editor for the Hugo-winning StarShipSofa until 2020 and has a BA in Film Studies and Creative Writing from UNSW. He carves out a living in Sydney, Australia with his family, where he loves watching weird movies, eating Japanese food, exploring cities, learning languages, cold weather and dark humour. Find him at https://jeremyszal.substack.com/ or @JeremySzal
people.name: Jeremy Szal

people.bio: Jesper is a professor of economics at Luleå University of Technology in Sweden. He usually works on whatever interests him at the moment and/or whatever has the most urgent deadline; this often entails research on environmental economics, natural resource economics, energy economics, development economics, or several of these at once. He has attended more than a dozen Worldcons and no longer has any idea how many conventions he has attended in total.
people.name: Jesper Stage

people.bio: Jessica Leman is an Indonesian children’s fiction comic writer and storyboard illustrator. She made her debut on the Ciayo Comics platform, and her work, the Magical Sweet Gula Trilogy, was later published internationally by Singaporean publisher Difference Engine. The first volume launched at the Ubud Writers & Readers Festival 2023. In addition to her work as a writer, she is also active as a Visual Communication Design lecturer at a university in Jakarta, where she shares her knowledge and experience in comics and storytelling with the next generation of creators.
people.name: Jessica Leman

people.bio: Jessica Maison is a Nebula Award winning comic creator, author, and screenwriter. Plastic Girl is her coming to age eco-punk novel trilogy set in a climate apocalypse. Her comic series, Mary Shelley's School for Monsters, is an IBPA Benjamin Franklin Gold Award winner and Foreword INDIES finalist. She co-wrote the upcoming gothic space horror comic series, Host Planet, and co-directed the time travel feature film, Own Worst Enemy. Her short fiction and comics appear in publications such as Terraform, Nightmare Theater, Systemic and Distorted Horror. She is the founder of Wicked Tree Press and the co-host of the Monster V. Monster podcast.
people.name: Jessica Maison

people.bio: Jessie Peterson has a Ph.D. in linguistics from the University of Colorado at Boulder and was a professor of linguistics for 13 years. She is now a full-time professional conlanger and works with her husband, David Peterson. Her work appears in a number of TV shows and films, including Warner Brothers’ Superman, Pixar’s Elemental, Legendary’s Dune: Part Two, Netflix’s Shadow and Bone. Jessie and David co-host the weekly live stream LangTime Studio on YouTube, and she is the author of the book How to Create a Language: The Conlang Guide (Cambridge University Press).
people.name: Jessie Peterson

people.bio:
Jim Hillin has been working as a Visual Effects Artist in motion pictures since 1987, and in that same year starting writing screenplays with his writing partner, Steve. Originally from Texas, Jim came to Los Angeles as a studio musician in the late 1970s and later segued into motion picture production. He became a member of the Animation Guild in 1987 and The Academy of Motion Pictures Arts and Sciences in 2002.

Learning from his mentor and writing partner, Syd Field, he completed 17 screenplays in the 80s and 90s. He started writing novels in 2021, and is now doing that fulltime. His debut novel “Soimnicreolisit” is being released this Summer from Spines Publishing.
people.name: Jim Hillin

people.bio:
James Joseph (J.J.) Styles first SF Con was 51 years ago when he attended Aussiecon 1 in Melbourne, Australia.
J. J. Styles has since attended many local, university, and regional conventions and about a dozen Worldcons held outside North America plus two in the USA.
J. J. has been a volunteer and panelist. Interests include cosplay, fantasy, fandom, gambling, gaming, history, horror, politics, SF, and travel.
J.J. was a member of Australian APAs and Editor and Publisher of Crux fanzine.
Badged as James Bond 007 (retired), J. J. was briefly a fashion model before working "On Her Majesty's Secret Service."
J. J. also worked as a Locomotive Driver for over forty years and is the inaugural National Vice President (Rail) of the Australian Rail, Tram and Bus Industry Union.
people.name: J. J. Styles

people.bio: J.J. Unthank is a fantasy author and former videogame programmer whose fantasy, murder mystery novel “Any More Questions For The Corpse?” comes out in the U.S. in August 2026.
people.name: J.J. Unthank

people.bio: Jim is a full-time SF&F writer, scientist (Ph.D. Electrical Engineering, specialty laser physics), and former running-dog-lackey for the bourgeois capitalist establishment. With 20 published books, he writes hard science fiction, epic fantasy and urban fantasy, frequently with strong, coming-of-age themes. His first success came through self-publishing, which led to contracts with traditional publishers like Open Road Media and Harper Collins Voyager. Jim has an abiding interest in all things scientific, like orbital mechanics, space travel, laser weapons, and other geekie stuff. He lives in Tucson, AZ with his wife Karen, and two extra-terrestrial aliens who claim to be a cats.
people.name: J. L. Doty

people.bio: Through her Physics teaching, Joanna strives to expand experiential, project-based, and inquiry-focused courses at her college. She worked with NASA as a graduate student and was a professional on Shuttle’s Return to Flight. As an educator, she leads student projects in High Altitude ballooning and sound rocket payload design. She is currently working with Louisiana Space Grant on small satellite development.
people.name: Joanna Rivers

people.bio: Joan Slonczewski wrote A Door into Ocean, the award-winning classic about ocean-dwelling Sharers who use biology and nonviolence to repel an interstellar invasion. Joan’s microbiology research discovers bizarre microbes in Antarctica, and shows how our gut bacteria rule our brains. Their fan favorite Brain Plague is sci-fi biology with romance: A starving artist on a gem-studded world accepts an agent's assignment to host a million microbial minds in her head. Joan's true-biology show "Dinosaurs on Weed Get Bird Flu" was a sensation at ICFA. Their lecture on "AI Personhood--Now?" was a hit at UC-Davis Center for AI and Experimental Futures, and at SF Frontier Tower. See: https://magazine.mindplex.ai/post/ai-personhood-now-minds-in-transit-with-joan-slonczewski
people.name: Joan Slonczewski

people.bio: Joe Haldeman has won five Hugos and five Nebulas and is an SFWA Grandmaster of science fiction. His best-known book is THE FOREVER WAR. His latest novel is WORK DONE FOR HIRE. He’s won the Rhysling Award for his poetry. Joe was a combat soldier in Vietnam, which strongly influences his work. He’s retired from M.I.T, where he taught every fall semester for 30 years. When Joe’s not writing or teaching, he paints, bicycles, plays the guitar, and is an amateur astronomer. He’s been married to Mary Gay Potter Haldeman for 61 years.
people.name: Joe Haldeman

people.bio: VP, Associate Publisher and Editorial Director, and founder of Saga Press at Simon and Schuster. I’m also a Hugo and World Fantasy award finalist.
people.name: Joe Monti

people.bio: Editor of Think Weirder: The Year's Best Science Fiction Ideas. Former publisher of Compelling Science Fiction magazine. Joe lives in Colorado with his wife and two children, where he talks a lot about computer processors and climbs rocks.
people.name: Joe Stech

people.bio: Dr. Joseph Westlake is the Director of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate’s Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters where he leads a world-class team in understanding Earth’s most important and life-sustaining star. Dr. Westlake oversees NASA’s work to study key space phenomena and improve situational awareness of the very space our astronauts, satellites, and robotic missions travel through as they explore the solar system and beyond. His portfolio also included NASA’s robust space weather research to help the U.S. Government better predict space weather, which can interfere with radio communications, affect GPS accuracy, and even–when extreme–affect electrical grids on the ground.
people.name: Joe Westlake

people.bio: Joey is a bilingual writer and aspiring director whose stories/screenplays span genres and mediums, drawing inspiration from a life across Vancouver, Taipei, Shanghai, and New York City. A passionate sci-fi & fantasy worldbuilder, he's published 2 novellas and 5 novels in Mandarin, and written English-language tie-in fiction for Riot Games’ League of Legends. His English-language sci-fi screenplay won Best Short Screenplay at the 2024 Austin Film Festival. He was also the inaugural recipient of George R. R. Martin’s Terran Award.
people.name: Joey Yu

people.bio:
Professional comic artist and also a lecturer in design and art major at several universities in Jakarta, mainly as a faculty member in Bina
Nusantara University (BINUS). Currently pursuing a doctoral degree in the arts with a creative research focus on comic creation,
exploring the theme of mixed identity in Indonesia, particularly between Korean and Indonesian heritage. He is the co-author of Magical Sweet Gula Trilogy which first volume was launched internationally at The Ubud Writers & Reader Festival 2023.
people.name: Johanes park

people.bio: John Chu is a microprocessor architect by day, a writer by night. His fiction has appeared in venues including Boston Review, Uncanny, Asimov's Science Fiction, Clarkesworld, and Reactor. His translations have been published at venues including Clarkesworld, The Big Book of SF. He has won the Hugo, Nebula, Locus, and Ignyte Awards, including the Best Short Story Hugo for "The Water That Falls on You from Nowhere" and the Best Novelette Nebula for "If You Find Yourself Speaking to God, Address God with the Informal You." The Subtle Art of Folding Space, his debut novel, was published by Tor in 2026.
people.name: John Chu

people.bio: John is a scientist by day, working on the interaction between the solar wind and Earth’s magnetic field, and won the Royal Astronomical Society’s Fowler Award for his work in his field. By night, he is the co-host of the Hugo Award-winning Octothorpe podcast. He is a keen tabletop gamer and GMs regularly; in all the other parts of the day, he alternates between feeling guilty he’s not keeping up with his TV shows/playing enough games/reducing his to-read pile.
people.name: John Coxon

people.bio: John Foyt (aka John Taloni) is a short story writer and occasional novelist. His serious fiction includes the short "Career Zombie" which was selected by Ellen Datlow for her Long List of Horror, and the novel "Compleat Martian Invasion," a Steampunk take on classic SF storylines from Wells, Verne and Burroughs. More humorous works always seem to include cats, as in his "Cat of Thunder" for a Mjolnir-wielding kitty, and several fanciful "Dr. Mew" novelettes.
people.name: John Foyt

people.bio: John G. McDaid is a science fiction writer and folk/filk singer-songwriter from Rhode Island. A Clarion workshop grad, he won the Theodore Sturgeon award in 1995. His hypermedia novel, "Uncle Buddy’s Phantom Funhouse," was included in an NEH digital conservation project. A four-time finalist for the writer/composer Pegasus, his debut studio album, Trail of Mars, won the 2021 John Culkin Award. He teaches media theory and reviews local theater for BroadwayWorld. http://johnmcdaid.bandcamp.com.
people.name: John McDaid

people.bio: Co- Host of YouTube channel Talking Story as well as a Co-Autor of the Strange Eons series.
people.name: John Minton

people.bio: John Picacio is the Hugo Award-winning co-author and illustrator of the USA Today-bestselling picture book THE INVISIBLE PARADE, created with #1 New York Times-bestselling author Leigh Bardugo. His award-winning cover art has illustrated 30 years worth of major science fiction, fantasy and horror books including works for George R. R. Martin's A SONG OF ICE AND FIRE series, as well as the STAR TREK and X-MEN franchises, plus classic novels by Rebecca Roanhorse, Michael Moorcock, James Tiptree, Jr., Frederik Pohl, Sheri S. Tepper, C. Robert Cargill, and many, many more. His artistic accolades include three Hugo Awards, nine Chesley Awards, six Locus Awards, and the World Fantasy Award.
people.name: John Picacio

people.bio: John Scalzi has an asteroid named after him. He's ridiculously proud of that.
people.name: John Scalzi

people.bio: Heinlein and Comics Fan. Active in the Heinlein Society and current Treasurer.
people.name: John Tilden

people.bio:
John W has been attending SF CONs since 1993 and leading Braiding and Balloon panels since 1995. He is a retired computer professional, and was an organizer for E.L.V.I.S. (The Emergency Link to Vital Internet Services) [1994-1999]
John can also speak on Audio-books, Beer, Chocolate, Photography …and especially Scotch Whisky.
Rumpus Room Co-Head at MiniCON 3 years
people.name: John Wardale

people.bio: Jo Miles writes optimistic science fiction and fantasy, including the Infinite Pantry cozy fantasy series, novella The Final Chronicle of Yeneh, and the Gifted of Brennex space opera trilogy. Their short stories have appeared in Fantasy & Science Fiction, Lightspeed, Uncanny, and more. Explore all their work and sign up for updates at www.jomiles.com.
people.name: Jo Miles

people.bio: Jonathan is a retired Marine colonel and a full-time hybrid writer living in Colorado Springs with his wife Kiwi and twin seven-year-old daughters Dani and Dari. He has over 140 published titles with 88 being novels. He is a USA Today Bestseller, a three-time Nebula Award finalist, and a two-time Dragon Award finalist. He is currently serving as the SFWA CFO.
people.name: Jonathan Brazee

people.bio: I am an incoming assistant professor in the Physics and Astronomy Department at California State University, San Bernardino (CSUSB), with a PhD in physics. My research focuses on quantum optics, quantum sensing, and quantum computing, exploring how quantum systems can be controlled and applied to advance technology and deepen our understanding of fundamental physics.
people.name: Jonathan Daniel

people.bio: Jon Pessin absolutely not a collection of weasels and ferrets in a trenchcoat, but a fully human person who has been human for more than 40 years now. Rather than chasing stoats, shrews, and other rodentia for food, he enjoys playing tabletop RPGs, making music, and eating human foods like pizza. His favorite part about congoing is probably costuming, such as the human costume he's certainly not wearing right now. When not attending conventions, he spends his time in northern Illinois scurrying through meado... I mean, sitting in offices and answering phone calls. He's also a children's entertainer (seriously this time), and works as a balloon twister, party entertainer, and Santa Claus. But not as a collection of weasels.
people.name: Jon "HobbitGuy" Pessin

people.bio: Jordan is a professional space geek. As an engineer at NASA JPL, he's worked on the Europa Clipper mission to Jupiter, spacecraft to study Earth, and more. He's had the great fortune to hold things in his hands that are now on other planets, but his favorite part of his job is sharing his love of space with others. While primarily a Trekkie, he also loves Star Wars, The Orville, Doctor Who, and more. His favorite authors include Ted Chiang, Becky Chambers, James S. A. Corey, Andy Weir, and Isaac Asimov. He also enjoys travel, the outdoors, and board games.
people.name: Jordan Ticktin

people.bio: Lifelong reader, BookTuber (@FineReads), host of the BookTube Creator Guild, owner of the new Reader-First Marketing newsletter, and Marketing nerd for nearly 15 years.
people.name: Josefine Fouarge

people.bio: Josh Sutphin writes politically and culturally engaged occult horror with an undercurrent of hope. He is also co-founder and principal designer for Shiraki Press and a veteran video game developer.
people.name: Josh Sutphin

people.bio: Joshua Bilmes established JABberwocky Literary Agency in 1994 and is one of the leading agents in sf/fantasy from #1 bestselling authors like Brandon Sanderson and Charlaine Harris to 2026 debut authors like Patrick Fitzgerald.
people.name: Joshua Bilmes

people.bio: Joshua Kronengold is a long-time fan, gamer, and filker. He wrote zines roleplaying games for decades in Alarums & Excursions, and now writes zines on the same topic in Ever & Anon
people.name: Joshua Kronengold

people.bio: Josh Wilson is an editor, journalist and writer in San Francisco, and publisher of The Fabulist Magazine, a home to fantastical fiction and art in print and digital editions. Stories published in The Fabulist have been finalists for the Pushcart Prize and the Shirley Jackson Awards. He is a recipient of the Society for Professional Journalists Sigma Delta Chi Award, and founder of the 501(c)3 organization Independent Arts & Media. https://fabulistmagazine.com/
people.name: Josh Wilson

people.bio: Joy is a professional artist, working mostly in blown and carved glass. Creating smaller sculptures like her Solar System Christmas Ornaments, to giant lobby sculptures, her work is collected worldwide. Joy had the honor of creating the Hugo Award Base for 2025 and 2014. She is also a master level, award winning costume designer. In her copious free time, she runs a little kitty rescue sanctuary in upstate New York.
people.name: Joy Alyssa Day

people.bio: Joyce Chng lives in Singapore. Their speculative fiction has appeared in The Apex Book of World SF II, We See A Different Frontier, Cranky Ladies of History, and Accessing The Future. Joyce also co-edited THE SEA IS OURS: Tales of Steampunk Southeast Asia with Jaymee Goh. Their novels span across wolf clans (Starfang: Rise of the Clan), vineyards (Water into Wine) and swordmaking forges (Fire Heart and Cold Steel) respectively. Joyce wrangles article and fiction editing at Strange Horizons. You can find them at http://awolfstale.wordpress.com and @jolantru.bsky.social on Bluesky. (Pronouns: she/her, they/their)
people.name: Joyce Chng

people.bio:
I have been going to conventions for 45 years (over 50 if you count my first convention which was Star Trek).
I am a long time volunteer - multiple departments
I love Costuming and Crafts
I am the widow of long time fan
I am the Mom of 3 fans
people.name: Joyce Grace

people.bio:
Joyce Lloyd is the chair of LAcon V the 2026 Worldcon.
She has been involved with Worldcons since 2006 (LA Con IV) where she was the Con Suite Second. Since then, she has worked as Hugo Administrator (Nippon 2007), Hotel Assistant (Denvention 3), Treasurer (Chicon 7), Facilities Division Head (LoneStarCon3 & Chicon 8), Finance Division Head (MidAmeriCon II), Timeline Assistant and Convention Center Liaison (Worldcon 76 in San Jose & Glasgow 2024), Facilities Deputy Division Head (Dublin 2019) and Exhibits Deputy Division Head (DisCon III).
In her spare time, she is regularly involved with local fan conventions with attendance from 100 to 30,000.
people.name: Joyce Lloyd

people.bio: J.R. Dawson (she/they) is a Nebula and Hugo finalist and the Golden Crown award-winning author of The First Bright Thing. They have had shorter works in places such as F&SF, Reactor, Lightspeed, and Uncanny. Dawson currently lives on Dakota land in Minnesota with her loving wife. She teaches at Drexel University’s MFA program for creative writing, and fills her free time with keeping her chaotic dogs out of trouble. Her latest book, The Lighthouse at the Edge of the World, is a sapphic Orpheus retelling and won the Society of Midland Authors award.
people.name: J.R. Dawson

people.bio:
Associate Professor J. Richard Stevens teaches graduate and undergraduate courses in new media theory, popular culture, and digital media skills at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Dr. Stevens’ research delves into the intersection of ideological formation and media message dissemination, with studies such as how cultural messages are formed and passed through popular culture, how technology infrastructure affects the context of media messages, communication technology policy and law, and how media and technology platforms are changing American public discourse.
people.name: J. Richard Stevens

people.bio: Scott lives with his husband Mark in a little Italian villa in Folsom, CA just outside of Sacramento. He was indoctrinated into fantasy and sci fi by his mother as a child and devoured her library, but as he grew up, he wondered where all the people like him were. He decided that if there weren’t queer characters in his favorite genres, he would write them himself. A Rainbow Award winning author, he runs Queer Sci Fi, QueeRomance Ink, Liminal Fiction and Other Worlds Ink with Mark, sites that celebrate fiction reflecting queer reality, and was the SFWA Indie Authors Committee chair for almost three years. He now runs the Sacramento Book Festival. He runs the Sacramento Book Festival and ran Nebula Con 2026.
people.name: J. Scott Coatsworth

people.bio: Dr. J.S. Fields is a professor and wood mycologist who has spent too much time around organic solvents. An avid woodturner and sculptor, they are best known for their work with "fungus puke" for artistic and scientific purposes - from natural dyes to solar cells and batteries. What they cannot do (yet) with science they explore in science fiction and fantasy - exploring the possibility of wooden spaceships and extraterrestrial fungus friends.
people.name: J.S. Fields

people.bio: Susan Ruff, part of the writing duo of Susan and John Ruff, is the co-author of epic fantasy/sword and sorcery novels, including the Doorway to Magic Trilogy. Recently, Susan became enchanted (so to speak) with cozy fantasy, and the duo began writing cozy fantasy under the pen name J.S. Ruff. Their latest fantasy novel Desserts for the Deserter was released in September 2025.
people.name: JS Ruff

people.bio: Just an ordinary guy from Florida who has been an active fan since for a long time. I read and review100 pieces of short fiction and create a Best of the Year list of SFFH novels for my SF Club. I write reviews and other articles for fanzines. I love SF in all its forms and I enjoy celebrating that.
people.name: Juan Sanmiguel

people.bio: Writer, editor, Clarion West, SFWA, she writes character-driven stories.
people.name: Jude-Marie Green

people.bio:
Entwife Judy has been my badge name for several decades. Now I'm getting serious—about both my WIP novel and also the startup organization that will promote Research and Development related to the worldbuilding scheme in it. Turns out that shirtsleeves-livable habitats, inside hollowed-out asteroids and using tether-spin-gravity, might be be feasible in mere decades. Somebody has to MAKE IT SO. We are creating the L4 Space Habitat Society therefore.
Otherwise, I work part-time and travel in my RV with my dog. Entwife Judy has been my badge name for several decades.
people.name: Judy Johnson (Entwife)

people.bio: Julia Bianco is the USA Today bestselling author of WITCH SEASON, out now from St. Martin's Press. She also works as a television writer and lives in Los Angeles with her fiancé and their cats, S’more and Rigatoni. She enjoys baking, reality television, and playing with her cats’ ears.
people.name: Julia Bianco

people.bio: Julia Vee was that GenX kid raised by libraries and still remains largely unsupervised. She writes with her friend from middle school, Ken Bebelle, and they have penned over 10 novels together. Their novel Ebony Gate, an Asian-inspired contemporary fantasy, was published by TOR and named a 2023 Golden Poppy Finalist for the Octavia E. Butler award. The series conclusion, Pearl City, released in 2025.
people.name: Julia Vee

people.bio: Julie Leong is the USA Today and Sunday Times bestselling author of The Teller of Small Fortunes and The Keeper of Magical Things. Her debut novel, The Teller of Small Fortunes, was a Book of the Month pick, an Amazon Editor’s Pick, and was named one of 2024’s Best Sci-fi, Fantasy, & Horror novels by BookPage. A daughter of Malaysian Chinese immigrants and a Yale graduate, she works on self-driving cars and other tech once considered science fiction by day, and writes warm, magical fiction by night. She currently lives in San Francisco with her husband and dog, and is unreasonably fond of spreadsheets and flambéeing things.
people.name: Julie Leong

people.bio: Julie Lew (she/they) loves all things fantasy and horror, the darker and queerer the better. They are the author of the adult gothic horror novel THE WIVES OF HERRICK HALL and the upcoming YA fantasy mystery DEATH IN VERSE. She lives in the Pacific Northwest with her partner, and when she’s not writing books about the magical and the monstrous, she’s likely playing endless games of fetch with her chihuahua-terrier mix pup, Kody.
people.name: Julie Lew

people.bio: Julie Nováková is a scientist active in astrobiology, educator and award-winning Czech author, editor and translator of science fiction, fantasy and detective stories. She published ten novels, one anthology, one story collection and over thirty short pieces in Czech. Her work in English appeared in Clarkesworld, Asimov’s, Analog, and elsewhere. Her works have been translated into multiple languages, and she translates Czech stories into English (in Tor.com, Strange Horizons, F&SF, Clarkesworld, and Welkin Magazine). She edited or co-edited an anthology of Czech speculative fiction in translation, Dreams From Beyond, a book of European SF in Filipino translation, Haka, an outreach ebook of astrobiological SF, Strangest of All, and its more ambitious follow-up print and ebook anthology Life Beyond Us (Laksa Media, upcoming in late 2022). Julie’s newest book is a story collection titled The Ship Whisperer (Arbiter Press, 2020). She is a recipient of the European fandom’s Encouragement Award and multiple Czech genre awards. She’s active in science outreach, education and nonfiction writing, and co-leads the outreach group of the European Astrobiology Institute. She’s a member of the XPRIZE Sci-fi Advisory Council.
people.name: Julie Novakova

people.bio:
Julie Soskins is a passionate bibliophile and a proud member of Generation X, whose love for literature and geek culture has shaped her life in myriad ways. With over a decade of experience attending conventions, Julie has become a familiar face at Worldcons and SF Bay Area conventions, constantly seeking out new book recommendations and inspirations from fellow enthusiasts.

A dedicated intersectional feminist, Julie actively champions equality and empowerment, using her platform to engage in meaningful conversations and promote awareness on important social issues. Her commitment to fostering inclusivity and diversity is echoed in her work running various book clubs, where she brings together readers of all backgrounds to share perspectives, explore new genres, and celebrate the written word.
people.name: Julie Soskins

people.bio: Juliet Brooks lives with her spouse, a lot of plants, her cat Moo, and a rotating cast of foster cats.
people.name: Juliet Brooks

people.bio: Juliette is an acclaimed writer of sociological science fiction, author of The Broken Trust series from DAW. Her work explores linguistic and cultural difference, reflecting her fascination with complex social systems. Her short fiction has appeared in Clarkesworld, Analog, and Rich Horton's 2019 Year's Best Science Fiction anthology. She is a linguist, anthropologist, and discourse analyst with a Ph.D. in Education specializing in Language, Literacy, and Culture. She lives in Melbourne, Australia with her family.
people.name: Juliette Wade

people.bio:
Julie Zetterberg has been making and wearing
costumes since 1975. She has appeared as
everything from Princess Leia
to Rocket Racoon; from Olive Oyl to Queen
Anne's Lace. She was costume guest of honor at
Marcon 39 and Rustycon 33, and co-chair of
Costume-Con 14. She is a past president of the
Beyond Reality Costumers' Guild. She lives in
Seattle with her husband, fellow costumer
Greg Sardo, and their two cats.
people.name: Julie Zetterberg

people.bio: Justin C. Key is a practicing psychiatrist and a speculative fiction writer. A graduate of Clarion West 2015, he is the author of the story collection The World Wasn’t Ready for You, and his stories have appeared in the Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Strange Horizons, Escape Pod, Lightspeed, and on Tor.com. His debut sci-fi novel, The Hospital at the End of the World, is out now from HarperCollins.
people.name: Justin C. Key

people.bio: I am a USA Today bestselling Epic Fantasy writer published by Tor in the US and Orbit in the UK
people.name: J.V.Jones

people.bio:
K. A. Bledsoe’s writing journey began at the age of six with a short story about kids growing up on a space station. Writing has been a constant despite other jobs like scooping ice cream, shoe salesman, pharmacy tech, band director, and more.

Born, raised and still residing in Arizona, the author continues to pen stories in all genres despite the distraction of house cats underfoot and the occasional bobcat or roadrunner strolling through the backyard.
people.name: K. A. Bledsoe

people.bio: Kaden Love is the author of the Paladins of the Harvest series (Elegy of a Fragmented Vineyard, 2 successful kickstarters) and Toothsucker (cyberpunk vampire series with 3 novels and more to come). He is a book influencer on instagram with over 39,000 followers and over 6,000 on TikTok. Outside of writing, he is a competitive marathon runner and avid reader with his wife, who illustrates book covers for a living.
people.name: Kaden Love

people.bio: Kaitlin is a queer, neurodivergent author and editor from the Pacific Northwest. Her short fiction has appeared in Adventitious and Wyngraf and placed in NYC Midnight twice. She is also the author of The Cartomancer's Curse, a sapphic romantasy novella. When she's not writing or falling in love with the latest book she's editing, she's swing dancing the night away. You can find her online at kaitlin-schmidt.com and @kaitlin.schmidt4.
people.name: Kaitlin Schmidt

people.bio: Kalyn Josephson is a NYT Bestselling author, sometimes-baker, and full-time consumer of too much tea. She lives on the California coast with two tiny black cats in a house in constant need of repair. She is the author of the Ravenfall series, The Storm Crow duology, the This Dark Descent duology, and The Library of Amorlin.
people.name: Kalyn Josephson

people.bio: Kamilah Cole is a USA Today & national indie bestselling Jamaican-American author, who has been nominated for a Dragon Award, a Lambda Award, a Lodestar Award, and an Astounding Award. She worked as a writer and entertainment editor at Bustle for four years, and her nonfiction has appeared in Marie Claire and Seventeen. A graduate of New York University, Kamilah lives in the Pacific Northwest, where she’s usually playing Kingdom Hearts for the hundredth time, quoting early SpongeBob SquarePants episodes, or crying her way through Zuko’s redemption arc in Avatar: The Last Airbender.
people.name: Kamilah Cole

people.bio: Kara Lenore is a science fiction author and alumna of the Viable Paradise workshop. Her debut novel, Beneath a Sun Deprived Sky, was a Publishers Weekly BookLife Editor’s Pick, and her manuscript Thia’s Key was a finalist in the Writers’ League of Texas 2025 Manuscript Contest. Kara spent part of her youth living in Japan and earned a doctorate in Japanese studies, experiences which influence her work.
people.name: Kara Lenore

people.bio: Kareem Badaruddin is the Mission Manager of the Voyager Interstellar Mission. He has been at JPL since 1994 and has served in line management as well as roles on Cassini, Dawn, SMAP, and various proposals and costing exercises. Kareem has an extensive background in flight system testbeds and in-flight anomaly investigation and resolution. He has demonstrated strong technical leadership in addressing serious anomalies that could have resulted in the loss of a spacecraft. He has been fortunate to rely on the exceptional skill and creativity of the Voyager flight team as well as the expert JPL anomaly teams.
people.name: Kareem Badaruddin

people.bio: Karen Willson is an accomplished entertainment writer and producer whose career spans animation, educational media, special effects, and live productions for audiences of all ages. She contributed nonfiction articles to Starlog Magazine and co-authored the “Talking About” advice series for girls. During the 1980s Animation Renaissance, she and her husband and writing partner, Chris Weber, scripted more than fifty children’s television episodes and created Dink, the Little Dinosaur for Ruby-Spears, which aired on CBS. Karen also wrote for Disney Comic Adventures and edited the long-running He-Man and the Masters of the Universe comic strip, later collected by Dark Horse.
people.name: Karen Willson

people.bio: Senior Curator of Literary Collections, The Huntington Library
people.name: Karla Nielsen

people.bio: Kat Bradbury is a best-selling author and game writer from Tucson, Arizona, as well as an award-winning marketer at World Anvil. She has seven published novels, as well as short fiction in Daily Science Fiction and various anthologies. Kat’s current ADHD hyperfixations include tabletop RPGs, classic movie monsters, 80s New Wave, and convincing people the ending of LOST was good, actually.
people.name: Kat Bradbury

people.bio: Kate Elliott has been publishing science fiction and fantasy novels and stories for over 30 years with a particular focus in immersive world building and epic stories of adventure and transformative cultural change. Her work has been nominated for the Nebula, World Fantasy, Norton, and Locus Awards. She lives in Hawaii where she writes, paddles outrigger canoes, and spoils her schnauzer.
people.name: Kate Elliott

people.bio: Kate Maruyama is the author of The Collective (Writ Large Press), Bleak Houses (Raw Dog Screaming Press), and Harrowgate (47North) and her novella Family Solstice was named Best Fiction Book of 2021 by Rue Morgue Magazine. Her short fiction has appeared in numerous anthologies and journals including Analog (twice) and Asimov's. She sits on the Board of Directors for the Shirley Jackson Awards and on the Diverse Works Inclusion Committee for the HWA. She writes, teaches, cooks, and eats in Los Angeles.
people.name: Kate Maruyama

people.bio: Kate Ristau is the President of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA) and the Executive Director of Willamette Writers. She is the author of three middle grade series, Clockbreakers, Mythwakers, and Wylde Wings, and the young adult series, Shadow Girl. You can read her essays in The New York Times and The Washington Post. She is the chair of the Tigard Public Library Board of Directors, and you can meet her online at Kateristau.com.
people.name: Kate Ristau

people.bio: Katherine Quevedo hails from Portland, Oregon, where she works as an analyst and lives with her husband and two sons. Her writing has won the Elgin Award, is a finalist for the Rhysling Award, and has been nominated for the Pushcart Prize. Her short stories and poems appear in Asimov’s, Nightmare Magazine, Fireside Magazine, and elsewhere. She is the author of the fantasy novella Thrice Petrified (Of Metal and Magic Publishing, 2025), the poetry chapbook The Inca Weaver’s Tales (Sword & Kettle Press, 2024), and a forthcoming book of video game poetry from Manawaker Studio. Find her at www.katherinequevedo.com.
people.name: Katherine Quevedo

people.bio: Kathleen Carr Foster is an award-winning author of speculative fiction. She earned an MFA from Boston University, where she was the recipient of the Florence Engel Randall Graduate Fiction Prize, and she won the Davis Prize for Fiction as an undergraduate at Wellesley College. She has also received an Emerging Artist Award from the St. Botolph Club Foundation, and her short fiction has been published in Slice Magazine, on Harper Perennial’s Fifty-Two Stories website, and in 236, BU Creative Writing’s Literary Journal. Her debut novel, The Jewel of Corlivo, will be published by Erewhon Books in October 2026. She teaches writing at the University of Massachusetts, Boston. A mother of two, she lives in Massachusetts with her family and an anxious rescue dog named Wendy. Visit her online at kathleencarrfoster.com.
people.name: Kathleen Carr Foster

people.bio: Kath O’Shea David has worked with puppets over 50 years. She is an Equity Stage Manager with an MFA from Yale. She is a published writer and editor of various works. As a writer, she is in a number of anthologies including “She’s a real cougar” in Bad Ass Mom edited by Mary Fan and “the Case of the Industrial Revolution” in They keep killed Glenn edited by Peter and Kathleen David. Her costumes have won awards at various science fiction conventions both for performance and workmanship. You can find her puppet work at Nostringasttachedpuppets.com.
people.name: Kath O David

people.bio: Kathryn Sullivan writes young adult science fiction and fantasy, including fantasy novel THE CRYSTAL THRONE and short story collection AGENTS, ADEPTS & APPRENTICES. Her Doctor Who-related works include the essay, “The Fanzine Factor”, in the Hugo winning CHICKS DIG TIME LORDS and essays in CHILDREN OF TIME: COMPANIONS OF DOCTOR WHO and OUTSIDE IN: 160 NEW PERSPECTIVES ON 160 DOCTOR WHO STORIES BY 160 WRITERS. She also has reviews in the Star Trek-related OUTSIDE IN BOLDLY GOES and OUTSIDE IN MAKES IT SO and the X-Files related OUTSIDE IN TRUSTS NO ONE. She is owned by a large cockatoo, who graciously allows her to write about other animals, as well as birdlike aliens. Kathryn lives in Winona, MN, where the river bluffs along the Mississippi River double as cliffs on alien planets or the deep mysterious forests in a magical world.
people.name: Kathryn Sullivan

people.bio: Kathy has been watching Dr. Who since she was in the womb. While technically Colin Baker should be her Doctor, she loved Peter Davison the best. Never missing an episode, Kathy enjoys discussing the finer points of wibbley-wobbley timey-wimey stuff with anyone who will sit still long enough. Ask her about Worldcon, the Hugo Awards, karaoke, labor law, or obscure trivia.
people.name: Kathy Bond

people.bio: Katie Hallahan is the author of the McKenna Ellerbeck series (The Twice-Sold Soul, The Twice-Wanted Witch), a queer contemporary fantasy romance. She has designed award-winning narrative adventure games at Phoenix Online Studios, an indie game studio she co-founded, including Cognition: An Erica Reed Thriller and Gabriel Knight 20th Anniversary Edition. She's an avid tabletop RPG player, amateur nail art enthusiast, diehard Buffy fan, and lover of all things pumpkin spice.
people.name: Katie Hallahan

people.bio: Katie Wu is an author of swoony and strange books. Born stateside but raised in Shanghai, she then studied computer science and fine arts at the University of Pennsylvania, and is now based in NYC. Her adult fantasy debut, MADDER LAKE, about two rivals falling in love at magic painting university, is forthcoming from Harper Voyager in 2027. When not writing, she enjoys painting, skiing, feeding her sourdough starter, and her two demonic cats.
people.name: Katie Wu

people.bio: Kat Kourbeti is a queer Greek/Serbian speculative fiction writer, culture critic, narrator and podcaster based in London, UK. She is a Hugo and British Fantasy Award-winning Senior Podcast Editor at Strange Horizons magazine, hosts The Write Song Podcast, and writes about SFF arts and theatre for the BSFA. She also organises Spectrum Writers, London's longest running SFFH critique and community group, while her day job is in theatre. Find her on all social media as @darthjuno.
people.name: Kat Kourbeti

people.bio:
Katrina Spillman grew up in the Pacific Northwest. She loves to write, and is particularly interested in character-driven speculative fiction and poetry. She is immensely proud of her debut YA Sci-Fi novel, Promise The Sky, which will be released by Ooligan Press in 2027. She most enjoys reading and writing stories that center diverse characters and voices.

Katrina received her BA and graduated Cum Laude from Portland State University’s History Department. She is the creator of the award winning documentary “Borders and Frontiers of Gender: Rethinking Cabeza de Vaca's Indigenous Encounters 1527-1536.”

The child of a scientist and a tarot card reader, she prefers the space between what is known and what is imagined.
people.name: Katrina Spillman

people.bio:
Dr. Kaylea Champion studies how people cooperate to build digital infrastructure like the web and cloud, including what gets maintained, what we assume about the future, and the risks we face. She is an Assistant Professor in Computing and Software Systems at the University of Washington Bothell, where she teaches software engineering with an emphasis on cybersecurity, evidence-based practices, and the intelligent use of artificial intelligence.

She enjoys connecting with general audiences about the relationships among technology and society (including, but not exclusively, AI) and brings evidence-based advice to questions about policy and strategy. She was a panelist at WorldCon in 2025 as well as Norwescon in 2024, 2025, and 2026. She's also spoken at a range of other community gatherings and events, including Mozilla's MozFest, SeaGL, Wikimania, FOSSY, CHAOSSCon, and Women in Data Science. She enjoys tromping through the woods, smashing goblins, conjuring data, and cooking for a crowd.
people.name: Kaylea Champion

people.bio: A cat-loving native of Texas, K.B. Bogen is a self-confessed knit-/yarn-aholic, spending much time knitting (with the help of her cats), inventorying her stash (also with the help of the cats), or fondling yarn anywhere within driving range (the cats don’t like road trips). She likes to cook and enjoys reading forensic anthropology books. Occasionally simultaneously. For over thirty years, she has been lurking behind the scenes editing, copy editing and repairing manuscripts. With the rise in the numbers of epublications, her client load has increased. Time to come out of the editorial closet! Fortunately, writing and editing are not mutually exclusive pursuits.
people.name: KB Bogen

people.bio: I write fun, quirky dark sci-fi and fantasy about fractious found families and monsters who want to be good, including the futuristic Post-Apocalyptic DJ series, which kicks off with So Your Biggest Fan is a Body Snatcher, and the action-packed novella, Destroying a World Eater for Beginners. I’m also an artist with a love for drawing skulls and creating papercut art. Thanks to reading many books on the topic to my nephew, I’m pretty good at pronouncing dinosaur names. My favorite to say is pachycephalosaurus. “Pachycephalosaurus.” Nice! But I totally had to look up how to spell it.
people.name: K.C. Cordell

people.bio: KC Grifant is an award-winning writer and editor based in Southern California whose horror, fantasy, science fiction, and weird west books and short stories have appeared in international magazines, games, podcasts, and Stoker-nominated anthologies. She is editor of several anthologies, co-founder of the San Diego Horror Writers Association (HWA), a SFWA mentor, and co-creator of Monster Gunslingers the game. In addition to teaching writing courses and workshops, she is a multi-award-winning nonfiction writer and editor who has penned hundreds of published science articles. Learn more at www.KCGrifant.com
people.name: KC Grifant

people.bio:
Keala Kendall is the New York Times and USA Today bestselling author of How Far I’ll Go and Nobody Gets Left Behind in Disney's A Twisted Tales series. Her groundbreaking horror debut, That Which Feeds Us: A Hawaiian Gothic, was the May pick for Reese Witherspoon’s Sunnie Reads book club and has been featured in BuzzFeed, Parade, Publishers Weekly, and Honolulu Civil Beat, with national syndication across Yahoo!, AOL, and MSN.

Hapa Native Hawaiian, she is a cofounder of Pacific Islanders in Publishing and a past organizer of the Books for Maui charity auction. Born in Honolulu, raised on Molokaʻi, she now lives as part of the Native Hawaiian diaspora in Los Angeles.
people.name: Keala Kendall

people.bio: Former worldcon chairman, translator of films, books, comics and computer games. First worldcon Heicon 1970. Have worked as ad sales person for quite a few worldcons and liason with printers around the world.
people.name: Kees van Toorn

people.bio: Dr. Keith Gremban is Co-Founder and CEO of Ceil Technologies Corporations and a research professor at the University of Colorado Boulder. Prior to joining the University, Keith was the Director of the Institute for Telecommunication Sciences (ITS), which is the research and engineering laboratory for the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA). Keith was a Program Manager at the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) where he managed a portfolio of programs in the areas of wireless communications and electronic warfare, and also worked in industry, managing and leading research and systems engineering projects. Keith’s research interests are in spectrum science, dynamic spectrum sharing, and wireless communications. Keith is a wannabe science fiction writer.
people.name: Keith Gremban

people.bio: Kelly Lagor is a scientist by day and a writer by night. She mostly writes science fiction and essays about science fiction, and her work has appeared in places like Sunday Morning Transport, Analog, Asimov’s Reactor, Uncanny, and Locus. She lives in San Diego with an assortment of plants and musical instruments, and you can follow along at kellylagor.com or @klagor on various social media for publishing announcements and other assorted ephemera.
people.name: Kelly Lagor

people.bio: Panel is for entire Voyager Flight Team. Kelly Perry is the Data Systems engineer on the Voyager Interstellar Mission.
people.name: Kelly L Perry

people.bio: Kel McDonald has been working in comics for almost two decades; most of that time has been spent on their webcomic, Sorcery 101. More recently, they have organized the Cautionary Fables and Fairytales anthology series and written the Eisner nominated mini-series The Stone King as well and won the Eisner for editing the Best Anthology You Died. They work on the comics of properties such as Buffy: The Vampire Slayer and Adventure Time. Most of their work is creator owned books such as the series Misfits of Avalon for Dark Horse Comics and Stars, Hide Your Fire for Iron Circus. They're currently working on their self-published series The City Between while working as the managing editor at Iron Circus Comics.
people.name: Kel McDonald

people.bio: Kemi Ashing-Giwa is an author and scientist-in-training. Her work includes The Splinter in the Sky, which won the Compton Crook Award and was a USA Today bestseller; This World Is Not Yours; and The King Must Die. Her short fiction, which has been nominated for an Ignyte Award and featured on the Locus Recommended Reading List, has been reprinted in collections including Some of the Best from Tor.com: 15th Anniversary Edition and The Year’s Top Tales of Space and Time. She is now pursuing a PhD in the Earth & Planetary Sciences department at Stanford.
people.name: Kemi Ashing-Giwa

people.bio: Jewelry artist since 2007, history and computer geek since 1987, SFF fan since 1978.
people.name: Kendra Tornheim

people.bio: Kent Bloom is a retired computer performance engineer and a retired attorney. He has been involved in fandom for over 50 years. He has chaired small conventions (DATclave and COSine) and a Worldcon (Denver 2008). He has volunteered at every level of Worldcon, from gopher to division head, multiple times. He is president of the Worldcon Heritage Organization, which collects and displays artifacts of previous Worldcons. He reads science fiction and high fantasy books. He has chaired the World Science Fiction Society (WSFS) business meeting. He is on the Secret Masters of Fandom (SMOF) email list but not otherwise active online.
people.name: Kent Bloom

people.bio: Kestrel Michaud is a classically trained, award-winning, and internationally recognized fine art quilter with a BFA in illustration. Her art quilts are large wall hangings made from thousands of pieces of fabric that are fused together and quilted. Kestrel and her art quilts have been featured on The Quilt Show and Quilting Arts TV on PBS. Kestrel teaches at conferences and on Patreon, she has exhibited in six countries, and her work has won grand prizes at the largest quilt shows in the world.
people.name: Kestrel Michaud

people.bio: Kevin is a life-long science fiction fan, a horror fan, and a public defender by day. He produces, edits, and creates the music for the Hugo Award-winning podcast Hugo, Girl
people.name: Kevin Anderson

people.bio:
Horror veteran Kevin M Glover is an indie comic writer/creator, multi-award-winning horror playwright, and a one-time rubber-suited B-Movie monster, appearing in the 90’s sci-fi schlocker, SYNGENOR.

A prolific low-budget filmmaker back in the day, Kevin produced several cult features including DINOSAUR VALLEY GIRLS, VENUS FLYTRAP, LOVE BITES and the spicy horror films MUMMY’S KISS, EROTIC RITES OF COUNTESS DRACULA and SISTERHOOD OF THE SHEWOLF. He also dabbled in acting, appearing with scream queens Linea Quigley and Michelle Bauer in ASSAULT OF THE PARTY NERDS, James Spader in JACKS BACK and a starring turn as a yuppie gone wrong in VENUS FLYTRAP.

Ten years ago, Kevin created the Scary Tales Publishing line of indie horror comics. His current comic titles include LADY FRANKENSTEIN, FRACTURED SCARY TALES, THEY’RE HEEERE! and MONSTERS VS. More recently, returning to theater, his published plays are all mulitple award winners. HIs much lauded courtroom drama with a monster twist, THE PEOPLE vs FRANKENSTEIN premiered last year in Massachusettes, getting rave reveiws for his novel interpretaiton of the classic monster. Both his epic western vampire novel, OUTLAW BLOOD, and his gruesome graphic novel about zombies at the Alamo, will be released later this year.
people.name: Kevin Glover

people.bio:
Kevin Roche recently retired after 40+ years at IBM Research Almaden, specializing in materials science for spintronics, and as an IBM Quantum Ambassador. A native of the San Francisco Bay Area, Kevin has been presenting on spintronics to the public since 2002 and Quantum Computing since 2017. He was a featured expert on magnetic levitation for Episode 4 of Science and Star Wars.
Kevin has been a fan since he learned to read, and his hobbies include bartending robots, costuming, and running science fiction conventions; he was Chair of the 76th World Science Fiction Convention in August 2018 and recently stepped aside as President of the International Costumers' Guild
people.name: Kevin Roche

people.bio: K.G. Anderson is a journalist, a speculative fiction writer, and a collector of easy recipes and difficult cats. She lives in Seattle in a house haunted by the bad remodeling decisions of the previous owners. A graduate of Viable Paradise, and the past chair of Clarion West, she writes and edits for B Cubed Press and helps host the Two Hour Transport reading series. Her short fiction collection, Patti 209: Fifteen Tales of the Very Near Future, came out in 2025. For links to more of her work, visit http://writerway.com/fiction
people.name: K.G. Anderson

people.bio: Kieron Gillen is a writer, game designer and recovering critic. As a comic writer, he's best known for co-creating books like the Wicked + the Divine, DIE, the Power Fantasy, Once & Future, Phonogram and more. When not doing his own works, he has written extensively for Marvel comics, on all the characters you've heard of and quite a few you probably haven't. He's based in Bath. The city, not the water immersion device, alas.
people.name: Kieron Gillen

people.bio: I have 30 years in front of the camera and behind the scenes in Hollywood. I currently have my own screen used props and costume resale business called Wookiedesigns as well as a prop building youtube channel. I've worked in front of the camera on Hero's, Roswell and Miracle Workers, and I've worked for Universal and Paramount behind the scenes. In the 80's I was the only girl in my D&D club, I hosted a cable access show called Starbase Dallas and I was a mascot for the Dallas Fantasy Fair with my original character Wonder Bunny! I still cosplay and play World of Warcraft and I've fought rapier and heavies in the SCA for 40 years. I am currently a member of a professional Improv group called Consensual Emu! I was a Nerd, a Dwarf, a Queen, a Geek and a Weirdo and some where along the way I became cool!
people.name: Kie Spring

people.bio:
At an early age, Kimberly Bea fell in love with Greek mythology, from the tales of Hermes’ mischief and Athena’s wisdom to the death-defying love of Orpheus and Eurydice. It was this love that led her to pursue graduate degrees in Ancient History, with comparative fields in medieval history and the ancient Near East. Her debut novel, a historical fantasy providing the back story for the Faery Queen in “Tam Lin,” The Changeling Queen, released from Erewhon Books in October 2025. Her follow up, THE CURSE OF FEATHERS, will release in 2026.
She blogs about researching historical fantasy on her website kimberlybea.com, and lives in California.
people.name: Kimberly Bea

people.bio: Former LA Basin resident Kim Iverson Headlee has been a critically acclaimed author since 1999 (Dawnflight, Simon & Schuster) and a student of Arthurian lore for more than half a century. In 2015, she became the first author to publish a sequel to any of Mark Twain's novels, and King Arthur's Sister in Washington's Court enjoyed high praise and sales rankings. Queen Morgan le Fay—the only major character Twain did not kill off—reprises her majestic glory to bring the story of Twain’s Connecticut Yankee, Hank Morgan, full circle in King Arthur's Sister: The Once and Future Queen.
people.name: Kim Iverson Headlee

people.bio:
Fantabulous, amazeballs, spectacularific... these are a few of the words that will be used to describe LA CON V if I am in attendance as a panelist and work shop facilitator.

I am an award winning novelist specialising in speculative fiction. To write is my purpose. Writing is more than important to me... it's vital. I bring passion, dedication, understanding and humor to every room I enter. I promise to be a valuable addition to the event.
people.name: Kimlyn Stanyon

people.bio: Kim Smuga-Otto is a fantasy author of the Boy Band & Dragon series and the novella "A Ghost's Story." She cohosts the writing advice podcast Words To Write By. She lives in Santa Cruz, California.
people.name: Kim Smuga-Otto

people.bio: K. M. Enright is the Sunday Times Bestselling author of MISTRESS OF LIES. Find out more about his writing at kmenright.com or follow him on social media at @KM_Enright.
people.name: K. M. Enright

people.bio: Krys Blackwood has been designing user interfaces for 30 years. After 20 years of hard time in Silicon Valley, she joined NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory 10 years ago and she's now designing the future of deep space operations. Her projects include the Deep Space Network, Europa Clipper and Lander, Perseverance, NISAR, and the Mars Sample Return mission. If that isn't enough nerdery for you, Krys is also a science fiction writer and cosplayer. Krys would like you to know that she fights for the user.
people.name: Krys Blackwood

people.bio: K. Valentin is the author of the critically acclaimed adult contemporary fantasy novel, An Amateur Witch's Guide to Murder. She has also been published in the Bag of Bones Horror Anthology, Cosmos: An Anthology of Dark Microfiction and the Latino Book Review Magazine. K hails from England and Las Vegas and presently calls rainy Washington home. This far-ranging combination of formative locations makes K very proper, occasionally scandalous, and extremely emo. When not writing about demons, she's writing about hackers or elves.
people.name: K. Valentin

people.bio: Kylie Adkins holds a Master's Degree in Literature and has worked with the Ray Bradbury Center in Indianapolis to promote and encourage adult literacy and lifelong learning for the last several years. She also works for the Indianapolis Public Library System where she helps out on their bookmobiles.
people.name: Kylie Adkins

people.bio: Kylie Lee Baker is the Sunday Times bestselling author of dark fantasy and horror novels such as The Keeper of Night, The Scarlet Alchemist, and Bat Eater and Other Names for Cora Zeng. She grew up in Boston and has since lived in Atlanta, Salamanca, and Seoul. Her writing is informed by her heritage (Japanese, Chinese, and Irish), as well as her experiences living abroad as both a student and teacher. She has a BA in creative writing and Spanish from Emory University and a MS in library and information science degree from Simmons University.
people.name: Kylie Lee Baker

people.bio: Lark Morgan Lu lives with a collection of succulents and tea. Their short fiction has appeared in The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Augur Magazine, and Pyre Magazine. Find them on various social media as @LarkMorganLu or find their newsletter on their website, larkmorganlu.com.
people.name: Lark Morgan Lu

people.bio: I've been a published writer since 1964. See Neutron Star, Ringworld, A Mote in God's Eye, Lucifer's Hammer, for a sampling.
people.name: Larry Niven

people.bio: A former NY editor, Laura Anne Gilman switched sides of the desk in 2004. Her work has been hailed as “a true American myth”by NPR, and praised for her “deft plotting and first-class characters” by Publishers Weekly. She has won the Endeavor Award for THE COLD EYE, and been shortlisted for a Nebula, (another) Endeavor, and a Washington State Book Award. Her work includes the Devil’s West trilogy, the Huntsmen books, the Cosa Nostradamus UF series, the Vineart trilogy, and several story collections.
people.name: Laura Anne Gilman

people.bio: Laura Antoniou is the author of the long-running Marketplace series of queer BDSM novels, known for their gender-diverse cast and intricate social worldbuilding around power exchange. A lifelong geek who began by editing the ’80s gaming/media magazine Gateways, she has always been interested in how subcultures build rules, hierarchies, and mythologies. She is also the author of the Rainbow Award–winning comedy mystery The Killer Wore Leather and co-author of the erotic fantasy Silk Threads. An editor, essayist, and frequent panelist, she writes about sexuality, fandom, and community from her home base in New York.
people.name: Laura Antoniou

people.bio: Laura Frankos has written in the fields of science fiction, fantasy, mystery, and theatre history. Her novel BROADWAY REVIVAL (time traveler saves George Gershwin from that tumor) was a Sidewise Award Finalist. She's also written THE BROADWAY MUSICAL QUIZ BOOK and is at work on a survey of musicals adapted from comics, which go back to the 1890s. She hangs around with Harry Turtledove a lot.
people.name: Laura Frankos

people.bio: Laura Picklesimer writes novels, screenplays and short stories in a variety of genres including sci fi, thriller and horror. She is the author of the debut novel KILL FOR LOVE (Unnamed Press, 2023). The book won the Launch Pad Prose Competition Top Book Prize and the Book Pipeline Grand Prize for Best Thriller, and was a finalist for a National Indie Excellence Award. Laura’s short stories have appeared in the Kenyon Review, Arkansas International, and Santa Ana River Review, among other publications. She recently co-wrote and produced the indie sci fi thriller ETERNAL PROPERTIES, which is based on characters from her upcoming novel CHASING RABBITS. An excerpt from Chasing Rabbits recently won Uncharted Magazine's 2026 Novel Excerpt Contest. Laura lives in Southern California and teaches English and creative writing.
people.name: Laura Picklesimer

people.bio: Laura Weyr has written two queer romance novels, The Eighth Key (winner of the Rainbow Award for Best High Fantasy Gay Romance) and Mirror of My Heart. She enjoys discussing fanfiction and fanworks (including the history of slash/queer fanworks from Star Trek to today), Japanese Anime and pop-culture, writing, and a wide variety of other topics.
people.name: Laura Weyr

people.bio: Dr. Laura Woodney is a Planetary Scientist and professor of Physics and Astronomy at California State University San Bernardino. She primarily studies small icy bodies in the solar system.
people.name: Laura Woodney

people.bio: Lauren C. Johnson attributes her upbringing in Florida, America's weirdest state, to her interest in the ecological and surreal. She's the author of The West Facade (SFWP, 2026) and lives in San Francisco, where she co-hosts Babylon Salon, a quarterly Bay Area reading series, and Club Chicxulub, a speculative reading and performance series.
people.name: Lauren C. Johnson

people.bio: Lauren C. Teffeau is a speculative fiction writer based in New Mexico. Her books include the eco-thriller Accelerated Growth Environment (Shiraki Press, 2026), the environmental fantasy A Hunger with No Name (University of Tampa Press, 2024), which took third place in the Speculative Fiction Indie Novella Championship, and the cyberpunk/solarpunk adventure Implanted (Angry Robot, 2018), which was shortlisted for the 2019 Compton Crook Award for best first SF/F/H novel and named a definitive work of climate fiction by Grist. Over twenty of her short stories have appeared in venues like Sunday Morning Transport, DreamForge Magazine, After Dinner Conversation, and the Stoker Award-nominated Chromophobia: A Strangehouse Anthology by Women in Horror.
people.name: Lauren C. Teffeau

people.bio: 2026 marks the 50th anniversary of my first Worldcon. Had discovered science fiction in the book rack next to the Zayre snack bar where I worked in the summer of 1973. Went from reading books about the making of Star Trek (Whitfield then Gerrold), to watching Star Trek, then reading Orbits and Dangerous Visions and finally The Left Hand of Darkness. Joined my first club in 1974, went to my first con in 1975 and started working on cons by my third con. After many years of convention work, I'm still working on retiring and focusing on various projects for FANAC.org and Fancyclopedia.org, particularly the digital recordings and digital photos projects. Married to Jim Mann since 1977, our daughter Leslie worked in international shipping until the Trump tariffs disappeared her job and is a gamer.
people.name: Laurie Mann

people.bio: Lavanya Lakshminarayan is the first Indian woman to be shortlisted for the Arthur C. Clarke Award. She is the multi-award-winning author of The Ten Percent Thief, Interstellar MegaChef, and Intergalactic Feast, with work translated into multiple languages. Her short fiction has appeared in The Best of World SF: Volume 2, The Big Book of Cyberpunk, Someone in Time, and other magazines and anthologies. A former game designer best known for building worlds for FarmVille and Mafia Wars, she lives in Bangalore, India.
people.name: Lavanya Lakshminarayan

people.bio: Lawrence Watt-Evans is the author of fifty novels and well over a hundred short stories -- mostly fantasy, but some SF and horror. His short story "Why I Left Harry's All-Night Hamburgers" won the Hugo in 1988. He has also written comic books, essays, poetry, etc. He has been president of HWA, and an officer in SFWA and Novelists Inc.
people.name: Lawrence Watt-Evans

people.bio: Leadie Jo Flowers received a BA from Stetson University in English and Russian studies. Also, she holds a Master of Fine Arts Writing Popular Fiction from Seton Hill University. She teaches English to private and business students and has taught at Moscow State University and The Russian Academy of Public Relations. Currently she is working on a global website for authors, educators and fans to grow the use of science fiction in the classroom, increasing students critical thinking skills and imagination as well as interest in STEM classes and careers. Her short stories have been published in three anthologies.
people.name: Leadie Jo Flowers

people.bio: I'm a sci-fi/fantasy fan whose love of the genre led me to a career in biotech. I'm interested in seeing WorldCon panels on the latest developments in cell and gene therapy, bioprinting, and cloning!
people.name: Leah Kesselman

people.bio: Leanne Schwartz is the autistic author of the young adult romantic fantasies A Prayer for Vengeance and To a Darker Shore, as well as the adult romance My Kind of Trouble under the name L. A. Schwartz. She has spent about half her life at either the library or the local theater, where she has played Lady Macbeth, Lady Capulet, Clytemnestra, and Hera—perhaps one reason she writes such vengeful, murderous girls. When she’s not teaching English and poetry, she can be found baking pizzelle, working with Authors Against Book Bans, and singing along to showtunes. Visit her on Instagram and BlueSky @SchwartzWords.
people.name: Leanne Schwartz

people.bio: Lee Harris is a multi-Hugo-nominated editor of science fiction, fantasy and horror. He was the first British editor ever to be nominated for a Hugo Award for editing. He loves the theatre (especially musicals) and if you ever invite him to karaoke, you’d better be prepared to give up that mic!
people.name: Lee Harris

people.bio:
Since the infancy of the internet, L. E. Eyring began her writing journey with a sharpened pencil, a pad of yellow legal paper, and many nonsensical ideas. Now, she creates worlds that are equal in beauty and horror, where love can be found in the strangest of hands (or claws, wings, etc.).

L. E. Eyring is set to make her debut in 2026 with City Owl Press. In her free time when she's not writing "monster romance," she watches educational videos and listens to audio books about nuclear physics, quantum mechanics, and theoretical astrophysics.
people.name: L. E. Eyring

people.bio: Leigh Bardugo is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Invisible Parade, The Familiar, and the Ninth House series. The Netflix original series Shadow and Bone brought together multiple titles from her Grishaverse which spans the Shadow and Bone trilogy, the Six of Crows duology, the King of Scars duology—and much more. Her short fiction has appeared in multiple anthologies including The Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy. She lives in Los Angeles and is an associate fellow of Pauli Murray College at Yale University.
people.name: Leigh Bardugo

people.bio: Lenny Dorsky, infamous for Halloween and Convention parties (ConFrancisco), was President of the SUNY StonyBrook Science Fiction Forum and was founder and film coordinator of the University of Arizona Science Fiction Club. He spent decades at JPL developing technologies and instruments. He led proposals for Planetary and Earth orbiting instruments and missions (including NASA’s Mapping Imaging Spectrometer for Europa [MISE], arriving at Jupiter in 2030, and Contribution to ARIEL Spectroscopy of Exoplanets [CASE] on an ESA launch in 2029). He holds the world record for most number of advanced directing workshops ever taken and has directed short films and plays, including the Grand Guignol plays at LA Con III.
people.name: Lenny Dorsky

people.bio: Zhen does creative work on screens and paper. Among other selves, they are a graphic designer and illustrator informed by research and concepts with honesty at its core. Their personal practice is motivated by gratitude, gathering, and giving form to the love around them. Currently based in sunny Selangor, Malaysia.
people.name: Leong Yi Zhen

people.bio: Leslie S. Klinger is the New York Times best-selling, multi-award winning author editor of annotated editions of the Sherlock Holmes stories, Dracula, Frankenstein, the works of H.P. Lovecraft, as well as Sandman and Watchmen
people.name: Leslie S Klinger

people.bio: Luis E. Torres is Peruvian-born writer with a passion for creating thoughtful hard SF space novels grounded in societal realities and infused with South American themes. He has 20+ years’ experience freelance-designing commercial tabletop role-playing game adventures, and his self-published hard science-fiction RPG Seven Worlds was nominated for an ENnie for Best Role-Playing Adventure of 2018, and also received the Atomic Rockets Seal of Approval for Scientific Accuracy. By day he’s a program manager supporting AI product development for a major Seattle technology company. He’s a member of SFWA’s Emerging Tech/AI committee, and is currently working on his third SF novel. L.E. Torres is a Peruvian-born science fiction author who writes space operas infused with Latin American culture and realistic science accuracy. A twenty-year veteran of role-playing game design, his self-published RPG Seven Worlds was nominated for an ENnie Award and received the Atomic Rockets Seal of Scientific Accuracy. An introvert with a passion for complex characters and bittersweet endings, Torres also composes electronic music and has spent forty years as a devoted science fiction fan. He writes stories that confront hopelessness with beauty, bringing precision and heart to tales of humanity among the stars.
people.name: L.E. Torres

people.bio: Lettie Prell’s short fiction has appeared in Analog, Apex, Clarkesworld, Tordotcom, WIRED magazine, Flash Fiction Online, and elsewhere. Several of her stories have been reprinted in anthologies, including The New Voices of Science Fiction (Tachyon), The Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy, and “best of the year” publications curated by Neil Clarke and Rich Horton. Some of her works have also been translated into Chinese, Japanese, and French.
people.name: Lettie Prell

people.bio: As Lex Nakashima: Attending Worldcons since IguanaConII; writer-directer for LX, Ltd. web series tentativley titled, "ClockWerx" As Lance Ikegawa: Master Costumer, won some awards, builds monster costumes especially.
people.name: Lex Nakashima

people.bio: I am a 22 year member of the SCA, and current King of the Kingdom of Caid. I participate in armored combat, and teach new fighters, as well as help run our society.
people.name: Liam MacGregor

people.bio:
Libby Schultz is an established copy and gaming writer, and published her debut speculative cyberpunk gamelit novel Win Condition, which won the Kirkus Star,, Booklife Editor's Pick, and the IndieBrag Medallion, inspired by her life in the crypto and gaming in industries.

She is also the founder and CEO of CipherCounts, and has worked at the forefront of the crypto industry since 2017, advising and educating innovators, institutions, Fortune 500 companies, Big 4 CPA firms, and the AICPA to build next generation financial systems. She is also a science fiction writer, licensed CPA, and technologist with a Master’s in Data Science (AI and information technology) from Carnegie Mellon.

Additionally relevant for WorldCon 2026: Author of Crypto’s Utopian Paradox (WorldCon 2025) Member of the WorldCon Academic Committee Studied Data Science and AI at Carnegie Mellon University 15+ years in computational analysis Ethical Shiba Inu breeder and archivist (7 years) Member of the AKC, SFSC, and NSCA Breeding program guided by Professor Greg Burns at CSU Veterinary Teaching Hospital, and Susanne Osaza, AKC Breeder of Merit
people.name: Libby Schultz

people.bio:
