Linda H. Codega is a writer, author, and award-winning entertainment journalist who has written about science fiction and fantasy media for nearly ten years. In 2024 they co-founded the tabletop roleplaying game news site Rascal News. They are a writer and editor for Fansplaining (https://fansplaining.com). In 2021 they won a Hugo as part of the editorial team of Strange Horizons for "Best Semi-Pro Zine." They specialize in writing about tabletop roleplaying games, SFF media, fandom, and queer intersections.

They most recently worked on Season 3 of Interview With the Vampire/The Vampire Lestat as the Writers' Room Assistant. Their first book, MOTHEATER, was released in 2025. Their second book, PASHA THE STORM, will publish in June 2026.

Lin is transgender and nonbinary and use they/them pronouns exclusively. They currently live in Los Angeles with their dog, Zigzag, after ten years in New York (but not in the city).
people.name: Lin Codega

people.bio: Lincoln James is a New York–based author of six thrillers — psychological, speculative, and dark. His books, including The Vanishing Eight, All the Time, and We Are Human, blend vintage atmosphere with modern dread: time travel and grief, bodily autonomy and evolution gone wrong, small towns hiding unspeakable things. A college professor specializing in communication and public speaking, he writes about identity, survival, and pasts that refuse to stay buried. His work has been featured by the Associated Press and national broadcast affiliates. Vintage Thrillers. Modern Nightmares.
people.name: Lincoln James

people.bio:
Lincoln Peters is an engineer, a photographer, and a historical swordfighter. He was the masquerade photographer at Worldcon 75, and in 2017 and 2018 he helped to put on the Children's Photography Workshop.

Since 2013, he has also worked with St. Michael's Salle d'Armes to provide swordfighting demos and lessons, to educate writers and fans on the differences between real fighting and stage fighting.

Lincoln has also watched the Maker Movement since its inception. He has built projects using Arduino and Raspberry Pi boards, and he is waiting for an affordable 3-D printer that can work with steel.
people.name: Lincoln Peters

people.bio: Linda D. Addison is the first African-American recipient of the HWA Bram Stoker Award® and author of six Bram Stoker Award winning collections, including Everything Endless written with Jamal Hodge, as well as a SFWA Nebula Award Finalist, a SFPA Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry, recipient of the HWA Lifetime Achievement Award and HWA Mentor of the Year. Her 2026 book: Carnivores & Other Lovers with Consuelo G. Flores, Andrea Goyan, Elizabeth Eve King & Elizabeth Wong.
people.name: Linda D. Addison

people.bio: Linda Deneroff has been in fandom for over 50 years. A lot has changed in that time.
people.name: Linda Deneroff

people.bio: Dr. Linda Spilker is a planetary scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory who has participated in NASA and international planetary missions for almost 50 years, including Voyager and Cassini. Spilker’s mission roles include mission leadership as well as design, planning, operation and scientific data analysis and modeling. As Cassini Project Scientist Dr. Spilker led a team of over 300 international scientists. She is currently the Voyager Project Scientist. She enjoys traveling and hiking in National Parks, including her favorite parks, Yosemite, Bryce and Zion.
people.name: Linda Spilker

people.bio: Lindsey Byrd is the author of the Tale of Two Crowns Duology and On The Subject of Griffons. She is a historian of medicine and the proud mother of a rambunctious australian shepherd.
people.name: Lindsey Byrd

people.bio: If you believe in dreams, discovery, and the fragile beauty of human life, this story will stay with you. This is the tragic and emotional story of a young scientist, Professor of Astronomy Star l'Etoile, who did not have time to make her most significant discovery in life due to her untimely death. This story is symbolic because the author of this comic, Navy Bird, died without ever seeing her main book, "Arlekino & Pirrot," published. She had been working on it for the last two years. She was killed at the age of 24.
people.name: Liora Bronshtein

people.bio: Lisa Hertel is an artist from a long line of artists. Formerly a pharmacist, Lisa has the usual fannish breadth of trivial knowledge. Lisa likes to work with kids as well as adults and believes everyone can do art and that everyone should own original art, and works hard to make that happen. They also revel in their geekiness.
people.name: Lisa Hertel

people.bio: Lisa Mix is the Director of University Archives & Special Collections at California State University Fullerton, where she works with the McNelly Science Fiction Collection.
people.name: Lisa Mix

people.bio: Lisa Padol is a second generation SF fan, a filker, a gamer, playtester and editor of games, and a player and writer of LARPS. She sings adequately and consistently fails to identify harp tunes when her husband, Joshua Kronengold, is noodling around on the harp.
people.name: Lisa Padol

people.bio:
LIZA GROEN TROMBI is the Hugo and World Fantasy Award winning Publisher and Editor-in-Chief of Locus Magazine. A life-long reader of science fiction, fantasy, and horror, she studied literature, history, and translation at university, and worked in several fields before joining the magazine in early 2003. She has been Editor-in-Chief and Publisher since 2009. Trombi also participates in convention panels and awards juries, runs the Locus Awards Weekend and writing workshops, publishes books with Locus Press, and serves as board president of the Locus Science Fiction Foundation.

She lives in California with her two daughters and a little dog, too.
people.name: Liza Groen Trombi

people.bio: Liz Argall is a cartoonist, mental health advocate, technical writer and co-founder of Ngombor Community Development Alliance in Uganda. Her work has appeared in multiple outlets, including Uncanny Magazine, Strange Horizons, Meanjin, and Friends of Lulu. Her webcomic --Thingswithout.com-- regularly appears online, where it has created several ripples of joy. Liz lives in Seattle, but her heart misses the big silly birds of Australia.
people.name: Liz Argall

people.bio: Liz Coleman is a licensed mental health counselor specializing in trauma and neurodiversity who works in community mental health in Seattle. She's been previously published in Lightspeed and Beneath Ceaseless Skies.
people.name: Liz Coleman

people.bio: Liz Levin is a high school English teacher and writer who lives near Chicago with one vociferous cat and the three other humans who cater to his needs. An alum of the Stonecoast MFA program and the Clarion Workshop, her work has appeared or will appear in Flash Fiction Online, Gavagai, Zooscape, Metaphorosis's Trunk: Stories that took the Long Way, and Scryptid Games's Tales From the Cryptids.
people.name: Liz Levin

people.bio:
L.J. Melvin is the author of the CURD IMMUNITY series, a YA climate fiction/hope punk adventure about microbiology and saving small pieces of the world.
As a kid, L.J. spent weekends reading science fiction in her dad’s electron microscopy lab and listening to dinner conversation about coalescing lipids, diamond knife sectioning, histology, and microbiology. She later taught English to at-risk youth, prisoners, and African high-schoolers as a Peace Corps Volunteer. She’s been a small business accountant, posturologist, structural bodyworker, and homeschooling parent and now spends her time in Lewis County, WA, gardening and writing science fiction novels.
people.name: L.J. Melvin

people.bio:
L.L. MacRae is a British fantasy author of character-driven stories and epic adventure. Her books contain dragons, bucket-loads of magic, less conventional characters, and are typically fun and hopeful.

She lives in a tiny village in the English countryside, has a degree in Psychology, and was a professional copywriter before going full-time as an author—swapping corporate copy for magic and dragons.
people.name: LL MacRae

people.bio: Logan Uber is an interdisciplinary scholar holding five master’s degrees across the fields of humanities, literature, environmental policy, creative writing, and intelligence studies. His research has been diverse and includes works related to the Pearl Poet, grizzly bears, coast redwood conservation, cosmology, and philosophy.
people.name: Logan Uber

people.bio: Lora Boehm has been part of the Society for Creative Anachronism practically her whole life. She’s seen the SCA evolve from a small group into the worldwide community it is today, and she’s been in the thick of that growth every step of the way. When she isn’t focused on serving and growing the SCA, Lora channels that same creative passion into the SoCal Rebel Legion and the 501st. Raised by Star Trek icons John and Bjo Trimble, she thrives at the intersection of history and fandom, dedicated to building the kind of welcoming, imaginative spaces where everyone can belong.
people.name: Lora Boehm

people.bio: Lorelei Esther is a young woman taking on the world. The youngest Hugo Finalist in the history of the award, she is an accomplished artist, having started her comic career at age nine with the famous Blue Bird (inspiration for the DC character of the same name). She has illustrated all of the books in The Kitra Saga and is the staff artist for Journey Press. She is an accomplished singer/songwriter, regularly performing live independently and with Galactic Journey. Her articles frequently appear on the Journey, and she has done introductions for the lauded Rediscovery: Science Fiction by Women series. A fangirl and activist at heart, Lorelei hopes to leave an impression on the world by educating, inspiring, and providing for the community.
people.name: Lorelei Esther

people.bio: Lori Anderson is a lawyer and co-host of the podcast Hugo, Girl! which takes a look at Hugo award-winning novels (and sometimes other things) through a feminist lens.
people.name: Lori Anderson

people.bio: A conservation scientist and third-culture Scot, Lorraine lives by the sea writing speculative fiction influenced by folklore and the wilderness. She is the multi-award winning author of several books, most recently the connected science fantasies We Are All Ghosts In The Forest and The Salt Oracle, which is an Arthur C. Clarke Award finalist.
people.name: Lorraine Wilson

people.bio: LOUISE RIOFRIO worked as Scientist at NASA Johnson Space Center in Houston and in Hawaii, and is known worldwide for discovering change in the Speed of Light. She is also an actress in TV and film, winning awards at multiple film festivals. She is author of popular books THE SPEED OF LIGHT and DISCOVERY: ALASKA TO HAWAII.
people.name: Louise Riofrio

people.bio: Luis Carlos Barragán is a writer and illustrator focused on science fiction, and has an MA in Islamic Art history from the American University in Cairo. He has published four sci-fi novels: Vagabunda Bogotá, winning Best Novel Award at Chamber of Commerce of Medellín and shortlisted for the Rómulo Gallegos Award; El Gusano short listed for the Isaac Asimov award in Puerto Real, Spain; Tierra Contrafuturo, and Eidolónica. His short story collection Parásitos Perfectos received the Idartes Publishing Grant. He has won the George Scanlon Award, Ucronías Peru’s Alternative History Award, Altered Carbon Short Story Award in Uruguay and the Sheridan le Fanu award in Madrid in 2024. Recently he also curated the anthology of Latin American science fiction, Máquinas Mestizas. His work has been translated to English, Chinese, Farsi and French. He has also illustrated a handful of cover arts and done the concept art of the indigenous futurism-virtual reality project Códice Futuro.
people.name: Luis Carlos Barragán Castro

people.bio: Luka Dowell hosts Solarpunk Now, a podcast envisioning hopeful futures through grounded discussions of the present. As an independent scholar affiliated with the Institute for Social Ecology, Luka researches SF texts and the communities surrounding them. Their published works include discussions of technology and collapse in solarpunk, as well as short fiction. Luka has also worked as a street poet-for-hire and the marketing lead for an independent publisher of diverse sci-fi.
people.name: Luka Dowell

people.bio: Writing far faster than his hands can withstand, Luke Chmilenko hails from the Great White North where he lives with his wife and two daughters. Toiling endlessly Luke juggles his time between a rapidly growing catalogue of series while playing far more video games than he would ever openly admit.
people.name: Luke Chmilenko

people.bio: Lynne Sargent is a Hamilton-based queer writer, aerialist, and holds a Ph.D in Applied Philosophy. They are the poetry editor at Utopia Science Fiction magazine. Their work has been nominated for Rhysling, Elgin, Best-of-the-Net and Aurora Awards, and has appeared in venues such as Augur Magazine, Strange Horizons, and Analog. Their work has also been supported through the Ontario Arts Council. Watch out for their non-fiction book Thought Experiment Revolution: How Philosophy in Science Fiction & Fantasy Changed the World, forthcoming from ECW Press. To find out more visit them at scribbledshadows.wordpress.com.
people.name: Lynne Sargent

people.bio: Lysz Flo is an AfroCaribbean Latine, polyglot, writer, indie author, The Estuary Collective member, Ignyte Award Winner for CNF, Creatively Exposed podcast host, Speculative Tin House Fall 2025 Fellow, Voodoonauts Summer 2020 Fellow/Educator in 2024 and Obsidian Black Listening 2022 Fellow. She released Soliloquy of an Ice Queen, March 2020. She is creative educator since 2020. Her poems can be found in FIYAH, iamb, Hellebore, Lolwe, Strange Horizons and has done various multimedia projects with O’ Miami. She is also an Online Crystal and Spiritual wellness shop owner at Astrolyszics.com
people.name: Lysz Flo

people.bio: Madeleine Holly-Rosing is the writer/creator of the steampunk supernatural graphic novel, prose, and audio drama series, Boston Metaphysical Society, the non-fiction book, Kickstarter for the Independent Creator, and the new graphic novel series, Morgana Pendragon. Boston Metaphysical Society (Vol. 1) was nominated for a Geekie Award and the Reader’s Choice Steampunk Chronicle award, and Morgana Pendragon #1 won Best Individual Issue in the inagural Zelda Awards. Recently, she was a guest writer on Joe Benitez’s, Lady Mechanika, with the story, The Mechanical Menagerie. Issue #3 from Image Comics will be available in July 2026.
people.name: Madeleine Holly-Rosing

people.bio: Madeline James is a fantasy author and worldbuilding content creator. Her first book, Because the Beasts Came, was published this year. She is best known for her worldbuilding YouTube channel, MadelineJamesWorldbuilds, running the online worldbuilding conference the Worldbuilding Festival and the in-person conference SpecCon.
people.name: Madeline James

people.bio: Makana Yamamoto was born on the island of Maui. Splitting their time between the Mainland and Hawaiʻi, Makana grew up on beaches and in snowbanks. Always a scientist at heart, Makana fell in love with sci-fi as a teen. A writer from childhood, fiction became the perfect medium for them to explore their interests as well as reconnect with their culture. Makana’s debut novel, HAMMAJANG LUCK, is a 2024 Locus Award Finalist. In their free time, Makana likes to hoard dice for their Dungeons & Dragons games, defeat bosses with their guildmates, and get way too invested in reality competition shows. They currently live in Boston with their wife and two cats.
people.name: Makana Yamamoto

people.bio:
Makiia Lucier is the author of Dragonfruit, Year of the Reaper, the Isle of Blood and Stone duology, and A Death-Struck Year. Her stories are inspired by history and mythology and have been called “brilliant” (Booklist), “moving,” (New York Times), “masterful” (Horn Book), and “breathtaking” (School Library Journal). They can be found on many notable lists, including NPR’s “Books We Love,” Kids' Indie Next, and the American Library Association’s ‘Best Fiction for Young Adults.’ She is a recipient of the Oregon Book Award for Young Adult Literature.

Makiia grew up on the Pacific island of Guam, not too far from the equator, and holds degrees in journalism and library science. She lives with her family in Portland, Oregon.
people.name: Makiia Lucier

people.bio:
Malachi Lily is a neurofunky, agender, liminal Black person born and based on the Lenape-hoking land of the U.S (Philly). Lily writes speculative fiction and metaphysical commentary through magick, Black-anarcho politics, and nature wisdom, deconstructing colonial fears around the unconscious, sexuality, and femininity. Their work draws heavily on equal parts ecological naturalist study and divination.

For nine years, they have worked as an illustrator and comic artist across editorial and narrative publications. For five years, they have been a professional TTRPG creator and a featured storyteller, serving as a PAX Unplugged PTI Fellow.

In 2022, they were a Writing in Color Lighthouse fellow. The following year, they were a Tinhouse and Roots.Wounds.Words. fellow, and in 2024, Lily was a writing resident at Stove Works, Queer Materials Lab, and Chateau Orquevaux. Currently, Lily is a Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association Fellow, a Trans Journalists Association Fellow, a Narrative Shifts Fellow, a columnist at Inglenook Lit, a McCormack Writing Center fellow, a culture writer for In These Times, and the Editor-in-Chief of Black and Pink Magazine.
people.name: Malachi Lily

people.bio: Manjula Menon has a background in Physics and Electrical Engineering. She writes at the intersection of science fiction and philosophy.
people.name: Manjula Menon

people.bio:
Maquel A. Jacob writes fluid beings in an ocean of stars with a little bit of romance and a touch of gore. Originally from the Windy City of Chicago, she now resides in Oregon. She is the author of three different series and has short stories in various anthologies and magazines. Her degrees are in Accounting, Business Administration, and Digital Film and Video. Member of SFWA, PNWA, NIWA, and ALLi.
As a big advocate for diversity, Maquel injects elements in her stories geared to encourage new ways of thinking through Sci-Fi, Fantasy and the Paranormal.
She is a HUGE Anime fan, loves a great bottle of wine, and rocks out to heavy metal music while spinning imaginary worlds in her head and daydreaming.
people.name: Maquel A. Jacob

people.bio: Marcella Ochoa is a filmmaker originally from San Antonio, Texas. She recently wrote and directed a supernatural short, THE HIDDEN, starrring Mishel Prada, Isabella Gomez, Jessica Marie Garcia, and Lucas Adams. Her previous Western horror short, HOUR OF BLOOD, starring Jesse Garcia and Isabella Leon received Best Short Film nominations for the Imagen Awards and Humanitas Prizes. Her thriller short she wrote and directed, WORRY DOLLS distributed by Crypt TV, received a Best Short Film Imagen Award nomination. Her short, MY NAME IS MARIA DE JESUS, premiered on HBO. She co-wrote a thriller, MADRES, for Blumhouse and Amazon and received an NAACP Image Award Nomination for Outstanding Writing. She’s written horror films for Paramount, New Line, and Universal and is repped by CAA and Media Evolution Group.
people.name: Marcella Ochoa

people.bio: A fan, and conrunner from Poland. Loves reading, playing tabletop games, and attending conventions. He also publishes two fanzines, and writes a blog about cons and fandom: www.FandomRover.com. In 2018 he was a GUFF delegate during Continuum convention in Melbourne, Australia.
people.name: Marcin "Alqua" Klak

people.bio: Twilight Zone Companion author Marc Scott Zicree has written iconic episodes of Star Trek TNG, DS9, Sliders, Babylon 5, Friday the 13th – The Series, Smurfs, He-Man, Super Friends, Real Ghostbusters, Animorphs and many more. His work has been nominated for the American Book Award, Hugo Award, Humanitas Prize, Nebula Award and has won the Saturn Award, Rondo Award, Writers Guild Diversity Award, TV Guide Award, and Lifetime Achievement Award from the Cardiff International Film Festival. With his wife Elaine, he is writing, directing and producing the TV series Space Command, plus a feature and five pilots for The Showrunners Network.
people.name: Marc Scott Zicree

people.bio: Margaret Dunlap is a screenwriter and author of more than a dozen published short stories and novelettes for Uncanny, Apex, The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction and as part of the Locus Award-nominated team behind Bookburners. Her television credits include cult-favorite The Middleman, Eureka, Blade Runner: Black Lotus, Batman: Caped Crusader and the Emmy-winning Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance. Find her on the web at www.margaretdunlap.com, or through her newsletter, the very accurately named Margaret’s Nearly Monthly News.
people.name: Margaret Dunlap

people.bio: Dr. Margaret Landis is an assistant professor, planetary scientist, and exploration nerd.
people.name: Margaret Landis

people.bio:
Margaret McGaffey Fisk (she/her) is a storyteller whose tales often cross genres and worlds to bring events and characters to life. She currently writes science fiction, fantasy, and romance, but will go wherever the story takes her.

In a different time, you’d find her before a bonfire, or with a mug of ale and a lute, spinning tales for all who are within earshot. Now, though, you can read her explorations of loyalty, love, and cultural conflict wherever you might be.
people.name: Margaret McGaffey Fisk

people.bio: Margaret Owen was born and raised at the end of the Oregon Trail and has worked in everything from thrift stores to presidential campaigns. She is the author of the bestselling Little Thieves trilogy and the critically-acclaimed Merciful Crow duology. In her free time, she enjoys exploring ill-advised travel destinations, raising money for social justice nonprofits through her illustrated work, and negotiating a hostage situation with her monstrous cats. She lives in Seattle.
people.name: Margaret Owen

people.bio: Margot Moore writes contemporary romcoms that play with genre. Her debut, FAKING FOR A FORTNIGHT, is set to release Spring 2027 with PRH/Berkley and features a Regency-themed immersive resort inspired by Westworld.
people.name: Margot Moore

people.bio: Marguerite is a dual-national American living in the UK. She's the President and CEO of the Escape Artists Foundation, a US 501(c)(3) nonprofit bringing free and accessible audio short fiction to a global audience. A practicing lawyer, Marguerite also loves performing in audio dramas and podcasts, community organizing, and teaching legal and business skills to independent creatives.
people.name: Marguerite Kenner

people.bio: Marguerite is Co-Chair of the Dublin 2029 Worldcon bid. A con-goer for over 20 years, she became a conrunner through her belief in shared joy, shared work, and shared achievement. She has been DH on 2 Worldcons, Vice Chair on 2 more, plus many other cons and roles. Outside cons, she is a Dublin-based project manager, trained singer, craft enthusiast, and lover of inks, music, and books. Her cats are learning “button talk,” so life now plays to the soundtrack of “Treat. Treat.”
people.name: Marguerite Smith

people.bio: For over 20 years, Maria Alexander has been a multiple Bram Stoker Award-winning author of horror and mystery novels, short fiction, screenplays, poetry, and essays. Her latest dark queer tale, Brimstone & Blades, slayed the 2025 Fall BookFest with three first-place awards in YA fiction, YA fantasy, and LGBTQ+ fiction. A lover of swords and esoteric arts, she can be found on Substack and other online platforms. For more, visit www.mariaalexander.net.
people.name: Maria Alexander

people.bio: Marie Brennan is a former anthropologist and folklorist who shamelessly leans on her academic fields for inspiration. She recently misapplied her professors' hard work to The Market of 100 Fortunes and The Waking of Angantyr. She is the Hugo Award-winning and Nebula and World Fantasy-nominated author of the Victorian adventure series The Memoirs of Lady Trent along with several other series, over ninety short stories, several poems, and the New Worlds series of worldbuilding guides; as half of M.A. Carrick, she has written the Rook and Rose epic fantasy trilogy. For more information and social media, visit linktr.ee/swan_tower.
people.name: Marie Brennan

people.bio: Marie Guthrie wrote the first doctoral dissertation on Robert A Heinlein. She served in Peace Corps (Moldova, 2003-5) and was a professor of English. She enjoys domestic and international travel, SCUBA, and is an actor, stage manager, and director.
people.name: Marie Guthrie

people.bio: Marie Parks is an LGBTQIA+ fantasy author and founder of Sandia Starforgers retreats for speculative fiction writers. Her writing has been called "a tapestry of emotion" by Mary Robinette Kowal and "impressive... fresh... and addictive" by David B. Coe. She coauthored paranormal thrillers Unrelenting and Undeniable with Jes Honard; Unrelenting, won the New Mexico Book Awards for best LGBTQ book. Marie was a finalist for the Futurescapes Award for Most Promising New Author for her fantasy heist, Flightless. She lives in New Mexico with her two rescue chihuahuas, where she loves to camp, hike, and eat green chile.
people.name: Marie Parks

people.bio:
Science fiction and fantasy critic. She won the 15th Japan Science Fiction Award for her book Techno-gynesis : Women’s SF and Feminism Criticism (Keisō Shobō, 1994) and the 2nd Japan Translation Award in the Philosophy category for her co-translation of Cyborg Feminism by Donna Haraway et al. (Treville, 1991).
She writes the science fiction and fantasy Book Review in the Thursday evening edition of the Nihon Keizai Shimbun; The Nikkei.
Although she is a professional critic known for her feminist analysis of pop culture, she has been an avid science fiction fan active in the fandom since high school. She is part of the first generation of Japanese Cosplay　 and was the first to introduce American Slash Fiction to the Japanese genre BL. In recognition of her unique fan activities, she received the 2021 Takumi Shibano Japan SF Fandom Award. She is a member of the F&HF Fan Club “Rolarius” and The Japanese Association for Gender Fantasy & Science Fiction. Through the latter, she has promoted the Sense of Gender Award ; Japanese Tiptree Award, which selects the best gender SF works of the year, since 2001. She served as chair of the Women Writers’ Committee of the Japan PEN Club (2003–2011).
people.name: Mari KOTANI

people.bio:
I have lived and professional experience. with neurodiversity inlcuding ADHD, austisim spectrum disorder, and chronic emotional dysregulation including complex PTSD.

I have been an attorney for 45 years, with over 30 years experience in dsablity law, including two decades as a Social Security Adminsitrative Law Judge.

I have five years experience as an adjunct professor of civil and criminal trial advocacy at Seattle University Law School.

I participated in panel discussions on neurodiversity at Seattle World Con in 2025 and I am a peer mentor/instructor for the NEABPD.

At Seattle World Con, I presented a craft session on use of con souvenirs in crafting and participated in a panel on genre crafts.

I am currently an Asst. Attorney General for the State of Washington. I live near Puget Sound in Washington, USA. I write short and novella length fiction, enjoy fiber arts from crossstitch to quilting, and perform stand up comedy when the shows don't run past my bedtime.
people.name: MARILYN S MAUER

people.bio: Mari Ness is a speculative poet, short fiction writer, and two time Hugo and one time Nebula finalist, with more than 350 short stories and poems in various zines and anthologies, including Reactor, Clarkesworld, Uncanny, Lightspeed, Nightmare, Apex, The Sunday Morning Transport, Baffling, Nature Futures, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Diabolical Plots, Three-Lobed Burning Eye, Strange Horizons, Bourbon Penn, and Haven Spec. Mari lives in central Florida, and when not writing, can sometimes be spotted talking to live oak trees.
people.name: Mari Ness

people.bio: Mark is the author of the LA Times bestselling Danger Boy time travel series for young readers of all ages, currently being reissued by by Water Dragon Publishing with a new series finale scheduled for next year, as well as the nanobot-infused "Max Random and the Zombie 500" from Graveside Press. By day -- or is that night? -- he covers Oscars, Emmys, and Hollywood dis-content as a showbiz columnist for publications on various continents, well ahead of their eventual geologic reunification.
people.name: Mark London Williams

people.bio:
Mark L. Van Name is a writer, technologist, and spoken word performer. As an author, he has published five novels (One Jump Ahead, Slanted Jack, Overthrowing Heaven, Children No More, and No Going Back), as well as an omnibus collection of his first two books (Jump Gate Twist); edited or co-edited four anthologies (Intersections: The Sycamore Hill Anthology, Transhuman, The Wild Side, and Onward, Drake!), and written many short stories. Those stories have appeared in a wide variety of books and magazines, as well as many original anthologies.

As a technologist, he is the CEO of a fact-based marketing and learning services firm, Principled Technologies, Inc., that is based in the Research Triangle area of North Carolina. He has worked with computer technology for his entire professional career and has published over a thousand articles in the computer trade press, as well as a broad assortment of essays and reviews.

As a spoken word artist, he has created and performed five shows—Science Magic Sex; Wake Up Horny, Wake Up Angry; Mr. Poor Choices; Mr. Poor Choices II: I Don’t Understand; and Mr. Poor Choices III: That Moment When—and also frequently leads humor panels at conventions.
people.name: Mark L. Van Name

people.bio: I am a retired computer professional, now a full member of SFWA, with two novels, 11,000 Years (2021,2023) and Becoming Terran (2024) - both reviewed for Asimov's, and currently published by Histria Books - and three pieces of short fiction in the Grantville Gazette, and one in Eric Flint's 1632 and beyond.
people.name: mark roth-whitworth

people.bio: A long time fan; my first convention was in 1978, first Worldcon in 1981. I'm a veteran of working on conventions at most levels. I've also dabbled in fanzine fandom and I'm a huge Tolkien geek.
people.name: Mark W. Richards

people.bio: Marley Rose-Teter lives in the Santa Cruz mountains with her partner, child, any number of house-rabbit friends, and a garage full of Halloween decorations. When not writing, she can be found directing local theatre or speaking at anime conventions. She goes at everything she does with her whole heart and strives always to be a bride married to amazement. Her debut novel, THE BONE BRIDES, a Sapphic YA fantasy, comes out September 29th from Page Street.
people.name: Marley Rose-Teter

people.bio: I'm an Angeleno born and raised. I've occasionally said I don't trust air I cannot see. I'm a retired web developer & renewable energy system consultant. I'm no scientist, but I've consumed a steady diet of science books/media as long as I can recall. The first book I remember reading was Man in Space about Mercury 7. My favorite kids' t.v. show? Mr. Wizard. My second favorite? Thunderbirds. Lately I've been exploring the promise/problems solarpunk literature. I've been reading/watching genre fiction a long, long time. My first convention was in Feb. 1979; a tiny gathering in Southern California called "Science Fiction Weekend." I wandered into a room where they were screening episodes of Commando Cody. I was transfixed, hooked, captured… doomed. Since then I've attended many a Westercon, Worldcon, NASFic, Galacticon, Gaylaxicon, Balticon, Equicon, Filmcon, Albacon, Fantasmacon, Boskone and Arisia.
people.name: Marlin May

people.bio: Marshall J. Moore is the author of The Henchperson's Guide to Unionizing, the Son of a Sailor cozy fantasy trilogy, the Rites of Resurrection epic fantasy trilogy, and over thirty published short stories. His story “Red Lanterns” won second place in the Baen Fantasy Adventure Award Short Story Contest. When not writing or talking about writing, you can find Marshall teaching Muay Thai or reading at his home in Atlanta with his wife, Megan, and their two cats, Delilah and Furiosa.
people.name: Marshall J. Moore

people.bio: Marshall Ryan Maresca is a fantasy and science-fiction writer, author of sixteen novels, most of which are part of the Maradaine Saga: Four braided series set amid the bustling streets and crime-ridden districts of the exotic city called Maradaine. He is also the author of the standalone dieselpunk fantasy, The Velocity of Revolution. He is a five-time Hugo finalist as the co-host of the podcast Worldbuilding for Masochists, and has been a playwright, an actor and an amateur chef. He lives in Austin, Texas with his family.
people.name: Marshall Ryan Maresca

people.bio: Martha Wells has been writing since 1993. Her work includes The Murderbot Diaries, The Books of the Raksura, the Ile-Rien series, and most recently Witch King and its sequel Queen Demon, as well as other novels, short fiction, non-fiction, and media tie-ins. She is a member of the Texas Literary Hall of Fame, and her work has won Nebula, Hugo, Locus Awards, and an Alex Award and a Dragon Award, and appeared on the World Fantasy, Philip K. Dick, and the BSFA Award ballots, as well as the New York Times, USA Today, and the Sunday Times Bestseller Lists. She is a consulting producer on the Apple TV Murderbot series.
people.name: Martha Wells

people.bio: Retired librarian, crafter of fantastical stuffed toys, quilts, jewelry, and other things, long-time fan.
people.name: Mary Aileen Buss

people.bio: I grew up rural in the sticks of the midwestern US. I have been in fandom events since my 20s, running small scale conventions, publishing zines, and running a gaming club. My day job was in supply chain for twenty-five years with an early focus on project-based cost reduction and later on iron industry procurement. For most of that time, I was using my daily computer access to write fanfiction and engage with online fan communities, most specifically those of NBC Heroes, Star Wars, The Old Guard, and The Murderbot Diaries.
people.name: Mary Baker

people.bio: Mary G. Thompson is the author of Precious Children and One Level Down (Tachyon) as well as The Word, Flicker and Mist, and other novels. Her contemporary thriller Amy Chelsea Stacie Dee was a winner of the 2017 Westchester Fiction Award and a finalist for the 2018-2019 Missouri Gateway award. Her short fiction has appeared in Dark Matter Magazine, Apex Magazine, and others. She holds an MFA in Writing for Children from The New School and completed the UCLA School of Theater, Film & Television's Professional Program in Screenwriting. She lives in Washington, DC.
people.name: Mary G. Thompson

people.bio: I have been playing in the SCA for over 25 years and enjoying SciFi for even longer.
people.name: Mary Kridler

people.bio: Mary-Michelle Moore is the STEM Teaching Librarian at the University of California, Riverside. She is interested in the representation of librarians, library work, and information literacy in online spaces, and in science fiction and fantasy, and popular culture. She has presented on these topics at WorldCon 76, ChiCon 8, Gallifrey One, and ACA/PCA Conferences.
people.name: Mary-Michelle Moore

people.bio: Mary Robinette Kowal is the USA Today Bestselling author of a dozen novels, including Apprehension and the Lady Astronaut series. A winner of the Hugo, Nebula, and Locus awards, she is also a professional puppeteer and award-winning audiobook narrator. She co-hosts the Writing Excuses podcast, served as SFWA President, and has an asteroid named after her. Also, her cat talks.
people.name: Mary Robinette Kowal

people.bio:
Mary Turzillo's Nebula-winner,"Mars Is no Place for Children," and her Analog novel An Old-Fashioned Martian Girl have been recommended reading on the International Space Station. She has been a finalist on the British SFA, Pushcart, Stoker, Dwarf Stars, and Rhysling ballots. Her poetry collection Lovers & Killers won the 2013 Elgin Award for Best Collection. Her collaboration with Marge Simon, Victims, also won an Elgin. Her latest two books are Cast from Darkness, also with Simon, and Cosmic Cats and Fantastic Furballs. Her current novel project Callisto features a young sword-slasher and her sarcastic time-traveling cat. Mary loves orange kittens, total eclipses, and her amazing husband Geoff Landis.

http://www.maryturzillo.com/
people.name: Mary Turzillo

people.bio: Mason A. Porter is a Professor of Mathematics at University of California, Los Angeles. He also has a secondary appointment in the Department of Sociology and is an External Professor of Santa Fe Institute. Mason is an applied mathematician and studies diverse problems in networks, complex systems, and nonlinear systems. He is a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society, American Physical Society, Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, and Network Science Society.
people.name: Mason A. Porter

people.bio: Mat has been with The Planetary Society for nearly 27 years, with 20 of these as the creator, host and producer of Planetary Radio. He now serves as Senior Communications Adviser.
people.name: Mat Kaplan

people.bio: Dr. Matteo Barbagallo, PhD from the Universidad Pablo de Olavide in Seville, has published and lectured on Martin's work across the Westeros saga, the Tales of Dunk and Egg, and the Wild Cards shared universe. He is a contributor to the Wild Cards blog, a publication that bridges scholarly and fan-community readerships. His research interests include adaptation studies, genre fiction, and the social dimensions of popular fantasy literature.
people.name: Matteo Barbagallo

people.bio: Named Wired Magazine’s ‘World’s Most Wired Comics Creator,’ Matteo Pizzolo is the bestselling author of speculative-fiction comics books including the CALEXIT ("It's not wish-fulfillment it's warning... but that's not all: it's superb." -Cory Doctorow, Boing Boing), ROGUE STATE ("The concepts Matt is presenting here are so familiar they should be terrifying." -Chuck D, Public Enemy), YOUNG TERRORISTS (#1 Bestselling Mature Readers Comic Of The Year, "Taps into an undercurrent of rage against the proverbial machine that is pervasive in the world around us." -Nerdist) and GODKILLER ("Wonderfully bizarre, wickedly delectable." -Kirkus Reviews starred review, Best Books Of The Year List).
people.name: Matteo Pizzolo

people.bio: Matteo Scarfò is a filmmaker with a passion for science fiction. After earning a degree in Languages, he devoted himself to independent cinema and theater. For many years, he has also taught Italian to foreign learners. Together with his wife, Jessica, he shares his life with a dog named Keats, after the poet John Keats. One day, he hopes to adapt Way Station by Clifford D. Simak for the screen. In the meantime, he has directed the sci fi films L'ultimo sole della notte (The Last Sun of the Night) and Esistenza Zero (Existence Zero), as well as the short film Pale Blue Dot: A Tale of Two Stargazers.
people.name: Matteo Scarfò

people.bio: Matt G. is a Black disabled poet, political sociologist, and educator from the 252 residing in the 919. He believes that poetry, like Wu-Tang, is forever and for the children. A graduate of UNC- Chapel Hill, Matt G. was a member of the spoken word group Wordsmiths and Ebony Readers Onyx Theatre (EROT). He competed in the College Unions Poetry Slam Invitational (CUPSI) ranking as high as a semi-finalist. Matt G. is a 2x member of the Bull City Slam Team in Durham, NC and a graduate fellow of The Watering Hole.
people.name: Matt G.

people.bio: Matt Harry is the author of six novels, including SORCERY FOR BEGINNERS, YOU ARE A FILMMAKER, and ASH LAND. He has worked as a TV editor, book editor, college professor, and pizza delivery technician. He co-hosts the podcast MONSTER V MONSTER with Jessica Maison. Matt lives in Los Angeles with his wife and two sons, all of whom (thankfully) like to read.
people.name: Matt Harry

people.bio: Matthew Cropley is a narrative designer and writer for video games, currently working as the narrative lead on TITAN QUEST II, a highly-anticipated ARPG based on Greek mythology now available to play in Early Access on Steam. Matthew has written video games full time since 2019. He has also worked as a writer in other mediums writing/directing plays, publishing fantasy short stories, articles, interviews, reviews, and more, for more than a decade. He’s very passionate about SFF writing in general, and especially loves reading weird fantasy novels.
people.name: Matthew Cropley

people.bio: Matthew S. Rotundo is an award-winning writer of science fiction, fantasy, and horror. His novels include WET WORK, the Prison World Revolt Series (PETRA, PETRA RELEASED, and PETRA Rising), and the forthcoming OATHBREAKER. He is a graduate of the Odyssey Writing Workshop. Matt also plays guitar and has been known to sing karaoke. He lives in Omaha, Nebraska, and assures you that he has heard all the jokes.
people.name: Matthew S. Rotundo

people.bio: Matt is the author of six novels, all set in the world created by the Circle War series, featuring new myths and Greek retellings. He's a lover of mythology and women's soccer, which is to say he's a fan of goddesses.
people.name: Matt King

people.bio:
Distinguished Prof of Physics&Astro UCLA; Natl Science Board (2020--26). Malkan has published over 600 articles in peer-reviewed journals, and has worked extensively on astronomy-related film and television shows, behind and in front of the camera.
Malkan uses a wide range of telescopes in space and on the ground to study the evolution of galaxies and their massive black holes.
people.name: Matt Malkan

people.bio: Matt Youngmark is the author of the Chooseomatic Books series, the Arabella Grimsbro YA novels, and the humorous fantasy series Spellmonkeys. He also wrote and drew the daily webcomic Conspiracy Friends, and in a previous life worked the newsprint mines at Tacoma Reporter and Pandemonium Magazine. His current work in progress is The Pilot Episode, a near-future Sci-Fi novela about accidentally stealing a spaceship and the dangers of late stage capitalism.
people.name: Matt Youngmark

people.bio: Maude Garrett is an LA-based Australian entertainment host who has spent her career professionally obsessed with all things geek - bringing that energy to TV, radio, Nerdist, BBC America, and NBC Universal. Whether she's interviewing your favorite actor or moderating a packed Comic-Con panel, she speaks fluent fandom and isn't afraid to use it. She's also the founder of Maude's Book Club, a thriving haven for SFF readers who like their reading lists with a side of chaos.
people.name: Maude Garrett

people.bio: Hugo-, Nebula-, and Locus Award winning author Max Gladstone has been thrown from a horse in Mongolia and once wrecked a bicycle in Angkor Wat. He is the author of many books, including Last Exit, the Craft Sequence of fantasy novels, and, with Amal El-Mohtar, the internationally bestselling This is How You Lose the Time War. His dreams are much nicer than you’d expect.
people.name: Max Gladstone

people.bio: Megan Haskell pens tales of myth, magic, and mayhem featuring fierce heroines and monsters of every size. She is the award-winning author of The Sanyare Chronicles, The War of the Nine Faerie Realms, and The Rise of Lilith series.
people.name: Megan Haskell

people.bio: Meghan Lancaster is an artist/designer working mainly with textiles in surface design and costume. She holds an MFA along with Certificates in Museum Studies (UW CPE) and Design (City & Guilds of London). Her fields of informative study are comparative religion, Jungian psychology, and quantum physics, and their points of intersection.
people.name: Meghan Lancaster

people.bio: Dr. Meg MacDonald (she/her) was Vice chair and co- Division Head for Promotions for Glasgow 2024 and co- Division Head for Programme for LAcon V. She was startled to find that conrunning involves filking, punning, and applying glitter to friends and strangers alike: along with emails, spreadsheets, and timelines. She has a PhD in English Literature, her thesis, “Gods Wall to Wall: Gods in Fantasy 1989-2020”, considers concepts of agency, belief and transforming grand narratives in genre fantasy. She works at the University of Glasgow as an Academic Consultancy Manager. She loves board games, cosplay, books of all styles, baking, knitting, and all sorts of nerdery.
people.name: Meg MacDonald

people.bio:
Meihan Boey is the Singaporean author of The Formidable Miss Cassidy (Epigram Books Fiction Prize co-winner 2021, Singapore Book Awards Best Literary Work 2022), The Enigmatic Madam Ingram (shortlisted EBFP 2023, for SBA Best Literary Work in 2023, longlisted for Dublin Literary Award) and The Mystical Mister Kay (Epigram Books Fiction Prize Winner 2025). The series is internationally published by Pushkin Press (UK), Harper Perennial (US), Bompiani (Italy) and Ombra (Albania).
Meihan's short stories have appeared in anthologies such as Fish Eats Lion Redux and Best New Singaporean Short Stories Volume 6. She's still trying to go Super Saiyan.
people.name: Meihan Boey

people.bio:
Melinda M. Snodgrass studied opera at the Conservatory of Vienna, graduated Magna cum Laude from U.N.M. with a degree in history, and went on to Law School. After 3 years as a lawyer, she realized she hated being a lawyer and turned to writing.
In 1988 she accepted a job on Star Trek: The Next Generation and began her Hollywood career where she has worked on staff on numerous shows and has written television pilots and feature films. She has just finished a science fiction movie script that is with her manager.

In the prose world she writes for and co-edits the shared world anthology series Wild Cards with George R. R. Martin. In addition, she writes her own novels. She is working on a fantasy novel, and a novel about the god Loki living in the modern world. Her space opera, Imperials, and her Carolingian series, are available.

For fun she rides her dressage horses, plays role playing games and video games.
people.name: Melinda M Snodgrass

people.bio: Melissa Bobe is the author of The Illustrated Woman, Season of the Witch, Sibyls, and the Millennial Witch Series, which includes Nascent Witch and its sequel Familiar Territory. Her collection Electric Trees won the 2023 New York Author Project, after which Melissa went on to win the Indie Author Project’s 2024 Indie Author of the Year Award. She has published shorter works with Flame Tree Fiction, Whisper House Press, Intrepidus Ink, Bards and Sages, Urhi Publishing, Wyldblood Press, and World Weaver Press. After years of teaching college English, Melissa now works as a librarian and a writing instructor. You can find her at abookbumble.com and on social media @abookbumble.
people.name: Melissa Bobe

people.bio:
Melissa is a long-time professional cat herder, as well as a reader, writer, fencer, dancer, and time traveler extraordinaire. She has worked in event running for over 25 years (including professional and fan-run events), and has served on the executive boards of multiple non-profits. She also worked for a time in 1848, and still likes to make her own writing ink.

An avid moss gardener, painter, and needleworker, Melissa delights in creating and tending to tiny things, and has been described as being aggressively whimsical. She is a delicate alpine flower who would much rather live somewhere above the 55th parallel.

She is a staunch defender of the serial comma, and believes that you can have it when you take it from her cold, clenched, dead hands.
people.name: Melissa Kocias

people.bio: Melissa's life took a sharp turn when she discovered costuming at her first sci-fi convention in the early 90's. Eventually costuming led to returning to school, where she completed the certificate program in fashion design at the New York Fashion Academy. After completing fashion school she opened Faerie Fingers Custom Costumes & Event Apparel where she spent 15 years creating costumes and unique event attire for clients around the U.S. Her current pursuits include watching anime, cosplaying with her daughter, and finding new opportunities for cosplay competition.
people.name: Melissa Quinn

people.bio: Merav Hoffman (she/they) is a writer, editor, poet, singer/songwriter, activist, community organizer, game maker, crafter, and gardener. Special interests include theater and stage magic, liturgical music, sociocultural history, flowering plants and trees, and live action role playing.
people.name: Merav Hoffman

people.bio: Mia Ginaé Watkins is a public speaker, writer, and award-winning filmmaker whose work in video games spans a decade. When it comes to public speaking, Mia has moderated and produced industry panels and roundtables at the Game Developers Conference, D.I.C.E., New Zealand Game Developers Conference, Emerald City Comic-Con, San Diego Comic-Con, Los Angeles Comic-Con, WonderCon, DreamCon, Music and Gaming Fest, and Music and Gaming West. She is currently working on a fantasy novel. Creativity, empathy, and storytelling are at the core of everything she does and what she plans to do next.
people.name: Mia Ginaé

people.bio: Mia V. Moss (they/them) is a science fiction & fantasy author from the Pacific Northwest, now living in the SF Bay area. They are the author of the cli-fi noir novella, MAI TAIS FOR THE LOST, and the upcoming epic fantasy novel, THE HERESY OF THIEVES. When they’re not writing, they enjoy running around feral outdoors, DMing tabletop campaigns, mixing cocktails, making big art, and admiring their enormous TBR pile. They would be delighted to share her cookies and gin.
people.name: Mia V. Moss

people.bio: Micaiah Johnson is the Compton Crook and Carl Brandon Award-winning author of The Space Between Worlds. Her debut novel was a Sunday Times Bestseller, an Editors’ Choice at The New York Times and was named one of best books of 2020 and one of the best science fiction books of the last decade by NPR. Her follow-up novel, Those Beyond the Wall, has been named one of NPR’s Best Books of 2024 and was a finalist for the Ursula Le Guin Prize. In her academic life she studies race, the unhuman, and death — topics she explores in her upcoming horror novel, The Unhaunting.
people.name: Micaiah Johnson

people.bio:
Michael Cassutt is a writer, producer and director with credits on many SF-Fantasy series, from THE TWILIGHT ZONE and MAX HEADROOM to THE DEAD ZONE and Z-NATION. He has also published 8 novels, most of them SF (THE STAR COUNTRY, the HEAVEN'S SHADOW trilogy with David S. Goyer) as well as fifty short stories for such publications as ISAAC ASIMOV'S SF MAGAZINE, THE MAGAZINE OF FANTASY & SCIENCE FICTION, and the former Tor.com.

He is also an expert on the history of human spaceflight, publishing two dozen articles and six books, most recently THE ASTRONAUT MAKER.

In 2024 he wrote and director a short film titled THE SUMMER MACHINE, based on a story by George R. R. Martin and starring Lina Esco, Matt Frewer and Charles Martin Smith.
people.name: Michael Cassutt

people.bio: Michael Damian Thomas is the nine-time Hugo, British Fantasy, World Fantasy, and Parsec Award-winning Publisher and Editor-in-Chief of the Locus Award-winning Uncanny Magazine and the Content Editor of the It's Storytime with Wil Wheaton podcast. Michael was a Hugo Award finalist as the former Managing Editor of Apex Magazine (2012-2013), co-edited the Hugo Award finalist essay anthology Queers Dig Time Lords (Mad Norwegian Press, 2013) with Sigrid Ellis, and co-edited the anthology Glitter & Mayhem (Apex Publications, 2013) with John Klima and Lynne M. Thomas. Michael was formerly the full-time caregiver of his late daughter, Caitlin. Caitlin had a rare congenital disorder called Aicardi syndrome.
people.name: Michael Damian Thomas

people.bio: Mike Donahue is a California native and an alumni of the USc School of Cinematic Arts. He has been active in fandom since 1981 when a flier for the first L-5 convention blew across campus and wrapped around his ankle, refusing to let go until he noticed Robert Heinlein was the GoH. Complications ensued for many decades and across many conventions and locales both real and imaginary. In the mundane world he worked in film post production and eventually for his sins became a film director and DGA member. He has directed 5 feature films and written, produced, and directed 2nd unit on several others. He hopes after working in film production for more than 45 years he will someday become an overnight success. No matter how hard fandom tries, he persists in attending conventions and offering unsolicited advice to anyone who will listen.
people.name: Michael Donahue

people.bio: Michael is a disabled, award-winning audio director known for his work on The Secret of St. Kilda and a department editor for the Strange Horizons. Based near Glasgow, Scotland, Michael works with audio for fiction, film and podcasts.
people.name: Michael Ireland

people.bio: Michael J. DeLuca is an environmental justice hermit, guerilla ranger and forager of invasive plants. His debut novel The Jaguar Mask was a Small Spec Book Award finalist. His novella Night Roll was a finalist for the Crawford Award. He publishes and edits for Reckoning, a journal of creative writing on environmental justice, and he runs the indie ebookstore Weightless Books. A son of Boston bricklayers, he lives in the post-industrial woodlands north of Detroit with partner, kid, cats, and microbes.
people.name: Michael J. DeLuca

people.bio: Michael Michel lives in Oregon with his wife and their "mini-me" children. When he isn't obsessively writing, he can be found exercising, exploring nature, enjoying comedy, or playing Warhammer. His favorite shows are Dark, The Wire, and Scavenger's Reign—clearly, he loves his heart to be abused. If you are foolish enough to challenge him in table tennis, he will gladly destroy you.
people.name: Michael Michel

people.bio: Michael Sinatra teaches English in NYC. He's edited the occasional book and helped write a few, including Draco Minimis: The World of the Little Dragons. He's currently working on a book about financial literacy and personal finance.
people.name: Michael Sinatra

people.bio: Michael Solis is Executive Director of Writers & Books, a literary arts center in Rochester, NY, where he leads programs, festivals, and community initiatives supporting writers at every stage. He is the author of the award-winning YA sci-fi novel Deficient, with its sequel, Feral Rising, forthcoming in 2026. A queer Latinx writer, his speculative fiction explores power, identity, and transformation. Michael has written for SFWA’s Planetside, serves as Co-Chair of the SFWA Middle Grade & Young Adult Committee, and sits on the Board of Directors of the Publishing Triangle.
people.name: Michael Solis

people.bio: Michael Stearns is the founder of Upstart Crow Literary. A former editorial director for HarperCollins, he has edited hundreds of best-selling, award-winning F&SF novels, among them books by Michael Grant, Diane Duane, Ursula K. Le Guin, Jane Yolen, Frances Hardinge, and more. He also runs a book packager where he co-created the #1 bestselling series FALLEN, as well as several dozen other titles. And, under the pen name Carter Roy, he is the author of the award-winning middle-grade fantasy adventure trilogy the Blood Guard.
people.name: Michael Stearns

people.bio: Michelle was the Exhibits Division Head for Seattle Worldcon 2025 and has held numerous positions at Norwescon including Publications Director, Member Services Director, and Secretary. Her special passion project is the Norwescon Little Free Library book exchange, where thousands of books get rehomed each year. She reviews contracts by day, prowls the Seattle goth scene by night, looks for any excuse to wear elf ears, and lives by the creed, “I read, therefore, I am.”
people.name: Michelle Morrell

people.bio: Michelle Witte is a literary agent with Mansion Street Literary Management, a boutique literary agency based in New York. As an agent, Michelle’s tastes vary widely, and she represents authors across the spectrum of books for all ages, from illustrated board and picture books to middle grade, young adult, new adult, and adult speculative fiction. Michelle is always on the lookout for fascinating stories that are well told, especially those with a distinct and distinctive voice. Her own published work includes Happy Little Accidents: The Wit and Wisdom of Bob Ross, and The Craptastic Guide to Pseudo-Swearing. Though she travels whenever possible, she mostly splits her time between Utah and New York.
people.name: Michelle Witte

people.bio: Michi Trota is a five-time Hugo Award-winning Filipino American writer, editor, and critic. Her work explores understanding identity through pop culture and using storytelling for collective liberation and empowerment. She is the Executive Editor at Green America and her publications include the Wing Luke Museum 2018-19 exhibit text for Worlds Beyond Here: Expanding the Universe of APA Science Fiction and Uncanny Magazine. She’s been featured in The Guardian, Chicago Tribune, and CNN: Philippines. Michi is part of the Filipino Young Leaders Program 2022 cohort and an alumna fire performer with Raks Geek/Raks Inferno Fire+Bellydance.
people.name: Michi Trota

people.bio: Midori is a sexuality educator, author, and artist specializing in BDSM topics. She is the founder of ForteFemme Women's Dominance Intensive. She also trains therapists through the Sexual Health Alliance. Her work moves between writing, teaching, and art. Her speculative fiction includes Master Han's Daughter and Silk Threads, co-authored with Cecilia Tan and Laura Antoniou. She authored The Seductive Art of Japanese Bondage, the first English-language book on Shibari, and Wild Side Sex: The Book of Kink. She will have art featured in the WorldCon Art Show, and will teach at the Stockroom on August 29th.
people.name: Midori

people.bio:
Miguel O. Mitchell, PhD (he/his/him) is a Black speculative poet, SFF author, visual artist, and retired chemistry professor. His poems have appeared in Amazing Stories, Dreams & Nightmares, Eye to the Telescope, FIYAH, Sauúti Terrors anthology, Scarlet Dragonfly Journal, Scifaikuest, Space & Time, Star*Line, and the anthology Year’s Best African Speculative Fiction (2022). Two of his poems were nominated for the 2022 Rhysling Award in the Long Poem category. Miguel has also published two poetry collections, Surrealia (Gnashing Teeth Publishing, 2024), Second Place winner in the 2025 Elgin Awards for Best Full-Length Speculative Poetry Book, and Periodic Table of Alien Species (Elements 1-86) (Barnes & Noble Press, 2021). He was the Editor of the 2025 Dwarf Stars anthology, was Co-editor (with David C. Kopaska-Merkel) of the 2023 Dwarf Stars anthology, and is Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of SpecPoVerse: An International Journal of Speculative Poetry (https://specpoverse.org).

In addition to poetry, Miguel has published the flash fiction stories "Finding the Path: (Space & Time 152 (July 2026)) and "Trading with Monsters" (Fantasy (Psychopomp) 90 (April 2023)) and the short stories "The Revenant Saga" (Scarlet Leaf Review, 10/9/2021) and "Synchronicity Redux" (Dirty Magick Magazine 22 (June 2026)).
people.name: Miguel O. Mitchell

people.bio: Mike is an animator, storyboard artist and director with over 20 years of experience in the industry. After working at Soup2Nuts in Boston for several years, he moved to Los Angeles for work at Nickelodeon and Warner Brothers.
people.name: Mike Nordstrom

people.bio:
Mike served 4 years in the U.S. Air Force as an Electronic Warfare Systems Specialist. After his service he began working at TRW Space & Technology (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems) from which he recently retired after almost 41 years.

Mike joined The Heinlein Society in 2001 and is a lifetime member. He is a member of THS board of directors. He previously chaired the blood drive committee and is currently the scholarship chair.
Mike lives in Long Beach, CA with his wife, Sharon. He has a predilection for wearing kilts, much like Lazarus Long.
people.name: Mike Sheffield

people.bio: Millie Abecassis is a writer of adult speculative fiction from France. She is a graduate of the Panthéon-Sorbonne University and now works in the biotech industry. Millie lives in San Jose, California with her spouse and their cats. You can learn more about her writing and other endeavors at www.millieabecassis.com.
people.name: Millie Abecassis

people.bio: Miriam Weinberg is a fan of many books, most people, and all dogs. As a nearly two decade publishing industry veteran, she was most recently an Executive Editor at Tor Publishing Group.
people.name: Miriam Weinberg

people.bio: Misha Grifka Wander (he/they) is a writer, designer, and editor based in the American Midwest. They obtained a PhD in English from the Ohio State University focusing on contemporary global speculative fiction and catastrophe. Currently, they work in operations at SFWA and serve as part of the editing collective for Hugo-nominated magazine Ancillary Review of Books.
people.name: Misha Grifka Wander

people.bio: Mitchell Burnside Clapp is the founder of Pioneer Rocketplane, which begat Rocketplane Limited. He graduated from MIT in 1984 with two degrees in Aerospace Engineering, one in Physics, and another in Russian. In 1988 he graduated from the USAF Test Pilot School. He has been an aerospace CEO, a DARPA program manager, and currently is the chief of aircraft design at Atropos group. He is also the winner of several Pegasus awards for filk music.
people.name: Mitchell Burnside Clapp

people.bio: M.J. Kuhn is a fantasy writer by night and a mild-mannered marketing employee by day. She is the internationally bestselling author of Among Thieves and Thick as Thieves and cohost of the SFF Addicts podcast and the FanFiAddict Book Club. She lives in the metro Detroit area with her very spoiled cats, Evie and Thorin Oakenshield. Find more information on M.J. on her website, www.mjkuhn.com.
people.name: M. J. Kuhn

people.bio: Molly O’Neill is a fantasy author and engineering geologist. She was born and raised in the Cotswolds and moved to Australia in 2019. She now lives in Sydney, on the land of the Bidjigal People. Molly writes fantasy books inspired by the beautiful landscapes of her two countries, and by the folklore of the British Isles. She particularly loves the darker Arthurian legends and the Welsh myths of the Mabinogion and often uses them as a foundation for her stories. Her works so far are Greenteeth and Nightshade & Oak
people.name: Molly O'Neill

people.bio: Mona Tewari has long been fascinated by the ways in which the narratives of legends and histories shape our views of the present. A graduate of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) and UCSF, Tewari practiced as a pediatric dentist for years before turning to writing fiction in her favorite genre: fantasy. As the daughter of two immigrants from India, she didn’t see herself represented in popular media while growing up and became determined to show her daughters they belong in every world.
people.name: Mona Tewari

people.bio: While being rained on near Portland, Oregon, Monte Lin edits, writes, and plays tabletop roleplaying games and writes short stories. His stories have been published at Cossmass Infinities, Cast of Wonders, Flame Tree Press anthologies, and others. His nonfiction has been published at Strange Horizons. He is managing editor of Uncanny Magazine and is an alum of the Clarion West and Tin House workshops. He can be found posting Doctor Who news, Asian American diaspora discourse, and his board game losses on Bluesky @montelin.bsky.social.
people.name: Monte Lin

people.bio: Morag Hannah, together with Erin Hardee, writes under the penname MK Hardy. With backgrounds ranging from higher education to science communication to ghost tours, they are devoted to storytelling in every aspect of their lives and work. Works: The Needfire (Solaris, 2025), The Haunting of Avis Lovelock (Solaris, 2026), Splasher (as Billie Host, Penguin 2026).
people.name: Morag Hannah

people.bio:
Morgan Hazelwood writes from her lair in Northern Virginia. She's been sharing tips from the big names, the medium names, and everyone else on 'Writing Tips & Writerly Musings' since 2015, first as a blogger, now as a streamer and podcaster. An actively querying fantasy author, her short story, Just a Hike In The Woods was published by the Dark Recesses Webzine in January of 2022.

When not writing, you can find her binge reading paranormal gay romances, learning to scroll saw, and taking pictures of the sky.
people.name: Morgan Hazelwood

people.bio: Moriko Handford is an author from Upton, MA. While not at work, she's bringing her family on wacky adventures. Her Substack is where she publishes videos and writings about various topics. Her most recent publication is a graphic novel called The Gold Ceiling about a ban of individuals having more than $1 billion in wealth. Moriko also has a memoir, A Trans Feminist's Past, and before that, she wrote a sci-fi trans romance called Flipping under her pen name, Forest Handford.
people.name: Moriko Handford

people.bio: M.T. Zimny is a young adult author out of the Pacific Northwest, where she subsists off of rainy days and ungodly amounts of overpriced coffee. Her writing is largely inspired by her background in human phsyiology, and she believes all the best fantasy is rooted in real-world science.
people.name: M.T. Zimny

people.bio:
My name is Muaiyd Abu Ali
I’m a physiotherapy supervisor at hospital Kings College, Londo Jeddah, I like to read science satisfaction stories, and I have a novel called the legend of the autogram it’s published since 2019 and translated to 5 language ..
people.name: Muaiyd Abu Ali

people.bio:
An inaugural inductee of the Podcast Academy’s Hall of Fame, Mur Lafferty began podcasting in 2004 and used the new medium to build a writing career from her work as a science fiction podcaster.

Mur has written 10 novels, 8 novellas, and 1 nonfiction book ranging from Star Wars to space murder mysteries to cozy fantasy. After winning the 2013 Astounding Award for Best New Writer, her work has been nominated for the Hugo, Nebula, Parsec, Philip K. Dick, Manly Wade Wellman, and Podcast Peer Awards. Her podcast Ditch Diggers, with Matt Wallace, won the 2018 Best Fancast Hugo Award.

With Valerie Valdes, Mur is the editor of eight-time Hugo finalist semiprozine Escape Pod.

Her nonfiction work has appeared in Knights of the Dinner Table and on the podcast The Dragon Page. In 2014, she received an MFA in popular fiction from the Stonecoast program at the University of Southern Maine.

She lives in Durham, NC, with her husband. She likes video games, tabletop games, murder mysteries, and dogs.
people.name: Mur Lafferty

people.bio: Myle Yan TAY is a writer of plays and prose. His debut novel, catskull, won Book of the Year and Best Literary Work at the Singapore Book Awards and was shortlisted for the Singapore Literature Prize. His plays Statement Piece and Brown Boys Don't Tell Jokes were staged by Checkpoint Theatre; both were nominated for "Best Production" and "Best Script" at the Straits Times! Life Theatre Awards. He has published essays, reviews, and fiction in The Hong Kong Review, The Cincinnati Review, The Chicago Reader, and more. He co-hosts "Comic Sans," produced by Andas Productions, an award-winning podcast about comics for those who are sans knowledge.
people.name: Myle Yan Tay

people.bio: Naomi Evelyn is a neurodivergent Teen and Technology Librarian, freelance writer, singer/songwriter, and artist with work published in Inklings Literary Magazine. In her spare time, she enjoys sculpting, making music, bookbinding, playing tennis, traveling, and many other creative hobbies. She is currently working on getting her upmarket speculative fiction book traditionally published, while doing freelance writing and illustration on the side.
people.name: Naomi Evelyn

people.bio: Naomi Novik has written the Scholomance trilogy, the novels UPROOTED and SPINNING SILVER, and the Temeraire series. She is a founder of the Archive of Our Own. She is currently working on an upcoming series called Folly, while building Wreccer in her copious free time. Her next publication will be a novella from Del Rey called THE LAKE WITCH.
people.name: Naomi Novik

people.bio: Natalie Wang is a Singaporean poet who writes about cats, ghosts, and womanhood, and maintains that they are all the same thing. Her debut collection of poetry The Woman Who Turned Into A Vending Machine is a book on womanhood and metamorphosis, and a tribute to the fox spirits and vengeful ghost women she read about as a child.
people.name: Natalie Wang

people.bio: Natania Barron believes in monsters and hopes you do, too. She’s the author of short stories, novellas, and over a dozen novels. All of these works contain monsters of one variety of another, but not all of them wear monstrous skins. She is also 1/3 of the Hugo-nominated Worldbuilding for Masochists podcast. When not traveling through imagined worlds, she lives in North Carolina with her family, where she traipses through the forest on a regular basis, bakes incessantly, drinks an inordinate amount of tea, and dreams of someday owning a haunted house of her own.
people.name: Natania Barron

people.bio: I have had a fascination in the paint world as I watched my parents make a successful living painting murals in their studio in the back of our house. I was 13 yrs old my first mural. I studied at CSUN and graduated with a BA and began my journey in the studios starting with CBS Television City. I have worked many major studios including Nickalodeon, Cartoon Network, Paramount, Sony, Warner Bros, Universal, ABC, Disney, NBC, Burbank Studios, Sunset Bronson, Red studios, etc, and for not only shows but theaters such as the Ahmanson, the Mark Taper, Dorothy Chandler, the Chaplin, the Kodak, the Dolby, Ford, etc to name off the top of my head. I am the lead at a prestigious scenery shop in North Hollywood called Centerline. I’ve done hundreds of shows and continue to thrive in this business with every job being customized to acheive their demands for entertainment. And now in my career , I have migrated to more high end events and museums where I can exploit my skills with other crafts in a themed hands on environment. Currently I am on my fourth project for the esteemed Academy Museum of Motion Picture in Los Angeles.
people.name: Nathan Duffy

people.bio: Nia "N.E." Davenport is an award-winning & bestselling Science Fiction/Fantasy and Romance author. Her recent October 2025 release, OUR VICIOUS OATHS, is a USA Today Bestseller. In addition, she's the co-founder of StorySpinner Entertainment, a book packager aimed at bringing the world fun, innovative, and inclusive stories. She attended the University of Southern California and studied Biological Sciences and Theatre. She has an M.A. in Secondary Education, she taught secondary English and Science for several years, and designs English/Language Arts curriculum for school districts across the US. When she isn’t writing, she enjoys vacationing with her family and being a huge foodie. She’s an advocate for diverse, reflective perspectives and protagonists in literature. You can find her online at www.nedavenport.com or on Threads/Instagram @nia.davenport, where she talks about binge-worthy TV, fun movies, and killer books.
people.name: N.E. Davenport

people.bio: Neil Clarke (neil-clarke.com) is the multi-award-winning editor of Clarkesworld Magazine and over a dozen anthologies, including the Best Science Fiction of the Year series. He is a four-time winner of the Hugo Award for Best Editor Short Form, four-time winner of the Chesley Award for Best Art Director, and two-time winner of the Locus Award for Best Editor. In 2019, Clarke received the SFWA Kate Wilhelm Solstice Award for distinguished contributions to the science fiction and fantasy community. He currently lives in New Jersey with his wife and two sons.
people.name: Neil Clarke

people.bio:
Neil Ottenstein obtained a PhD in theoretical nuclear physics in 1990 and since then has been working in flight dynamics for one of two NASA Goddard Space Flight Center contractors. He is currently the
contractor flight dynamics lead for the Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission.

He has been reading science fiction and fantasy most of his life, and going to science fiction conventions since 1980 (and a couple of comic book conventions before that). Babylon 5 is his favorite television program
people.name: Neil Ottenstein

people.bio: Neil Williamson is an award-winning, multi-genre writer, editor and musician from Glasgow, Scotland. His latest books are The Packet, a Scottish historical science fiction novella, and Hand-Me-Downs, a collection of horror stories about weird bequests and inheritances.
people.name: Neil Williamson

people.bio: Neo Edmund is a New York Times Best-Selling Author, Screenwriter Comic Book Scribe, and an Actor. Neo is the author of the USA Today bestselling novel series The Red Riding Alpha Huntress Chronicles. Neo's most recent works include multiple Power Rangers novels, a kids graphic novel series The Grimms Town Terror Tales, and John Carpenter's Tales for HalloweeNights. Neo has written for Hasbro, Saban, Penguin Books, Random House, History Channel, Discovery Channel, Animal Planet, Spike TV, JumpStart Interactive, Zenoscope, and Storm King Productions.
people.name: Neo Edmund

people.bio: Nero is a Seattle-based indigenous Panamanian and Mexican web cartoonist with 10+ years in the adult comics scene. His work has been published by Iron Circus Comics, COYOTE, The Nib, and more. He is also one of the founders of Cartoonists United, an organization that seeks to improve working conditions for cartoonists everywhere.
people.name: Nero Villagallos O'Reilly

people.bio: Ng Yi-Sheng is a queer Singaporean writer, researcher and activist with an ADHD-fuelled fascination with Southeast Asian history and myth. His books include the historical fantasy novel Utama and the short story collection Lion City. His fictions and essays—including the influential “Spicepunk Manifesto: Towards a Critical Movement of Southeast Asian Heritage-Inspired SFF”—have appeared in Clarkesworld, Strange Horizons, The Best of World SF and Speculative Insight. He's a two-time winner of the Singapore Literature Prize and has been a finalist for the Seiun Award and the Epigram Books Fiction Prize.
people.name: Ng Yi-Sheng

people.bio: Nick Dragon started skulking the streets of Los Angeles when it was nothing but tar pits and hippies. He writes, directs, shoots and edits narrative film, and has a fondness for weird and surreal parables. He knows what evil lurks in the hearts of men. He likes pie and vaccines.
people.name: Nick Dragon

people.bio: Nick Mamatas is the author of several novels, including I Am Providence and Kalivas!, Or Another Tempest. His short fiction has appeared in Best American Mystery Stories, Asimov's Science Fiction, Tor.com and many other venues. Much of it was recently collected in The People's Republic of Everything. Nick is also an anthologist; his latest is 120 Murders; Dark Fiction Inspired by Alternative Music. Nick's fiction and editorial work has won a Bram Stoker Award and had been nominated for World Fantasy, Shirley Jackson, and Locus awards.
people.name: Nick Mamatas

people.bio: Nicole Carlson was around at LACon IV, which means she is Of A Certain Age. She is recently retired from a 20+ year career in tech and is currently pursuing a second bachelors in Anthropology at CSU East Bay.
people.name: Nicole Carlson

people.bio: Nicole de Meneses is an award-winning writer, director, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. She is the founder of Dark Rainbow Films, a production company dedicated to creating independent genre films that center LGBTQ+ characters as the heroes, villains, and complex protagonists of their own stories. Her feature debut, Dead in Love, screened internationally and is available on multiple streaming platforms. Nicole also serves as Executive Director of the Blood & Popcorn Film Festival, championing emerging horror filmmakers. She is currently developing Last Bite, a sapphic vampire thriller set in San Francisco.
people.name: Nicole de Meneses

people.bio:
Nikhil Koparkar is a composer known for creating compelling scores for Film, Television, and Gaming. He is best known for composing "The Hills of Tanchico," the breakout musical number from Amazon's hit fantasy series The Wheel of Time, which has since accumulated millions of streams, spawned fan cover versions, and inspired JordanCon, the world's premier Wheel of Time convention, to name their 2026 event TanchiCon in its honor. The song was nominated for an SCL Award alongside industry luminaries such as Ludwig Göransson, Diane Warren, Ed Sheeran and John Mayer.

His work on the psychological horror film Dead Whisper, released theatrically, earning him a nomination for the prestigious SCL Awards in the David Raksin Award for Emerging Talent category.

In 2023, he wrote the official main theme for Riot Games’ League Of Legends - Lunar New Year Campaign, which is featured in all their videos, in-game, as well as the foundation for other composers’ music

He previously worked as an additional composer alongside Lorne Balfe at 14th Street Music, writing and arranging music on TV shows like Netflix’s Life On Our Planet, Amazon’s The Wheel Of Time, HBO’s His Dark Materials, and the Hulu docu-series, Victoria’s Secret: Angels & Demons.
people.name: Nikhil Koparkar

people.bio:
From playing the DM in Dungeons and Dragons to writing fantasy novels, Nikhil Prabala loves storytelling, delighting in fantasy fiction from the epic to the cozy and everywhere in between. THE DUCHESS OF KOKORA is his first published novel with STEEL EMPRESS concluding the duology and releasing in August 2026.

Born and raised in Austin, Texas, he graduated from Stanford in 2019 and is currently based in the Bay Area. In his free time he enjoys ballroom dancing, singing, playing the guitar, tabletop games, and spending time with friends and family.

To connect with him on social media, you can find him as @nprabala on both Instagram and TikTok.
people.name: Nikhil Prabala

people.bio: Noel Belknap is an Emmy nominated animation industry professional. Working since 2009 on TV shows, such as: The Marvelous Misadventures of Flapjack, Rick and Morty, Teen Titans Go, The Ghost and Molly McGee. Noel also directed and art directed the indy pilot Guys Next Door. That project led Eric Kaplan and Noel Belknap to be creative partners and form Kapknap Animation. Noel lives in Los Angeles with too many dogs and an average amount of wrist pain, for an animator.
people.name: Noel Belknap

people.bio:
