Noor Rahman writes science fiction and runs "Write on Track," a Substack about conquering writer's block and self-doubt. As a former trial lawyer who quit BigLaw to write a novel, she brings an analytical lens to the creative process—especially for neurodivergent writers. Her essays on professional rejection, career pivots, and the qualities of good fiction have sparked lively Substack-wide debates. A list of her published poems and short stories is available on noorjahanrahman.com.

She is also the founder of Verb Foundry, an independent literary studio in San Francisco building Vesper, an agentic-AI book recommendation app. Instead of leaning on bestseller lists or star averages, Vesper evaluates books across more than a dozen characteristics--the qualities that shape how immersive, lasting, and accessible stories are--and matches readers to books based on their preferences across those axes.
people.name: Noor Rahman

people.bio: Noor Tannir is a Lebanese writer, curator, and cultural practitioner currently based in New York, where she is pursuing her MFA in Creative Nonfiction at Sarah Lawrence College. She had previously worked as a Junior Curator for independent art initiative Barjeel Art Foundation in Sharjah, UAE and graduated from the American University of Beirut in 2018 with a BA in Art History and minors in Philosophy and Film & Visual Culture. Her work has most recently appeared in Şerābi Zine's 2024 zine-anthology, Ebony Tomatoes Collective's Perennial Song, mt7rk and is forthcoming in Difference Engine's anthology Free to Play (October 2026). Her manuscript was longlisted for the Azhar Writing Prize 2025, and received an honorable mention in Nightboat Books' 2025 Prose Reading Period.
people.name: Noor Tannir

people.bio: (fuller: EverythingInTheUniverse.com. Patchy: Wikipedia.org.) MA History of Science & Technology, UC Berkeley. Taught astronomy 31yr at UC Berkeley, +elsewhere. Editor, The Journal of Irreproducible Results, the science humor magazine. Knowledgeable about spaceflight (on 2 panels, WorldCon 2018); publishing books including my 2 in SF; telescopes (co-designer of Astroscan); planet crust layers; road trips; thiotimoline.
people.name: Norman Sperling

people.bio: <s>Five</s> Six-time Hugo-finalist fanzine editor and photographer.
people.name: Olav Rokne

people.bio: Olga Batygin is an AI startup and philanthropic leader with over 15 years bridging science and industry. As Director of Deep Tech and Space at XPRIZE, she partners with sponsors and internal colleagues to shape prizes that drive breakthrough innovation. She spent a decade at Caltech, first in the lab and later in administration, then co-founded and led Lucinetic, an EdTech venture she built into a GeoAI platform before selling the core IP. A published author and speaker, she also serves on the Caltech Entrepreneurs Forum executive committee, in the expert network at Fusion Fund, and on the board at G100.
people.name: Olga Batygin

people.bio: Olivia Waite writes queer historical romance, sff, and essays. She is the romance fiction columnist for the New York Times Book Review.
people.name: Olivia Waite

people.bio: Long-time fan, married at a con, father of a fan, book and game reviewer, RPG gamer, TAFF delegate, Wikipedia admin
people.name: "Orange Mike" Lowrey

people.bio: Logan Bruce has been writing science fiction novels and movie reviews since the latter years of the twentieth century.
people.name: Orbzine

people.bio: Oriana Leckert is the Head of Publishing at Kickstarter, where she helps creators bring a marvelous array of literary projects to life. She’s written and edited for Vice, MTV News, Slate, Hyperallergic, Gothamist, Atlas Obscura, and many more. Her first book, Brooklyn Spaces: 50 Hubs of Culture and Creativity, grew out of a multi-year project chronicling the rise and fall of under-the-radar creative places across New York City. Follow her at @orianabklyn on most social platforms.
people.name: Oriana Leckert

people.bio:
Palmer has been writing fiction since she was eight. She received her BA in American Studies from Wesleyan University, with concentrations in Religion and Race Relations.

She currently works in Silicon Valley in the gaming industry and high tech. In addition, Palmer holds a certificate in Chinese Acupressure, is a certified solar panel installer, and studied Tibetan Buddhism with the 14th Dalai Lama.

She lives and writes in the magical redwood forest of the Santa Cruz Mountains, California.
people.name: Palmer Pickering

people.bio: Patricia is an accomplished Fantasy artist working in watercolor. Her style is clearly influenced by the Japanese wood block prints from the Edo period called, Ukiyo-e, which translates to “pictures of the floating world,” keeping her paintings light and delicate, but with the bold colors and patterns typical of the latter end of that period. She pursued her love of art through two degrees, BFA at the University at Buffalo and a MA at Syracuse University. In 2002, she began exhibiting in art shows all across the country and has won numerous awards for her Japanese style work. In addition, she and her husband, Michael Sinatra, wrote and illustrated, Draco Minimus: The World of the Little Dragons and recently Patricia wrote and illustrated, Watercolor the Essential Guide for Beginners. Patricia continues to show at convention art shows and lives in New York City with her family. You can see more of her art at www.patriciamccrackenart.com
people.name: Patricia McCracken

people.bio: Patricia Taylor is a member of and volunteer with the Renegade Bookbinding Guild. Over the last four years she's bound more than 200 books, ranging from fanfic to artist's books to literary classics.
people.name: Patricia Taylor

people.bio: Patrick Nielsen Hayden was a full-time SF & fantasy editor at Tor Books for 37 years. For his original anthology Starlight 1 (Tor, 1996), he won a World Fantasy Award; he also won three Hugo Awards for his editorial work. With his wife, Teresa Nielsen Hayden, he's among the regular instructors at the Viable Paradise writers' workshop. He and Teresa were among the guests of honor at the 2016 Worldcon.
people.name: Patrick Nielsen Hayden

people.bio: Originally from NYC where I was working mainly as an actor on stage. I started making small shorts to create my own work. Since moving to LA I've been focusing more on film and on expanding those shorts. I've always been a fan of fringe historical events. Stories based in reality but have some fantastical element are what I'm drawn to. Being able tell a fantastical story rooted in the real world with practical effects is what excites me as a filmmaker. I'm a fan of Sci-Fi and old B-movies and love exploring their worlds.
people.name: Patrick Pizzolorusso

people.bio:
Fanzine fan / professional graphic artist, designer, and editor; first fanzine published in 1977. Awards of note:
  • "Best Fanzine" Hugo Award, 1988, for The Texas SF Inquirer
  • "Best Special Publication" FAAn Award, 2021, for Outworlds 71 / Afterworlds, with co-editors Jeanne Bowman, Alan Rosenthal, Rich Coad, and (posthumously) Bill Bowers
  • "Best Special Publication" FAAn Award, 2022, for the Daangerous Visions faanthology, with Sandra Bond and Rob Jackson
  • "Best Special Publication" FAAn Award, 2026, for Dancing to Architecture (edited by Doug Bell, design/layout by Pat Virzi)
people.name: Pat Virzi

people.bio: I have been attending conventions since Noreascon in 1971, am a filker, military space systems veteran, and long-time convention volunteer. I served as a pocketbook holder for the many people on stage in the Mad Three Party costume entry at LA Con in was it 1984? (I'm one of the original members of MCFI, parent corporation of various conventions including Noreason II, Noreascon 3, and Noreascon 4)
people.name: Paula Lieberman

people.bio: Dr. Paul Frommer, creator of the Na’vi language for James Cameron’s Avatar franchise, is Professor Emeritus of Clinical Business Communication at USC’s Marshall School of Business. He is also principal co-author of Looking at Languages, a workbook for elementary linguistics classes. Frommer has worked on the Na’vi content of the three Avatar movies and the video game, Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora, and continues to expand the language for an international community of Na’vi enthusiasts. He also developed Barsoomian, the Martian language for the film John Carter.
people.name: Paul Frommer

people.bio:
Biography for Paul Henry Fresco, the Wizard of Weird--Futurism and Surrealism Artist
As an Experimentalist, Paul's work is a combination of futurism, expressionism, nature, android and human body forms. He juxtaposes the realistic next to the mechanical. He uses bold colors in his abstracts and surrealistic artworks, and soft colors that reflect nature in other works. He primarily paints in acrylics on canvas, and explores collages. He is an master jeweler and creates unique designs in sterling, utiling a variety of beautiful stones and CZ's.
Paul is concerned about the future. "Technology continues to advance at quantum speeds which many humans cannot assimilate. (Don't you hate trying to use the AI customer serivce lines?)". His androids also wonder about their futures...will they continue to be objective, or will they bcome more sensitive, with emotions, like humans?
Paul gets some of his ideas from old sci-fi movies and dreams eternally affected by ether that was administered to him during surgeries as a child. Yes, they persist. He also has lived in New York, Ohio, Arizona, Alaska, Norway, and now is back in California where he is a Studio Artist at Destination: Art in Torrance, and a Gallery Artist at the Orange County Fine Arts Showcase Gallery. He and his wife Carol Anne, a photographer, live in the South Bay area.
You can purchase his work from fresco-creations.net, Etsy, Ebay, and at saatchiart.com.
people.name: Paul Henry Fresco

people.bio: Paul Kwinn has been involved in filk music for 36 years, winning a Pegasus Award. He has recorded two albums with his group Puzzlebox: "Assembly Required" (available on Spotify) and "Tumbleweird" (available on Bandcamp).
people.name: Paul Kwinn

people.bio: Paul Weimer is an award nominated fan writer and podcaster who has been active in the Science fiction community for over a decade,.
people.name: Paul weimer

people.bio:
Pedro Iniguez is a Mexican-American Bram Stoker, Elgin, and Dwarf Stars Award-winning science fiction and horror writer from Los Angeles, California. Pedro’s expansive work covers poetry, short fiction, novels, children’s literature, comics, nonfiction, and essays.

He is the author of Mexicans on the Moon: Speculative Poetry from a Possible Future, The Build-A-Monster Workshop, Fever Dreams of a Parasite, Echoes and Embers: Speculative Stories, and The Fib, his debut picture book, among others.

Apart from leading writing workshops and speaking at several colleges, he has also been a sensitivity reader and has ghostwritten for award-winning apps and online clients.
people.name: Pedro Iniguez

people.bio: Perrianne Lurie is a long time fan who ran the Green Room for Balticon for many years. She was the Hugo Ceremony director for Torcon 3 and the Email Liaison and Deputy Program Division Director for BucCONeer. She is active in strategy (Euro) board gaming and has GMed at Euroquest, Prezcon and other gaming conventions. She watches way too much television and (mostly art house) movies. She retired from the Pennsylvania Department of Health in 2020, where she was a public health physician and infectious disease epidemiologist. She now lives in suburban Maryland.
people.name: Perrianne Lurie

people.bio: Peter Adrian Behravesh is an Iranian-American writer, editor, audio producer, and narrator, as well as a story lead for Magic: The Gathering. For these endeavors, he has won the Miller and British Fantasy Awards and has been nominated for the Hugo, Ignyte, and Aurora Awards. His interactive novel Heavens’ Revolution: A Lion Among the Cypress is available from Choice of Games, and his essay “Pearls from a Dark Cloud: Monsters in Persian Myth” appears in The Oxford Handbook of Monsters in Classical Myth. He co-edited the Iran+100 anthology. You can read his sporadic ramblings at peteradrianbehravesh.com, or on Bluesky @behravesh.
people.name: Peter Adrian Behravesh

people.bio: A leading innovator in computer architecture, Peter Glaskowsky helped found, fund, and build x86 microprocessor startup Montalvo Systems. He was a computer architect at Esperanto Technologies, a machine-learning semiconductor company in Silicon Valley. He is a co-inventor on 30 U.S. patents, has authored two books on computer graphics, co-authored two books on space elevators, and has been active in science fiction fandom for 50 years.
people.name: Peter Glaskowsky

people.bio: Petrusha (Peter Polygalov) is a newer member of the SCA who enjoys archery, heavy combat, crafting, and brewing.
people.name: Peter Polygalov

people.bio: Petrea Mitchell is a lifelong fan of all sorts, currently a reader, gamer, and writer of the newsletter SMOF News (smofnews.substack.com).
people.name: Petrea Mitchell

people.bio:
PHILIP FRACASSI is a USA Today bestselling, Bram Stoker and British Fantasy Award-nominated author of six novels, three story collections, and more than twenty published short stories.

His work has been translated into numerous languages, and his stories have appeared in publications such as Best Horror of the Year, Nightmare Magazine, Interzone, and Southwest Review.

His screenplays have been produced by Disney and Lifetime, and his work has been optioned by multiple studios and production companies.
people.name: Philip Fracassi

people.bio: Phoenix Alexander (he/him) is a queer, Greek-Cypriot author and curator of SF/F and horror. He is the Editor-in-Chief of Vector: the Journal of the British Science Fiction Association, and has published over 30 short stories and articles. He holds a Ph.D. in English and African American Studies from Yale University, and a BA and MA from Queen Mary, University of London. In his day job, he is the curator of the Eaton Collection of Science Fiction and Fantasy at the University of California, Riverside, where he stewards one of the world’s largest cataloged collections of science fiction, fantasy, and other genre materials.
people.name: Phoenix Alexander

people.bio: After spending 20 years in Hawaii as a public health nurse and nurse educator, Phyllis Eide returned to her home state, Washington, to finish out her academic career at Washington State University College of Nursing. In 2010, she completed a certificate in Climate Change from University of Washington, and has done presentations on climate change and health to senior nursing students for over 15 years.
people.name: Phyllis Eide

people.bio: Porscha is a poet and genre-bending writer and artist with a love for Afrofuturism and the speculative. She's an RPG enthusiast and a dreamer of worlds. She is a graduate fellow of The Watering Hole Poetry and the author of the poetry collection "Low Bridge High Water" Her writing has appeared in the award winning anthology "Ask: Building Consent Culture" as well as in Callaloo, ANMY, and other publications. Keep up with Porscha on her website Porschawrites.com and on her Substack of the same name.
people.name: Porscha Simmons

people.bio: A 2016 MBA graduate and published author, Priya Sridhar has been writing fantasy and science fiction for fifteen years, and counting. Capstone published the Powered series, and Unnerving Press published Offstage Offerings. Priya lives in Miami, Florida with her family
people.name: Priya Sridhar

people.bio:
Rachanee Lumayno is an actress, voiceover artist, screenwriter, avid gamer and amateur dodgeball player. She grew up in Michigan, where she spent way too much of her free time reading fantasy novels. So when she decided to try her hand at writing a book, it made sense that it would be in her favorite genre. The Kingdom Legacy series marks her debut as an author.

Her first novel, Heir of Amber and Fire, was named a Best Book Winner for Young Adult - Fantasy/ Sci-Fi in the 2024 Spring PenCraft Seasonal Book Awards.

Visit rachanee.net for more info and to join the newsletter or find her at rachaneelumayno on Instagram.
people.name: Rachanee Lumayno

people.bio: Rachel Gutin is a writer and special education teacher. Her short fiction has appeared in a number of publications including Escape Pod, Cast of Wonders, and Baffling Magazine. She lives in Brooklyn, NY, and is a member of the organizing team for Brooklyn Speculative Fiction Writers. You can find her online at rachelgutin.wordpress.com.
people.name: Rachel Gutin

people.bio: Rachel Hartman is the author of five YA fantasy novels, most notably SERAPHINA, TESS OF THE ROAD, and AMONG GHOSTS. She lives, writes, curls, and walks her whippet in Vancouver, BC.
people.name: Rachel Hartman

people.bio: Rachel thinks that now is an excellent time for us all to be kind to each other. Yes, really. Oh, and tell your cat she said hi. Her fiction is published in places like PseudoPod, On Spec, and The Quiet Ones' 2025 Annual. You can find links to her work at www.rachelunger.com and her occasional thoughts about writing at @rachelunger.bsky.social.
people.name: Rachel Unger

people.bio: Rae White is a queer non-binary transgender writer, and author of Milk Teeth (UQP 2018), Exactly As I Am (UQP 2022), and All the Colours of the Rainbow (Lothian Children’s Books 2025), with illustrations by Sha’an d’Anthes. They won the Thomas Shapcott Poetry Prize, and have been shortlisted for the Prime Minister’s Literary Awards, Queensland Literary Awards, and Victorian Premier's Literary Awards. Rae is the Creative Director and Founder of Uplift Poetry, a community poetry initiative; Founding Editor of #EnbyLife, a journal for non-binary and gender diverse creatives; and a co-host on the 4ZZZ radio show Tranzmission.
people.name: Rae White

people.bio: Rain Vega is a nonbinary, disabled, neurodivergent, Latine writer living in South Texas. Their previous poems have appeared in The Sagebrush Review and tend to focus on mental health, magical realism, and dreams. You can find them @rainvega.bsky.social
people.name: Rain Vega

people.bio: Rajeev Prasad is a physician and speculative fiction writer. His stories appears regularly in Clarkesworld and The Magazine of Fantasy and Science fiction with several reprints and anthologies.
people.name: Rajeev Prasad

people.bio: Greetings! I'm R. A. Meenan. I'm a University-level English professor, celebrating 15 years in teaching, and a Magepunk author publishing since 2016. I'm the author of The Zyearth Chronicles, a dark magepunk fantasy touching on difficult topics like redemption, grief, prejudice, and more, all wrapped in a theme of community and working together for the greater good.
people.name: R. A. Meenan

people.bio: Randee Dawn is the bestselling author of the funny pop culture fantasy "Tune in Tomorrow" (Rebellion/Solaris) and its 2026 follow up in the "Tune"-iverse, "We Interrupt This Program." In 2025 her dark fantasies "The Only Song Worth Singing" and "Leave No Trace" were published by ArcManor/Caezik. A veteran entertainment journalist for The LA Times, Variety and Today.com, Randee hosts the Brooklyn Books & Booze monthly reading series and hosts a seminar about "How to Be Interviewed." She lives in Brooklyn.
people.name: Randee Dawn

people.bio: Randy Smith has been hanging around Fandom for over forty-five years. During that time he has helped run conventions, written for fanzines, pubbed an APAZine, collected books, comics, and old prozines, and been involved in more fanac than he cares to think about. His interests include fan history and culture, social change, and religion. If you see him around the convention in a clergy collar, it is not a costume. He is also an ordained United Methodist pastor serving a church in San Jose, California.
people.name: Randy Smith

people.bio: Raven (she/her) is happiest when reconstructing food from literature (of the 19th century or space variety), constructing fantastical garments (of the 19th century or space variety), frolicking in a ballroom (of the 19th century or space variety), and finding ways to combine all three. You can find her discussing dance scholarship (of the 19th century and space variety) in short video form on TikTok @plaidpetticoats.
people.name: Raven Stern

people.bio: Ray Tabler is a published author of humorous science fiction and fantasy. Originally from Louisville, KY, Ray chased the northbound dollar and lodged in the frozen wilds of Michigan. His four published novels are available from Histria Books. His short fiction has appeared in Baen's Universe, Cosmic Crime Stories, Escape Pod, and various anthologies.
people.name: Ray Tabler

people.bio: Rebecca A. Demarest (she/her) is an award-winning author, poet, playwright, book designer, and writing instructor living in Seattle, WA with her husband and three muppets. Her work has appeared alongside authors like Cat Rambo, been dramatized for the stage and NPR, and her novels are available at your favorite bookstore. When not being held hostage by words, you can find her at her day job, tending to her indoor jungle, crafting, sewing, playtesting tabletop role playing games, and failing to teach her dogs new tricks. For more information on her work, please visit rebeccademarest.com or follow on BlueSky @writerlybliss‬.
people.name: Rebecca A. Demarest

people.bio: Rebecca Inch-Partridge works as a freelance editor for over eight years. She wrote her first novel, Saver Rebecca Meets Captain Kirk, when she was in 3rd grade. Since then, she’s gone on to have three novels published. Abby’s Fire: A Mt. Prospect Mystery is a paranormal, mystery, romance that she co-authored with her aunt. Escaping the Dashia and the sequel Hunting the Dashia are YA science fantasy novels set in the Paraxous Star Cluster. Rebecca is also a writing coach and a writing instructor, who teaches a “Write that Book in Ten Week” workshop through Sierra College. She loves helping writers turn their lumps of coal into diamonds. Ripartridge.com
people.name: Rebecca Inch-Partridge

people.bio: Rebecca Matte is a literary agent and contract manager at Bradford Literary Agency, representing YA and Adult SFF and romance. In her other life, she works as an attorney for the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and manages a small legal practice focusing on IP and contract issues. She spends most of her time playing board games and ttrpgs with friends in NYC and online.
people.name: Rebecca Matte

people.bio:
Rémy is a life-long space enthusiast and science communicator, always ready and eager to talk all things galactic, stellar, planetary, or even alien! What started with library rentals of Magic School Bus VHS tapes led to a degree in astronomy and atmospheric science, as well as a passion for education and outreach.

She worked as a planetarium operator, presenter, manager, and script writer/performer before becoming a Network Operations Project Engineer for the Deep Space Network, helping dozens of spacecraft talk to us back here on her favorite planet, Earth.
people.name: Rémy Morgan

people.bio: Renée Camus is a dancer, teacher, and choreographer in the Los Angeles area who focuses on English country dancing (ECD; the style seen in Jane Austen movies). She writes new English country dances, and teaches classes in ECD, ballroom, historical dance, and other dance styles. She just published a new book of English country dances and created an accompanying 2-CD set of recordings to go with them, both called Choreograffiti. She’s also a writer and editor.
people.name: Renée Camus

people.bio: Reuben "Tihi" Hayslett is a queer storyteller, author and activist. His sci-fi novel, Orbital Bebop, is published by RIZE, an imprint of Running Wild Press. His debut short story collection was named Best Indie Fiction by Kirkus in 2019. Hayslett is currently the Executive Director of the Center for Story-based Strategy.
people.name: Reuben "Tihi" Hayslett

people.bio:
Rhiannon "Gibbitt" Rhys-Jones has been attending conventions since 1991 She's worked on them, and spoken at them. She is also an editor, a wordsmith, a gamer, and a loyal servant to a cat.
She has worked every position you can think of in conventions. Thanks to her sister, Bobby DuFault. She asked her to go to a concom meeting for her, so she went, and has not looked back since. Her brother, Gene Armstrong got her back into it after her husband passed in 2021.
She and her husband started Dragondyne Publishing in 2001, and in 2009 came out with Neverwhen which was a love letter to RPGs.
Gibbitt plans on being on con coms until she physically can't.
people.name: Rhiannon "Gibbitt" Rhys-Jones

people.bio:
Ric Bretschneider is a technologist, trouble maker, and problem solver whose interests outstretch his available time by a significant magnitude. When adulting, he splits his time between attempting to raise the quality of the world's business communications, particularly presenting, and a love of software design and development. A professional software developer for decades, your computer likely has at least one application he's worked on.

The rest of the time he obsessively collects geek activities. Lately he's been into pro and fan applications of e-communities and podcasting. He's proud of the over the nearly 700 podcast episodes he produced and contributed to over the last two decades. When he has a moment, Ric reads books and comics, and plays analog board, card games and retro video games. He's here to help people, it's what he does.
people.name: Ric Bretschneider

people.bio: I am best known for my voice acting, mostly for Sierra Online. But I did plenty of game programming and design as well, and am the author of "Eric and the Gazebo". I can easily fit on any panel involving humor or games. I have been on many panels for Worldcons past. I got a standing ovation at the Adventure Fan Faire in 2004. Use me if you want. I am there all convention.
people.name: Richard Aronson

people.bio: Richard Gilliam is a veteran writer/editor. He's worked widely in both fiction and non-fiction.
people.name: Richard Gilliam

people.bio: Richard H Moon is an award-winning screenwriter, producer, family man, care-provider for several dogs and cats, a curler, archer, hiker, musician, physics tutor, SFF nerd, literature aficionado, history obsessive, and kitten fosterer. He has a physics degree, but has never let that get in his way. He’s always ready to geek out about story and character and deep meaning and also cool robots, and he supports every human out there who is making art with their own hands and bodies and minds. He lives with his family in Southern California, on the ancestral and unceded land of the Hahamongna people.
people.name: Richard H Moon

people.bio: I am a Tai Chi instructor and Chinese calligrapher.
people.name: Richard Man

people.bio:
Born in England, Richard started out as a writer of plays, revues and TV, for such shows as Not the Nine o’Clock News. Rowan Atkinson performed his Schoolmaster sketch in John Cleese’s The Secret Policeman’s Ball. To celebrate Rowan’s 70th birthday, the Schoolmaster sketch was nominated in The Guardian in January 2025 as Number One in a list of Rowan's Top Ten film appearances.

 UK TV credits include The Famous Five, The Flying Kiwi, The Optimist, The Worst of Hollywood, and a lifetime of script editing. On being hired by Columbia Pictures TV, Richard moved with his family to Los Angeles in 1992 to work with Blake Hunter and Marty Cohan, creators of Who’s the Boss? His lyrics have been recorded by talents as diverse as Dom de Luise, Eric Idle, Vanessa Williams, Plácido Domingo and Hello Kitty. He directed Jack Black in Stravinsky’s The Soldier’s Tale (LACMA). Richard has written libretti for several new operas produced by the LA Opera, with composer Lee Holdridge (composer of movies such as Splash and Old Gringo, and TV shows Beauty and the Beast, Moonlighting, et al.). Richard has also written new English versions of German and Italian classic operas.

New Rock New Role (2023) was Richard’s fiction debut. New Rock New Realm, the second book in the New Rock fantasy adventure series, was published in 2024, followed in 2025 by New Rock New Rules. The concluding book in the story, New Rock New Roads, will be published in November 2026.

Full credits (and reviews, and free chapters) at www.richardsparks.com.
people.name: Richard Sparks

people.bio:
Richard Swan is a critically acclaimed British genre writer. He is the author of the Sunday Times bestselling Empire of the Wolf and Great Silence trilogies, the Decurion Saga (2026), and short fiction for Black Library and Grimdark Magazine. His work has been translated into nine languages.

Richard is a qualified lawyer, and before writing full time spent ten years litigating multimillion pound commercial disputes in London. He currently lives in Sydney with his wife and three young sons.
people.name: Richard Swan

people.bio: Rich Horton is an editor of anthologies, including a Best of the Year collection from Prime Books that ran from 2007 through 2021, and a forthcoming anthology of philosophical SF from MIT Press. He also writes essays and reviews at his Substack.
people.name: Rich Horton

people.bio: Rio Lombana writes speculative fiction from Seattle, where they like to hike in the dry season and train martial arts while it rains. Raised in the Carolinas in the Southern Baptist church, they are the apostate eldest daughter of a Latina mother and a white father. Their work is published in Escape Pod, PseudoPod, Heartlines Spec, Small Wonders, and elsewhere. They're a Viable Paradise 2025 alum and NYC Midnight winner. Find them at riolombana.com and everywhere online @riolombana.
people.name: Rio Lombana

people.bio: River is a MediaWiki developer best known for having built much of Leaguepedia, the League of Legends esports wiki. Over the years, she's contributed to hundreds of gaming and fiction wikis as well as the chainmaille wiki, which she founded in 2025 as a replacement for mailleartisans.org. River loves talking about the divide between structured and unstructured data and ways to make community knowledge sharing more accessible to everyone. She has a blog at https://river.me.
people.name: River

people.bio:
R. James Doyle (aka Richard J. Doyle) held technical and managerial roles in Information and Data Science at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) over a career arc spanning forty years. He worked primarily at the exciting interface of space exploration and computer science, with a focus on autonomous space systems. He remains an active technical consultant.

Richard holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science specializing in Artificial Intelligence from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). He was a member of a JPL team that consulted on the Babylon 5 sci-fi TV Series in the 1990s. He had the pleasure of visiting Sir Arthur C. Clarke in Sri Lanka, in the year 2001.
people.name: R. James Doyle

people.bio: Laurraine Tutihasi has been reading sf&f since 1951 and discovered fandom in 1973 after attending her first convention, a worldcon. She has published fanzines, attended and worked on numerous conventions, participated in local clubs, belonged to numerous APAs, written reviews and other articles for fanzines, and even sold some artwork. She is currently a member of ANZAPA and StippleAPA and publishes her own fanzine, which is distributed on paper and in PDF format. In her other life, she has been a librarian and a programmer, among other things, and is currently retired and living in Arizona.
people.name: R-Laurraine Tutihasi

people.bio: R.L. Lynn is a former high-school and college math teacher who has had a passion for writing since a young age but only found the time, ironically, after becoming a new mom. She now finds time to write in between working as an online math tutor and stay-at-home mom. She can both cut a rug on the ballroom floor as well as wield an epee. She possesses a vivid imagination and a deep desire to spread messages of hope and empowerment in a world that can sometimes seem awash in negativity. She enjoys writing fantasy fiction with strong female protagonists, romance, and fast-paced plots. Her debut novel, STEPSISTERS, the first book in a twisted fairytale trilogy, was published October 2025.
people.name: R.L. Lynn

people.bio:
RM Ambrose is a speculative fiction writer and the editor of Vital: The Future of Healthcare. He is SFWA Associate Member, an receveived his MFA from the Stonecoast Creative Writing program with dual concentrations in Popular Fiction and Scriptwriting, and attended the Taos Toolbox writer’s workshop.

His short story, “Olive Branch,” appeared in Friends Journal’s 2024 annual fiction issue.

Multiple works that he’s edited have made Year’s Best anthologies, such as Justin C. Key’s “The Algorithm Will See You Now,” as well as stories by Julie Nováková and Simone Heller (from Future SF Digest #8, which he guest edited). Two original stories from Vital (Key’s, as well as Seanan McGuire’s) are finalists for the Dinjos Award for disability representation in speculative fiction. For several years he also served as Assistant Fiction Editor at the Hugo award winning StarshipSofa podcast.

RM’s short fiction has received two Writers of the Future Award honorable mentions, and his essays have appeared in numerous Southern California newspapers and Friends Journal.

He is a lifelong Quaker and pacifist, holds a 1st degree black belt in Aikido, studied Anthropology and speaks three languages, and has over two decades’ experience in web and software development.
people.name: RM Ambrose

people.bio:
Robert is the author of the Hugo Award-winning novel The Tainted Cup and its sequel A Drop of Corruption, as well as The Divine Cities trilogy and The Founders Trilogy.

His work has received the Edgar Award, the Shirley Jackson Award, and the Phillip K. Dick Citation of Excellence, and he has been shortlisted for the World Fantasy, British Fantasy, and Locus Awards. He also dug a very good french drain in his backyard back in 2019.
people.name: Robert Jackson Bennett

people.bio: Robert James has published numerous articles on Golden Age science fiction and five books about the movies, and spent a decade helping to research the Robert Heinlein biography. He found the lost manuscript of Heinlein's first novel, For Us, the Living, and currently holds the record for most panels at any convention ever: 21 at the Heinlein Centennial. He has been teaching for almost forty years, with a doctorate from UCLA and an enormous amount of patience...
people.name: Robert James, Ph.D.

people.bio: Robert J. Sawyer, a guest of honor at the 2023 Worldcon, won the 2003 Hugo Award for best novel of the year (for *Hominids*) and has twelve other Hugo nominations to his credit. He's also won the best-Novel Nebula Award (for *The Terminal Experiment*) and a record-setting 16 Canadian Aurora Awards, plus the Robert A. Heinlein Award and NESFA's Skylark. Rob is a member of the Order of Canada, the highest honor given by his country. The ABC TV series *FlashForward* was based on his novel of the same name, and his latest novel is *The Downloaded 2: Ghosts in the Machine*.
people.name: Robert J. Sawyer

people.bio: Robert Mitchell Evans has been a sailor, a dishwasher, a shipyard worker, a cashier, and currently his day-job is in the non-profit healthcare industry. He resides in San Diego, California and can frequently be found haunting southern California SF conventions. His SF/Noir novel Vulcan's Forge was published by FlameTree Press in March 2020 and he is a member of SFWA & HWA.
people.name: Robert Mitchell Evans

people.bio: Robert Silverberg has been a professional science fiction writer since 1955. He has won a number of Hugo and Nebula awards, was Guest of Honor at the 1970 Worldcon, and was named a Grand Master by the Science Fiction Writers of America.
people.name: Robert Silverberg

people.bio:
Robin Hobb is best known for The Farseer Trilogy (Assassin's Apprentice, Royal Assassin and Assassin's Quest) and the sequels in The Realm of the Elderlings. Robin Hobb also writes as Megan Lindholm. In 2017, San Diego Comic Con awarded her an Inkpot award for her works. In 2021, she was awarded the World Fantasy Lifetime Achievement award.
She resides in rural Washington State and enjoys gardening on her smallholding with chickens, ducks and geese.
people.name: Robin Hobb

people.bio: I work in strategic communications with a decade of experience with integrated campaigns and audience development across global institutions, international clients, and mission-driven organizations. Drawing on both professional experience and academic research in creative economies, I approach storytelling as both an artistic and strategic practice. My research examines how intellectual property, cultural assets, and storytelling contribute to economic development, innovation, and global influence.
people.name: Rochele Rosa

people.bio: Rogelio Fojo is an Uruguayan-born filmmaker, former award-winning journalist, and science writer whose work bridges science fiction and cinema. After studying filmmaking in Los Angeles, he directed the Kodak-funded, award-winning short film Chimera, followed by other acclaimed shorts including Mary, The Movie Pitch, and The Stooge, written by Christopher Priest and starring Robert Picardo. His current project is One Million Times, an ambitious sci-fi/time travel series developed with JPL scientist R. James Doyle and now expanding into a collaborative anthology published by Elsewhen Press.
people.name: Rogelio Fojo

people.bio:
Deeply rooted in the sci-fi genre, Ronald D. Moore got his start in the entertainment business on the writing staff of Star Trek: The Next Generation. During his tenure there, he wrote or co-wrote 27 episodes, including the two-hour series finale “All Good Things,” for which he won the prestigious Hugo Award in 1994. That same year, Moore was honored with an Emmy® Award nomination and was eventually promoted to Producer.

In 1994, Moore joined the writing staff of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine as Supervising Producer and was elevated to Co-Executive Producer the following year. Moore spent five seasons on the series until the end of its successful run in 1999.

Moore also served briefly as Executive Consultant on the USA cable series Good vs. Evil before joining the staff of Roswell as Executive Producer. After two seasons in that post, he took over the reins as Showrunner from Creator Jason Katims in its final year.

In the fall of 2002, Moore was named Showrunner and Executive Producer of HBO’s critically acclaimed one-hour drama Carnivàle.

In 2003, Moore created the re-imagined series, Battlestar Galactica, and served as Showrunner/Executive Producer of the series, which ran for four seasons. Battlestar Galactica was honored with a prestigious Peabody® Award and twice as an official selection of the AFI (American Film Institute) top television programs for 2005 and 2006. The debut episode, “33,” won Moore his second Hugo Award, alongside director Michael Rymer, for Best Dramatic Presentation, Short Form. In 2006, Moore was nominated for an Emmy® Award for Best Writing in a Dramatic Series, and in 2008, he won an Emmy® for the Battlestar Galactica webisodes.

In 2008, Moore co-wrote the pilot to the spin-off series Caprica, a drama set 58 years before the events of Battlestar Galactica. He served as Executive Producer for the run of the series.

In 2010, Moore’s production company, Tall Ship Productions, signed an overall deal with Sony Television to develop and produce television series, including the Golden Globes®-nominated historical fantasy series Outlander for Starz, based upon the bestselling novels by Diana Gabaldon, and the original science fiction alternative history series For All Mankind for AppleTV+. He also served as Executive Producer on the Amazon/Channel 4 anthology series, Philip K. Dick’s Electric Dreams, as well as the SyFy original series, Helix.

After a decade working at Sony Television, Tall Ship Productions inked an overall deal with Disney’s 20th Television from 2020-2024, and has now returned to Sony Television once more to begin a new overall deal as of June 2024. Under the Tall Ship banner, Moore is currently producing both Outlander and its prequel series Blood of My Blood, as well as For All Mankind and its own spinoff series, Star City.

Moore is a native of Chowchilla, California and attended Cornell University, where he studied political science. He lives in California with his wife, Terry. He has three children – Robin, Roxy and Jonathan.
people.name: Ronald D. Moore

people.bio: Ron Kaiser ;has taught high school and college writing classes for 20 years. His teaching and writing have been featured on the Chicken Soup for the Soul podcast, NH Chronicle, NH Magazine, and other places. He published his debut fantasy novel, Mystralhaven, this year, through Fantastic Books out of New York, and he has published more stories in Chicken Soup for the Soul than anyone--20. He is a regular at Boskone in Boston, and will presenting his book as well as moderating panels there this February. He has had many adventures as a teacher. He has been surrounded by the police on a field trip, and he once chased a completely naked student (who painted red from head to toe, and who had invaded their homecoming pep rally) through the streets. He is also a veteran of the Army National Guard, though the only action he saw was punching an aggressive raccoon. He lives and teaches in Moultonborough New Hampshire with his forgiving wife, incredible son, and incorrigible cats.
people.name: Ronald W Kaiser

people.bio:
Ron Oakes is a self-published fantasy writer and, sometimes, a science fiction writer. He has published works under his own name and as Randall Fox through Kindle Direct Publishing and elsewhere.

As Ron Oakes, he has written works in a traditional high fantasy setting, The Northlands. The Northlands have seen nearly 2000 years of peace following the end of The Last War, where the forces of The Free Kindreds—elves, dwarves, and men—fought back against the forces led by the rebellious Rai—angelic beings created by The God Alilun—Yurmbrear.

The first of these stories, The Phoenix Knives, is available.

As Randall Fox, he has written shorter works set in a furry setting resembling the European Renaissance. This world features an eclectic mix of anthropomorphic animals living together in a united society. It blends adventure, politics, and a bit of daily life as we follow Randall through his adventures.

Several novellas in this series are now available, starting with Flight of the Heretics.
people.name: Ron Oakes

people.bio: Roseanna Pendlebury is a London-based reviewer mainly interested in scifi and fantasy, but occasionally prone to dabble in historical and mythological fiction. She is currently an editor at Hugo and Ignyte award winning fanzine Nerds of a Feather, has a column on small press novellas at the Ancillary Review of Books and has her own blog at readerofelse. When not reading, she can be found watching rugby, making bookmarks and generally collecting too many crafting hobbies.
people.name: Roseanna Pendlebury

people.bio: Rosemary Claire Smith is the 2023 winner of the Sidewise Award for Alternate History for Apollo in Retrograde. Her first novel, Saurotopia, was just published. She is also a four-time finalist for Analog Magazine's readers' award. Her book review columns appear in every other issue of Analog Magazine. Somehow, her alternate histories, future romances, time-travel tales, reworked mythologies, horror stories, and essays have snuck onto the pages of Amazing Stories, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Fantastic Stories, The Reinvented Heart, The Reinvented Detective, and other periodicals and anthologies. Rosemary's stories draw upon her fascination with dinosaurs, her experiences as a field archaeologist excavating prehistoric sites around the United States. Her RPG, T-Rex Time Machine is available from Choice of Games. Follow her on social media @RCWordsmith and www.rcwordsmith.com for her recent works, upcoming appearances, and thoughts on recent dinosaur discoveries.
people.name: Rosemary Claire Smith

people.bio: Dr. Ross Mead is the Founder and CEO of Semio AI, an LA-based robotics software startup, and Executive Director of Semio Community, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit for human-robot interaction science. He holds a PhD in Computer Science from USC. His research on socially assistive robots and computational modeling of social behaviors provides foundations for Semio's software. Dr. Mead serves on the Board of Directors for AI LA and the KISS Institute for Practical Robotics, promoting AI and STEM literacy. He has advised companies including Disney, National Geographic, and Intel, and was a cast member on Syfy's Robot Combat League.
people.name: Ross Mead

people.bio:
R. P. Singletary's 120,000-word experimental/ecological debut novel SPEAK SOFTLY AMONG ICEBERGS out Shakespeare Day (that's April 23rd) 2026 from ATL's queer indie press Parlyaree. "A stunning exploration of family, ecology, addiction, life, and what we leave behind. His writing, told from multiple voices and perspectives within the same page or paragraph, is like poetic theater: meant to be read aloud," according to its publisher. "Singletary has created something unique, ambitious, and unlike anything else on the shelf....A bold, imaginative work that showcases a remarkable literary voice." --Goodreads reviewer
SINGLETARY writes across genres as a rural America native and dabbles in other media. Authors Guild + Dramatists Guild.
people.name: R. P. Singletary

people.bio:
RUSSELL DAVIS has written and sold in virtually every genre of fiction, under many pseudonyms. He has written or ghost written in many media tie-in worlds, including Transformers, Twilight Zone, and The Librarian. His original novels were almost noticed and his short fiction has appeared in anthologies like Under Cover of Darkness and In the Shadow of Evil. He has worked as an editor and book packager, creating original anthology titles ranging from westerns like Lawless to fantasy like Courts of the Fey. His most recent releases include a re-issuing of the Jenna Solitaire series and he’s working on a new collection.

He was the president of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA) from 2008 - 2010, and is currently the Operations Director.
people.name: Russell Davis

people.bio: As a child, Russell’s fate was sealed the evening his parents took him to see Star Wars. Practically obsessed with spaceships, robots and dragons for his entire life, he pursued a career in animation. Eventually he stumbled into a new group of friends, who went on to create the award winning web-series Adventures of the League of S.T.E.A.M. The League also gave him his first taste of writing, winning “Best Screenplay” in the 2017 Dublin Web Festival as a result. Encouraged by that experience, he finally got around to writing his first book.
people.name: Russell Isler

people.bio:
Russ Nickel is an award-winning screenwriter and narrative designer, and the co-founder of OmniMegaSuperCorp, the indie studio behind the upcoming comedy RPG Ledgerbound.

He was lead writer on the smash-hit Helldivers 2 and co-founded Tappity, a gamified education platform with over 100,000 users.

When he's not writing, he's probably escaping a room, playing Magic: The Gathering, or drinking what he swears is his last coffee of the day.
people.name: Russ Nickel

people.bio:
Ruth Frances Long / Jessica Thorne writes romance and fantasy from the heart which often strays into weird and wonderful liminal places. She works in a specialized library of rare & occasionally crazy books.

As Ruth Frances Long she writes fantasy, often about scary fairies. In 2015 she won the European Science Fiction Society Spirit of Dedication Award for Best Author of Children’s Science Fiction and Fantasy for A Crack in Everything. Her latest series Feral Gods, an adult fantasy trilogy from Hodderscape featuring “an alternate-Renaissance fantasy world and inspired by the early days of printing in Europe” begins with The Book of Gold, continues with The Lore of Silver (November 2025) and finishes with The God of Bronze (November 2026). The Book of Gold was longlisted for the 2025 BSFA award and was selected for the Locus Recommended Reading List for 2024.

As Jessica Thorne she writes adult fantasy women’s fiction, which wanders from Space Opera to time travel to epic fantasy, including The Lost Queen trilogy (A Touch of Shadows, A Kiss of Flame and A Crown of Darkness), The Water Witch, The Bookbinder’s Daughter, The Lost Girl’s of Foxfield Hall, The Queen’s Wing, The Hollow King duology (Mageborn and Nightborn). The Stone’s Heart was nominated for the Romantic Novelists’ Association Romantic Fantasy novel of the year in 2020. Her Irish gothic romance Wildewood came out in January 2026and her new series with Boldwood begins 14 September 2026 with The Teacup Dragon Sanctuary.
people.name: Ruth Frances Long / Jessica Thorne

links.othersocialmedia: Also on instagram and Facebook as JessThorneBooks

people.bio:
Ryan Cahill is the Sunday Times and USA Today Bestselling author of the epic fantasy series, The Bound and The Broken.

Born and raised in Ireland, Ryan spent some years honing his craft amongst the rolling hills and hobbit holes of Middle-Earth, New Zealand, before returning home to conquer the world.

There are three things Ryan has always told himself about writing. Write the books you want to read. Write the books that your younger self would be proud of you for reading. Make sure they have dragons.
people.name: Ryan Cahill

people.bio: Ryan Nichols is a professor of philosophy at Cal State Fullerton. He is first author of a book (with F. Miller & N. Smith) called Philosophy Through Science Fiction. His data science work includes a 2014 paper (w/ B. Purzycki and J. Lynn) that was presented at the Reno worldcon called "Toward a Science of Science Fiction." He lives 6.2 miles away from the Anaheim C.C.
people.name: Ryan Nichols

people.bio:
Ryan is the author of Seven Recipes for Revolution and the What We Eat trilogy. After escaping his hometown in Central Florida, Ryan began
studying to become a chemical engineer. He was sure he would one day be an asteroid miner. Since then, he's worked in game design, Broadway musical production, and even taught English to
middle schoolers. Ryan lives in Oakland with his partner and their dog, which may be a demon. He now works to defend democracy at UC Berkeley, which still doesn't involve chemical engineering.
people.name: Ryan Rose

people.bio: Ryan Snopek is a history PhD candidate at York University in Toronto. His research focuses on ordinary people understood the relationship between science, spirituality, and ideology in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
people.name: Ryan Snopek

people.bio: Sadie Milla graduated from UNC Greensboro with a BA in Religious Studies, and now supervises two group homes for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. She finds that developing visual aids, learning clients’ communication styles, thinking about religion, and interpreting speculative fiction all use the same corner of her mind. Sadie lives in Chapel Hill with her spouse and two cats (one sweet and one terrible).
people.name: Sadie Milla

people.bio:
Sagan Yee (he/they) is a queer media artist whose practice roams restlessly across animation, games, speculative fiction, art installation, fandom, and community organizing. From 2016 to 2020, they were the executive director of Hand Eye Society, a Toronto-based videogame arts non-profit. In 2026, he got his MFA in Design Media Arts from UCLA, where he was also an event coordinator at the UCLA Game Lab. Their stories have appeared in places like Best Microfiction, Tales & Feathers, Apex, and Lightspeed.

Most recently, Sagan participated in the Manufactured Ecosystems anthology initiative, which pairs climate scientists with writers to envision speculative applications of biomimicry technologies. Sagan’s current project is Last Call for the Redding District, a narrative videogame about spawning mermaids.
people.name: Sagan Yee

people.bio: Salinee Goldenberg is a speculative fiction writer and multimedia artist who lives in Washington DC, and is drawn to outsider perspectives. She is the author of The Last Phi Hunter and Way of the Walker, published by Angry Robot. A biracial, bisexual, diaspora writer, Sal often explores themes of identity, obsession and alienation in her work. Previously, she worked at Bethesda Softworks creating narrative trailers for games such as Skyrim, Fallout 4 and Dishonored, and now produces videos for Minecraft. When not writing, she likes to paint, listen to records, and play in punk bands.
people.name: Salinee Goldenberg

people.bio: Sally Wiener Grotta (she/her), is an award-winning writer, photographer, and speaker. Her two newest books are Of Being Women, (NobleFusion Press), feminist science fiction tales, and Daughters of Eve (Bayit Publishing), an essay collection. Her experience as a globetrotting journalist covering a wide diversity of cultures flavors her stories, art, and presentations with a sense of wonder, appreciation for human potential, and a healthy dose of common sense. She is the host of Judith Magazine’s Tell Me More interview podcast, and a member of The Authors Guild and SFWA. Visit her at SallyWienerGrotta.com and SallyWienerGrotta.substack.com.
people.name: Sally Wiener Grotta

people.bio: Samantha Mills is an award-winning science fiction and fantasy author living in Southern California. Her short story, "Rabbit Test," won multiple awards in 2023. Her science fantasy novel, The Wings Upon Her Back, won the Compton Crook Award for best SFFH debut and was a finalist for the World Fantasy Award for Best Novel in 2025. Her first short story collection, Rabbit Test and Other Stories, is available now! You can find more at www.samtasticbooks.com.
people.name: Samantha Mills

people.bio: Samantha Haney Press is an award-winning artist based in the Midwestern US. She's worked as an art director, printer, and game store clerk, and in her free time, she helps run conventions, serves as the secretary of the Association of Science Fiction & Fantasy Artists, and writes a lot of fanfiction.
people.name: Sam Haney Press

people.bio: Sam Scheiner is a long-time fan and scientist. His scientific areas of expertise are ecology and evolution, where he has published 11 books and over 120 scientific papers. He has also co-authored a book with SF author Phyllis Eisenstein on arthritis. He has retired from the U.S. National Science Foundation where he worked giving away money, but continues as an active researcher. He is a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science and recently received the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Society for the Study of Evolution.
people.name: Sam Scheiner

people.bio: Sandra Rosner is an author, lore writer, IP manager, TTRPG producer, developmental editor, and co-host of the 3RPG Podcast who works primarily in fantasy, horror, and sci-fi. Her published works include: World of Warcraft: The Dragonflight Codex & Runescape: the Official Cookbook. When not crafting worlds of her own, Sandra enjoys tabletop, MMORPGs, and streaming her gameplay on Twitch as LadyvonFrost.
people.name: Sandra Rosner

people.bio: Sandy is a long time fan and has been involved in costuming since she was about 15. She is also into educational technology, regular technology, and enjoys reading science fiction and fantasy.
people.name: Sandy Manning

people.bio: Sara Callori is a physics professor at California State University San Bernardino, where she has been since 2015 after a two-year stint shooting neutrons at things in Australia. Her research background is in experimental studies of nanometer-scale magnetic and ferroelectric films. In addition to her scientific work, she is the co-host of the Frenemy Trivia podcast and has been on four game shows, including Jeopardy! and Wheel of Fortune.
people.name: Sara Callori

people.bio: Sara is a Hugo award winning mixed media artist and president of ASFA.
people.name: Sara Felix

people.bio:
Sara Hashem is the USA Today and Sunday Times bestselling author of The Jasad Heir and The Jasad Crown. An Egyptian-American writer from California, Sara has lived in five cities and three countries, but her love of fantasy and magical realms emerged during the years her family lived in Egypt.

When she isn’t busy rewatching her comfort shows or desperately trying to keep her plants alive, Sara can be found buried under coffee-ringed notebooks.
people.name: Sara Hashem

people.bio: Sarah Gulde is a four-time Hugo Finalist, a three-time Honorary Citizen of Disneyland, and a diehard Trekkie. She lives in a former arboretum in Portland, OR.
people.name: Sarah Gulde

people.bio: Sarah Langan's a three-time Stoker Award-winning writer, whose novels (A BETTER WORLD, GOOD NEIGHBORS, THE MISSING, etc.) have made best of the year lists at NPR, Newsweek, The Irish Times, AARP, and PW. Her short stories have appeared in NIGHTMARE, F&SF, WIRED, Year's Best Horror, Year's Best Dark Fantasy and Horror, Year's Best Science Fiction and Fantasy, etc. She has an MFA from Columbia University, an MS in Environmental Health Science/ Toxicology from NYU, and lives in Los Angeles with her family. Her sixth novel TRAD WIFE is coming from Tor UK on May 14, 2026 and via Atria/S&S in the US on September 29, 2026.
people.name: Sarah Langan

people.bio: Sarah Pinsker is the Hugo, Nebula, and Philip K Dick Award winning author of A Song For A New Day, We Are Satellites, Sooner or Later Everything Falls Into the Sea, Lost Places, Haunt Sweet Home. She also has over sixty works of published short fiction, including "Where Oaken Hearts Do Gather." She is a singer/songwriter with four albums on independent labels and author-in-residence for the Kratz Center for Creative Writing at Goucher College. She lives in Baltimore, Maryland with her wife and two weird dogs.
people.name: Sarah Pinsker

people.bio: Sarah Rees Brennan was born in Ireland by the sea. In a previous life she was a New York Times bestselling, Lodestar finalist, Carnegie nominated writer of YA fiction. Her first work of adult fantasy, the portal fantasy LONG LIVE EVIL, was on the New York Times 2024 Best of Fantasy as a ‘careening meta-fantasy delight,’ was a #1 Sunday Times bestseller and a USA Today bestseller, and a Locus finalist. She’s written tie-ins for Netflix, Disney and Marvel. The sequel to LONG LIVE EVIL, ALL HAIL CHAOS, is out now. Talk to her about villains or musicals!
people.name: Sarah Rees Brennan

people.bio: Sarah Sward has over fifteen years of administrative experience. She’s worked for all sizes of companies and in all types of positions. Currently, she’s an independent admin who works for Hugo & Nebula winning author, Mary Robinette Kowal, and the Hugo winning podcast, Writing Excuses. In her spare time she is working on her novel and making stickers. Sarah lives in the land of 10,000 lakes with her husband, 4 cats, and is constantly fighting the battle of where to put all her yarn.
people.name: Sarah Sward

people.bio: Sara Itka is a born and raised South Floridian, meaning she believes “Fall” is when a hurricane comes and blows leaves off the trees. When she isn't working through her seemingly infinite To Be Read list, she can usually be found procrastinating working on her seemingly infinite To Be Written list. Her favorite procrastination methods include procrasti-linguistics, procrasti-making-youtube playlists-for-projects, procrasti-dancing-to-the-playlists, and procrasti-brewing-tea. If you want to help her procrastinate, come find her at saraitka.com!
people.name: Sara Itka

people.bio:
Sara Light-Waller is an independent archivist, writer, and illustrator whose work focuses on the material, cultural, and psychological history of early science fiction and adventure literature. She holds an M.A. in Anthropology from the University of Arizona, with a specialization in zooarchaeology, and a B.A. in Anthropological Archaeology from Bryn Mawr College. While at Arizona, she served as a teaching assistant in zooarchaeology and historic archaeology and studied scientific illustration under Donald B. Sayner, one of the country’s most respected scientific illustrators and educators, whose emphasis on accuracy, observation, and visual literacy deeply informs her approach.

Light-Waller approaches pulp magazines, fan cultures, and early genre fiction as archaeological strata rather than curiosities, emphasizing context, historical mindset, and audience reception. She is the founder of Lucina Press and the host of The Rocketeer podcast, which examines science fiction not only as imaginative literature but as a cultural survival mechanism during the interwar and wartime years.
people.name: Sara Light-Waller

people.bio: S.B. Divya (she/any) is a lover of science, math, fiction, and the Oxford comma. She is the award winning author of The Alloy Era duology and the novel Machinehood. Her short stories have appeared in numerous magazines and anthologies, and she is a former editor of Escape Pod, the weekly science fiction podcast. She has been a finalist for the Nebula, Hugo, Ignyte, and Locus Awards. Divya holds degrees in Computational Neuroscience from Caltech, and Signal Processing from UC San Diego.
people.name: SB Divya

people.bio:
A graduate UC Berkeley and Chapman University, Scott Russell is a writer, editor, screenwriter, and creative consultant whose work spans film & television, comics, prose, and education. As Senior Editor for Fox Kids Magazine, Scott helped bring iconic properties like Spider-Man, Goosebumps, and The Tick to life in print, shaping stories for millions of young readers. His screenwriting credits include award-winning short and feature films and he has written for Disney Imagineering, the History Chanel, Warner Interactive, and dozens of independent production companies. His prose work ranges from literary novels to science fiction and fantasy stories.

A longtime contributor to the Southern California literary and arts scene, Scott has also developed writing programs, taught composition and storytelling at the college level, and produced media content for national nonprofits. He has won dozens of awards for his writing, including the ProMax Gold Medalion, GDC Writer’s Night, and NYCMidnight. He is currently finishing Spirits of the Glenwood, a novel with magical realism elements, and Changeling, a folkloric fantasy novel.
people.name: Scott David Russell

people.bio: Scott Edelman has published 135+ short stories in magazines and anthologies, many of which have been collected in These Words Are Haunted, What Will Come After (a finalist for the Shirley Jackson Memorial Award), Tell Me Like You Done Before, Things That Never Happened (about which Publishers Weekly wrote, "his talent is undeniable"), and (most recently) 101 Things to Do Before You're Downloaded. He is an eight-time Bram Stoker Award finalist. Additionally, he is the host of the Hugo Award-nominated Eating the Fantastic podcast, which since February 2016 has allowed listeners to eavesdrop on his meals with science fiction, fantasy, and horror creators.
people.name: Scott Edelman

people.bio: Scott Kilburn is the author of the dark fantasy novels “Summoning a Lost Fey’ and ‘Consort to a Dark Fey’. He was inspired to write the novels after trips to Scotland researching ghosts, the fey, and other spirits. He is also a visual effects artist and supervisor who has worked on over fifty features, television, and streaming productions including ‘Life of Pi’, Peter Jackson’s ‘King Kong’, ‘Doom Patrol’, and ‘Twisted Metal’. He lives in Southern California with his wife and a cat-sized dog. When he’s not writing he enjoys searching for unique single malt scotches as the spirits move him.
people.name: Scott Kilburn

people.bio: Scott Lefton is an artist and engineer in Melrose, Massachusetts. His art focuses on sculptural and useful metal, wood, and glass, plus Photoshop. He is occasionally serious about photography. His engineering work involves consulting in the areas of new product design and mechanical design, plus prototype fabrication. He does electronics when necessary, mostly as Arduinos used for electromechanical control applications. He has a well equipped workshop and a major tool buying habit, which 3D printers have insinuated their way into. Art informs his engineering, and engineering informs his art. He created the 2004 Hugo base and the half-scale Hugo rocket that was displayed on the ISS. His current obsessions include developing better ways of precision forming stained glass sheets into complex 3D shapes.
people.name: Scott Lefton

people.bio: Scott Lynch was born in St. Paul, Minnesota in 1978, the first of three brothers. Early in life he worked as a dishwasher, a waiter, a graphic designer, an office manager, a cook, and a game supplement self-publisher before accidentally selling his first novel, The Lies of Locke Lamora, in 2004. From 2005 to 2016 Scott also served as a paid-on-call firefighter in Wisconsin. Scott currently lives in Massachusetts with his wife, award-winning SF/F novelist Elizabeth Bear, plus four cats (Duncan, Gurney, Molly, and Fafhrd) and a pair of Icelandic horses (a gelding named Ormr and a mare named Spola).
people.name: Scott Lynch

people.bio: Scott is a professional software developer in the chemistry field and an amateur maker of robots, Star Wars props, small electronics
people.name: Scott MacHaffie

people.bio: Scott Woodard has written for TV, audio, tabletop roleplaying games, fiction, and nonfiction. He began his career in film as a practical special effects fabricator and puppeteer before moving on to work in television as a Promax Award-winning promo writer/producer for Warner Bros. and Disney. His other work includes Doctor Who and Dark Shadows audio dramas for Big Finish Productions, tabletop RPGs for Pinnacle Entertainment Group including the Flash Gordon Roleplaying Game, and a nonfiction guide to sword and sorcery films for Green Ronin Publishing. Scott is a Full and active member of the SFWA.
people.name: Scott Woodard

people.bio: Seanan McGuire writes things. Good luck making her stop. Seriously, good luck. Heroes have failed and fallen.
people.name: Seanan McGuire

people.bio: Sean writes short fiction, particularly science fiction. A high school student living in Shanghai, he enjoys experimenting with diverse narrative styles and storytelling forms. To him, science fiction is not simply a genre of speculation about turmoil, luck, or conspiracies in the future. Instead, it is an optimistic act of imagination- one that helps us envision and shape the world we hope to create.
people.name: Sean Feng

people.bio: Launching a new sf/f publisher, Sean is joining his lifelong love of science fiction and fantasy with his experiences in brand consulting and decision support modeling to get entertaining books into the hands of readers. His interests include AI and robotics, epic fantasy, law and technology, cultural impacts, economics, biotechnology, first contacts, and the numinous.
people.name: Sean Mead

people.bio: seeley quest is a trans disabled environmentalist in Canada since 2017, Toronto since 2024, in literary, body-based, and multimedia arts and education for equity, who presented in the San Francisco Bay Area 2001-14, with Sins Invalid 2007-2015. Hir play “Crooked” is in At the Intersection of Disability and Drama, first narrative game debuted for Canada’s National AccessAbility Week 2020, and sie’s published journalism and poetry. Sie inaugurated the Quebec Writers’ Federation disabled writers’ workshop, has led “Poetry, Prose, and Dramatic Writing From the Body-Mind” for Workman Arts, and “Writing Futures With Resiliency” for the Writers’ Federation of Nova Scotia.
people.name: seeley quest

people.bio:
Shahid Mahmud is the founder and publisher of Arc Manor, one of the most decorated speculative-fiction small presses in the United States, with works that have won the Hugo, Nebula, World Fantasy, Prometheus, and other major awards. In 2021, Arc Manor published Robert A. Heinlein’s final novel, The Pursuit of the Pankera, based on a rediscovered manuscript.

Arc Manor is currently working with Mercedes Lackey on the long-awaited final volume of the Halfblood Chronicles, originally created with Andre Norton, and is helping redefine Harry Turtledove as a fantasy writer through the acclaimed City of Shadows series.

Before founding Arc Manor in 2006, Mahmud worked in finance managing multibillion-dollar portfolios for the City of San Diego, where his contributions were recognized when the Acting Mayor proclaimed November 7, 2005, as Shahid Mahmud Day.
people.name: Shahid

people.bio: Shana is a historian of technology and food. She has volunteered on four Worldcon committees and is currently chair of the Science Fiction Foundation. She collects chocolate, baked goods, and bridges.
people.name: Shana Worthen

people.bio: Shane Hawk is a horror writer, editor, and creator of the Native Horror Index. He serves as a contributing editor at Counterpoint Press, where he exclusively acquires and edits works by Indigenous North American writers. His writing career began in 2020 with the release of his short story collection Anoka. Hawk is the coeditor of the bestselling anthology series Never Whistle at Night and cowriter of the horror stage play The Land Has Spoken. He lives in San Diego, California, with his wife and daughter, and is an enrolled member of the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes of Oklahoma.
people.name: Shane Hawk

people.bio: Shantell Powell is a swamp hag and elder goth raised in an apocalyptic cult on the land and off the grid. She’s a McCormack Writing Center (formerly Tin House) scholar, and a graduate of SFU’s The Writers’ Studio and the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity’s horror residency. An Aurora finalist, and a Journey and Pushcart nominee, her writing is in The Malahat Review, The Deadlands, Nightmare, and dozens more. She wrangles chinchillas and gets filthy in the woods.
people.name: Shantell Powell

people.bio: Sharon was born in Sweden to American parents and grew up in Wisconsin near Lake Michigan. Her love of stories translated into an English degree, and then she went on to get her MA and PhD in medieval and early modern literature, and she graduated with her creative writing MFA in fiction in 2021. She is an Associate Professor of Shakespeare, medieval literature, and creative writing in beautiful Alaska, and author of the Sunday Times top-ten bestseller, Shield Maiden, published by Orbit in 2023.
people.name: Sharon Emmerichs

people.bio: Sharon Diane King (Ph.D., UCLA Comparative Literature) is Associate at UCLA's CMRS and a scholar, writer, translator, and since 1990 the director of the early modern theatre troupe Les Enfans Sans Abri. Her fiction has appeared in Die Laughing, Dark Recesses Press, Galaxy's Edge, Kaleidotrope, Creepy Podcast, All Due Respect, and several anthologies by both Third Flatiron Press and Dragon's Roost Press. Her latest academic work appears in The Post Zombie: Essays on the Current and Future State of the Walking Dead (McFarland 2025). She is owned by two small but formidable dragons.
people.name: Sharon King

people.bio: Sharon Sheffield has been a fan of genre fiction since she could read. She has degrees in Linguistics & Anthropology and Divinity. An Episcopal priest, she moonlights as a writer, historical reenactor, and musician. She loves reading, singing, crafting, and perpetrating bad puns on friends. She believes that religion and science fiction seek answers to some of the same questions, that some of the best theology right now is happening in genre fiction, and that respectful dialog is essential to keeping both religion and genre fiction vital.
people.name: Sharon Sheffield

people.bio: Writer, convention organizer, web editor.
people.name: Shaun Lyon

people.bio: Shay Kauwe is a Native Hawaiian author from Hawaiʻi. Her debut novel The Killing Spell (Saga/Solaris) was the first traditionally published adult fantasy novel by a Hawaiian writer. Her modern gothic, House of Salt (Saga), is forthcoming. Shay holds a M.Ed, was named an NCTE Early Educator of Color in 2021, and received an E OLA award from the Hawaiian Council in 2022. A member of Pacific Islanders in Publishing, Shay works to amplify the voices of writers from the Pacific.
people.name: Shay Kauwe

people.bio: USA Today and Sunday Times bestselling author Shen Tao immigrated to Canada at a young age, and grew up inspired by both Chinese and Western stories. Her debut novel, The Poet Empress, will be translated into 17 languages.
people.name: Shen Tao

people.bio: Sherwood Smith has published over fifty books, one of which was an Anne Lindbergh Honor Book; she’s twice been a finalist for the Mythopoeic Fantasy Award and once a Nebula finalist. She teaches writing at Viable Paradise Writing Workshop on Martha’s Vineyard. Website at sherwoodsmith.net, and she has a Patreon, where she posts chapters in draft.
people.name: Sherwood Smith

people.bio: Shlomi is an Austin-based author who's published short SFF/Horror stories as well as the alt-history Shmuley Myers detective thriller series under the pseudonym Sol Sharp. He also facilitates the QuickSilverQuills critique group, which includes Elizabeth Moon, David Warner, and Paige Roberts. He collaborated with Elizabeth Moon on a new novel in the Paksenarrion Universe. Horngard, due out October 6 by Baen Books.
people.name: Shlomi Harif

people.bio: Sho (they/them) is a clinical mental health therapist, drama therapist, disability justice advocate, and PhD student. Before moving into psychology, Sho worked as an editor for Edge, the largest genre fiction independent publication in Canada. At University of Michigan, Sho coded science fiction and fantasy stories for the Genre Evolution Project and served as project manager on the Re: Berman Project, which investigated and challenged claims that the golden age of science fiction is dead. Sho has done research on the therapeutic applications of role playing games has also published academically on disability justice, drama therapy, and fat identity. If the name Sho Glick sounds familiar, you may have read Robert J. Sawyer's WWW trilogy, in which Sho had the privilege of being Tuckerized. Sho identifies as fat, queer, nonbinary, white-bodied, Jewish, dis/abled, and neurodivergent.
people.name: Sho

people.bio: Sierra Branham grew up around the mountains of Alaska but now calls the mountains of Utah home. She holds a license in clinical social work and could probably talk your ear off about therapeutic modalities. Her short fiction has been published in venues such as Apex Magazine and Small Wonders and her debut novel, Love Galaxy recently released with DAW Books. When not spinning words into stories, she can be found hiking with her goats, skiing, or juggling kitchen knives. Sign up for her newsletter at www.sierrabranham.com or perceive her on Instagram at @authorsierrabranham.
people.name: Sierra Branham

people.bio: Simon Pryor is a Life Member of the Mathematical Association of Victoria (MAV). He has over 35 years experience as CEO and manager to an array of professional, education and industry associations demonstrating the all-round abilities called for in association work, from providing leadership, management and vision, through to the detail that goes into overseeing events such as the MAV Conference (annually hosts over 2,000 participants, presenters and exhibitors). He has commercial experience with ten years as Chairman of Mountain Goat Beer Pty Ltd, a successful start-up now owned by Asahi Breweries. He served as Mayor and Councillor at the City of Brunswick and was company secretary for 7 years of Performing Arts Moreland, an NFP responsible for the Brunswick Music Festival and Sydney Road Street Party. He served as a President of the Australasian Society of Association Executives (AuSAE) for six years and is now a Life Member.
people.name: Simon Pryor

people.bio: SJ Groenewegen is the author of numerous works, most recently The Disinformation War (GoldSF, 2023/24) and Lethbridge-Stewart: A Most Haunted Man (Candy Jar Books, 2022). SJ appears often as a panellist at Eastercons and Worldcons, and has given talks and readings at literature festivals. SJ’s 20-year career in criminal justice in Australia and the UK earned them a British Empire Medal for services to LGBTQIA people.
people.name: SJ Groenewegen

people.bio: Skottie Miller is a VP and Technology Fellow at DreamWorks Animation, specializing in Infrastructure strategy and operations
people.name: Skottie Miller

people.bio: S. M. Hallow is a speculative fiction author who loves history, fairytales, and Frankenstein. Her short story “How to Stay Married To Baba Yaga” was selected for the Best of Fantasy, Vol. 3, edited by Paula Guran, and included in the Locus 2023 Recommended Reading List. Her longer fiction includes her novella How to Survive This Fairytale (2025) and debut novel The Halls of the Dead (Harper Voyager, 2026). Find out more at www.smhallow.com.
people.name: S. M. Hallow

people.bio: S.M. Mack is a 2019 MFA recipient in popular fiction from USM Stonecoast, the 2017 first place winner of the Katherine Patterson Prize for Young Adult Writing, and a Clarion 2012 grad. Her debut novella, Death Valley Blooms, was published by Neon Hemlock in 2025; her short fiction has also appeared in Fireside Fiction, Vine Leaves Literary Journal's "Best of 2015" anthology, and the Clarion class of 2012's seven Rainbow Anthologies, among others. Find her online at @whatsmacksaid on Bsky, @what_smacksaid on Instagram, or sign up for her monthly author newsletter on her website at whatsmacksaid.com.
people.name: S.M. Mack

people.bio:
Raised in the small aisle of her family’s shop in Hanoi’s Old Quarter, Solar Hoàng (she/her) writes epic family saga and grand fantasies. With a background in data analytics and engineering, her occupational hazard may include books that blend magic with science, where pain is necessary and heroes are optional.

When not writing, she’s recovering from drinking too much Vietnamese coffee. Keep up with her at @solrhoang.
people.name: Solar Hoàng

people.bio:
Solomon Uhiara is a Nigerian science fiction writer, conceptual photographer, and engineer whose creative work blends technology, culture, and the African experience into bold narratives. His writing has been published widely, with short stories, essays, poetry and interviews appearing in several issues of Dark Matter Magazine, Omenana Magazine, The World’s Revolution, AfricanWriter Magazine, Journal of the Fantastic in the Arts, Polutexni, Eye to the Telescope, Tor, StarLine, and Open Country Magazine. He was a Nommo Awards finalist for his acclaimed short story “LOOM,” which explored themes of memory, Alzheimers, survival, family, and Afrofuturism. His story “The Extermination Device of the Blacksmith” was voice-performed by Altered-Carbon actor Ato Essandoh,
In addition to his publications, Solomon has been active in the Nigerian speculative fiction community.
