He moderated virtual panels during the last Science Fiction World Convention in Seattle, USA, 2025 contributing to global conversations about Nigerian influences in storytelling and speculative futures. His debut science fiction and fantasy novel, Dust Engines, will be released in Fall 2026 by Dark Matter INK Imprint (USA).
people.name: Solomon Uhiara

people.bio: Somto Ihezue is a writer and filmmaker. He is an MFA fellow in Creative Writing at the University of Maryland. Somto writes about longing, spirits, land, and joy in Igbo communities. His work has won the Locus Award and The Perkoff Prize, and has been a finalist for the Nebula Award, the British Fantasy Award, the Ignyte, the Nommo, and the ALCS Tom-Gallon Trust Award. His writing has appeared and is forthcoming in Clarkesworld, Reckoning, Strange Horizons, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, PodCastle and others. He is the co-editor of Will This Be a Problem? The Anthology.
people.name: Somto Ihezue

people.bio: Sonia is an award winning writer and editor who writes stories inspired by Palestinian folklore and history. Her work has appeared in ArabLit Quarterly, Beladi, FIYAH, Lackington’s Magazine, Seize the Press, and other venues. Her stories have been anthologized in Xenocultivars: Stories of Queer Growth, Year’s Best Canadian Fantasy & Science Fiction, If There’s Anyone Left Vol 4, INARA: Light of Utopia, and more.
people.name: Sonia Sulaiman

people.bio: Sophia Babai is an author, cultural consultant, and creativity & embodiment coach. She writes literary speculative fiction about ghosts, grief, and families lost and found. Her clients have published numerous bestsellers and won awards including the Hugo, Nebula, and Astounding Award for New Author.
people.name: Sophia Babai

people.bio:
Sophie Burnham (they/them) is the award-winning author of genre-defying and unapologetically queer speculative fiction. Sargassa, the first in their Ex Romana trilogy, won the 2024 Sidewise Award and was shortlisted for the Locus. The sequel Bloodtide was longlisted for the BSFA. They would like you to know that this series is really less about the Roman Empire and more about why it shouldn't be your Roman Empire.

They live in Scotland, where they research queer folkloristics and futures literacy at the University of Edinburgh. They have been a participating writer in—and the script doctor behind—multiple studio film and television projects. This are a current Astounding Award finalist.
people.name: Sophie Burnham

people.bio: S. Qiouyi Lu is a writer and translator based in Los Angeles, CA. Ær debut biocyberpunk novella In the Watchful City is out now from Tordotcom Publishing. S. is currently working on a sociolinguistic scifantasy novel titled Razing Babel set in the same universe as In the Watchful City and centered on themes of the body, sex & intimacy, community, linguicide, and radicalization. You can find out more about S. at ær website s.qiouyi.lu.
people.name: S. Qiouyi Lu

people.bio:
Stan Sakai is the creator of Usagi Yojimbo, a graphic novel series featuring a samurai rabbit living in seventeenth century Japan. Usagi has been published in eighteen languages and Sakai has been honored with a number of awards including twelve Eisners, the Japanese American National Museum’s Cultural Ambassador Award, two National Cartoonists Society Silver Reubens, and an American Library Association Award. Skillful weaving of history, folklore, and Japanese culture has made Usagi Yojimbo a favorite among educators as a curriculum tool.

Usagi has been a part of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles in their TV series, comic books, and toy lines.

Sakai, in partnership with Gaumont Studios, Atomic Monster, and Dark Horse Entertainment, created Samurai Rabbit: The Usagi Chronicles for Netflix.

Stan is married to Julie Sakai with whom he collaborated on the Eisner Award winning Chibi Usagi and the Attack of the Heebie Chibis. In 2021 Sakai was inducted into the Eisner Hall of Fame.
people.name: Stan Sakai

people.bio: Starblight Bindery is a self-taught fan fiction book artist who creates one-of-a-kind, handmade bespoke books for personal use, with a side mission to make home bookbinding more accessible for everyone. I believe fanbinding is an act of resistance and self-determination and endeavor to democratize bookbinding through innovating accessible equipment and distributing supplies to aspiring home bookbinders.
people.name: Starblight Bindery

people.bio: Stefan has produced, directed and produced nearly 3,000 audiobooks for Skyboat Audio and major publishers. His company, Skyboat Media has published over 400 titles. He has narrated countless audiobooks, including titles by Orson Scott Card Robert Silverberg, Alex Bledsoe, Ben Bova, Harlan Ellison. Stefan has won 2 Grammys and 2 Hugos for Lightspeed Magazine. He is a Golden Voice by AudioFile Magazine. Stefan has directed hundreds of stage productions and chaired departments at the University level. He is the renowned voice of Albrecht Entrati in the Warframe video game series. He wass Special Guest at Boskone63 this year.
people.name: Stefan Rudnicki

people.bio: Stephanie Stein is a senior editor at Tor Publishing Group, where she publishes primarily science fiction and fantasy for the Tor Books list.
people.name: Stephanie Stein

people.bio:
Award-winning author Stephannie Tallent is a 1989 West Point graduate. Since then she’s served in the Army as a Military Intelligence officer, gotten a Zoology degree, went to vet school, worked as a small animal veterinarian, and designed and published knitting patterns and books.

She’s now writing everything from fantasy to science fiction to mysteries to romance.
people.name: Stephannie Tallent

people.bio:
Stephen was born in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa and resident in Oxford, since being an Academic Visitor to the African Studies Centre, University of Oxford in 2022. Stephen was awarded the Best Novella by an African in the 7th Nommo Awards at Glasgow WorldCon in 2024 for his Sauúti-based novella, "Undulation". Stephen was awarded a literary grant by the Royal Literary Fund in 2024, providing financial assistance to write while recognising the literary merit of his body of work and literature-related activities. This has enabled him to focus on his current novel.
Stephen's first short story was published in 2015 in Malawi and his debut speculative fiction novel, Soul Searching, was shortlisted for the Nommo Awards in 2021. His YA fantasy novel, Bones & Runes, first published in the UK in 2022, is due for worldwide release in 2026. Stephen is one of the eleven African writers in the Afro-centric Sauúti Collective science-fantasy shared-world.
people.name: Stephen Embleton

people.bio: Stephen W. Potts is a retired academic and an author of books and articles on genre fiction, especially sf and fantasy, alongside editorials, reviews, and short creative work. His study of Russian authors Arkady and Boris Strugatsky earned the J. Lloyd Eaton Award for science fiction criticism. He was Scholar Guest of Honor at the 1991 Mythcon and one of the Tolkien specialists featured in the 2002 TV documentary Page to Screen: The Lord of the Rings. Recent projects include two science fiction anthologies co-edited with David Brin, Chasing Shadows (2017) and Project Solar Sail (2024).
people.name: Stephen W Potts

people.bio: Steve Collins is a guidance and control engineer at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Steve is currently a GNC systems engineer on the Psyche project. During his long career at JPL, Steve has supported all the Mars rover missions including Perseverance, Curiosity, Spirit and Opportunity. He has worked on numerous small body missions including Epoxi, Dawn, Deep Impact, Deep Space One, as well as Galileo and long ago, Mars Observer. Steve's job is keeping the spacecraft pointed the right direction, making trajectory corrections and figuring out "what the heck just happened??" When he's not flying some robotic spacecraft around the solar system, Steve can be found acting, dancing, or jamming on the Theremin.
people.name: Steve Collins

people.bio: Steve Gillett has been a frequent contributor to _Analog_ and wrote a science column for _Amazing_ back in the day. He is also the author of _World-Building_ (Writer’s Digest Press, 1995), which with the author’s impeccable sense of timing came out just before the first exoplanet discoveries. In recent years he has been interested in the staggering implications of molecular-scale nanotechnology to resource extraction and pollution control (which become the same problem), and his book on this topic has finally appeared (_Nanotechnology and the Resource Fallacy_, Pan-Stanford Publications, 2018). He was previously on the faculty of the University of Nevada’s late-lamented Mackay School of Mines and lives outside Reno, Nevada.
people.name: Steve Gillett

people.bio: Steven Barnes is a novelist, television writer, and director. His latest novel, ICE VEGAS, written with Larry Niven, is out this summer. His debut short film, THE KEEPER, was directed and written with his wife Tananarive Due. He lives in Southern California with his wife and son.
people.name: Steven Barnes

people.bio: Steven Popkes' work has been a Nebula finalist and included in many Best Of anthologies. By day he is an aerospace software engineer. He and his wife life outside of Boston and raise bananas and turtles.
people.name: Steven Popkes

people.bio: Steven Radecki has been writing stories for as long as he can remember. He is the author of Building Baby Brother and a handful of short stories. After earning a degree in Information and Computer Science, he authored several technical papers about computer technology and one non-fiction book about developing multimedia applications. Now, he focuses on writing novels and screenplays. He is a technical writer and a certified project manager, managing projects for several high-tech companies in Silicon Valley. He is also the Executive Producer of the Small Publishing in a Big Universe podcast.
people.name: Steven Radecki

people.bio: Steven Shaviro is Emeritus Professor of English at Wayne State University. He has written a number of books of science fiction criticism, including Discognition, Extreme Fabulations, and Fluid Futures.
people.name: Steven Shaviro

people.bio:
Stewart Hotston lives in the UK. With a Celtic-Indian mother and a father of North African/Ukranian descent, Stewart is a somewhat confused second-generation immigrant living in the UK who has written many short stories and several novels including the BSFA finalist, Project Hanuman and the BFA and Speculative Chaos finalist, The Entropy of Loss.

Alongside fiction, he writes literary criticism including for the Hugo nominated, Nerds of a Feather.

He is a long time larper and co-owner of Flowstate Games which among other games, runs Curious Pastimes, a 1500 player UK based fantasy LARP.

Stewart is also the chair of the British Science Fiction Association and the treasurer of the British Fantasy Society.
people.name: Stew Hotston (he/him)

people.bio: Storm Humbert lives with his wife, Casey, son, Sylas, and their cats, Nugget and Honey Mustard, in Michigan. In his free time, Storm likes to be with his wife, play games, and work out. His writing has appeared in Andromeda Spaceways, Interzone, Apex, Galaxy’s Edge, and other magazines, along with many anthologies. He is also a winner of the Writers of the Future contest and has work forthcoming from other markets. Storm and some friends also own and operate a small press: Calendar of Fools. Their most recent project, and Storm's editorial debut, “Intergalactic Rejects,” released June 20, 2025, and their third anthology, "Missed-Fits" is due out at the end of this year.
people.name: Storm Humbert

people.bio: Sue Burke is a writer and translator. Her novel Semiosis, which imagined a planet where plants are intelligent, was nominated for the Arthur C. Clarke Award, John W. Campbell Memorial Award, and the Locus Best First Novel Award. Its sequels are Interference and Usurpation, and her other novels are Immunity Index and Dual Memory. She has also written short stories, poetry, journalism, and essays, and she won the 2016 Alicia Gordon Award for Word Artistry in Translation from the American Translators Association. She’s a wide-horizons Midwesterner currently living in Chicago, Illinois.
people.name: Sue Burke

people.bio:
Although Sue Dawe works on a variety of themes with different media, she is best known for her fantasy airbrushed designs, which have appeared in magazines and on back-to school products, posters, greeting cards, games, and Franklin Mint plates. Sue enjoys fantasy and period costume design, and teaching at San Diego Miramar College. She frequently attends science-fiction conventions, where she has been known, on occasion, to participate in late night high jinks.

More recently, Sue has been included in several anthologies with Emerald Cove Press, both writing and illustrating stories.
people.name: Sue Dawe

people.bio: On the board of the Otherwise Award (formerly Tiptree). Stand-up comedian. Open source software project manager. Fanvidder. Co-editor of the anthology Thoughtcrime Experiments (2009). Lives in New York City.
people.name: Sumana Harihareswara

people.bio: Susan has been active in fandom for more than 40 years as a costumer, masquerade emcee, and all-around fan. She has worked as a book reviewer for Publisher's Weekly and the Amazon Breakthrough Novel Contest and ran the Hugo Awards ceremony in 2012. Professionally, she is a social dance historian who conducts balls, teaches dance workshops, and DJs for blues and waltz events.
people.name: Susan de Guardiola

people.bio:
Susie Williamson is a speculative fiction writer based in Devon, UK. She is the author of the award-winning fantasy fiction series, Blood Gift Chronicles, published by Stairwell Books. The series features themes of social and environmental justice, magic, animism and dragons. Susie's short stories incorporate weird and cosmic fiction, blending speculative, and surrealism into ordinary settings. Her short fiction, articles and poetry have appeared in a number of collections including Dreamcatcher magazine, The Other Stories podcast, The Power of Place anthology, Destinations anthology and Focus magazine.

Susie started life as a science teacher in the UK before travelling to teach English as a foreign language in the Sudan, followed by several years teaching Literacy in South Africa. On her return, she settled in Devon and began a career in creative writing. She is also an artist and poet, with a lifelong love of the natural world.
people.name: Susie Williamson

people.bio: Since discovering SF fandom in the mid-1960’s, Suzanne Tompkins (Suzle) has co-edited four fanzines (The Spanish Inquisition and Mainstream, with husband Jerry Kaufman, received Hugo nominations); helped found an SF club (WPSFA in Pittsburgh); and helped run numerous SF cons (Seattle Potlatches, Corflus, and several Worldcons). She was the 2005 TransAtlanticFanFund delegate, then served as the North American TAFF administrator until 2008. In real life, Suzle works as an association manager/meeting planner and on the Clarion West Writers Workshop staff. She and Jerry publish Littlebrook, found on line at http://www.efanzines.com/.
people.name: Suzle

people.bio: Dr. Sven von Vittorelli is a Berlin-based writer, moderator, climate and biodiversity expert. He has worked extensively on a variety of sustainability issues in both public and private sectors, research and NGO’s.
people.name: Sven von Vittorelli

people.bio: Tabitha Lord’s indie-published science fiction novel, HORIZON, won the Writer’s Digest Grand Prize in 2016. She has short fiction published with World-Weaver Press, Grimbold Books, Inkd Publishing and on podcasts including Tales to Terrify and Starship Sofa. Under the pen name Maggie Clare, she writes all the steamy stuff including romantic suspense, contemporary romance, and dark erotic romance. Tabitha is the past Vice President of the Association of RI Authors (ARIA) and a partner and senior writer at Book Club Babble, a top-searched website for reviews and book club questions. Tabitha has presented at writing conferences and moderated numerous panels at Comic Cons and World Cons, and while she doesn’t cosplay, she does fangirl. She’s a recovering nomad, having spent the last three years exploring the country in an RV with her husband and menagerie of fur babies. She’s recently settled in Pasadena, CA where she’s focused on completing her MFA at Western Colorado University.
people.name: Tabitha Jorgensen

people.bio: T.A. Chan is a human being trying to live her best life on this floating piece of space rock. With a passion for anything that is wonderfully weird, fantasy and sci-fi books quickly became her favorite genres to play in. She enjoys crafting character-focused stories that explore the human experience, as well as plots that twist and challenge expectations. Her insatiable curiosity of the natural world inspires much of her writing. When she’s not typing away, she’s probably begging her plants not to die and spoiling the dog. She also has an unhealthy obsession with manatees, triangles, and dark chocolate.
people.name: T.A. Chan

people.bio: Tad Daley, JD, PhD, is currently President of the Americans for Democratic Action Foundation of Southern California, and a member of an expert commission now endeavoring to frame a “Second United Nations Charter.” He has advised and collaborated with three members of the U.S. House of Representatives and two United States senators on policies designed to pursue the global public good. He spent many years at both UCLA and the RAND Corporation think tank. He’s author of the book Apocalypse Never: Forging the Path to a Nuclear Weapon-Free World from Rutgers University Press. And he hopes in his lifetime to see the end of eternal arms races between separate sovereign states, the abolition of war, and the unification of humankind.
people.name: Tad Daley, JD, PhD

people.bio: Takayuki Tatsumi: major books include: Full Metal Apache: Transactions between Cyberpunk Japan and Avant-Pop America (Duke UP, 2006, the winner of the 2010 IAFA [International Association for the Fantastic in the Arts] Distinguished Scholarship Award). He also received the 2025 SFRA Lifetime Contribution to SF Scholarship Award. Co-editor of The Routledge Companion to Transnational American Studies (Routledge, 2019), he has also published a variety of essays in PMLA, Critique, Extrapolation, Science Fiction Studies, Mechademia, ARTS and elsewhere on subjects ranging from the American Renaissance to post-cyberpunk fiction and film.
people.name: Takayuki Tatsumi

people.bio: Tamika Thompson is author of The Curse of Hester Gardens. A former journalist and producer, she is also author of Unshod, Cackling, and Naked, which is the 2024 Next Generation Indie Book Awards Winner for Horror, as well as author of Salamander Justice. Her work has appeared in several speculative fiction anthologies as well as in Andromeda Spaceways Magazine, Interzone, Prairie Schooner, and The New York Times, among others. She lives in the San Francisco Bay Area, where she hosts her own blog and newsletter, Tamika Talks Terror. Visit her online at tamikathompson.com or on social media @tamikadthompson.
people.name: Tamika Thompson

people.bio: Convention runner and cocktails & booze historian.
people.name: Tammy Coxen

people.bio:
TANANARIVE DUE (tah-nah-nah-REEVE doo) is an award-winning author who teaches Black Horror and Afrofuturism at UCLA.

A leading voice in Black speculative fiction for more than 20 years, Due has won an American Book Award, an NAACP Image Award, and a British Fantasy Award, and her writing has been included in best-of-the-year anthologies. Her books include The Reformatory (winner of a Los Angeles Times Book Prize, Chautauqua Prize, Bram Stoker Award, Shirley Jackson Award, World Fantasy Award, and a New York Times Notable Book), The Wishing Pool and Other Stories, Ghost Summer: Stories, My Soul to Keep, and The Good House. She and her late mother, civil rights activist Patricia Stephens Due, co-authored Freedom in the Family: A Mother-Daughter Memoir of the Fight for Civil Rights.

She was an executive producer on Shudder's groundbreaking documentary Horror Noire: A History of Black Horror. She and her husband/collaborator, Steven Barnes, wrote "A Small Town" for Season 2 of Jordan Peele’s "The Twilight Zone" on Paramount Plus, and two segments of Shudder’s anthology film Horror Noire. They also recently co-directed their horror short film, The Keeper. Due and Barnes co-host a podcast, "Lifewriting: Write for Your Life!" She and her husband live with their son, Jason.
people.name: Tananarive Due

people.bio: Tanya DePass is the founder & Director of I Need Diverse Games, Rivals of Waterdeep Producer & Cast Member, a partnered Twitch variety broadcaster, and RPG developer/writer/consultant. They're the Creator & Creative Director for Into the Mother Lands RPG. Additionally, Tanys is a Senior Annenberg Civics Media Fellow at USC. Their work to make the industry more inclusive has been highlighted in Game Changer, Directed by Tina Charles, WNBA star & olympian as well as filmmaker. The short documentary premiered at Tribeca 2021, as part of the Queen Collective. They currently serve as the Board Chair for Take This, and have been a full BAFTA US member since 2024.
people.name: Tanya DePass

people.bio: Tara Campbell is a writer, teacher, Kimbilio Fellow, and fiction co-editor at Barrelhouse. Publication credits include Masters Review, Wigleaf, Electric Literature, CRAFT Literary, Uncharted Magazine, Daily Science Fiction, Strange Horizons, and Escape Pod/Artemis Rising. She's the author of the eco sci-fi novel TreeVolution, two hybrid collections of poetry and prose, two short story collections, and a chapbook of sestinas. Her second novel, City of Dancing Gargoyles (SFWP), was a finalist for the 2025 Philip K. Dick Award. She's taught creative writing at venues such as Johns Hopkins University, American University, Clarion West, The Writer's Center, and Hugo House.
people.name: Tara Campbell

people.bio: In addition to all things sci-fi, I have been a collector of robots, droids, and cyborgs for over 40yrs, and I’m approaching 300 in my collection. I’m interested in how people curate their collections. I also attended a short-lived school on robotics in Chicago.
people.name: Tara Oakes

people.bio: Tara Sim is the critically acclaimed author of the Dark Gods Saga, the We Shall Be Monsters duology, the Scavenge the Stars duology, and the Timekeeper trilogy. She can typically be found wandering the wilds of the Bay Area, California. When she’s not chasing cats or lurking in bookstores, she writes books about magic, murder, and mayhem.
people.name: Tara Sim

people.bio: Since 1974 I've been, alternately, an actress, writer, artist, animator, producer and director for computer games, film and theater. Currently I am a producer/director with two films on Amazon Prime and Tubi and more coming!
people.name: Taunya Gren

people.bio:
T.D. Orel is an indie author and content creator from Huntington Beach, CA. He is the author of the YA fantasy series, the Titan’s Nest Saga.

Beyond writing, T. D. has built a thriving digital presence through social media, where his “inner-thoughts” skits have reached millions of viewers on Instagram and TikTok. His content exclusively highlights sci-fi and fantasy media in literature, film, television, and gaming.
people.name: T. D. Orel

people.bio:
David Thayer, better known by the pen name Teddy Harvia (an anagram), is an American science fiction fan artist. He was born in Oklahoma but grew up in and resides in Dallas, Texas.

Teddy Harvia has won the Hugo Award for Best Fan Artist four times, and has been nominated an additional sixteen times for the award. For his service to Southern science fiction fandom, Harvia was presented the Rebel Award by the Southern Fandom Confederation in 1997 at that year's DeepSouthCon.

David Thayer was chair of the bid to host the Worldcon in Cancún, Mexico, in 2003. (The bid lost to Torcon III and the 61st World Science Fiction Convention was held in Toronto.)
people.name: Teddy Harvia

people.bio: I'm a linguistic student currentl working on my master's degree. In my free time I study and teach the Na'vi language, a constructed language from the Avatar movies.
people.name: Tekre

people.bio: Teresa Nielsen Hayden has edited books by, among others, Poul Anderson, Avram Davidson, John M. Ford, Jane Lindskold, James White, Robert Charles Wilson, Jo Walton, and Charles Stross. At various points in her career she has also edited comic books, literary criticism, and utopian literature. Her essay collection Making Book (NESFA Press, 1994) was a finalist for the Hugo Award; for other writing and publishing, she has been a Hugo finalist four more times. In 2016 she and Patrick were guests of honor at the Worldcon. A second collection, Making Conversation, was published by NESFA Press in connection with that.
people.name: Teresa Nielsen Hayden

people.bio:
Terese Mason Pierre (she/her) is an award-winning Canadian writer and editor whose work has appeared in Uncanny, Fantasy Magazine, Star*Line, Best Canadian Fantasy and Science Fiction, and elsewhere online and in print. Her work has been nominated for Best of the Net, the Aurora Award, and the Ignyte Award. Her second chapbook, Manifest, won a third-place Elgin Award, and was shortlisted for the bpNichol Chapbook Award, for chapbooks published in Canada. In 2023, she was named a Writer’s Trust Rising Star, and she is a winner of Writer’s Trust Journey Prize, Canada’s most prestigious award for short fiction. She has completed residencies at Island Scribe and the Banff Centre.

While she originally wanted to be a pediatrician, Terese has always found a home in creative writing. She studied Bioethics at the University of Toronto, while creating and developing literary arts programming at the Hart House Student Literary and Library Committee—hosting creative writing workshops and organizing panels and events. She continued her education with a Masters Degree in Philosophy from York University, and graduated from a Master in Fine Arts in Creative Writing in 2025, from the University of Guelph. Currently, she works at the Toronto Public Library, hosting programs for diverse communities.

Terese currently lives in Toronto and is an active member of her local literary community. She has co-hosted poetry reading series, spoken at conferences and festivals, organized literary events, judged writing contests, facilitated creative writing workshops—including with Clarion West—and mentored emerging writers. She edits for Augur Magazine, a Canadian speculative literature journal. Since 2018, she has been a Poetry Editor, a Senior Editor and co-Editor-in-Chief. Currently, she serves as Augur’s Chief Programming Officer—leading the creation of programs, events and initiatives—and co-Director of AugurCon, Augur‘s biennial speculative literature conference.

Myth is Terese’s debut poetry collection, from House of Anansi Press, which explores family, island landscapes, love, and memory. She is also the editor of As The Earth Dreams, an anthology of Black Canadian speculative short fiction.

When not writing, working, or editing, Terese plays in four different D&D campaigns (mostly spellcasters), attends the occasional play or comedy show, bakes when inspired, hosts parties for her friends, and binges TV with her cat, Benjamin.
people.name: Terese Mason Pierre

people.bio: Terilee is an archaeologist/anthropologist, part time professor and full-time nerd. Their most popular course is ANTH 314: Anthropology of Zombies. A long time larper and ttrpg player and GM, whose games often have a focus on history. They write & present academic articles on a range of topics including popular culture, STS (science & technology studies), digital ethnography (online cultures), and memory studies, and they discuss popular culture and its fandoms in their anthropology courses. Aka geek. Academic publications https://orcid.org/0009-0002-2930-5425
people.name: Terilee Edwards-Hewitt

people.bio: Terrence is a long time gamer, writer, and convention attendee and runner.
people.name: Terrence Miltner

people.bio: Terri Ash is the manager, artist wrangler, and professional killjoy at Geek Calligraphy, as well as a freelance wrangler. She has been part of organized fandom for 17 years, disorganized fandom for much longer. A voracious consumer of many kinds of SFF media, nothing makes Terri happier than talking about it for hours, especially if you get her started on the Jewish origins of superheroes or feminism in SFF. This will be her seventh Worldcon, and her first year as a Hugo Finalist.
people.name: Terri Ash

people.bio: Terri Wells is an editor with more than 20 years of professional experience that encompasses both long form and short form science fiction, fantasy, memoir, local news, K-12 educational material, and much more. She has worked for start-up companies and large corporations, most recently Houghton Mifflin Harcourt. In 2022, at the Chicago WorldCon, she started freelance editing full time.
people.name: Terri Wells

people.bio:
Terry Lee Brussel-Rogers, Co-author of Fifty Years of Polyamory in America:A Guided Tour of a Growing Movement (published in 2022) is a Lifetime Member of the Heinlein Society. She founded Live the Dream in 1987.

Live the Dream is for those who, having read the writings of such authors as Robert A Heinlein, Spider Robinson, Robert Rimmer & Marion Zimmer Bradley are now ready to Live such alternative lifestyle as multiply-committed relationships, group marriage and group living--Polyamory. It is the oldest continuing Nest of Church of All Worlds (CAW), the first legally recognized Neo-Pagan religion in the US. CAW is based on the one in Heinlein's Stranger In A Strange Land.

Professionally, Terry is a Certified Clinical Hypnotherapist and relationship coach since 1969. She is also a fourth-generation matchmaker who ran her family's introduction service for forty years.
people.name: Terry Lee Brussel-Rogers

people.bio: Theodora Goss is the World Fantasy, Locus, and Mythopoeic Award-winning author of the Athena Club trilogy of novels, including The Strange Case of the Alchemist’s Daughter, European Travel for the Monstrous Gentlewoman, and The Sinister Mystery of the Mesmerizing Girl. Her other publications include short story and poetry collections In the Forest of Forgetting, Songs for Ophelia, Snow White Learns Witchcraft, The Collected Enchantments, and Letters from an Imaginary Country as well as novella The Thorn and the Blossom. She has been a finalist for the Nebula, Crawford, and Shirley Jackson Awards, as well as on the Tiptree Award Honor List. Her work has been translated into fifteen languages. You can find her at theodoragoss.com.
people.name: Theodora Goss

people.bio: I'm Tess Tanenbaum, a queer, polyamorous, neurodivergent, transgender woman. I have a doctorate in interactive storytelling, and published extensively during my academic career before deciding I was ready to start telling my own stories instead of just mentoring the next generation of storytellers. Now I live in rural Illinois where I just finished my first novel - a mashup between a queer romance and a magical girl fantasy story. I also write and perform speculative poetry, produce music, create audio dramas, and brew magical black walnut ink.
people.name: Theresa Jean Tanenbaum ("Tess")

people.bio: Thomas Ha is a writer of speculative short fiction whose work has won the Nebula, Locus, and Philip K. Dick Special Citation. He has also been nominated for the Hugo, Ignyte, and Shirley Jackson Awards, among others. You can find his stories in publications including Clarkesworld, Lightspeed Magazine, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Weird Horror Magazine, and more. His work has also appeared in The Best American Science Fiction & Fantasy and The Year's Best Dark Fantasy & Horror. His debut short story collection, Uncertain Sons and Other Stories, is available at Undertow Publications and wherever books are sold. Thomas grew up in Honolulu and, after a decade plus of living in the northeast, now resides in Los Angeles with his family.
people.name: Thomas Ha

people.bio: Tia Tashiro is a multiracial science fiction and fantasy writer hailing from the Pacific Northwest. She has won a Derringer Award and been a finalist for the Hugo, Locus, Sturgeon, and Astounding Award for her short fiction. By day, she works in cognitive science; by night, she writes; and in between, she dabbles in stained glass and juggling, though never at the same time. Her short fiction is published in Uncanny, Clarkesworld, Diabolical Plots, and Apex, among other venues. Find her at tiatashiro.com.
people.name: Tia Tashiro

people.bio: Tiffani Angus (PhD) is a multi BSFA- and BFS-award finalist for her debut novel Threading the Labyrinth and for non-fiction (with co-author Val Nolan) for Spec Fic for Newbies: A Beginner’s Guide to Writing Subgenres of Science Fiction, Fantasy, and Horror Vol. 1 (2023) and Vol. 2 (2024), both of which also made the Locus Recommended Reading List. Volume 3 launched March 2026. She spent over a decade teaching creative writing at universities in the US and UK and works as a freelance editor, runs the typesetting/formatting business Book Polishers, and leads various writing workshops in person and online.
people.name: Tiffani Angus

people.bio: Tim Griffin is a retired teacher; an award-winning singer/songwriter; and the founding director (now emeritus) of Griffin Education, a small nonprofit dedicated to raising academic achievement in STEM and other subjects through fun educational music. Think "Schoolhouse Rock" and you've got the basic idea. It's all free at www.GriffinEd.org
people.name: Tim Griffin

people.bio:
Tim Kirk is a designer and illustrator with wide experience in a broad media spectrum—from theme park and museum exhibit design to book illustration and greeting cards. Tim’s first job out of college was with Hallmark Cards, Inc., where he worked as a greeting card designer. In 1980 he joined the Walt Disney Company as an Imagineer—first as an employee (for 22 years), and currently as a contractor. Tim was also a partner in Kirk Design Incorporated, which designed and produced (among other projects) the Science Fiction Museum and Hall of Fame in Seattle for Paul Allen.

Tim is a five-time winner of the prestigious Hugo Award for science fiction and fantasy fan art. Professionally, he has illustrated stories by L. Sprague de Camp, Lord Dunsany, Robert E. Howard, Darryl Schweitzer, Lin Carter, Mary Elizabeth Counselman, L. Frank Baum, Harlan Ellison, Ray Bradbury and Fritz Leiber. He was the first American artist to illustrate the J.R.R. Tolkien Calendar for Ballantine Books (published in 1975), and more of his Tolkien work is featured in the Greisinger Museum in Switzerland. In 2024, two of Tim’s illustration projects have just been published: The Knight and Knave of Swords by Fritz Leiber from Centipede Press, and The Complete John the Balladeer by Manly Wade Wellman from Haffner Press. Tim’s illustrations for the long awaited The Last Dangerous Visions, edited by Harlan Ellison, will appear later in 2024.

Tim was a principal designer on Tokyo DisneySea and the Disney-MGM Studio Tour theme park for Walt Disney World. He also did design work for the 2003 Walt Disney Pictures production, The Haunted Mansion. Other clients include Thinkwell Design and Production, The Hettema Group, Zeitgeist Design and Production, Rethink Leisure and Entertainment, Henson Associates, the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, the University of Notre Dame, Ghirardelli Chocolate, the Parsonage of Aimee Semple McPherson (in Los Angeles), the National Tourist Administration of China, The Lotte Group, and the Mini Time Machine of Miniatures in Tucson, Arizona.
people.name: Tim Kirk

people.bio: I am a doctor of linguistics and teach and study at California State University, Fullerton. I am also on the board of the Western Institute for Endangered Language Documentation. I work with the Barbareño/Ventureño Band of Mission Indians on language revitalization. On the side, I enjoy fountain pens, coin-collecting, and conlangs.
people.name: Timothy Henry-Rodriguez

people.bio: Author. Game writer for Regicide, Oathsworn, and others. Founder of Labyrinth Magazine. Mental health advocate. 100K+ books sold. 1.2M+ YouTube.
people.name: Timothy Hickson

people.bio: Tim Powers is the author of nineteen novels, including The Anubis Gates and Declare. He has won the Locus Award three times and the World Fantasy Award three times. He and his wife, Serena, live with a number of cats and dogs in San Bernardino, California.
people.name: Tim Powers

people.bio: TJ Burnside Clapp has been a cosplayer, filksinger, songwriter, artist, convention organizer, and guest at dozens of conventions for over 50 years. She published the Star Trek fanzine FESARIUS, has won several Pegasus Awards for Excellence in Filking, and is a member of the Filk Hall of Fame. She is probably best known for going viral on the internet with her homemade X-Wing pilot costume which she made in 1977 at the age of 16, which has been viewed millions of times and was retweeted by Mark Hamill.
people.name: TJ Burnside Clapp

people.bio: T. K. Rex is a science fiction and fantasy author from the western states, whose stories can be read in more than forty publications, including The Sunday Morning Transport, Apex Magazine, Asimov's, Strange Horizons, and their debut collection, The Wildcraft Drones (Stelliform Press, 2026). They're an alumni of the Clarion, Taos Toolbox and Futurescapes workshops, a Pushcart nominee, a friendly acquaintance of spiders, and twenty-year denizen of San Francisco. T. K.'s stories, socials, and newsletter can be found at tkrex.wtf.
people.name: T. K. Rex

people.bio: Toby MacNutt is a queer, nonbinary trans, disabled artist, author, and teacher living in rural Vermont.
people.name: Toby MacNutt

people.bio: Todd has been involved in fandom since the eighties. They have staffed dozens of conventions and have been active in newsletters, anime viewing clubs, parody fan dubs, room parties, anime rooms, and anime music videos. They study Japanese on and off and have visited Japan on a budget and survived attending Comic Market. They're currently on a Worldcon perfect attendance streak since 2006 LAcon IV). Attending the Chengdu Worldcon alone was an adventure. They enjoy craft projects, writing, and travel. They currently work remotely. They primarily use Linux at home and are asexual and non-binary. Three cats deign to share their abode in Portland with Todd in exchange for housekeeping.
people.name: Todd Allis

people.bio: odd Barber is a JPL senior propulsion engineer and will mark 35 years at JPL this October. Focusing almost exclusively on propulsion mission operations, Barber has flown about two dozen JPL missions throughout the solar system, beginning with Galileo in 1990 and continuing into 2025 with Europa Clipper. The bulk of his career has been spent on Galileo, Cassini, and Voyager, with plenty of smaller missions thrown in to diversify his portfolio. He received NASA's Exceptional Achievement Award in 1996 for his work on Galileo. In 2018, Barber was also honored to receive NASA’s Exceptional Public Service Medal for heading up Cassini’s propulsion team for nearly two decades. Mr. Barber is a native of Wichita, Kansas, and attended MIT between 1984 and 1990, obtaining B.S. and M.S. degrees in aerospace engineering, with a humanities concentration in music.
people.name: Todd J. Barber

people.bio: Tom Coughlin, President, Coughlin Associates is a digital storage analyst and business/ technology consultant. He has over 40 years in the data storage industry with engineering and senior management positions. Coughlin Associates consults, publishes books and market and technology reports and puts on digital storage and memory-oriented events. He is a regular contributor for forbes.com and M&E organization websites. He is an IEEE Fellow, 2025 IEEE Past President, Past-President IEEE-USA, Past Director IEEE Region 6 and Past Chair Santa Clara Valley IEEE Section, and is also active with SNIA and SMPTE. For more information on Tom Coughlin go to www.tomcoughlin.com.
people.name: Tom Coughlin

people.bio:
Tom D Wright is a Science Fiction author who lives in the Pacific Northwest with his wife, a small pack of dogs and a cat. He also writes Paranormal Romance under a pseudonym (Mika Kosey) and is open about his neurodivergence – ADD, ASD and childhood PTSD – a potent combination. When not writing, he likes camping and stargazing with his 12″ telescope.
He graduated with an MA in Psychology from Bowie State University in Bowie, Maryland, served on the Board for Cascade Writers and is a Full Member of SFWA.
people.name: Tom D Wright

people.bio: Illustrator from the UK
people.name: Tom Roberts

people.bio: Former Worldcon co-chair, former GOH, current massage therapist, collector, longp-time fan
people.name: Tom Whitmore

people.bio:
Tonantzin Carmelo is a SAG Award-nominated actress whose multifaceted career spans film, television, theater, and major video game franchises. She first captured international attention with her breakthrough role in Steven Spielberg’s epic miniseries Into the West, earning critical acclaim and a Screen Actors Guild Award nomination.
A powerful screen presence, Carmelo has built a diverse portfolio of recent high-profile television roles. She starred as a series regular in NBC’s sci-fi drama La Brea and has delivered memorable recurring performances in AMC’s Dark Winds, CBS’ NCIS: Origins, and the BBC/Amazon Western The English. On the big screen, her leading performance in the indie thriller Imprint earned her Best Actress honors at the American Indian Film Festival.
Beyond traditional screen acting, Carmelo is a prominent voice and performance-capture artist, lending her talents to blockbuster video games like Cyberpunk 2077, Dead Space, and Lego Marvel’s Avengers. She is also an accomplished choreographer, dancer, and cultural consultant whose creative vision has shaped projects ranging from Amazon's animated series Undone to the critically acclaimed opera Sweetland.
Deeply dedicated to cultural and environmental preservation, Carmelo is the founding artistic force behind Toveema, a Tongva song ensemble. She is an active member of the Tongva Language Committee, has studied numerous Indigenous dialects, and champions the rewilding of her ancestral homelands. A Southern California native of Indigenous and Latina heritage, Carmelo balances her extensive performance career with her vital work as a community educator in the Los Angeles/Tovaangar area.
people.name: Tonantzin Carmelo

people.bio:
Tracey Baptiste is a New York Times bestselling author of twenty-six books for children. Born and raised in Trinidad and Tobago, her popular Jumbies Trilogy draws on Trinidadian folklore and mythology, a series that includes The Jumbies, Rise of the Jumbies and The Jumbie God’s Revenge, as well as the picture book Looking for a Jumbie.

She writes picture books, middle grade, and young adult, fiction and nonfiction, and has contributed to several anthologies. Among her most popular books are Minecraft: The Crash, which has been translated into multiple languages, and nonfiction and historical books including African Icons: Ten People Who Shaped History and Because Claudette. She has also contributed to young adult anthologies, notably 2019’s Black Enough: Stories of Being Young & Black in America.

Her books have received starred reviews from School Library Journal, Publishers Weekly, and Kirkus and have been named in best books of the year roundups for NPR, Kirkus, School Library Journal, Publisher’s Weekly, the New York Public Library, Brightly, We Need Diverse Books, and Bank Street. They have also been on shortlists for several awards such as the Jane Adams Children’s Book Award, the Massachusetts Book Award, and the Texas Topaz Reading List with a unanimous recommendation. Her most recent novels include Moko Magic: Carnival Chaos, Supergoat Girl, and Boy 2.0 and its sequel Kid X.

Her debut novel, Angel’s Grace, was named a Kansas NEA Reading Circle List Junior Title.

When Baptiste is not writing, she visits schools all over the world, and teaches in the low residency MFA program at the University of San Francisco.

You can find Tracey online at traceybaptiste.com and connect with her on Instagram at @traceybaptistewrites.
people.name: Tracey Baptiste

people.bio: Tracy Byrnes is a singer-songwriter, performer, and one half of the Americana duo The Fallen Stars. Known for her warm vocals, sharp storytelling, and engaging stage presence, she has toured extensively throughout the United States and Europe. Alongside husband Bobbo Byrnes, she brings songs to life with equal parts heart, humor, and adventure. At LosCon, Tracy joins The Fallen Stars in celebrating the world of Firefly through music inspired by the beloved series' themes of hope, independence, and finding family among fellow travelers.
people.name: Tracy Byrnes

people.bio:
Tracy Drain is a flight systems engineer who has helped to develop, test, and operate a variety of robotic spacecraft for deep space exploration over the past 25+ years. Her passion for space grew from an early love of science fiction – she soaked up Star Trek, Star Wars, and Battlestar Galactica, plus sci-fi and fantasy books by the armload. With her eye on a career in space, she studied Mechanical Engineering at the University of Kentucky and interned at the NASA Langley Research Center. After earning a master’s degree in mechanical engineering at Georgia Tech, she landed a full-time position at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in 2000.

As a systems engineer, Tracy works with teams of engineers and scientists to ensure all the parts of a spacecraft (telecommunications, thermal, power, software, etc.), the science instruments, and the mission (spacecraft/instruments, ground data system, mission design and navigation, etc.) are designed to work well together to accomplish the mission goals. Her previous missions have included the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, the Kepler mission (an Exoplanet hunter), the Juno mission (orbiting Jupiter) and the Psyche mission (now on its way to study an asteroid). She is currently the Chief Engineer in operations for the Europa Clipper mission which successfully launched in October 2024 and is now on its 5.5-year cruise to Jupiter. After arrival in the Jovian system, Clipper will study Europa – one of the most scientifically exciting moons in our solar system!

A life-long learner, Tracy loves encouraging people to nurture their curiosity and explore the wonders around us, as expressed in her TEDx talk “A Childlike Sense of Wonder: The Curious World of an Aerospace Engineer” and shared in her Nat Geo Live stage show “Cosmic Adventures.” She has joined the advisory board for the University of Kentucky’s Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. She serves on the planning committee for the National Academy of Science’s Science and Entertainment Exchange, which aims to partner with the entertainment industry to make science more accessible and inspiring to the general public. She also serves on the advisory board of Arizona State University’s Interplanetary Initiative, which seeks to create a positive future for humans in space. In her spare time, she enjoys reading, watching a variety of shows including sci-fi and Korean dramas, studying languages (Spanish and… Korean!), and traveling.
people.name: Tracy Drain

people.bio: Trang Thanh Tran writes speculative stories with big emotions. When not writing, they can be found over-caffeinating on iced coffee and watching zombie movies. Their debut novel She Is a Haunting was an instant New York Times and Indie bestseller, a William C. Morris Debut Award finalist, and a Bram Stoker Award winner.
people.name: Trang Thanh Tran

people.bio: With nearly 30 years of experience in the enterprise software industry and a background in sales engineering, solutions architecture, and product management/marketing, Trevor has held senior positions at both startups and large companies, including: Cisco, Capital One, and Ciena. Passionate about full-cycle innovation and agile development, Trevor has been instrumental in both improving the company’s internal processes and pushing the team to climb to the highest heights possible; his steady guidance has kept OpenDrives grounded, focused, and constantly results oriented.
people.name: Trevor Morgan

people.bio: Triona's debut novel SOCKS & SECRET QUESTS, a MG cozy-adjacent fantasy with magic knitting, releases September 29, 2026 from Atheneum/S&S. She writes books and designs knitting patterns in beautiful Oregon wine country, where she lives with her husband and three kids in a house overflowing with yarn, board games, and books.
people.name: Triona Murphy

people.bio: Trip is a writer, a doctor of the academic persuasion, and a researcher of all things pursuant to bargains, exchanges, and compacts of a faery nature. It is inadvisable to attempt to make a deal with him. He has been, in the past, a reluctant cowboy, an Ivy League collegian, and an itinerant marketing professional. He’s 1/2 of multiple writing partnerships, 1/3 of the founding triumvirate of Bona Books, and 100% geek. Mostly harmless.
people.name: Trip Galey

people.bio: Freelance editor and former journalist Trish Matson has loved science fiction and fantasy since childhood; horror came later. She also enjoys roleplaying games.
people.name: Trish Matson

people.bio: T. R. Napper is a multi-award-winning author. His honours include the prestigious Australian Aurealis five times. His short fiction has appeared in Asimov’s, The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Grimdark Magazine, and numerous others. Napper received a creative writing doctorate for his thesis: Noir, Cyberpunk, and Asian Modernity (yes, he is a Doctor of Cyberpunk). Before turning to writing, T. R. Napper was an aid worker, delivering humanitarian programs throughout Southeast Asia for a decade. He was a resident of the Old Quarter in Hanoi for several years, the setting for his acclaimed debut novel, 36 Streets.
people.name: T R Napper

people.bio:
T.T. Gibran (they/them) is a Black (Soulaan) and first-generation Palestinian speculative fiction writer. They attended the Clarion West, Tin House, and Juniper workshops, and their fiction has appeared in FIYAH.

They've earned degrees in Physics and Data Science, a fellowship from DeepMind, a grant from the National Science Foundation, and published in the Journal of Applied Physics.

Gibran's stories draw heavily on their ancestry, from the swamps of South Carolina through the shores of Haifa, to blend African and Arab mythologies with alternate histories and dystopian futures.
people.name: T.T. Gibran

people.bio:
Ursula Vernon is one of those disheartening Renaissance women who can write, draw and, when necessary, can wrangle the occasional stray turtle. – SFSite.com

Ursula Vernon, aka T. Kingfisher is the author and illustrator of far more projects than is probably healthy. She has written over fifteen books for children, at least a dozen novels for adults, an epic webcomic called Digger and various short stories and other odds and ends.

The daughter of an artist, she spent her youth attempting to rebel, but eventually succumbed to the siren song of paint (although not before getting a degree in anthropology.) Ursula grew up in Oregon and Arizona, went to college at Macalester College in Minnesota, and stayed there for ten years, until she finally learned to drive in deep snow and was obligated to leave the state.

Having moved across the country several times, she eventually settled in Pittsboro, North Carolina, where she works full-time as an artist and creator of oddities. She lives with her husband and his chickens.

A bibliography of her works can be found at Wikipedia.
people.name: Ursula Vernon

people.bio: Valerie Estelle Frankel is the author of over 100 books on pop culture, including Hunting for Meaning in The Mandalorian; The Villain's Journey; and Star Wars Meets the Eras of Feminism. Many of her books focus on gender in fiction, from her heroine's journey guides From Girl to Goddess and Buffy and the Heroine's Journey to The Trans Hero's Journey and The Many Faces of Katniss Everdeen. Her Chelm for the Holidays (2019) was a PJ Library book, and now she's the editor of Jewish Science Fiction and Fantasy, publishing an academic series for Bloomsbury/Lexington Press. Once a lecturer at San Jose State University, she now teaches at Mission College and San Jose City College and speaks often at conferences. VEFrankel.com
people.name: Valerie Estelle Frankel

people.bio: Valerie Valdes lives in an elaborate meme palace with her husband and kids, where she writes, edits and moonlights as a muse. When she isn’t co-editing Escape Pod, she enjoys crafting bespoke artisanal curses, playing video games, and admiring the outdoors from the safety of her living room. Her debut novel Chilling Effect was shortlisted for the 2021 Arthur C. Clarke Award, and her short fiction and poetry have been featured in Uncanny Magazine, Magic: the Gathering and numerous anthologies. Writing as Lia Amador, her first contemporary fantasy romance novel, Witch You Would, was published by Avon Books in September 2025.
people.name: Valerie Valdes

people.bio: Vanessa MacLaren-Wray (she/her) creates worlds where people—human or otherwise—matter. She’s the author of All That Was Asked, Shadows of Insurrection, and Flames of Attrition, plus the middle-grade space-opera novel The Smugglers. Her short fiction and poetry have appeared with Dragon Gems and in the award-winning Fault Zone anthologies. She guest-hosts for the podcast Small Publishing in a Big Universe and is an active member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America (SFWA), Broad Universe, and Strong Women-Strange Worlds.
people.name: Vanessa MacLaren-Wray

people.bio: Van Hoang is the author of Girl Giant and the Monkey King, Girl Giant and the Jade War, and Auntie Q's Golden Claws Nail Salon for middle grade readers. Her adult debut novel The Monstrous Misses Mai released in 2024, with Silver and Smoke in 2025. She earned her bachelor’s in English at the University of New Mexico and her master’s in library information science at San Jose State University. She was born in Vietnam, grew in up Orange County, California, and now resides in Los Angeles with her family.
people.name: Van Hoang

people.bio: Veronica G. Henry is the author of Bacchanal, The Mambo Reina and The Scorched Earth duologies, and The People's Library. Her work has debuted at #1 on multiple Amazon bestseller charts, was an editors’ pick for Best Fantasy, and shortlisted for the Silver Falchion and Manly Wade Wellman awards. She is a Viable Paradise alum. Her stories have appeared in the Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Tor.com, and FIYAH Literary Magazine.
people.name: Veronica G. Henry

people.bio: Victoria Aveyard is the #1 NYT Bestselling author of the RED QUEEN series and the REALM BREAKER trilogy. Her books have sold millions of copies world wide and been translated into 40+ languages. She currently resides in Los Angeles with her husband and a a very spoiled Labrador named Indy. "We named the dog Indiana."
people.name: Victoria Aveyard

people.bio: Victoria N. Shi is a Chinese American sci-fi/fantasy and fabulist author, and Clarion West graduate (2025). Her short fiction appears in Analog Science Fiction & Fact, the BSFA’s Fission, and Escape Pod, and forthcoming in khōréō. She works in mental health, specializing in trauma and anxiety. Her hobbies include tending her aquarium and aggressively researching odd behaviors in her houseplants. Ernie Chiara (Fuse Literary) represents her novels.
people.name: Victoria N. Shi

people.bio: I've been a science fiction and fantasy illustrator for nearly 60 years, am an SF Hall of Fame inductee (2011) and an Illustrators Hall of Fame Inductee (2019) and am a former president of the Society of Illustrators and a Hugo Award winning Best Professional Artist winner (1979). I also authored a book devoted to the genre in 19967 entitled Infinite Worlds: The Fantastic Art of Science Fiction.
people.name: Vincent Di Fate

people.bio:
Vincent Docherty is a fan and con-runner, who co-chaired the Glasgow Worldcons in 1995 and 2005. Born in Scotland, his home town is Glasgow, where he studied and researched in Chemistry. His career in the energy industry has taken him to London, Muscat (Oman) and The Hague, where he currently lives.
He had an early interest in SF, Space and Science, and at 16, he attended the first SF convention in Glasgow, quickly becoming involved in organizing SF societies and conventions, including British National Eastercons and Worldcons.
He has been Fan Guest of Honour at the UK Eastercon and other cons and was presented with the 2014 Big Heart and 2025 First Fandom Hall of Fame awards. He was a Hugo finalist for Best Fanzine in 2018 and 2024, as part of Team Journey Planet.
He remains an active con-runner and programme participant, including chairing the 2011, 2021 and 2026 SMOFcons, Hugo Award Administration, the music program and symphonic concert lead for the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Worldcons and Chair advisor and Division Head for the Dublin 2019 and Glasgow 2024 Worldcons.
people.name: Vincent Docherty

people.bio: Vincent J. Roth is the creator and executive producer at Surge of Power Enterprises, which produces indie superhero movies that contain lots of celebrities, campy all-ages humor, tons of Easter Eggs for geek fans, and feature cinema’s first out gay superhero – Surge! Vincent is a corporate attorney by day, but by night, his creative side comes out, expressed in writing scripts, designing costumes, making props and portraying the superhero, Surge.
people.name: Vincent J Roth

people.bio: I am a professor of Biological Sciences at Northern Illinois University. My areas of research specialization are vertebrate paleontology, functional and comparative morphology. My most active present research focuses on sabertooth carnivores, especially Smilodon fatalis, the iconic sabertooth cat that is known primarily from the asphalt seeps at Rancho La Brea. I study both living and extinct vertebrates, primarily mammals, including living tree and extinct ground sloths, hippos and extinct lobe finned fishes, specifically the coelacanths. Other areas of my research include biological aspects of forensic sciences.
people.name: Virginia L. Naples

people.bio: Virginia has been a science fiction and fantasy fan since childhood but only discovered conventions in 2012. Since then she has contributed to programme at Eastercons, Worldcons, Nine Worlds, and Octocon and been head of programme at three Eastercons. In her day job she works at a university and co-teaches a module on the politics and economics of science fiction. In her spare time she likes to make ceramics, sew, and tell the cats how beautiful they are.
people.name: Virginia Preston

people.bio: V.M. Ayala (she/they) is a queer disabled Mexican American sci-fi/fantasy writer. She loves dragons, space, their partner, and giant robots. Their work has appeared in Lightspeed, Escape Pod, The Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy 2024, and elsewhere. She is also a streamer and TTRPG actual play performer—as well as one of the co-founders of OTHERSIDE, a queer speculative magazine. You can find her most social media places @spacevalkyries or at spacevalkyries.com.
people.name: V.M. Ayala

people.bio: Vyvre Argent (they/them) is a queer nonbinary writer who lives in Southern California. They are the author of SKULLRUNNER, the first book in The Godreaper Rebellions series.
people.name: Vyvre Argent

people.bio:
Walter Jon Williams was the writer guest of honor at Worldcon 2017.

His first novel to attract serious public attention was Hardwired (1986), described by Roger Zelazny as "a tough, sleek juggernaut of a story, punctuated by strobe-light movements, coursing to the wail of jets and the twang of steel guitars." In 2001 he won a Nebula Award for his novelette, “Daddy’s World,” and won again in 2005 for “The Green Leopard Plague.”

Walter lives in New Mexico.
people.name: Walter Jon Williams

people.bio: I, W. A. Thomasson, have read science fiction most of my long life. I came to conventions late, with my first con in 1982, but have been a regular panelist for 30 years. I also volunteered for Access after my eyes went bad (age-related macular degeneration), but have now retired from SMOFdom. I obtained a PhD in biochemistry more than a half-century ago but, finding I lacked the patience for research, switched into science and medical writing. I formally retired in 2019 but have now completed a sword-and-sorcery novel (to be self-published, alas!) and several short stories. My interests are very broad, with a special focus n all aspects of near and far futures, sociopolitical as well as technological.
people.name: WA THOMASSON

people.bio: I write for lovers of the future, the past, the mysterious, and the fantastic. I have six books in print under two different names with three different publishers. My latest novel was a semi-finalist for the Ozma award. I am a frequent panelist at ReaderCon, Arisia, and Boskone, was a panelist at Worldcon 2022 and will be at Worldcon 2026. I'm a full member of the Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Association and the Author's Guild. When not writing, I can often be found haunting the bookstores of the Boston area to the dismay of my budget.
people.name: W.B.J. Williams

people.bio: Wen Wen Yang is a Chinese American from the Bronx, New York. She graduated from Barnard College of Columbia University with a degree in English and creative writing. You can find her short fiction in The Rumpus, Cast of Wonders and more. An up-to-date bibliography is on WenWenWrites.com. She listens to audiobooks at three times speed and talks almost as fast.
people.name: Wen Wen Yang

people.bio: Wen-yi Lee is the Nebula Award-nominated author of When They Burned the Butterfly, Where Rivers Made the Gods, and The Dark We Know, and editor of forthcoming horror anthology The Kids Came Back Wrong. Her work often speculates on history, troubling women, and ghosts, and has appeared in short form in venues like Lightspeed, Uncanny, Reactor, and anthologies including Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy. Currently based in Singapore, she has been supported by the Clarion West Octavia E Butler Scholarship, the Singapore National Arts Council, and the UK National Centre for Writing. She is a Forbes Asia 30 Under 30 honoree. Find her on socials @wenyilee_
people.name: Wen-yi Lee

people.bio:
Weyodi OldBear is a citizen of the Comanche Nation and an award-winning science fiction author, poet, and Nebula Award-finalist game designer(Coyote&Crow). Her novel “As Many Ships As Stars”, released in October of 2024 by Android Press, received warm reviews from Publishers Weekly. Her short story “Red Lessons” was the winner of the national Indigenous Futurist Prize. The first book in her trilogy series “The Root and The Seed”, based on the story “Red Lessons” due to be released by Android in June 2026, received a glowing review from celebrated Indigenous Horror storyteller and editor Shane Hawk. Her comic credits include the “A Howl” anthology edited by Beth laPensee, the Lakota Legal Collective’s Guide for Water Protectors published by Stanford University Press, and upcoming comics from Warpaint Studios, A Tribe Called Geek comics, and Green Archer Comics.
From speaking at conferences and summits on topics ranging from Native Representation in Video Games to the Roles of Activism and Resistance in Science Fiction, to being a keynote speaker at the fourth Shifting Seasons Summit: Implementing Climate Resistance, Weyodi continues to validate her 1977 diagnosis of ADHD on a daily basis.
people.name: Weyodi OldBear

people.bio: Will Anderson is a filmmaker, videographer, and actor from Indianapolis, Indiana. He graduated from Purdue University in 2025 with degrees in Film/Video Production and Marketing, where he produced videos for corporations and organizations, worked on numerous student film productions, and starred in a feature-length film. Will made his directorial debut with Selfless, a horror-comedy short film exploring human nature and the complexities of mental health. Now based in Los Angeles, California, he continues to pursue a career in film and video, driven by a passion for telling compelling stories.
people.name: Will Anderson

people.bio: William C. Tracy writes and publishes queer science fiction and fantasy through his indie press Space Wizard Science Fantasy. His works include The Dissolutionverse and accompanying RPG Spells of the Symphony, Fruits of the Gods, The Biomass Conflux, and The Shifting Lands. He also has a nonfiction book, How to Operate Your Body, about body mechanics and correct posture. William is an NC native, has a master’s in mechanical engineering, teaches Wado-Ryu karate, and keeps bees.
people.name: William C. Tracy

people.bio: William Frank, a.k.a. "scifantasy," is a geek and a lawyer, in roughly that order. Professionally, he specializes in intellectual property law, has interned for the Electronic Frontier Foundation and the Creative Commons, and was a computer programmer before he turned to evil-err, law. Fannishly, he has interests in pretty much everything, but the filkroom would be a good first place to look for him.
people.name: William Frank

people.bio: William F. Wu is a science fiction, fantasy, and crime author whose traditionally published books include 13 novels, one scholarly work, and a collection of short stories. His short fiction has been nominated for the Hugo Award twice, for the Nebula Award twice, and once for the World Fantasy Award. His novels Hong on the Range and The Temple of Forgotten Spirits are available as reprint editions in paperback, ebook, and audio book editions through Boruma Publishing. For more information, see williamfwu.com.
people.name: William F. Wu

people.bio:
William Ledbetter is a Nebula Award winning author with three novels and more than seventy speculative fiction short stories and non-fiction articles published in five languages, in publications such as Asimov's, Fantasy & Science Fiction, Analog, Escape Pod and the SFWA blog.
He's been a space and technology geek since childhood and spent most of his non-writing career in the aerospace industry. He is a member of SFWA and lives near Dallas with his wife, a needy dog and three spoiled cats.
people.name: William Ledbetter

people.bio: Born in WV, Will Morton lives in the Los Angeles area with his wife Yvonne. A retired electrical engineer with 16 years’ experience working on the Space Shuttle program, he is a writer with a passion for languages. Active locally with various polyglot groups, he has studied over a dozen natural and constructed languages.
people.name: Will Morton

people.bio:
Wilson Kincaid is a Los Angeles-based science fiction author and futurist whose work explores the intersection of technology and humanity. With a decades-long, award winning career in the entertainment industry (as Eric Wilson), he has contributed to some of the most innovative and technologically advanced projects across film and television, including The Matrix, The Marvel Universe, and the opening of The Sphere in Las Vegas, among many others. He currently works at Flawless AI developing tools for filmmakers to re-articulate the mouths to match new dialogue.

His debut novel, The Murder Algorithm, has been praised for its seamless integration of complex technological concepts into a gripping narrative, drawing comparisons to the speculative storytelling found in Black Mirror. It has won recognition and placed as a semi-finalist in international competitions.

Kincaid writes that "science fiction serves as a medium to pose significant questions, with compelling stories providing entertaining, thought-provoking, and revealing insights into human nature and our future."
people.name: Wilson Kincaid

people.bio: W. Jade Young is an author, editor, writing advisor, and game designer from Indiana, U.S. She holds a Master’s in Fine Arts in creative writing and English from Southern New Hampshire University and has been published in literary magazines and anthologies. She runs the Writers’ Symposium at InConJunction in Indiana. She is the founder of Bad Habit Publishing, an independent publishing outfit, and is the author of The Rainbow Quill Writing Tool and Tarot Deck for Storytellers.
people.name: W. Jade Young

people.bio: Wole Talabi is an engineer, writer and editor from Nigeria. He is the author of the SF thriller THE FIST OF MEMORY (2026) and the urban fantasy novel SHIGIDI AND THE BRASS HEAD OF OBALUFON (2023) which was one of the Washington Post's ten best science and fantasy novels of 2023, nominated for the Nebula, World Fantasy, Locus, and other major awards. His short fiction is collected in the books CONVERGENCE PROBLEMS (2024) and INCOMPLETE SOLUTIONS (2019). Talabi’s writing has earned him the Sidewise Award for Alternate History, the Nommo award for African speculative fiction, and multiple nominations, including as a finalist for the Hugo, Nebula, Locus awards and the Caine Prize for African Writing. He has edited five anthologies. He currently lives in Perth, Australia.
people.name: Wole Talabi

people.bio: Xan van Rooyen is an award-winning autistic, non-binary storyteller from South Africa, currently living in Finland. Xan has a Master’s degree in music, and–when not teaching–enjoys conjuring strange worlds and creating quirky characters. You can find Xan’s stories in the likes of Three-Lobed Burning Eye, Daily Science Fiction, and Galaxy’s Edge among others. They have also written several novels including YA Gothic cyberpunk novel This Exquisite Decay (Tiny Ghost Press) and adult dark fantasy novel Born of Malice (Ruadan Books). Xan is also part of the Sauútiverse, with stories in the multi award-nominated anthology Mothersound (Android Press) as well as Sauúti Terrors (Flame Tree Press). Feel free to say hi on socials @xan_writer or @xanvanrooyen.
people.name: Xan van Rooyen

people.bio: Xu is a first generation bilingual immigrant comedian, writer, actor and TTRPG enthusiast. She made the classic jump from tech consultant to the arts. Her writing bylines include Reductress, McSweeneyes, Weekly Humorist and more. She has a forthcoming story in Analog, is part of the Clarion 2026 class, and lives in California.
people.name: Xu Mason

people.bio: Yana Galindo is a Spanish and French tutor and podcaster based in the Washington, D.C. area. She holds a B.A. in Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL) and a minor in Spanish. She is the host of the Spanish language podcast “espaÑolismo” and the French podcast “français finesse”. Her passions include learning languages, reading fantasy literature, and amateur photography.
people.name: Yana Galindo

people.bio:
Born and raise in East Lansing, MI, lived most of my life in Sadui Arabia.
BS in Computer Engineering from KAU, Graduate Studies in Future Technologies from Singularity University.
Serial Entreprenuer, co-founder of Yatakhayalooc Co. Ltd that was founded to nurtuer and grow Arabian SFF. Author of Yaqteenya the first Arabic Alt-History novel, co author of HWJN, Somewhere! & Binyameen, and translator of several works such as Drath Vader & Wild Cards to Arabic.
people.name: Yasser M Bahjatt

people.bio: Yume Kitasei (www.yumekitasei.com) is a Japanese and American writer of science fiction. She is the author of three novels, Saltcrop, The Stardust Grail, and The Deep Sky. Her books have been published in half a dozen languages, included in "Best of the Year" lists by The Washington Post, NPR, and Kirkus, and shortlisted for the Libby and Goodreads Choice. She lives in Brooklyn with two cats, Boondoggle and Filibuster, and chirps occasionally @Yumewrites at Instagram and Blue Sky.
people.name: Yume Kitasei

people.bio:
Yvette Keller is the planet earth authority on Douglas Adams literary tourism, the 2023 Towel Day Ambassador, and the author of Douglas Adams’ London guide from Herb Lester and Associates.

Her short fiction leans toward SF/Fantasy at an extravagantly relaxed angle. You can find her work in literary magazines such as Enheduanna, Imitation Fruit Literary Magazine, and The Santa Barbara Literary Journal.

For fun, Yvette time travels in self-made historical costumes, reads constantly, and performs in short-form improv and live storytelling shows. She lives in the world of the television phenomenon, Psych, finding contract work as a business consultant, an industrial voiceover professional, and a holistic detective.
people.name: Yvette Keller

people.bio: I was born and raised in Los Angeles and worked in aerospace for 20+ years, including the Space Shuttle program for 12 years. A lifelong photographer, I expanded into other art media including membership in the Pastel Society of the West Coast. I am currently studying Spanish, Irish, Esperanto, Old English, and Navajo. My husband and I have been involved in fandom for nearly 40 years.
people.name: Yvonne Fay Morton

people.bio:
Zain Memon is a visionary game designer and transmedia creator who pioneered South Asia’s modern tabletop renaissance.
His political strategy board game SHASN is India's most played modern tabletop game. It has won IndieCade’s Social Impact Award and reached players in over 70 countries. Its sequel SHASN: AZADI, hailed as the "blueprint for semi-cooperative game design," became the first tabletop game honored by Games for Change. Memon has established games as transformative learning systems through his approach to play as pedagogy

His political strategy board game SHASN is India's most played modern tabletop game. It has won IndieCade's Social Impact Award and reached players in over 70 countries. Its sequel SHASN: AZADI, hailed as the "blueprint for semi-cooperative game design" became the first tabletop game honored by Games for Change. Memon has established games as transformative learning systems through his approach to play as pedagogy.
people.name: Zain Memon

people.bio:
Zhui Ning Chang is a Malaysian editor, writer, translator and researcher based in London, UK. They are editor-in-chief at IGNYTE-winning and Hugo-nominated khōréō magazine, where they acquire and edit cutting-edge speculative fiction by immigrant and diaspora writers.

As a writer, Zhui Ning’s writing includes the time travel adventure Asian Pirate Musical and queer romcom Seashore Yuanfen, as well as translations and essays published with PEN Malaysia, Science Fiction Studies, Strange Horizons, The BSFA Review, and more. Recently, Zhui Ning completed a PhD at Birkbeck, University of London, writing about race, decoloniality, and the publishing industry via Southeast Asian speculative fiction.
people.name: Zhui Ning Chang

people.bio: Zoe Cunningham was born into a fantasy world. She spent her childhood immersed in books by authors including Douglas Adams, Isaac Asimov and Ursula Le Guin. She continued to evade the real world by studying science - physics, chemistry and eventually a mathematics degree at Cambridge University, before taking a job as a computer programmer at a startup. Real-life finally caught up with Zoe when she became Managing Director of the software firm in 2012, and she used her new adulting skills to quadruple the turnover of the business. ATIC is Zoe’s return to the fantasy land she wishes she never left, although sadly she still retains excellent financial and management skills.
people.name: Zoe Cunningham

people.bio: Zoe is a Nebula and BAFTA-nominated, GDC and Peabody award-winning writer and game designer who wrote on the medieval murder mystery game, Pentiment. She has an M.Phil in Medieval Studies from Trinity College Dublin and is currently a professional narrative designer and writer. In her spare time, she co-hosts the Maniculum Podcast, where she is dedicated to breaking down the anachronisms of modern medievalist fantasy and bringing the magic of the Middle Ages to life for storytellers, GMs, and creatives alike. She also provides resources to aspiring narrative designers looking to get into the craft.
people.name: Zoe Franznick
